articles.title: What we learned from Nvidia's first earnings call without Jensen Huang - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
What we learned from Nvidia’s first earnings call without Jensen Huang
Nvidia Corp. reported its quarterly results this week, and contrary to the prevailing narrative, the sky didn’t fall.
Revenue more than doubled year-over-year. The Vera Rubin chip platform achieved the fastest product ramp in the company’s history, and management raised its fiscal 2028 growth outlook to roughly 75%, up from 70%. By all accounts, it was a solid beat and raise.
This was Nvidia’s first earnings call without co-founder Jensen Huang, whose resignation as president and chief executive was announced on Nov. 12. Board Chair Harvey Jones told investors that the resignation followed the “disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms.” Hours after Huang publicly said he would be willing to return, Jones said the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” and would not take questions about the circumstances or the board’s ongoing investigation.
Colette Kress, the longtime chief financial officer who is now also serving as interim CEO, set the tone in her first minute: “Our ambition will not change. Our passion for innovation will not change, and our commitment to customers, partners, and shareholders will not change.”
After listening to the call, I believe Nvidia answered the short-term question and left the long-term one open. The company made a convincing case that it can execute without its founder. It has yet to show who decides where it goes next. Here are five things we learned and what they mean for those who buy, budget for or operate artificial intelligence infrastructure.
1. The machine will run without the founder
The fear going into the call was disruption. The quarter closed before Huang’s exit, so the results can’t settle that. The guidance can, and it went up. Hyperscalers brought Vera Rubin into production in about a month, half the time Grace Blackwell required. The roadmap is set through Vera Rubin Ultra next year and Feynman in 2028, and Kress said the supply agreements extend through the end of the decade.
She explained that the past month has been “Business as usual.” Kress added, “We’ve engaged with our customers, suppliers and partners. They’re all 100% behind us.” She also noted that TSMC leadership was at Nvidia’s offices this week.
I have long held that Nvidia’s moat was never the silicon. It’s the accumulated layers of systems, software and supply chain built around it. The past week was the first real test of that view, and so far, it’s holding. A yearly product cadence this complex runs on thousands of engineers and a supply chain planned years in advance.
Asked about talent retention, Kress acknowledged that “there are diverse opinions” among employees while insisting they are “committed to doing their life’s work” at Nvidia. The company’s talent can’t be overstated, and although Huang was the face of the company, the employees are what made it tick.
Earlier this week, Cisco Systems Inc. CEO Chuck Robbins appeared with Brian Sozzi. When asked whether he still trusts Nvidia, Robbins replied immediately, “Absolutely.” He added, “The industry’s bigger than one person. I don’t care how good you are. There are a lot of smart people. There are 42,000 people at Nvidia. So I’m not all that concerned.” Huang may have been the most visible Nvidia employee, but the company is full of smart, driven people. Leadership understands this, and I expect turnover to have minimal impact.
Employee retention is a top-of-mind issue for Nvidia executives. Business Insider reported this week that the company held its first all-hands meeting after Huang. The article noted that Kress announced plans to accelerate pay raises and equity grants, Jones discussed the CEO search and Buck outlined the roadmap. It’s reasonable to believe that Huang’s departure was a shock to employees, but the business goes on, and I expect things to settle down in short order.
For information technology buyers, nothing changes about what you’ve ordered or planned over the next 18 to 24 months. Don’t pause a deployment because of a leadership headline. The advice I gave in August still applies: Welcome Nvidia’s simplification and hedge the dependency.
2. The board wants a diplomat as much as a technologist
One of the more interesting comments on the call came from Jones, not Kress. In describing the CEO search, which will consider both internal and external candidates, he said the board “appreciates that we’re living in a world where advanced silicon technologies and national security dynamics are driving major changes in our marketplace. Our new CEO will need to navigate those waters carefully.”
That was paired with immediate action. On the morning of earnings, the board created a standing national security and export control oversight committee of three directors that will retain outside experts. Kress disclosed that Nvidia is no longer shipping licensed Hopper data center products to China and noted that the U.S. Commerce Department issued new export controls this week, which the company “still has some time to study.”
Huang was a product visionary who also served as the industry’s chief diplomat. The board is now signaling that fluency in Washington is a core requirement, on par with technical vision.
For IT leaders at multinationals, export policy is now a deployment variable. The new Commerce rule is intended to block remote access to advanced chips via data centers in third countries, so the location of your capacity and who can access it are now compliance questions. Bring your compliance team into AI infrastructure planning early.
3. Allocation has become a readiness test
With demand still far ahead of supply, who gets Nvidia systems matters more than what they cost. Kress laid out the criteria more clearly than I’ve heard before. First are land, power and shell, meaning whether a customer’s facility is ready to receive and use the gear in the quarter it ships. Second is capital. Third, for customers that aren’t investment-grade, is proof of off-take, or evidence that someone has committed to use the capacity.
“All are getting the same pricing,” Kress said. “That is super important for us, and we just need to assure that they are ready on their side in terms of being able to accept the compute.”
Those same factors were incorporated into the guidance. Kress said the outlook “considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of end customer demand, and our customers’ access to capital.” The reality is that the AI bottleneck has shifted from the chip to the building, the grid and the balance sheet. Nvidia is serving as the industry’s underwriter, determining who is ready.
The lesson for enterprise buyers is that readiness is the currency. If you want on-premises systems, secure power, cooling and funding before requesting allocation. If you can’t, buy capacity from a provider that has already cleared this hurdle. In my view, this also helps explain why sovereign AI is growing so quickly for Nvidia. Those projects often arrive with land and power already in place.
4. Nvidia’s checkbook is getting pickier
Over the past year, Nvidia has used its balance sheet to seed the ecosystem through guarantees, investments, and commitments to neoclouds and AI labs. Though neoclouds remain important, Kress brought a different tone to this audience. She said Nvidia will “continue to be disciplined and selective” in supporting neoclouds and that it is “rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees” as other sources of capital become available. Asked about vendor financing, she acknowledged that “a lot of things have changed over this last quarter.”
Two notable details emerged during the call. When Bernstein Research analyst Stacy Rasgon pressed on what he read as new disclosure language about neocloud commitments, Kress explained that Nvidia’s guarantees take effect only after a partner has raised its own debt and equity, built the facility and installed the compute. If the project stalls, the guarantee lapses.
“Is it new? No. Did we change anything? No,” she said. Even so, spelling it out clarifies Nvidia’s participation in neoclouds. When asked about uses of capital beyond the share buyback, which she said Nvidia still plans to complete, she put suppliers first: “The top priority is going to be our suppliers.” Prepayments to expand capacity come before customer financing, which will be reserved for “very strong customers.”
This was a critical piece of information for investors. I’ve previously compared vendor-financed neoclouds to the CLECs of the internet era, where the financing organization was left holding the bag. A CFO-led Nvidia appears to see the same risk. The result is a shakeout in which well-capitalized neoclouds with contracted demand grow stronger, while thinly funded ones struggle to secure systems. This should offer some comfort to investors that circular financing has been de-risked.
The flip side is that someone still must fund the buildout outside the hyperscalers. Kress pointed to infrastructure capital partners establishing financing platforms. Whether that money arrives as fast as Nvidia steps back is what to watch for.
My advice to IT buyers is to ask, before signing a multiyear deal with a neocloud, how it’s financed, how much capacity is committed and where it stands in Nvidia’s allocation queue. Those were niche questions a year ago. They should be standard due diligence now.
5. Agents are pulling demand well beyond the GPU
The demand story has shifted from training models to running agents, broadening what customers need from Nvidia. Citing OpenRouter data, Kress said agentic workloads now account for roughly 80% of tokens. Falling token prices are driving more usage, keeping GPU rental rates climbing.
The CPU growth story shouldn’t surprise anyone. In May, I wrote that agentic AI opens a massive new spigot for Nvidia on the CPU side. This quarter, demand outpaced supply. “Agentic AI is driving extraordinary demand for CPUs, far outstripping supply,” Kress said, noting that Nvidia’s Vera CPU is now adopted by CoreWeave, Meta, Nscale and Open AI. Agents spend much of their time calling tools, running code and moving data, which is general-purpose work. A CPU shortage amid a GPU boom shows how quickly the workload is changing.
Nvidia is also filling in the layers above and around the hardware. The agent safety platform pairs OpenShell, which limits what agents can access, with Sentry, which runs on BlueField data processing units and monitors agent behavior in silicon. In my view, the biggest barrier to deploying agents in production is control, not model quality.
The network is part of this, too. Kress said co-packaged optics is in volume production, and Lambda’s deployment, announced at this week’s SC26 conference, is the first large-scale proof point. Nvidia is a formidable networking vendor, though buyers mixing accelerators will still want to weigh a network supplier that isn’t also selling a competing chip.
For IT buyers, plan CPU capacity for agent workloads now, and insist that agent controls reside outside the model, in infrastructure you can audit.
Dark-horse CEO candidates
The question of who the new CEO will be might not be just about Nvidia but about the entire industry. If the board goes internal, Ian Buck seems to be the frontrunner. Externally, the names most bandied about are Advanced Micro Devices Inc. CEO Lisa Su, Arm Ltd. CEO Rene Haas and Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian, or we could see Manuvir Das make a comeback and return to the company.
Most industry watchers describe Nvidia as a chip company, a view that is about a decade out of date. Nvidia’s value comes from the full systems it has built around its silicon. Each is a stack tailored to an industry: hardware, libraries, frameworks, pretrained models, simulation and developer tools, all tuned to work together.
The next CEO must treat silicon as a key layer of an open, secure, agentic enterprise stack. Enterprises won’t buy GPUs. They’ll buy outcomes: agents that run safely on governed data across clouds, on-premises and at the edge. Whoever runs Nvidia next must sell that outcome, play well within an ecosystem Nvidia doesn’t fully control, and make security a core part of the platform. Here are three dark-horse candidates to consider:
Matt Garman. The Amazon Web Services Inc. CEO has led the world’s largest cloud through the shift to AI. He knows what it takes to turn infrastructure into consumable services at enormous scale. Garman also lives the open-stack approach: AWS offers model choice, runs its own Trainium chips alongside Nvidia’s, and sells to enterprises that want flexibility rather than lock-in. He would bring operational discipline and a deep feel for the customer. The question is whether Nvidia’s biggest customer-turned-competitor can credibly lead the supplier.
Jeetu Patel, Cisco Systems Inc.’s president and chief product officer, is the best storyteller in enterprise tech after Huang himself. He has spent the past few years rebuilding Cisco’s portfolio around secure AI infrastructure, integrating networking, security and observability into a single platform. That is exactly the “open, secure, agentic” stack Nvidia must deliver. Patel thinks in platforms, moves quickly,and has been personally using AI agents to shape his product views. He also has deep enterprise credibility, which Nvidia needs more than additional credibility with hyperscalers.
Charlie Giancarlo, CEO of Everpure (formerly Pure Storage), may be the most underrated name here. He built networking businesses at Cisco, spent time in private equity, and has repositioned Pure as a data management company. Storage revenue is growing thanks to hyperscaler wins. Giancarlo understands that agentic AI depends on data and that the data layer and the network are where enterprise AI succeeds or fails. He is a systems thinker who has led a platform transition before.
Two final points on the CEO hire: For some reason, there is a tremendous amount of industry chatter that Jensen Huang was the only person at Nvidia with key relationships with suppliers, partners, and other ecosystem providers. I know for a fact that is not true. Nvidia’s leadership, which includes Buck, Deb Shoquist (executive vice president of operations), Nico Caprez (vice president of global AI development), Gilad Shainer and Kevin Deierling (networking leadership), Kress and others, all have deep relationships with the ecosystem.
Also, I wouldn’t expect the board to make a snap decision about its next CEO. The roadmap is baked beyond Feynman, and the company can continue for a couple of years, if needed. This is an important hire; the board should take its time and ensure it’s the right person.
Final thoughts
This call confirmed what many industry watchers, including me, have long believed: The moat was built in layers, and those layers held. Supply is constrained, the roadmap is set and customers are still asking for more than Nvidia can build.
Kress closed the call by saying, “We’ve got this.” On execution, I believe her. Kress is a steady hand right now, and the discipline she brings to capital allocation should make the AI buildout healthier. The bets that created Nvidia’s position, though, were placed years before the market arrived. Post-Jensen, Nvidia will continue to perform as it did; as Robbins put it, no one is bigger than the industry.
My advice to IT buyers is to stick with current plans and closely monitor the CEO search. Since Nvidia’s roadmap is baked through Feynman and beyond, it can ride momentum for the next two years or longer.
Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

articles.title: Seagate’s shuckable 20TB desktop hard drive is down to $500
articles.text:
Seagate’s shuckable 20TB Expansion desktop hard drive drops to $500 ahead of Black Friday
An early Black Friday price cut on one of our favorite desktop hard drives for work and media backups
When it comes to desktop hard drives , Seagate remains one of our favorite picks - notably, the Expansion line, which comes in a range of capacities. But for serious storage, I recommend the 20TB version for archiving, business use, and media backups.
The cheapest I can find it is direct from Seagate, where the Expansion Desktop 20TB is down to $500 (was $630). That works out at around 2.75 cents per usable gigabyte once the drive is formatted. At Newegg, it's still selling for $700, while it's $730 at Amazon. So the manufacturer is offering the best deal ahead of Black Friday.
This hard drive unit gives you plenty of disk-based storage for backups, expanding a desktop's capacity, or consolidating large files. It’s also an ideal option if you need somewhere to archive years’ worth of photos or videos. It's also shuckable - which is great for NAS and home server builders looking to prise open the enclosure and slot their own SATA drive inside (warranty be damned!).
Today’s best Seagate Expansion 20TB hard drive deal
The 20TB model is cheaper from Seagate than anywhere else I've seen right now. Featuring fast USB 3.0 transfer speeds, it's compatible with Windows, macOS, and ChromeOS. The unit also comes with Seagate's Rescue Data Recovery Services software for additional backup protection.
Why we recommend the Seagate Expansion 20TB
Reliability and that huge storage capacity are the two main reasons why we recommend the Seagate Expansion Desktop Drive.
But what I especially like is the simple plug-and-play nature of the device. Connecting over USB, it's a case of connecting it to your Windows, Mac, or Chromebook and you're ready to start backing up.
It includes Seagate Rescue Data Recovery Services, alongside a two-year limited warranty. It's also worth noting that this isn't a portable drive. There's no BUS-power here, so it uses an external power adapter, which is included. For a home office setup, it's ideal.
Price context and historical value
At $499.99, the drive comes to about $27.47 per usable terabyte after formatting, which makes this a very tempting option for large-scale desktop storage, backup, and expansion.
As I've noted, this is the cheapest price I've found on the drive, which is being sold for over $200 more at Newegg and Amazon. And for comparison, Newegg has the 16TB model priced at $450. So, for the extra $50, you're gaining an additional 4TB storage.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Seagate Expansion if… you need a large and reliable desktop drive for backups, media, and long-term storage
❌ Skip the Seagate Expansion if… you need portable storage or fast SSD-level transfer speeds.

articles.title: FinBursa names Angelica Tigan CRO to lead US and global expansion
articles.text:
FinBursa names Angelica Tigan CRO to lead US and global expansion
- New York-based private markets technology company FinBursa has appointed Angelica Tigan as Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) to oversee global sales and partnerships, with an immediate focus on expanding its presence in the US.
- Tigan brings nearly 20 years of experience in private markets technology, having held sales leadership roles at BlackRock's Aladdin business and eFront, alongside previous positions at Intralinks and Gen II Fund Services.
- Co-founded and led by CEO Ismail Badereldine, FinBursa provides an AI-powered platform for private equity, venture capital, private credit, real estate and M&A firms, integrating investment CRM, deal management, fundraising, investor relations and virtual data rooms.
- The appointment follows the launch of FinBursa 360, which incorporates ALF, an agentic AI system designed to support investment research, due diligence, investor identification, fundraising and M&A transactions through five specialised AI agents and an orchestrator.
Press release:
FinBursa, the intelligent front office for private markets, has appointed Angelica Tigan, a former BlackRock and eFront sales leader, as Chief Revenue Officer to lead its global commercial expansion following the launch of FinBursa 360. Based in the US, Tigan will lead sales and partnerships worldwide, with an immediate focus on the US.
Tigan brings close to two decades in private markets technology, having built, led and scaled sales teams at BlackRock (Aladdin) and eFront, with previous experience at Intralinks and Gen II Fund Services.
FinBursa 360 is an all-in-one platform for private equity, private credit, real estate, venture capital and M&A advisory firms, family offices, wealth managers, placement agents and fund administrators. It brings investment CRM, deal flow and deal management, virtual data rooms (VDR), fundraising, opportunity distribution, investor relations and investor portals into one system of record.
AI built into the platform, not bolted on
ALF, FinBursa's agentic AI, runs five specialised AI agents and an orchestrator for fund managers, capital allocators and M&A advisors. Its relationship intelligence maps who knows whom across the firm and surfaces warm introductions to investors and buyers. Its research agent switches on for any deal, fundraise, sale or portfolio company, monitoring news and RSS feeds across its industry and geography for AI signals that help teams reduce risk and act on opportunities faster.
For fund managers and investors running due diligence, ALF reviews data room documents, flags contradictions, and drafts investment committee materials. For firms raising capital, it identifies best-fit investors from mandates, past commitments, recent engagement and AI signals, with shortlists and draft outreach. For sell-side M&A advisors, it helps prepare the CIM, build data rooms, shortlist buyers using AI signals, and track buyer outreach at every stage.
Ismail Badereldine, co-founder and CEO of FinBursa, said: "In the AI era, private markets firms need a connected front office, and we expect demand to grow sharply. Angelica understands what these firms value most, and knows how to turn great technology into real results for them. Her appointment will accelerate our growth in the US and globally."
Angelica Tigan, FinBursa's Chief Revenue Officer, added: "I've spent my career helping private capital firms get more from their technology, and FinBursa stands out. It's a modern, AI-native platform that connects the front office first, so AI can do far more. Firms can be up and running in days rather than months, without long implementation projects, and the return on investment is clear. I see a significant opportunity to bring this globally, particularly in the US."

articles.title: Gemini 4 Neon : Google continue de dégainer de nouveaux modèles d'IA, au risque de vous embrouiller
articles.text:
Fin septembre, on avait droit à Gemini 4 Argon. Moins d’un mois plus tard, c’était Gemini 4 Carbon qui arrivait et la semaine dernière, c’était au tour de Gemini 4 Hydrogen d’apparaître. Cette fois-ci, c’est Gemini 4 Neon qui est là, avec la promesse d’un modèle intermédiaire entre performances et coûts maîtrisés.
Gemini 4 Neon : un modèle entre deux extrêmes
Comme Google l’explique dans son billet de blog qui annonce ce modèle, Gemini 4 Neon est conçu pour les travaux qui demandent à la fois du raisonnement avancé et une exécution rapide. Programmation, analyse de données, recherche scientifique, synthèse de documents, automatisation de tâches… ce Neon sait a priori tout faire. Google le positionne entre Carbon, réservé aux gros projets, et Hydrogen, plus optimisé pour les usages quotidiens.
C’est pourquoi Gemini 4 Neon vise les tâches fréquentes, mais complexes. C’est parfait pour faire de l’analyse de tableurs, de PDF, de graphiques ou de fichiers audio/vidéo. Des tâches qui peuvent être régulières en entreprise et avec une IA qui veut s’intégrer dans la routine des travailleurs. Ce modèle possède une fenêtre de contexte d’un million de tokens. Pour le moment, Gemini 4 Neon est accessible aux utilisateurs abonnés à Google AI Pro ou AI Ultra dans l’application Gemini.
Pourquoi Google multiplie les modèles d’IA
Google ne sort pas Neon par simple effet d’annonce, à l’instar d’Argon, de Carbon ou d’Hydrogen. Ces différentes versions ne changent pas beaucoup entre elles, c’est toujours Gemini 4 derrière. Mais avec Neon, l’entreprise cherche à éviter le compromis habituel entre un modèle très puissant, mais lent et coûteux, et un modèle rapide, mais limité sur les tâches complexes.
Le géant de l’IA a donc enfin créé une famille de modèles : Hydrogen remplace les usages rapides, Carbon est destiné aux projets qui demandent de la précision et Argon est juste en dessous de Carbon en termes de performances. Neon vient donc se glisser entre Hydrogen et Argon/Carbon, avec un coût moins élevé : 3 dollars par million de tokens en entrée et de 15 dollars par million en sortie. À court terme, Neon est cependant plus cher au token que Carbon (2 et 10 dollars) ; c’est normal, puisque Carbon profite d’une réduction de 95% jusqu’au 30 novembre.
Google n’est d’ailleurs pas le seul à publier un modèle dit intermédiaire. OpenAI aussi s’y est penché récemment avec GPT-6.1 Terra sorti le mois dernier. Lui aussi est dans la même niche : un niveau intermédiaire, conçu pour des tâches professionnelles et complexes. Néanmoins, le prix n’est pas le même, puisque le modèle d’OpenAI est trois fois moins cher.

articles.title: Yellowjackets (Canal+) : on a vu les premiers épisodes de la saison 4, voici notre avis
articles.text:
Yellowjackets (Canal+) : on a vu les premiers épisodes de la saison 4, voici notre avis
La quatrième et dernière saison de la célèbre série Yellowjackets arrive cette semaine sur Paramount+. Voici ce qu'on a pensé des premiers épisodes, garanti sans spoiler.
Les footballeuses de Yellowjackets sont de retour dans une quatrième et ultime saison de cette série dramatique, attendue le 20 novembre sur Paramount+. Une dernière salve d'épisodes donc pour cette histoire entre survie, horreur et thriller psychologique.
En amont de la diffusion, Les Numériques a pu voir huit des 10 épisodes qui composent cette saison 4. Voici notre avis, garanti sans spoiler.
L'histoire de la saison 4
Tandis que dans les années 1990, les survivantes s'efforcent d'effacer toute trace de leurs fautes avant l'arrivée des secours, une ancienne amante refait surface dans les années 2020, et pas par hasard. Les retrouvailles s'annoncent tout sauf joyeuses. Elles risquent de piquer.
Une série en fin de course
Voilà maintenant quatre saisons que les spectateurs de Yellowjackets regardent la série en espérant percer ses mystères. Que se trame-t-il vraiment dans les bois sauvages du Grand Nord ? Les forces surnaturelles qui imbibent la série sont-elles réelles ou le fruit d'une situation traumatisante ? Quatre saisons que les scénaristes du show persistent à cultiver l'ambiguïté.
Dans la dernière saison du show, ce refus de donner une réponse définitive et de laisser planer le doute finit par donner le sentiment que la série tourne en rond, car le récit ne semble pas véritablement progresser. Il passe même d'une intrigue à deux vitesses à trois chronologies différentes, ralentissant encore plus la narration.
On suit d'une part les Yellowjackets adolescentes une fois secourus, alors qu'elles s'ajustent tant bien que mal à un retour à la normale. Ensuite, on les voit aussi avant l'arrivée des secours, tentant de masquer les horribles actes qu'elles ont commis pour survivre. Enfin, le récit se poursuit toujours dans les années 2020, tandis que les versions adultes des personnages sont rattrapées par le passé.
Le problème, c'est que ces différents pans du récit ne sont pas tous égaux, et au bout des huit épisodes que nous avons pu voir, on se demande encore et toujours où cela va finir par nous mener. L'histoire apparaît coincée entre des personnages auto-destructeurs, une intrigue dans le présent semblant ne pas savoir quoi raconter, et une tension qui s'effiloche plus la série arrive à sa fin.
C'est cependant toujours dans le passé que la série trouve sa plus grande force, aussi bien dans les scènes montrant les Yellowjackets lors de leurs derniers jours dans la nature, que celles consacrées à leur retour à la civilisation. Shauna, Misty, Taissa ou encore Van sont alors contraintes de réconcilier la vie normale avec tout ce qu'elles ont traversé dans la forêt, et la série nous entraîne donc sur un terrain encore inexploité jusqu'à maintenant.
Malheureusement, si cet aspect du récit est rafraîchissant, on regrette de constater que la série peine à captiver sur tous les fronts, d'autant plus que la distribution des versions adultes des protagonistes est toujours aussi excellente. De Christina Ricci à Melanie Lynskey en passant par Hilary Swank et Tawny Cypress, toutes brillent à l'écran, malgré une intrigue bancale.
En somme, la dernière saison de Yellowjackets, handicapée par des arcs narratifs inégaux, une ambiguïté usée et une tension trop diluée, s'avère plutôt fade. Quand bien même il nous reste encore deux épisodes à voir, il en demeure que la série termine sa course essoufflée, en grand besoin de s'arrêter.
La saison 4 de Yellowjackets est disponible à partir du vendredi 20 novembre, en exclusivité sur Paramount+ dont l'offre est aussi incluse dans le bouquet Ciné Séries de Canal+.

articles.title: IA ajudou a descobrir falha crítica no Java • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
IA ajudou a descobrir falha crítica no Java
Brecha pode permitir invasões remotas em sistemas vulneráveis. Oracle já liberou uma correção.
Falha pode permitir execução remota de códigos e comprometer sistemas de empresas, bancos e órgãos públicos.
Uma startup de cibersegurança descobriu, com ajuda de inteligência artificial, uma vulnerabilidade crítica no Java, linguagem de programação utilizada por empresas de diversos setores. Batizada de Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a falha pode permitir que invasores executem códigos de forma remota e assumam o controle de sistemas vulneráveis.
A descoberta foi feita pela empresa Calif e contou com o apoio do GPT-6 Cyber, modelo de cibersegurança da OpenAI. No relatório técnico, o pesquisador Quang Luong também descreve o uso do agente Codex.
A empresa afirma que o pesquisador levou cerca de uma hora para encontrar a vulnerabilidade e mais duas para desenvolver a primeira exploração funcional. O custo com o uso de IA teria ficado abaixo de US$ 200 (cerca de R$ 1.070 em conversão direta).
O problema está no decodificador Base64 do OpenJDK. A ferramenta converte informações codificadas em Base64 para seu formato original, algo comum em processos de autenticação, transferência de arquivos e comunicação entre sistemas. Segundo a Calif, uma sequência de 64 letras “A” seguida de um sinal de igual pode acionar a vulnerabilidade em determinadas instalações.
O erro está em uma otimização que utiliza instruções específicas de processadores para acelerar a decodificação. A falha pode provocar travamentos, exposição de informações e, em certas situações, permitir a execução remota de códigos. A Calif demonstrou explorações em aplicações como Keycloak, Atlassian Jira, Confluence, Jenkins e JFrog Artifactory.
Isso não significa que qualquer computador com Java esteja vulnerável. A vulnerabilidade afeta versões específicas do OpenJDK executadas em processadores x86-64 compatíveis com AVX-512 VBMI. Sistemas com processadores ARM64 não são considerados afetados.
A descoberta amplia uma sequência de vulnerabilidades identificadas com auxílio de IA. Em outubro, a própria Calif também esteve envolvida na descoberta de problemas no PHP, que afetaram servidores e serviços públicos.
A Oracle publicou uma atualização de segurança na terça-feira (17/11) para corrigir a vulnerabilidade. A falha foi classificada pela fabricante como de alta gravidade. A Agência de Segurança Cibernética e de Infraestrutura dos Estados Unidos (CISA) recomendou que organizações instalem imediatamente as correções disponíveis. O alerta também orienta administradores a identificar versões vulneráveis do Java, inclusive as incorporadas a aplicativos de terceiros.
Autoridades da Alemanha e dos Países Baixos informaram que, até quarta-feira (18/11), não havia registros conhecidos de ataques bem-sucedidos utilizando a vulnerabilidade. Isso não elimina o risco, especialmente porque os detalhes técnicos já foram divulgados.

articles.title: Guía de GTA 6: cómo conseguir más vehículos y ampliar los espacios disponibles
articles.text:
En GTA 6, encontrar un auto y hacerlo tuyo son cosas distintas. Puedes robar vehículos para desplazarte, pero para incorporarlos a tu colección personal tendrás que registrarlos. Ese proceso se desbloquea al avanzar en la historia y tiene un límite de espacios que podrás ampliar con garajes o mediante ciertas misiones.
Una guía indica que durante el primer capítulo no podrás cambiar el vehículo personal de Jason, aunque sí podrás conducir autos robados. Para desbloquear el registro, tendrás que avanzar hasta el capítulo 2 y completar la misión “Moses (Take A Vehicle to Moses)”. Allí conocerás a Moses y accederás a su taller en Port Gellhorn, donde podrás revisar tus espacios, reparar vehículos y registrarlos.
Cómo registrar un auto y sumarlo a tu colección
Antes de llevar un vehículo al taller de Moses, tendrás que revisar si cumple los requisitos para ser registrado. Según la guía, al principio solo podrás registrar autos sin rastreador. Para comprobarlo, usarás la aplicación Waink del teléfono del personaje. Que un auto sea caro o llamativo no significa que puedas incorporarlo de inmediato a tu colección.
Si el vehículo es apto, condúcelo hasta el taller y revisa cuántos espacios tienes disponibles en la pantalla de registro. Si queda lugar, podrás completar el proceso. Si tu colección ya está llena, tendrás que liberar un espacio vendiendo un auto o aumentar tu capacidad antes de registrar otro.
Guardar un vehículo en un garaje también puede servir para conservarlo mientras esperas desbloquear su registro. Pero estacionarlo no lo convierte en un vehículo personal: para que aparezca entre los autos que puedes solicitar, tendrás que completar el registro.
Al comienzo del capítulo 3 se ampliarán las opciones. La guía señala que podrás vender autos robados en cualquier Pay ’n’ Spray y registrar vehículos que tengan rastreadores estándar. Esto facilitará el proceso, aunque no eliminará el límite de espacios: aun con más opciones de registro, necesitarás tener capacidad disponible.
Garajes para ampliar el espacio
Una forma de conservar más vehículos registrados será comprar garajes adicionales. Más adelante en el capítulo 2 recibirás la aplicación Vice City Real Estate, con la que podrás adquirir propiedades en distintas zonas de Leonida. Los garajes sumarán espacios para guardar vehículos y ampliar tu colección.
El precio dependerá de la propiedad, así que convendrá revisar cuánto cuesta antes de comprarla. Si necesitas espacio pronto y tienes dinero suficiente, podrás adquirir un garaje. Si puedes esperar, también tendrás una opción ligada a la historia: hacia la mitad del juego, Valentina te dará acceso a un garaje en Ocean Beach que añadirá dos espacios para vehículos personales.
Si no tienes lugar para un nuevo auto, vender uno de los que ya registraste liberará un espacio. Así podrás reemplazarlo sin comprar una propiedad. La decisión dependerá de si prefieres conservar los vehículos que ya tienes o ampliar la capacidad total.
Cómo encontrar los autos que ya tienes
Una vez que registres varios vehículos, podrás consultar cuáles están disponibles desde la aplicación Scooter Bros en el teléfono. Allí revisarás tu lista de vehículos personales y podrás elegir uno para que se lo lleven al personaje. También podrás visitar el taller de Moses o un Pay ’n’ Spray para ver los vehículos guardados.
En resumen, el proceso tendrá tres pasos: avanzar en la historia para desbloquear el registro, comprobar que el auto pueda registrarse y asegurarte de tener espacio. Los garajes comprados y el desbloqueo de Valentina permitirán ampliar el límite; vender un vehículo, en cambio, solo liberará un espacio ocupado. Así podrás decidir cuándo guardar un auto, cuándo sumarlo a tu colección y cuándo buscar más capacidad.

articles.title: Egypt's Connect Money raises $3.5 million pre-Series A
articles.text:
Egypt's Connect Money raises $3.5 million pre-Series A
- Egypt-based fintech Connect Money has raised $3.5 million in a pre-Series A round led by existing investors Mohamed Farouk, Algebra Ventures and DisrupTech Ventures. The transaction combines new capital with secondary share sales, allowing several early investors to make partial exits.
- Founded in 2024 by Ayman Essawy, Marwan Kenawy and Momtaz Moussa, Connect Money provides embedded finance infrastructure that enables businesses to issue branded prepaid cards and integrate financial services without building their own banking systems.
- Operating under a licence from the Central Bank of Egypt, the company manages card issuance, regulatory compliance, programme management and daily operations through partnerships with banks, payment processors and card networks. It has issued more than 300,000 cards across six sectors.
- The funding brings Connect Money's reported cumulative financing to $11.5 million and will support expansion into Saudi Arabia and Morocco, including regulatory licensing and local technology infrastructure. The company is pursuing a Saudi Central Bank licence and targeting a Moroccan launch in the first half of 2027.
Press release:
Egyptian fintech startup Connect Money has raised $3.5 million in a pre-Series A funding round led by existing investors Mohamed Farouk, Algebra Ventures and DisrupTech Ventures, as it prepares to expand its embedded finance services into Saudi Arabia and Morocco.
The transaction combines fresh investment with secondary share sales, providing partial exits for several early investors. The company did not disclose how much of the $3.5 million represents new capital.
The round brings Connect Money's reported cumulative funding to $11.5 million, following an $8 million seed round in June 2024.
Founded in Egypt in 2024 by Ayman Essawy, Marwan Kenawy and Momtaz Moussa, Connect Money provides embedded finance infrastructure that allows businesses to offer branded prepaid cards and integrate financial services into their existing products.
Operating under a licence from the Central Bank of Egypt, the company works with banks, payment processors and card networks to manage card issuance, regulatory compliance, programme management and daily operations.
Connect Money said it has issued more than 300,000 cards across six sectors, including retail, fintech, agritech, education, oil and gas, and platforms serving small and medium-sized enterprises.
The new investment will support the company's planned entry into Saudi Arabia and Morocco, with a focus on securing regulatory approvals and establishing the infrastructure required to operate in both markets.
In Saudi Arabia, Connect Money is seeking a licence from the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA). In Morocco, it is building its local operational and technology infrastructure ahead of a planned commercial launch in the first half of 2027.
The expansion will extend Connect Money's embedded finance services beyond Egypt, as it targets businesses seeking to offer payment products without developing their own banking infrastructure.

articles.title: Panique chez Meta : l’agent IA Muse serait un véritable cauchemar pour la vie privée des utilisateurs
articles.text:
Un vent de panique circule dans les rangs de Meta. D’après des documents internes, son agent phare, Muse, fouille des messages privés et fait peser un doute sur la protection des données de ses utilisateurs. Voici tout ce que l’on sait.
Lancé en septembre, Muse a trouvé son public en un temps record avec une ascension fulgurante. Sa promesse : accomplir toute une ribambelle de tâches à la place de l’utilisateur, qu’il s’agisse de répondre aux e-mails, de réserver un restaurant ou de faire des achats en ligne. Il représente la réponse tant espérée par Mark Zuckerberg pour venir concurrencer les OpenAI, Anthropic et Google. Mais cette montée en puissance ne se fait visiblement pas sans écarts, révèle une enquête édifiante de Reuters.
Les alertes internes se multiplient
L’agence de presse a en effet pu consulter de nombreux messages internes échangés entre les employés du géant des réseaux sociaux, spécifiquement dans un groupe où ils signalent les problèmes à l’équipe qui développe l’agent. Le constat est glaçant : Ils y décrivent une intelligence artificielle qui prend la parole sans qu’on le lui demande, et dont certains messages ne semblent pas leur être adressés.
Par exemple, un employé qui discutait météo et marées avec Muse a reçu, sans rien demander, les soldes de deux comptes bancaires qui n’étaient pas les siens. Sa collègue a eu droit à un rappel pour répondre à un message de sa sœur sur Signal, messagerie chiffrée qu’elle n’avait jamais connectée à l’agent. « Cela ressemble à une atteinte extrême à la vie privée. Je ne lui ai certainement pas donné accès à d’autres applications », a-t-elle écrit.
Une troisième personne s’est vue proposer de contacter le vendeur d’une table basse qui n’était pas la sienne, suggérant une potentielle fuite de données entre comptes. Et ce n’est pas tout, car certains y auraient même laissé de l’argent. Un salarié a ainsi vu l’abonnement d’assurance de son chien grimper de 200 à 888 dollars par mois, tandis qu’un autre s’est retrouvé avec une réservation Airbnb non remboursable validée sans son accord.
Un problème qui dépasse Meta
Alors que ces incidents sont survenus dès septembre, et se sont poursuivis jusqu’à novembre, Daniel Roberts, porte-parole de Meta, évoque des « incidents isolés » résultant d’hallucinations, pas de fuites de données.
Mais pour en avoir le cœur net, Reuters a contacté Signal et l’AI Now Institute, un organisme qui étudie l’impact de l’IA sur la société. Et leurs tests ont démontré que l’agent peut effectivement lire des messages en contournant l’outil de connexion prévu par Meta. Sur Android, il passerait par l’accès aux notifications, une permission accordée dès l’installation et qui serait activée par défaut. Si les requêtes sont bloquées sur iPhone, l’IA détournerait les outils d’accessibilité conçus pour les personnes en situation de handicap sur Mac.
Dans ce contexte, Meredith Whittaker, présidente de Signal, accuse Meta d’avoir lancé Muse « sans montrer le moindre respect pour la vie privée ou la cybersécurité de base ». Elle exige que les applications puissent purement refuser les agents IA, et que les systèmes d’exploitation fassent respecter cette règle. Pour sa part, Apple a déployé une mise à jour de macOS qui limite l’usage de ces outils d’accessibilité et crée des permissions dédiées aux agents.
Mais dans ses conditions d’utilisation, Meta rend l’utilisateur responsable des actions de Muse. Ces nouvelles dérives risquent malgré tout d’entacher la réputation de l’entreprise, une habituée des scandales liés à la vie privée. Car de nombreux abus ont également été constatés avec l’utilisation de ses lunettes connectées.
- Tâches complètes de bout en bout
- Contrôles d’accès très détaillés
- Travail autonome en arrière-plan

articles.title: Unos científicos de la Universidad de Pensilvania quieren usar mantas de emergencia para construir edificaciones lunares
articles.text:
La tecnología ha dado muchas vueltas desde que se escribió el cuento de “Los tres cerditos”. Ahora las mejores casas no llevan solo ladrillo, sino que también están recubiertas de plástico. Al menos, es así si vas a vivir en la Luna. Y es que en los futuros asentamientos lunares no se valorará únicamente la resistencia de los materiales. También se buscarán aquellos que aíslen mejor de las temperaturas extremas, tanto altas como bajas. Existen algunas opciones que aíslan muy bien, como los aerogeles o los recubrimientos multicapa clásicos. Sin embargo, son demasiado frágiles para un ambiente tan extremo. Por eso, unos ingenieros han estado buscando alternativas hasta dar con una propuesta interesante: usar el material de las mantas de emergencia.
Capas apiladas de Mylar. Las mantas de emergencia están hechas con BoPET (tereftalato de polietileno orientado biaxialmente), un material conocido comercialmente como Mylar, que se obtiene estirando el PET clásico en dos direcciones. Así, se consigue una lámina mucho más fina y resistente. Pero no solo es resistente. Si se le añade aluminio, refleja muy bien la radiación infrarroja, por lo que se convierte en un aislante térmico ideal. Esa es justamente la razón por la que esta combinación se usa para fabricar mantas de emergencia, como las que se emplean para tapar a corredores de maratón tras un ejercicio extremo o a las víctimas de un accidente o desastre natural.
Los ingenieros de la Escuela de Ingeniería y Ciencias Aplicadas de la Universidad de Pensilvania quisieron usar esta misma combinación de materiales para ver si sería útil en la Luna. Pero no necesitaban solo que fuera un buen aislante. También requerían un material resistente. Por eso, probaron a apilar capas muy finas de Mylar, una sobre otra, añadiendo óxido de aluminio para no perder su efecto aislante.
Difícil, pero útil. El procedimiento no fue coser y cantar. Las capas eran tan finas que, según explicaron estos científicos, solo con respirar cerca de ellas podían salir volando. Las manipularon con ayuda de unas pinzas y lograron un prototipo de un centímetro cuadrado. De ahí a las construcciones lunares hay un camino larguísimo, pero al menos sirvió para comprobar en el laboratorio si este material, al que han bautizado como HyLIFS, tiene las cualidades esperadas.
Vaya si las tiene. En ese centímetro cuadrado encontraron un material con una conductividad térmica extremadamente baja, de unos 2,2 mW/m·K. Eso significa que aísla muy bien, tanto de altas como de bajas temperaturas. Para hacernos más o menos una idea. Para hacernos una idea, la conductividad térmica de los ladrillos puede ser de más de 1.000 mW/m·K. Por otro lado, la muestra resistió una presión de 20 megapascales, comparable a concentrar unos 200 kilogramos en un área del tamaño de la punta de un dedo. Esta prueba de resistencia se repitió 10 veces seguidas con idénticos resultados, así que la estructura del material sigue resistiendo después de soportar presiones altas muchas veces seguidas.
Partículas microscópicas. Al analizar mediante microscopía este nuevo material, los científicos vieron que gran parte del calor pasa de una lámina a otra por los puntos de contacto de unas partículas microscópicas ‘antiadherentes’ que los fabricantes añaden al Mylar para que las capas no se peguen. Es decir, estas partículas, necesarias para separar las capas, son también el principal camino por el que se cuela el calor, lo que abre la puerta a mejorar el aislamiento optimizándolas.
Un largo viaje y una estancia inhóspita. Los materiales que se usen en las construcciones lunares deben poder doblarse, golpearse y someterse a altas presiones, tanto durante el viaje a la Luna como durante la construcción y una vez en su destino. Por eso es tan importante combinar resistencia y aislamiento. Estos científicos lo han conseguido, pero en un tamaño muy reducido. Ahora habrá que comprobar que, efectivamente, las propiedades se mantienen en fragmentos más grandes de materiales.
Además, es importante encontrar un método de producción más rápido, ya que hacerlo manualmente con unas pinzas no es viable si se van a fabricar grandes rollos. Y, para terminar, será necesario seguir investigando para comprobar que resiste bien a golpes, arañazos y flexiones repetidas. Esto es solo el principio, pero parece que las mantas de emergencia podrían tener una aplicación inesperada en la Luna.

articles.title: Power-efficient inference chips let enterprises own AI hardware - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI inference servers shrink to fit the air-cooled racks enterprises already run
Power-efficient inference chips are becoming the entry price for enterprises that want to run AI on hardware they own.
As AI shifts from building models to running them every day, costly graphics processing unit racks and the liquid cooling they demand keep many companies renting compute instead. That gap is opening room for challengers to the incumbent chipmakers. Axelera AI B.V. built its business at the edge with low-power chips and edge AI development tools, and it is now taking that technology into data center infrastructure, according to Manuel Botija (pictured), vice president and head of product at Axelera.
“Enterprises cannot own their own infrastructure. They’re locked out because of the cost and the power,” Botija said. “We are enabling them now to own it. It’s not that we are helping the world save power or save money — which we are — but it’s that we are unlocking use cases that were simply not possible before.”
Botija spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how power-efficient inference chips are heading for the data center and how enterprises locked out by the cost and power of GPU racks can own their own AI infrastructure instead of renting compute. (* Disclosure below.)
Power-efficient inference chips head for the data center
Axelera’s Europa chip has been shipping since September. Ahead of SC26, the company unveiled Titania, a third-generation architecture that scales the design up to a 400-watt chip. The resulting six-kilowatt server is built to perform like leading data center GPUs while fitting into the existing 20- to 30-kilowatt air-cooled racks of an ordinary enterprise data center, Botija explained.
“Having a six-kilowatt server that can perform like a data centre GPU is a pretty big deal,” he said. “It basically means that they have some storage equipment, some networking equipment, some traditional CPU equipment, and next to all of that, they can also insert some AI inference hardware acceleration without needing to go and rebuild another server room or another data center.”
For enterprises that would rather own their AI hardware than pay a recurring cloud bill, the barriers have been steep. A GPU rack costs at least $1 million, often far more, and usually requires liquid cooling, Botija noted. Axelera’s answer rests on digital in-memory computing, a technique that grew out of its founders’ research and gives the company’s power-efficient inference chips a performance-per-watt advantage.
“Now you can own your own infrastructure,” Botija said. “You can amortize those investments and … reduce your opex, and therefore be more profitable as a company.”
Here’s the complete video interview, part of SiliconANGLE’s and theCUBE’s coverage of SC26:

articles.title: Before you judge Sandpapergate, watch these 3 documentaries
articles.text:
Before you judge Sandpapergate, watch these 3 documentaries
Three documentaries you need to watch before judging sandpapergate
It just won't go away for Cricket Australia.
Eight years after Cameron Bancroft was caught using sandpaper to tamper with the ball during the 2018 Test series in South Africa, fresh allegations have emerged suggesting that more people knew about the plan than just Bancroft, captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner.
Much of the renewed controversy stems from Usman Khawaja's recently released autobiography, Sabr, in which he claims that knowledge of the ball-tampering extended throughout the Australian team, including players and staff. His account has since received support from Warner, Bancroft and former Australia bowler Chadd Sayers, who was part of the 2018 squad.
However, current Australian Test captain Pat Cummins has strongly rejected Khawaja's claims, describing them as "complete and utter nonsense" during an extraordinary 70-minute press conference last week.
Cricket Australia has now announced a voluntary forum, giving former and current players and staff an opportunity to share their recollections of the scandal. But with no new investigation, sanctions or guaranteed public findings, will it really uncover anything new?
Before making up your mind, we recommend watching these three documentaries to gain a deeper perspective on one of cricket's biggest scandals.
Read More: How to watch New Zealand vs India 1st Test
Crossing The Line - 2018
Produced by South Africa's Supersport, Crossing The Line is perhaps the most insightful of all the documentaries exploring Sandpapergate. Featuring perspectives from Shaun Pollock, Graeme Smith, Shane Warne, Allan Border, Michael Holding and Michael Haysman, it offers a fascinating range of viewpoints on the controversy.
Rather than focusing solely on the ball-tampering incident, the documentary examines the Test series as a whole, providing valuable context on the long-standing rivalry and animosity between Australia and South Africa, both before and after the scandal.
At just 56 minutes long, it's an ideal watch if you have an hour to spare.
The Test - 2020
While The Test is by no means a documentary dedicated solely to Sandpapergate, it's arguably the best choice if you want to understand the scandal's impact on Australian cricket culture.
The opening episode explores the background and fallout of the controversy before following Justin Langer and Tim Paine as they attempt to rebuild the team's reputation, restore public trust and steer Australian cricket into a new era.
The Cause, The Crime, The Impacts - 2023
Although an independent three-part series available on SB Media's YouTube channel, this documentary neatly pieces together the Sandpapergate scandal across three carefully structured episodes: The Cause, The Crime and The Impacts.
While it doesn't necessarily uncover anything new, it's an excellent way to get a comprehensive understanding of what happened, why it happened and the lasting impact the scandal has had on Australian cricket culture.

articles.title: Guerre contre l’IPTV : l’un des plus gros sites pirates de Turquie ferme ses portes
articles.text:
Un nouveau géant du piratage vient de tomber. L’Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment (ACE) a annoncé la fermeture définitive de Dizigom, l’un des plus importants sites de streaming illégal de Turquie. La plateforme, qui comptait environ 21 millions de visites par mois, permettait de regarder gratuitement des films et des séries. Pour rappel, l’ACE est une coalition internationale qui réunit plus de 50 grands groupes de l’industrie du divertissement, dont Amazon, Apple TV, Netflix, Paramount, Sony Pictures, Universal, Disney et Warner Bros. Discovery.
À lire aussi : Un géant de l’IPTV pirate indien cesse ses activités
Trois ans d’enquête pour faire tomber Dizigom
La coalition a ouvert une enquête sur Dizigom dès 2023. Avec l’aide de la police et la justice de la Turquie, elle a cherché à identifier tous les responsables du site, à débusquer leurs biens et à cartographier l’infrastructure technique du service. Les investigations ont fini par porter leurs fruits.
Face aux poursuites pénales brandies par l’ACE, les pirates à l’origine de Dizigom ont fini par accepter un accord à l’amiable. Ils se sont engagés à fermer définitivement le service et à céder 16 noms de domaine à l’ACE. Désormais, toutes les adresses du site renvoient vers une page qui présente les dangers du piratage et fait la liste des offres de streaming légales.
« La fermeture de Dizigom est une nouvelle étape importante pour perturber les activités illégales qui profitent de contenus créatifs volés », se félicite Larissa Knapp, vice-présidente exécutive de la Motion Picture Association, chargée de la protection des contenus, ajoutant que « ces opérations ne s’arrêtent pas à un seul site web ».
À lire aussi : Ils revendaient des boîtiers IPTV en France – la justice les condamne à une lourde sanction
Une première en Turquie
Dizigom est la première affaire pénale lancée par l’ACE en Turquie. Elle a ouvert la voie à plus de dix autres enquêtes analogues à l’encontre de géants du streaming illégal. La chute de Dizigom s’inscrit dans le cadre d’une vaste offensive contre l’IPTV pirate. Ces derniers mois, l’ACE a fait tomber AnimePlay, une plateforme d’anime aux plus de 5 millions d’utilisateurs, puis le réseau de streaming sportif PirloTV et ses 44 noms de domaine.
Ces fermetures ne suffisent pas toujours à mettre un terme aux activités des pirates. Cet été, HBO a fait tomber le géant du streaming illégal Streamzy.to, mais le site pirate est revenu presque aussitôt sur Internet. C’est précisément pourquoi l’ACE s’attaque de plus en plus aux personnes derrière les sites pirates, et pas seulement aux adresses. Cette approche permet une perturbation plus durable des géants du streaming illégal.

articles.title: Cinq appareils, un seul abonnement : Norton 360 Deluxe passe à 39,99 €
articles.text:
Norton 360 Deluxe : le bon calcul pour protéger plusieurs appareils à moindre coût
Avec Norton 360 Deluxe, cinq appareils bénéficient d'une protection complète pour 39,99 € la première année. Une formule qui peut réduire la facture lorsqu'elle est partagée entre plusieurs membres du foyer.
Norton 360 Deluxe : une protection complète pour cinq appareils
Norton 360 Deluxe est proposé à 39,99 € la première année pour protéger jusqu'à cinq appareils. Un tarif qui mérite l'attention des familles équipées de plusieurs ordinateurs, smartphones et tablettes. Plutôt que de souscrire plusieurs abonnements de sécurité, cette formule permet de regrouper les protections dans une seule offre.
Le calcul est assez simple : si les cinq appareils sont utilisés, le coût revient à environ 8 € par appareil pour douze mois. Une répartition intéressante pour un foyer dans lequel plusieurs personnes utilisent quotidiennement Internet, que ce soit pour travailler, étudier ou consulter leurs contenus préférés.
L'abonnement comprend notamment :
- Un antivirus contre les virus, logiciels malveillants, ransomwares et tentatives de piratage.
- Un VPN pour renforcer la confidentialité des connexions et protéger les données lors de la navigation.
- Une surveillance du Dark Web qui permet d'être alerté si certaines informations personnelles apparaissent sur des espaces où circulent des données volées.
- Un contrôle parental pour accompagner les enfants dans leur utilisation d'Internet et définir des limites de temps d'écran.
- 50 Go de sauvegarde cloud pour conserver une copie de fichiers importants.
- Un gestionnaire de mots de passe pour faciliter la gestion des identifiants.
- Une protection contre les arnaques, notamment celles diffusées par SMS ou à travers des vidéos truquées (deepfakes).
La formule intègre également un moniteur de confidentialité. L'ensemble fonctionne sur Windows, macOS, Android et iOS. Il est donc possible de répartir les cinq protections entre différents types d'appareils, sans devoir utiliser exclusivement des ordinateurs de la même marque.
Un prix attractif, mais attention au renouvellement
L'intérêt de Norton 360 Deluxe tient aussi aux outils réunis dans l'abonnement. VPN, gestionnaire de mots de passe, contrôle parental et sauvegarde cloud complètent l'antivirus sans multiplier les services.
Pour les familles, le contrôle parental permet notamment d'encadrer la navigation des enfants. Norton ajoute aussi Norton Genie, un assistant qui aide à repérer les arnaques en ligne et à mieux comprendre les menaces.
Il reste toutefois un point à vérifier avant de souscrire : le tarif de renouvellement. L'offre est attractive la première année, mais le renouvellement peut alourdir la facture. Mieux vaut vérifier son montant avant de souscrire.
Au final, Norton 360 Deluxe offre une solution pratique pour protéger les appareils de toute la famille. À 39,99 € la première année, le coût reste limité si les cinq appareils sont utilisés. Reste à vérifier le prix après douze mois.

articles.title: Jensen Huang y su esposa trasladaron USD 10.500 millones en acciones de Nvidia a un fideicomiso antes de los casos de infidelidad
articles.text:
Jensen Huang y su esposa Lori trasladaron más de 10.500 millones de dólares en acciones de Nvidia a un fideicomiso familiar irrevocable en marzo de 2026, ocho meses antes de que una serie de presuntas infidelidades, incluida la de una posible espia china, terminara con la renuncia del empresario a la dirección de la compañía que él mismo cofundó.
La operación, revelada por registros ante la Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) y citada por el medio Barron’s, consistió en el traspaso de 59 millones de acciones al Huang Irrevocable Remainder Trust. Asesores patrimoniales consultados por esa publicación la describieron como “una de las transferencias de riqueza más impactantes” que hayan observado.
Cómo se armó el fideicomiso familiar de Huang
El movimiento no fue una decisión espontánea sino el desenlace de una estrategia diseñada una década antes. El 18 de marzo de 2016, un mes después de una presentación de resultados en la que Jensen Huang había destacado el futuro de la inteligencia artificial para los chips de la compañía (entonces usados sobre todo en videojuegos), el matrimonio constituyó cuatro grantor retained annuity trusts (GRATs).
Dos de esos fideicomisos tenían una duración habitual de cuatro años. Los otros dos, en cambio, se extendieron por una década, un plazo que Barron’s calificó como “mucho menos popular” entre este tipo de instrumentos por el riesgo que implica proyectar su crecimiento a largo plazo.
Un GRAT es un fideicomiso que permite transferir activos a herederos con una carga impositiva reducida: el beneficiario conserva una anualidad durante un plazo fijo y, al vencer, el remanente pasa libre de impuesto federal a la sucesión, generalmente a los hijos. Esa es la figura que usaron los Huang en 2016.
Los dos GRATs a diez años se financiaron con 51 millones de dólares en acciones de Nvidia. El valor de esos títulos escaló un 22.161% en ese lapso, impulsado por el auge del mercado de la inteligencia artificial, hasta transformar aquellos 51 millones en los 10.500 millones que finalmente ingresaron al fideicomiso familiar en marzo pasado.
El abogado especializado en fideicomisos y sucesiones Joshua Caswell lo resumió a Barron’s: “Esto para mí es indicativo de alguien que tenía mucha fe en sí mismo y en la compañía, pero que no sabía cuándo ocurriría el evento de liquidez”.
Según el medio, no trascendió cuál de los dos hijos adultos del matrimonio, Madison y Spencer, ambos empleados de Nvidia, resulta beneficiario del fideicomiso.
El escándalo que llegó meses después
La transferencia quedó formalizada en marzo, mucho antes de que se conociera la crisis que terminaría por sacar a Huang de la conducción de Nvidia. En mayo, el secretario de Estado Marco Rubio advirtió al presidente Donald Trump que la relación sentimental de Huang con una empresaria china representaba un riesgo de contrainteligencia para Estados Unidos, según había informado inicialmente The New York Times.
Esa mujer fue identificada como Alice Huang (sin parentesco con el empresario), señalada como una presunta espía vinculada a China. El Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de ese país calificó las acusaciones de “especulación infundada y un intento de difamar y manchar a China”, de acuerdo con CNN.
A ese episodio se sumaron luego versiones sobre otros dos presuntos vínculos extramatrimoniales, en estos casos con subordinadas dentro de la propia Nvidia.
El cúmulo de denuncias derivó en la renuncia de Jensen Huang como presidente y director ejecutivo el jueves 12 de noviembre, cargo que ocupaba desde que cofundó la empresa en 1993 junto a Chris Malachowsky y Curtis Priem. El directorio designó a la directora financiera Colette Kress como CEO interina.
El impacto llegó también a la cotización bursátil: las acciones de Nvidia cayeron un 3% el lunes 16 de noviembre, lo que borró unos 100.000 millones de dólares de su capitalización de mercado, según The Guardian, y acumulaban una baja superior al 30% en el último mes. De acuerdo con Bloomberg, el valor de mercado de la compañía quedó por debajo de los 4 billones de dólares por primera vez desde julio de 2025.

articles.title: Black Friday Amazon : un grand classique des casques à réduction de bruit passe à -43%
articles.text:
Le casque sans fil Sony WH-1000XM5 bénéficie d’une réduction de 43 % chez Amazon pendant le Black Friday : son prix passe de 419 € à 237,83 €, et sa livraison est offerte à tous les clients du site.
Qu’il s’agisse d’atténuer les bruits dans les transports en commun ou de limiter l’impact des conversations de bureau au travail, l’usage d’un casque doté d’une réduction active du bruit efficace peut tout changer. Si vous ne savez pas vers quel modèle vous tourner, sachez qu’en ce moment, Amazon propose le Sony WH-1000XM5 à 237,83 €. Il s’agit d’un casque Bluetooth qui a déjà largement fait ses preuves, et qui peut convenir pour un usage régulier en déplacement ou en télétravail.
Le casque Sony WH-1000XM5 à réduction de bruit est disponible à 237,83 € chez Amazon durant le Black Friday.
Pourquoi choisir le Sony WH-1000XM5 ?
- Pour sa réduction active du bruit : elle atténue les sons environnants pour mieux profiter de sa musique ou se concentrer.
- Pour sa connexion multipoint : le casque peut rester connecté à un ordinateur et à un smartphone en même temps afin de passer facilement de l’un à l’autre.
- Pour son autonomie : Sony annonce jusqu’à 30 heures d’écoute avec la réduction de bruit activée.
Un casque pratique au bureau comme à l’extérieur
Si vous prenez les transports en commun pour vous rendre au travail, il est possible que vous ayez besoin de passer de votre smartphone à votre ordinateur une fois arrivé au bureau. Le Sony WH-1000XM5 vous évite d’avoir à jongler entre vos appareils grâce à sa connexion multipoint, qui lui permet de rester connecté à deux appareils en même temps. Ses commandes tactiles permettent de gérer la lecture et le volume directement sur l’écouteur, tandis qu’un mode ambiant laisse passer les sons extérieurs si vous avez besoin de garder le contact avec votre entourage.
Notre test du Sony WH-1000XM5 a accordé la note de 9 sur 10 au casque, en saluant notamment ses qualités d’isolation et ses nombreux réglages. Son autonomie peut monter jusqu’à 30 heures, ce qui permet d’espacer les recharges.
Un casque sans fil qui aurait pu être plus compact
Le casque WH-1000XM5 de Sony est confortable à porter, mais il faut tenir compte du fait que ses oreillettes ne se replient pas vers l’intérieur de l’arceau. Il occupe donc davantage de place dans un sac qu’un casque pliable, et sa housse de transport s’avère assez volumineuse.
✅ Les points forts
- Réduction active du bruit et mode ambiant.
- Connexion Bluetooth à deux appareils.
- Jusqu’à 30 heures d’autonomie annoncées avec réduction de bruit.
❌ Les limites
- Arceau non pliable pour le transport.
- Port USB-C qui ne prend pas en charge l’audio USB.
Disponible pour 237,83 € au lieu de 419 €, le casque Sony WH-1000XM5 bénéficie de 43 % de remise chez Amazon.
Le casque sans fil Sony WH-1000XM5 convient aux personnes qui ne peuvent pas se passer de musique au quotidien, ou encore à celles qui ont tendance à travailler dans un environnement bruyant. Sa réduction de bruit très efficace et sa connexion multipoint sont de vrais atouts.
Par contre, si vous cherchez un casque pliable qui prend peu de place quand vous ne le portez pas, ce n’est peut-être pas le modèle auquel vous devez vous intéresser en priorité.

articles.title: Microsoft's official Agent Framework Python package on PyPI hijacked to push login-stealing malware
articles.text:
Microsoft's official Agent Framework Python package on PyPI hijacked to push login-stealing malware
Attackers push two versions in roughly half an hour
- Attackers compromised Microsoft’s Agent Framework package on PyPI and inserted malware designed to steal credentials and cloud tokens
- Malicious versions targeted Azure, AWS, GitHub, OpenAI, Docker, and other developer platforms before being removed
- Developers who installed the affected releases should rotate secrets, investigate environments, and treat systems as compromised
Threat actors broke into Microsoft’s official Agent Framework Python package on PyPI and used it to disseminate infostealing malware to hundreds of thousands of developers that rely on it daily. Fortunately, the attack was spotted and stopped rather quickly - although that doesn’t mean there were no victims.
The Microsoft Agent Framework Python package is an open source toolkit that helps developers build AI agents and applications where multiple AI agents can work together to complete different tasks.
It provides the building blocks for creating AI assistants that can use tools and follow instructions, as well as to interact with other agents and handle more complex tasks.
Gone in 31 minutes
For a relatively new tool, Agent Framework is gaining plenty of traction, with monthly downloads reaching almost 200,000 these days.
On November 17, 2026, someone released version 1.26.1 containing an infostealer that executed automatically when Python boots up, even in environments where the Agent Framework package was not imported. It kept its dependency on the earlier package (1.26.0), meaning the framework would function properly while the malware would do its work in the background.
The tool was designed to steal login credentials and other secrets from environment variables, as well as to nab local configuration files and other running processes. It targeted Azure, AWS, GitHub, Docker, Hugging Face, OpenAI, and numerous other services. What’s more, it tried to steal Azure managed identity access tokens, as well as Azure DevOps OIDC tokens.
PyPI took exactly 31 minutes to spot the intrusion and quarantine the malicious version. However, two minutes later, a second attack took place. Version 1.26.2 added GitHub Actions OIDC token requests, as well as searches of GitHub runner directories. The interesting thing about the second attack is that the threat actors somehow maintained access to Microsoft’s PyPI account even after the first cleansing. PyPI removed the second version approximately eight minutes after upload.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
We don’t know if the attack was successful and if any developers lost their secrets as a result. According to PyPIStats.org, the tool has approximately 6,900 downloads a day, or around 287 an hour. Therefore, the malicious versions were potentially downloaded around 150 times.
If you were among those who downloaded versions 1.26.1 or 1.26.2, remove it immediately and treat the system it was installed on as potentially compromised. It’s also worth mentioning that simply downgrading to a clean version is not enough, since the secrets were probably already exfiltrated. Therefore, make sure to check the environment for suspicious files, particularly the .pth files associated with the attack, and consider rebuilding affected environments from the ground up.
What to do in case of an infection
Also, all passwords should be considered exposed, including API keys, access tokens, and other secrets - make sure to revoke and replace them. Furthermore, make sure to review your Azure, AWS, GitHub, and other service accounts for suspicious activity, including unexpected logins or access requests. Finally, anyone using the package in automated build systems, particularly GitHub Actions, should investigate those environments as well.
The attack was spotted and documented by a number of security researchers, including Wiz, Aikido Security, Socket, and others. According to some researchers, the first malicious release used agent_framework_meta.pth to execute the credential stealer in agent_framework_meta/_telemetry.py during Python startup, while the second restored the original package initializer and moved the malicious code to af_runtime_diag.pth and af_runtime_diag.py.
Both versions were sending harvested information to the same server, located at https://webhook[.]site/d381fd80-ec62-42ad-8f5c-d1b15103c9bb.
No threat actors claimed responsibility for the attack and we don’t know how they gained access to Microsoft’s official PyPI project. The Windows maker has not issued a comment or a statement.

articles.title: Raptor chip stacks 3D DRAM to tackle inference memory limits - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
D-Matrix bets stacked DRAM can solve inference’s memory bandwidth problem
As artificial intelligence workloads shift to inference, memory bandwidth decides whether hardware generates tokens quickly or sits idle. D-Matrix Corp. is answering with Raptor, a second-generation chip stacking 3D DRAM beneath its compute logic.
AI infrastructure has become a systems game, and winners combine memory, interconnect and software into cohesive designs, according to Satyam Srivastava (pictured), fellow at d-Matrix.
“It’s no longer a chip problem. Chip plays a part of it. Memory bandwidth is a fundamental advantage that has to be solved,” Srivastava said. “The next is energy efficiency. The next is interconnect efficiency. The next is software cohesiveness.”
Srivastava spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed d-Matrix’s Raptor chip and its stacked 3D DRAM, inference memory bandwidth and the shift toward heterogeneous computing. (* Disclosure below.)
Raptor brings a stacked-memory tier to inference
D-Matrix proves each risky technology on a test chip first. Jayhawk proved die-to-die connectivity, and Jayhawk II validated digital in-memory computing. The Corsair accelerator combined both and entered full production earlier this year, Srivastava explained.
“Fast forward, we have the Pavehawk chip, test chip, which is proving out 3D DRAM stacked underneath the logic die, which serves as the core technology for Raptor, which is our second-generation chip coming out next year,” Srivastava said.
Stacking keeps the distributed memory architecture intact but moves memory cells onto a separate layer rather than consuming logic die area. Data travels a short distance and never crosses an interposer. That puts 3D DRAM in a new tier between SRAM and high-bandwidth memory, Srivastava said.
“So you’re getting 10 times higher energy efficiency compared to HBM, 10 times higher bandwidth compared to HBM, where it sits in between SRAM and HBM in terms of capacity,” Srivastava said.
Pairing a Corsair-based server with an existing Hopper GPU fleet can raise utilization from about 20% to as much as 80%, meaning more tokens per dollar, Srivastava noted. D-Matrix has also adopted NVLink Fusion rackscale infrastructure from Nvidia Corp. to connect its accelerators to Nvidia’s AI factories.
“For us, it unlocks the opportunity to participate in a very established ecosystem, the world’s most popular AI factory. We get access to a very hardened design of an MGX rack,” Srivastava said.
The partnership points toward heterogeneous computing, where software orchestrates GPUs, CPUs and accelerators such as Raptor as one system, with the cluster as the unit of computing, Srivastava explained.
“So think of a chip, but that chip is an entire cluster and it has many different hardware units,” Srivastava said. “Some are GPUs, some are CPUs, some are ASIC accelerators, and you can use whichever one you like to serve the needs of the workload the best.”

articles.title: Mauvaise nouvelle si vous attendez l'iMac OLED : Apple bloque sur ces deux points
articles.text:
Après l’Apple Watch, l’iPhone et le récent lancement du MacBook Pro avec écran tactile, l’iMac devait logiquement suivre le cours de l’histoire en adoptant un écran OLED d’ici 2029. Mais sous l’impulsion de John Ternus, le nouveau PDG d’Apple en poste depuis septembre, la firme de Cupertino réévalue de fond en comble la viabilité commerciale de certains de ses projets.
Des coûts de production trop lourds face aux ventes de l’iMac
Apple se heurte d’abord à une équation tarifaire particulièrement défavorable pour son ordinateur de bureau. Contrairement aux smartphones ou aux PC portables de la marque qui s’écoulent à des dizaines de millions d’exemplaires, l’iMac représente un volume de ventes moins important, ce qui empêche d’amortir facilement le surcoût de fabrication des panneaux OLED par rapport aux LCD. Ajoutez à cela la hausse récente du prix des puces mémoire et la facture globale des composants pèse de plus en plus lourd, pour Apple comme pour le consommateur final.
Cette prudence de la part d’Apple s’explique également par le ralentissement des ventes des appareils équipés de cette technologie. Les expéditions globales de panneaux OLED pour l’iPad Pro devraient ainsi chuter de 18 % cette année, passant de 6 millions à 4,9 millions d’unités. Dans le détail, Samsung Display verrait ses livraisons s’effondrer de 2,1 à 1,5 million d’unités, tandis que LG Display reculerait de 3,9 à 3,4 millions. Malgré l’utilisation d’une structure « tandem » à deux couches émettrices, le prix de vente élevé de la tablette a freiné les ardeurs des acheteurs, incitant Apple à réfléchir à deux fois avant de changer la technologie d’affichage de son iMac.
Un retour pragmatique à la technologie LCD à l’horizon 2029
Apple avait pourtant initié des démarches auprès des industriels du secteur. Des demandes d’information avaient été envoyées l’an dernier pour concevoir un écran de 24 pouces affichant une luminosité de 600 cd/m2 et une densité de 218 ppi. Samsung Display développait pour l’occasion une dalle QD-OLED à cinq couches afin de garantir une brillance optimale et une excellente durée de vie. De son côté, LG Display étudiait des dalles WOLED et le procédé FLiPP pour 2030. Mais les développements chez LG Display pour ce premier iMac OLED seraient désormais suspendus.
À lire : Test iMac 24 M3 (2023) : un boost de puissance bienvenu, et quelques regrets
Pour éviter de faire grimper en flèche le prix payé par les consommateurs, Apple choisit donc de revoir ses priorités et de prolonger la vie du LCD sur l’iMac. Le constructeur a récemment sollicité BOE et d’autres fournisseurs afin d’étudier la création de nouveaux panneaux LCD prévus pour un lancement autour de 2029. Ce choix pragmatique permettrait ainsi de préserver un prix d’entrée accessible pour les familles et les professionnels, qui sont les deux principales cibles de l’iMac.
