MSI Unveils the EdgeMesa N AI+ Series, Powering the Future of AI Teammates
MSI, a global leader in AI computing and innovative technology solutions, introduces the EdgeMesa N AI+ Series, a compact AI desktop designed to bring powerful local AI computing into everyday workspaces. Powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark, the new series combines advanced AI acceleration with MSI's thoughtful engineering, enabling developers, creators, and AI enthusiasts to build, run, and deploy AI applications locally. With Windows 11 and a space-saving design, it provides a practical platform for turning AI experimentation into real-world workflows while maintaining greater control over data and computing resources.
Designed for continuous AI workloads, the EdgeMesa N AI+ Series features a refined 1.3-liter aluminium chassis with a fingerprint-resistant finish. Its MSI AI Pulse Cooling System integrates Vapor Chamber technology and dual turbo fans to manage heat efficiently, helping sustain 140 W TDP performance and support reliable 24/7 AI agent operation. This combination brings demanding AI computing to desktops without occupying valuable workspace.As AI evolves from a simple tool that responds to commands into a more intelligent teammate capable of reasoning, planning, and taking action, the EdgeMesa N AI+ Series supports a new generation of autonomous AI applications. Developers can create coding assistants, build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) applications using private knowledge bases, and deploy agents to automate repetitive tasks. These practical applications range from document processing and knowledge management to vision AI and voice-based interactions, bringing NVIDIA's vision of moving "From Tool to Teammate" closer to everyday users.
NVIDIA RTX Spark unites NVIDIA AI, RTX graphics, and unified memory in one slim, powerful Windows PC. Designed to run larger AI models locally—without cloud dependency—and move between creative work, development, and immersive gaming without missing a beat. Connect apps, tools, and workflows into one seamless experience. Private by default. RTX Spark brings NVIDIA's full-stack AI platform, ready for the AI workloads of today and whatever comes next. Delivered on the familiar, trusted Windows platform.
At its core, the NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X superchip combines a 6,144-core NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU with a 20-core NVIDIA Grace CPU, delivering up to 1 petaflop of FP4 AI performance. With up to 128 GB of LPDDR5X unified memory and native NVIDIA CUDA acceleration, the system enables developers to run larger AI models, prototype applications, and accelerate inference locally. Creators benefit from NVIDIA Studio acceleration for 3D rendering, video editing, and AI-assisted content generation, while gamers can enjoy NVIDIA RTX technologies, including ray tracing, DLSS, and Reflex.
High-speed connectivity extends these capabilities beyond a single desktop. With 10 Gb LAN and Wi-Fi 7, users can transfer large datasets and support connected AI workflows, while 20 Gbps USB-C and up to four displays enable flexible multitasking. NVIDIA Personal AI Router (PAIR) technology further enables compatible devices to form a personal AI inference cluster, intelligently routing independent inference requests across available local computing nodes to maximize resource utilization.
By combining NVIDIA RTX Spark performance with MSI's compact design, sustained cooling, and practical AI capabilities, the EdgeMesa N AI+ Series provides a versatile foundation for developing, creating, and working alongside intelligent AI agents.

articles.title: Intel continues layoffs with cuts to its IT department, hundreds of employees reportedly affected — company’s workforce reduced by 27,800 under Lip-Bu Tan
articles.text:
Intel continues layoffs with cuts to its IT department, hundreds of employees reportedly affected — company’s workforce reduced by 27,800 under Lip-Bu Tan
Hundreds of people possibly affected.
Intel has reduced its workforce by approximately 27,800 employees under Lip-Bu Tan, based on the company's reported headcount figures, but this does not seem to be enough. The company has reportedly initiated another round of layoffs, this time across its global information technology (IT) organization, as its chief executive continues to reduce expenses and simplify the company's operations, reports Business Insider.
The latest cuts in Intel's IT organization reportedly began on November 16, although Intel has not disclosed how many employees will lose their jobs, notes TrendForce citing CTech. Some employees claim that the reductions could affect a double-digit percentage of the department's workforce of around 2,607 people at 55 sites in 53 countries, so we are talking about at least 260 people if we are talking about a 10% reduction, or as much as 520 if we are talking about a 20% reduction. One has to keep in mind that these estimates have not been independently verified. Intel has neither confirmed the number of affected employees nor identified the specific teams involved. Instead, the company reiterated to Business Insider that it regularly reviews its workforce to ensure that personnel and financial resources correspond to its strategic priorities.
The latest reductions follow several rounds of layoffs throughout 2026. In July, Intel eliminated positions in its Data Center and AI Group. Between July and October, the company submitted nine Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) notices in California, which covered 222 employees, according to Business Insider. The most recent notice, filed on October 22, concerned 67 permanent job cuts at Intel's Folsom campus (which mostly specializes in R&D, hardware validation, and software development), effective October 31. As of November 17, no additional WARN notices had been reported.
Intel employed 81,100 people as of September 27, 2026, including 76,500 employees at Intel itself and another 4,600 at Mobileye and other subsidiaries. This compares with 85,100 employees at the end of 2025 and 108,900 a year earlier, which means that the company's workforce declined by 4,000 since December, 2025, and 27,800 since December, 2024. respectively.
Intel's workforce reductions began well before Lip-Bu Tan became chief executive in 2025. In 2024, his predecessor Pat Gelsinger announced plans to eliminate more than 15,000 positions, or approximately 15% of the company’s workforce. Tan has continued to reduce expenses, eliminate management layers, and discontinue lower-priority projects as Intel attempts to cut costs and reduce losses/improve profitability.

Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Deployment services drive Supermicro's race to time to online - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Today’s data centers weren’t built for AI racks, so liquid-cooling sidecars get bolted on
Deployment services are becoming the real battleground in AI infrastructure as buyers discover that shipping hardware is only half the job. With GPU supply tight and refresh cycles accelerating, neoclouds and enterprises are judging suppliers on how quickly an AI factory actually goes live.
Server makers that once competed on time to market are now measured on time to production. Super Micro Computer Inc., which reported a $60 billion order backlog in July, has stretched its server building-block model to cover entire data centers and is putting speed ahead of GPU count. Neoclouds want factories running fast, while enterprises now see inference and agentic AI as here to stay, according to Matthew Thauberger (pictured), chief revenue officer of Supermicro.
“It’s not just enough to deliver to the customers. They want it online as quickly as possible. Time is money,” Thauberger said.
Thauberger spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how deployment services are driving the race to time to online and how liquid cooling retrofits help older facilities take on modern AI racks. (* Disclosure below.)
Deployment services and the race to time to online
Customers are leaning on suppliers for far more than boxes. Allocation and deployment services are the two biggest requests Supermicro hears, and its service teams bring systems up, run customer workloads and hand off only once everything is running, Thauberger explained.
“We know that we’re in a constrained environment. There’s no secret on that. So customers are basically asking Supermicro how quickly you can get allocation, how quickly you can bring it online, and how quickly you can have people out on site to deploy those,” Thauberger said.
Older facilities pose another hurdle. Many weren’t designed for the liquid cooling and power density of modern AI racks, so Supermicro offers retrofit options such as sidecars and in-row coolant distribution units, according to Thauberger. The company has also added pre-assembled AI racks to its building-block lineup to shorten installs.
“We have the largest liquid cooling capacity based in California. We’re a U.S.-headquartered company, and the ability for us to have as much liquid cooling capacity as we have inside the U.S. allows us to deploy to these AI factories quick inside the United States,” Thauberger said.

articles.title: iPhone 20 Pro : à peine passé à l’aluminium, Apple voudrait déjà revenir au titane
articles.text:
Chez Apple, l’amour d’un matériau dure parfois le temps d’un cycle produit. Après avoir vanté les mérites du titane sur les iPhone 15 Pro et 16 Pro, la firme de Cupertino avait surpris son monde en 2025 en revenant à une coque unibody en aluminium sur l’iPhone 17 Pro et confirmé sur le 18 Pro.
Un choix dicté par la physique : couplé à une nouvelle chambre à vapeur, l’aluminium offrait une bien meilleure conductivité thermique pour maintenir les performances dans la durée. Mais ce pragmatisme a laissé un goût d’inachevé chez certains utilisateurs, nostalgiques du toucher plus noble et de la résistance accrue du titane. Qu’ils se rassurent : à en croire les dernières indiscrétions relayées par MacRumors, la parenthèse aluminium pourrait déjà toucher à sa fin.
Un châssis en titane et des courbes inspirées de l’iPhone Air
L’information émane de Fixed Focus Digital, un leaker actif sur le réseau social chinois Weibo. Selon lui, Apple testerait actuellement des prototypes d’« iPhone 20 Pro » dotés d’un cadre en titane et d’une silhouette nettement plus arrondie. L’informateur compare cette esthétique à celle de l’iPhone Air, mais avec des courbes beaucoup plus prononcées.
Plus tôt dans la semaine, cette même source affirmait déjà que les modèles du 20e anniversaire reprendraient le verre de l’iPhone Air, retravaillé pour s’incurver sur les quatre côtés autour d’une fine bordure métallique polie. Dès le mois d’août, Fixed Focus Digital soutenait d’ailleurs qu’Apple avait adapté les lignes de production de l’iPhone Air pour façonner ces nouvelles pièces en verre.
Ce scénario rejoint très directement les révélations de Mark Gurman. Le journaliste de Bloomberg, lui aussi très bien informé lorsqu’on parle de la firme à la pomme, indiquait récemment que Cupertino préparait des façades avant et arrière en verre s’incurvant sur les tranches autour d’une mince bande métallique. Un compromis retenu après l’abandon en cours de route d’un prototype encore plus radical où le verre remplaçait davantage de métal, avance-t-il.
La plus grosse refonte depuis l’iPhone X, mais deux designs en balance
Aux yeux de Mark Gurman, ce chantier représente tout simplement la plus vaste refonte de la gamme Pro depuis l’iPhone X. Toutefois, l’ampleur exacte de ces nouvelles courbes ferait encore l’objet d’arbitrages en interne.
Le leaker Ice Universe a aussi ajouté son grain de sel. Il assure ainsi qu’Apple planche sur quatre modèles répartis selon deux philosophies : deux appareils équipés d’un verre plat, et deux autres dotés d’un verre incurvé sur les quatre bords.
La firme explorerait cette piste depuis déjà trois ans. Sur les déclinaisons incurvées, les bordures mesureraient environ 1 mm et deviendraient quasi imperceptibles de face grâce à l’effet optique du verre.
Reste à savoir ce qui survivra réellement aux phases de validation industrielle. Les rumeurs portent sur du matériel encore au stade de l’ingénierie préliminaire, laissant la porte ouverte à des ajustements d’ici la commercialisation attendue à l’automne 2027. D’ici là, Apple aura encore tout le temps de trancher sur le matériau final.

articles.title: Meet SE à 59 €, Tiny 3 Lite 4K à 159 € : OBSBOT baisse ses prix
articles.text:
Pour le Black Friday, OBSBOT met plusieurs de ses webcams en promotion. De la petite Meet SE à la Tiny 3 Lite avec suivi intelligent en 4K, voici cinq modèles à considérer, avec des réductions pouvant atteindre 40 %.
Bien que discrète, la webcam tient une place importante dans nos usages. Réunions en visioconférence, cours à distance, streaming, création de contenu… Elle accompagne aussi bien les journées de travail que les loisirs. Et si les modèles intégrés à nos laptops peuvent suffire, ils montrent parfois leurs limites dès que l’on recherche une image plus nette, un cadrage plus soigné ou un son de meilleure qualité.
C’est justement sur ce terrain que la marque OBSBOT entend se démarquer. La marque profite du Black Friday pour réduire le prix de plusieurs webcams de sa gamme, avec des offres annoncées du 19 au 30 novembre.
Quelle webcam choisir pour les visioconférences du quotidien ? La Meet SE tombe à 59 €
Pour s’équiper, sans faire exploser la facture, la OBSBOT Meet SE constitue une porte d’entrée très intéressante dans l’univers de la marque. Cette webcam Full HD s’adresse avant tout à celles et ceux qui multiplient les appels vidéo, suivent des cours à distance ou souhaitent améliorer leur image pendant leurs sessions de streaming occasionnelles.
Son capteur CMOS BSI de 1/2,8” mise notamment sur de bonnes performances en basse lumière, avec une technologie HDR pensée pour mieux gérer les scènes contrastées. La Meet SE peut filmer en 1080p jusqu’à 100 images par seconde, tandis que ses fonctions AI Auto Framing ajustent automatiquement le cadrage pour garder l’utilisateur au centre de l’image. Petit plus toujours pratique, le contrôle par gestes permet également de piloter certaines fonctions, sans jamais avoir à manipuler directement la caméra.
Compacte et légère (33,2 grammes), elle dispose aussi d’un cache de confidentialité magnétique et peut être orientée en mode portrait. En somme, une webcam à la fois simple à installer et à utiliser, qui viendra aisément couvrir l’essentiel pour les appels du quotidien.
Son autre argument pendant le Black Friday reste évidemment son prix, puisque la Meet SE passe de 99 à 59 euros, soit une réduction de plus de 40 %. Une remise particulièrement intéressante pour qui souhaite remplacer la webcam intégrée de son ordinateur, sans investir dans un modèle haut de gamme.
Webcam PTZ 4K : la Tiny 3 Lite profite de 30 % de réduction
Pour des besoins plus avancés, on monte en gamme avec le modèle OBSBOT Tiny 3 Lite. Cette webcam PTZ (pour Pan-Tilt-Zoom) 4K de dernière génération intègre une nacelle motorisée à deux axes, capable de suivre physiquement les mouvements de l’utilisateur. Un atout indéniable pour les présentations, les cours, les démonstrations et autres sessions de streaming, durant lesquelles on ne reste pas forcément assis devant son écran.
Son système AI Tracking 2.0 propose même plusieurs modes de suivi, pour cadrer une personne, un groupe ou encore une zone définie en amont. De son côté, l’Auto Zoom adapte le plan en fonction des déplacements, tandis que les commandes vocales et gestuelles facilitent le pilotage à distance. De quoi conserver un cadrage propre sans jamais avoir à réajuster la caméra à la main.
La Tiny 3 Lite ne mise pas uniquement sur son suivi intelligent. Son capteur CMOS Exmor RS de 1/2” et 48 mégapixels permet de filmer en 4K à 30 images par seconde, mais aussi en 1080p à 120 i/s. Son système audio spatial à trois microphones propose cinq modes, qui permettent d’adapter le rendu à différents contextes, de la mise en avant d’une voix individuelle à un son stéréo immersif. La Tiny 3 Lite intègre également les fonctions Voice Locator et Voice Tracking. Elle peut aussi se connecter directement au microphone sans fil OBSBOT Vox SE.
Dotée d’un boîtier en alliage d'aluminium de seulement 73 grammes, cette webcam combine suivi mécanique, vidéo 4K et fonctionnalités audio avancées dans un format compact. Et vous l’aurez compris, l’autre bonne nouvelle, c’est que pendant le Black Friday, son tarif passe de 229 à 159 euros, soit plus de 30 % de réduction.
Meet Flip : la webcam 4K pliable qui mise sur la mobilité (et la confidentialité)
Tout le monde n’a pas nécessairement besoin d’une nacelle motorisée ou d’un suivi physique. Pour les utilisateurs qui se déplacent régulièrement, travaillent dans différents endroits ou souhaitent simplement avoir l’esprit tranquille grâce à un cache-objectif physique lorsque la webcam n’est pas utilisée, la OBSBOT Meet Flip propose une approche bien différente. Sa conception pliable et son poids de seulement 37,7 grammes en font une webcam particulièrement facile à transporter.
Son support réglable permet de la fixer rapidement (et solidement) sur un ordinateur portable ou un moniteur. Côté confidentialité, une fois repliée, sa structure recouvre physiquement l’objectif et active le mode veille. Un détail appréciable lorsqu’on souhaite être certain que la caméra ne filme pas. Malgré son format compact, elle embarque un capteur Sony Exmor RS de 1/2” capable de filmer en 4K à 30 images par seconde, avec HDR et autofocus PDAF (pour Phase Detection AutoFocus).
La Meet Flip intègre également deux microphones, plusieurs modes audio et une réduction de bruit par IA. Côté vidéo, l’Auto Framing ajuste automatiquement le cadrage pour garder les participants dans le champ, tandis que la fonction Gesture Control permet de piloter certaines fonctions à distance. Elle se distingue aussi avec AI Magic Notes, un outil capable de transformer les échanges en transcriptions, résumés et listes d’actions.
Pendant cette période de promotion, son prix passe de 129 à 103 euros, soit une remise de 20 %. Un tarif très intéressant pour une webcam 4K qui mise autant sur la portabilité que sur les fonctionnalités dédiées aux réunions.
Pour le Black Friday, deux autres modèles sont également concernés par les promotions OBSBOT. La Tiny 2 Lite, alternative PTZ 4K plus abordable à la Tiny 3 Lite, passe de 199 à 144 euros (-27 %). Enfin, la nouvelle Meet SE 2, qui apporte une définition 2K (2K en 30fps et 1080p en 100fps) à la gamme accessible de la marque, est quant à elle proposée à 92 euros au lieu de 109 euros (-15 %).
Les différentes offres Black Friday OBSBOT sont annoncées du 19 au 30 novembre. De quoi trouver une webcam adaptée à ses usages, que l’on cherche simplement à améliorer ses appels vidéo ou à s’équiper d’un modèle plus ambitieux pour créer du contenu.

articles.title: EPFO approves systematic withdrawal plan for retiring members
articles.text:
EPFO approves systematic withdrawal plan for retiring members
Retiring members can now opt for receiving their retirement savings in periodic installments instead of a lump sum amount.
The retirement fund body Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) on Thursday approved a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for its retiring members to receive their accumulated provident fund savings in periodic instalments instead of withdrawing the entire corpus at once.
Under the SWP, retiring members of the EPFO will receive their accumulated provident fund savings in periodic installments instead of withdrawing the entire amount at once, a Labour Ministry release said.
The decision was taken at the 240th meeting of the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) of the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF), chaired by Union Minister for Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports, Mansukh Mandaviya.
The Board approved a proposal to introduce a Systematic Withdrawal Plan, enabling retiring EPF members to receive their accumulated provident fund savings in periodic installments instead of withdrawing the entire amount at once.
This reform will enable retiring members to withdraw their accumulated provident fund savings at regular intervals, such as monthly, quarterly or half-yearly, based on their preference.
This facility would provide members with a structured source of periodic income while allowing the remaining corpus to continue generating returns, thereby helping augment their retirement income and supplement their pension benefits.
The facility would be entirely voluntary, with no compulsion on members to opt for withdrawals.
The option may also be extended to eligible family members/beneficiaries, ensuring greater flexibility and financial security for the family. This aims to ensure stable post-retirement income, reduce reinvestment risks, strengthen fund sustainability, and extend social security coverage to gig and platform workers.
SWP will enable members to convert their retirement savings into a stable and predictable stream of systematic withdrawals post-retirement, while preserving ownership of the underlying corpus.
Approximately 6.32 lakh EPF members aged above 55 years with provident fund accumulations exceeding Rs 5 lakh are expected to be the primary beneficiaries of the proposed SWP framework during the initial phase.

articles.title: Google just gave Gemini the run of your Mac — three days after Apple tightened the rules
articles.text:
Google just gave Gemini the run of your Mac — three days after Apple tightened the rules
Google is adding computer use to its Gemini app for macOS. The assistant can now work across desktop applications, local files and websites in a separate background window. Users can continue working while Gemini navigates menus, fills out forms, and moves between applications without taking control of their screen.
The feature includes a live preview in the chat so users can monitor the agent’s activity, pause execution, and approve actions when necessary.
The company’s announcement Thursday comes just three days after Apple introduced tighter permission controls for macOS automation.
The company’s announcement Thursday comes just three days after Apple introduced tighter permission controls for macOS automation. Google hasn’t explained how Gemini will operate under the new restrictions.
Apple tightens agent permissions
The macOS 27.3 beta 2 changes split Device Control and Data Access permissions into two categories, System & App Protection Override, and Accessibility.
Apps requesting broad system access will face more explicit permission prompts, and users can approve individual requests instead of granting ongoing access.
Developers building desktop agents will also need to account for least-privilege access, since users can restrict or revoke permissions while an agent is running.
Gemini’s new Mac powers
Google says Gemini can pull shipping details from local PDFs, collect dashboard metrics, and screenshots for a Google Slides presentation, edit batches of photos, and work with 3D design software.
Users can decide which applications Gemini can access and stop a session whenever they want. Google hasn’t detailed how the background window is isolated from the rest of macOS, how Gemini tracks work across applications, or which actions need user approval.
Google’s existing computer-use API
Google introduced computer use with Gemini 2.5 in October 2025 and later integrated it directly into Gemini 3.5 Flash.
According to the developer documentation, the model works from screenshots and sends actions back to the client for execution. Developers still manage the execution environment, and the API includes configurable safety policies, and optional screenshot scanning for prompt injection.
The new Mac feature is part of the consumer Gemini app, not a separate developer API.
The new Mac feature is part of the consumer Gemini app, not a separate developer API. It’s unclear whether the app uses the same execution architecture or whether Google plans to open its background environment to third-party developers.
Where Google stays silent
The company has documented prompt-injection safeguards for its developer-facing computer-use tools but hasn’t said which protections are built into the Mac app. Agents with access to local files and privileged applications also risk untrusted input reaching the agent harness, and influencing the actions it executes.
Reliability questions remain unanswered since the company has not shared any performance figures for the Mac app or explained what happens when an action fails, or an application behaves unexpectedly.
Rollout, requirements and tiers
Gemini computer use is rolling out in English in the United States for personal Google accounts belonging to users 18 and older. The feature requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS Sequoia 15.0 or later and a Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscription.

articles.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.
U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)
Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported.
The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.
By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee.
The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.
As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.
November 17, 2026: Nvidia posts strong quarterly earnings, says it does not plan to reinstate Huang
Nvidia reported its quarterly earnings on Tuesday, which beat Wall Street expectations with $115.8 billion in revenue, up 103% year-over-year. Despite the unknowns the company faces without Huang involved, interim CEO Colette Kress said that full-year revenue is also on track to exceed expectations. The company also plans to raise its outlook for the 2028 fiscal year, indicating confidence that this unexpected leadership change won’t get in the way of its trajectory.
“We have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap,” Kress said. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual. We’ve engaged with our customers, we’ve engaged with our suppliers, our partners. They’re all 100% behind us.”
Nvidia chairman Harvey C. Jones affirmed that the company is not considering reinstating Huang. Kress also said that Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, ending the company’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country.
November 17, 2026: Huang says he sees ‘outpouring’ of calls for him to return, says he ‘would be honored’ to return as CEO
Jensen Huang posted his first public statement since he admitted to having an extramarital affair more than a week earlier.
“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he wrote.
Many of Huang’s colleagues in the tech industry, including Elon Musk, Anduril founder Palmer Luckey, and Y Combinator President and CEO Garry Tan, have called for his return.
November 13, 2026: Huang was not confident in his successor, Colette Kress; reports describe Huang as ‘broken’
More reports continue to roll out that illustrate the shock and severity of Huang’s resignation from Nvidia.
Bloomberg reported that Huang looked “broken and shattered, his legendary energy depleted” by the time he surrendered his role on Wednesday night, uttering phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.”
Separately, The Wall Street Journal reported that Huang had been critical of his CFO and current interim CEO, Colette Kress. Huang is said to have described Kress as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation this summer, and he had described Kress as someone who could not help him steer strategy or decision-making.
November 12, 2026: Democrats launch investigation into Nvidia; Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick summoned to testify before Senate Banking Committee
In a scathing letter sent to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Representative Richard Neal (D-MA) and Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) said they will investigate how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China, especially after Trump was briefed about Huang’s relationship with a purported Chinese spy.
“Although [Lutnick] and President Trump were reportedly briefed on this intelligence, the Administration did not appear to acknowledge this evident national security threat. On the contrary: despite reportedly learning of Mr. Huang’s compromising relationship last fall, President Trump granted Nvidia permission to sell its advanced H200 AI chips to China in December 2025 in exchange for a cut of the export sales,” the letter states.
That same evening, Senator Tim Scott (R-SC) requested that Huang and Lutnick both testify before the Senate Banking Committee.
“The American people deserve answers,” Scott wrote on X.
November 12, 2026: Huang was having a third affair with another Nvidia employee, according to Reuters
After Huang was already ousted from Nvidia, we continued to learn more incriminating claims about the former CEO. According to Reuters, Huang had a third affair with an additional, unnamed employee of Nvidia.
November 12, 2026: Jensen Huang resigns, CFO Colette Kress named as interim CEO; Huang agrees to testify before Congress
Nvidia said its board had accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress, will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang.
Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993.
Later in the day, Huang confirmed that he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26.
“Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”
The testimony is expected to take place behind closed doors, but Mast believes the briefing will be recorded and transcribed.
November 11, 2026: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang
After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days.
Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said. The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan.
November 11, 2026: Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, NYT says
The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.
According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.
November 11, 2026: Congress plans to subpoena Huang to answer questions about affair
Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressmen to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China Committee Chairman John Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed.
November 9, 2026: Huang pulls out of various speaking engagements
The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.
November 9-10, 2026: Details emerge about the business relationships between Nvidia and the alleged spy
Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported. The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.
Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported. Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.
In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.
November 8, 2026: Trump shows support for Nvidia CEO, calls him a “fine person”
On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.
“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.
When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia, Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”
November 8, 2026: Huang admits to affair in public message to Nvidia employees; Nvidia board of directors begins investigation
Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”
“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.
Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.
November 5, 2026: Three Republican committee chairmen ask Huang for closed-door briefing
Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.
“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote. “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.”
October 29, 2026: Jensen Huang publicly revealed to have developed ‘close relationship’ with suspected Chinese spy
U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the New York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship.
An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary.
“Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.”
Spring 2026: A secret memo circulates in the Trump administration about Nvidia CEO’s alleged relationship with Chinese spy
U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo.
Late 2025: President Trump briefed on U.S. surveillance of Alice Huang and her relationship to Nvidia CEO but does not take action
Around the same time, per the New York Times’ report, U.S. President Donald Trump was briefed about intelligence findings that possible Chinese spy Alice Huang had formed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. Trump did not act on this information.
The Nvidia CEO, an ally of Trump, has repeatedly advocated for the U.S. government to let Nvidia expand its business in China.
October 2025: U.S. and Singapore each investigate Megaspeed over possible Chinese export violations
Megaspeed was confirmed to be under investigation by both the U.S. and Singaporean governments in October 2025. As a customer of Nvidia, Megaspeed was suspected of helping Chinese companies get around American embargoes on chip exports.
Megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service.
Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born.
These investigations into Megaspeed highlighted concerns about the degree to which Nvidia is able to track its chip exports. At the time, an Nvidia spokesperson told press that the company did not have “any reason to believe products had been diverted.”
“NVIDIA visited multiple Megaspeed sites yet again earlier this week and confirmed what we previously observed — Megaspeed is running a small commercial cloud, like many other companies throughout the world, as allowed by U.S. export control rules,” the Nvidia spokesperson said at the time.

articles.title: NAND Flash Prices Set to Decline in 2027 as Chinese CSP Order Cuts Outweigh North American Demand Growth
articles.text:
Thursday, November 19th 2026
NAND Flash Prices Set to Decline in 2027 as Chinese CSP Order Cuts Outweigh North American Demand Growth
TrendForce's latest memory industry research indicates that the global NAND Flash market is expected to see a reversal in supply-demand dynamics in 2027. With supply set to grow rapidly, substantial cuts to enterprise SSD orders from Chinese CSPs—coupled with a potential further contraction in consumer electronics demand—are expected to exacerbate oversupply. 
TrendForce forecasts that the overall NAND Flash contract prices will begin declining in the first quarter of 2027, with quarterly price drops potentially widening as the year progresses. TrendForce estimates that global NAND Flash industry CapEx will increase 26.7% YoY to US$29.9 billion in 2027.Strong demand for high-performance storage in North America continues to drive manufacturers to expand capacity and upgrade process technology. Meanwhile, rising QLC penetration and the transition to higher-layer-count NAND technologies will further boost bit output. Although some suppliers may slightly slow their expansion plans in response to sluggish consumer demand, global NAND Flash bit supply is still projected to grow by somewhere between 25-30% YoY in 2027.
Enterprise SSDs remain the primary growth driver for the NAND Flash industry, but regional demand trends are increasingly diverging. In North America, U.S.-based CSPs have recently raised their 2027 demand forecasts again, supported by AI agent and general-purpose server projects already under construction. 
Chinese CSPs, however, are facing challenges including GPU shortages, elevated inventory levels, and intensifying competition over token pricing. As a result, they have reduced their total enterprise SSD orders for 2027 by an amount that exceeds the additional demand from U.S.-based CSPs.
In the consumer market, inventories of low-cost memory are expected to be depleted in 2027, putting upward pressure on finished-device prices and further weighing on shipments. Additionally, brands seeking to control bill-of-materials (BOM) costs will need to reduce storage capacity specifications, resulting in a significant decline in average capacity per device and further widening the demand shortfall.
NAND Flash prices forecast to fall 0-5% QoQ in 1Q27, with all product categories entering a downward cycle from 2Q27
TrendForce notes that continued downward revisions to global consumer electronics shipments, along with reduced enterprise SSD orders in China, have already begun to weigh on NAND Flash contract prices in the fourth quarter of 2026. 
In response, TrendForce has lowered its forecast for quarterly contract price increases to 8-13%. Weakening demand has also intensified inventory-clearing pressure in distribution channels, triggering a sharp correction of more than 20% in spot prices recently.
Looking ahead to 2027, cuts to enterprise SSD demand from Chinese CSPs are expected to offset order growth in North America, while supply growth will significantly outpace demand throughout the year. As oversupply intensifies, TrendForce forecasts that overall NAND Flash contract prices will decline by 0-5% QoQ in the first quarter, with all product categories entering a downward price cycle beginning in the second quarter.
TrendForce emphasizes that the market outlook will depend on the pace of inventory reduction among Chinese CSPs, changes to restrictions on overseas GPU procurement, and whether consumer electronics manufacturers continue adopting lower memory specifications in 2028. 
Another key factor will be the direction of US policy following the mid-term election, particularly whether any changes affect major AI data center projects planned for 2028 that are still in the planning and permitting stages. The pace of project approvals and capital expenditure will directly influence advance inventory procurement in the second half of 2027.

articles.title: Google turns to Blue Origin for a rocket, but its long-term problem remains
articles.text:
Blue Origin announced Thursday that its New Glenn rocket will launch data center satellites for Google in 2029 as part of that company’s Project Suncatcher program.
Google disclosed it was working on scalable orbiting data centers about a year ago and characterized the project as one of its research “moonshots.” The mission on New Glenn is designed to deploy satellites, each with computing capacity at roughly the scale of a data center rack, into Sun-synchronous orbit where they can receive nearly continuous solar energy.
“Project Suncatcher is a long-term moonshot to scale AI infrastructure in space by tapping into the abundant solar power in orbit,” said Travis Beals, senior director of Project Suncatcher at Google, in the news release. “This dedicated launch with Blue Origin represents a crucial milestone on our roadmap as we expand the boundaries of what’s possible for the future of compute.”
Catching a ride while they still can
The announcement comes as US commercial heavy lift rockets, including New Glenn, are filling up their capacity through the year 2030. The Google mission will fly on the 7×2 variant of the New Glenn rocket, the smaller version of the vehicle that has launched three times to date.
The purpose of the 2029 launch will likely be to test the ability to network solar-powered satellites equipped with AI chips and demonstrate machine-learning compute in space. In that sense, it will be a technology demonstration. Google did not say who it was contracting with to build the satellites, which may weigh something on the order of several tons.
Perhaps the bigger question for Google is not whether it can make this technology work—but whether it is tenable for a company to have ambitions for a large constellation of orbital data centers in the 2030s without its own launch vehicle.
Need for super cheap launch
There remain a lot of questions about the economic viability of orbital data centers, but almost everyone agrees on one universal truth: Without ultra low-cost, heavy lift capability, there is no way that data centers in space can be economically competitive with terrestrial data centers.

articles.title: Kickstarter-Hit Flipper One: Was du mit diesem kleinen Linux-Computer machen kannst
articles.text:
Flipper One: Dieses Linux-Multitool wird gerade zum Kickstarter-Hit
Es gibt Kickstarter-Kampagnen bei denen sich schnell abzeichnet, dass sie im Sand verlaufen und das jeweilige Produkt niemals wirklich das Licht der Welt erblicken wird – und es gibt das Projekt Flipper One. Nur zwei Tage nach ihrem Startschuss am 17. November hat die Kampagne schon das 46-Fache (Stand 19. November, 18:30 Uhr) ihres Finanzierungsziels erreicht. Mit 27 verbleibenden Tagen wird dieser Wert wohl noch deutlich weiter steigen.
Flipper One ist auf der Crowdfunding-Plattform also ein voller Erfolg. Grund genug, sich das kleine Gadget, um das es geht, einmal genauer anzuschauen.
Flipper One ist kein Nachfolger des Flipper Zero
Flipper One ist ein handlicher Linux-Computer, der als Netzwerk-Multitool genutzt werden kann. Der Hersteller Flipper Devices bezeichnet es als ein offenes Linux-Multitool für High-Performance-Computing und IP-Networking.
Anders als der Name vermuten lässt, handelt es sich nicht um ein Nachfolgemodell des Flipper Zero des Herstellers, den wir euch 2023 als Hacking-Tool vorgestellt haben. Stattdessen ist Flipper One ein eigenständiges Produkt, das allerdings ebenso nicht als Spielzeug konzipiert ist und in einer Vielzahl an Szenarien Anwendung finden kann.
Als Beispiele nennt der Hersteller etwa Netzwerkdiagnose oder auch Mediaplayer. Dazu ist der Flipper One mit allerhand Specs ausgestattet.
Diese Hardware und Anschlüsse bietet das Linux-Multitool
Das handliche Gadget, das 15,5 x 6,7 x 4 Zentimeter misst, wird von einem 8-Kern-ARM-Prozessor (RK3576) mit dedizierter NPU und GPU angetrieben. Als Betriebssystem läuft Flipper OS, das auf Debian Linux basiert, also quelloffen arbeitet. Das bedeutet, dass Nutzer:innen nach Lust, Laune und eigenen Fähigkeiten Apps und Anwendungen für den Flipper One entwickeln können.
Besonders ist die große Bandbreite in Sachen Anschlüsse, die kaum Wünsche für verschiedenste Anwendungsfälle offenlässt: Neben USB-C und HDMI-Ports verfügt der Flipper One auch über Gigabit-Ethernet-, PCIe-, SATA- und USB-3.0-Schnittstellen. Das Tool unterstützt Wi-Fi 6E, außerdem lässt es sich dank M.2-Slot beispielsweise um ein 5G-Modem oder ein LoRa Mesh-Networking-Funkmodul erweitern. Auf der Kickstarter-Seite wird zudem ein SDR-Radio-Modul (Software Defined Radio) als Erweiterung angekündigt.
Wichtig zu beachten ist, dass der Flipper One im Gegensatz zum Zero nicht auf NFC, RFID, Infrarot und Sub-1GHz-Frequenzen setzt.
Wann der Flipper One ausgeliefert werden soll
Laut Hersteller sind etwa 90 Prozent der technischen Spezifikationen final, Änderungen sind aber weiterhin möglich. Eine Auflistung aller Tech Specs findet sich auf der Website des Herstellers.
Auch ein Blick auf die Kampagnen-Seite bei Kickstarter lohnt sich, da Flipper Devices hier Anwendungsszenarien vorschlägt und alle Knöpfe, Anschlüsse und Kontrollleuchten im Detail zeigt und erklärt. Und auch die stetig kletternde Unterstützungssumme im zweistelligen Millionenbereich ist durchaus spannend zu beobachten.
Flipper Devices gibt an, dass die Auslieferung des Flipper One an Unterstützer:innen im Juli 2027 erfolgen soll. Angesichts der längst zigfach übertroffenen Zielsumme stehen die Chancen wohl gut, dass es wirklich zu Produktion und Auslieferung kommen wird. Die Kolleg:innen von Heise erinnern jedoch daran, dass der Flipper Zero trotz ebenfalls sehr guter Finanzierungskampagne erst ein Jahr später als angekündigt ausgeliefert wurde.
Wer selbst noch mit einsteigen möchte, hat noch bis zum 17. Dezember Zeit und kann sich das Multitool für 399 US-Dollar sichern. Bundles mit Erweiterungsmodulen werden ebenfalls angeboten.

articles.title: Proton Lumo AI
articles.text:
Lumo is a privacy-focused AI assistant designed to help users tackle everyday tasks, explore ideas, and boost productivity without compromising their personal information.
Unlike many mainstream AI chatbots, Lumo puts privacy at the forefront. Conversations are protected with zero-access encryption, meaning that even Proton cannot read them. The service is designed to keep user data private rather than using conversations for advertising or AI model training.
Developed by the team behind Proton Mail and Proton VPN, Lumo combines AI-powered assistance with Proton's established approach to privacy and security. The project is backed by the nonprofit Proton Foundation.
Features
Your chats are yours and yours alone
The questions you ask Lumo – about your work, your health, or your ideas – aren't accessible to us. So they can never be used to target ads, shape what you see online, or build a personal profile that third parties could exploit.
Safeguarded by advanced security
Your conversations are saved with zero-access encryption so that you're the only one who can read them. Proton can never see them, and neither can anyone else.
With transparent code you can trust
Unlike with other AI assistants, Lumo's code is fully open source, so anyone can verify that it's private and secure – and that we never use your data to train AI models.
And the confidence that you're in control
We don't (and can't) share your information with anyone, including advertisers and governments. And Lumo is a European service that complies with GDPR, so you can delete your account at any time.
What Lumo can help you do
Create images
Turn descriptions into images in seconds. Refine and iterate until every detail matches your vision. Your ideas will never be reused by Lumo's model to inspire someone else's design.
Dive deeper
Get clear, personalized answers to complex questions in seconds. Gain new insights, explore ideas, and get real-time information with built-in web search knowing your queries are never used for targeted ads.
Stay on schedule
Set up a morning inbox summary, a weekly news recap, or a monthly breakdown of your expenditures. Lumo takes care of it on time, every time. Your data stays protected the whole way with you in control of every action.
Get organized
Turn a chaotic workload into a clear, prioritized plan with one prompt. Get support for visa renewals, tax filing, or school applications without putting sensitive documents and information at risk.
Analyze data
Make sense of confidential reports and research findings in seconds. Extract key insights, uncover trends, and summarize data with the confidence that your information won't appear in future AI outputs.
Work smarter
Review code, manage projects, and explore big ideas with full context. Link files and folders from Proton Drive to work efficiently, securely, and without compromising sensitive data.
Visualize instantly
Transform spreadsheets and reports into presentation-ready visuals with a single prompt. Spot trends and outliers, compare results, and share what matters while keeping your data private.
Is Lumo free to download and use?
Yes, you can download Lumo for desktop or mobile and get started with a free Proton account. Paid plans offer additional features and higher usage limits.
Does Lumo use your conversations to train AI models?
No, Proton states that Lumo does not use conversations or personal information to train AI models. Saved chats are protected with zero-access encryption, and user data is not used for targeted advertising.
What's the difference between Lumo Desktop and the mobile apps?
Lumo Desktop lets you connect your apps and local files, use connected tools, and schedule tasks. The mobile apps are designed for using Lumo on the go, with features such as dictation for asking questions without typing.
Can I use Connectors and Schedules on mobile?
Today, Connectors and Schedules are only available through the Lumo Desktop app. Download the app for Windows, macOS, or Linux to access these capabilities.

articles.title: Inside Amazon Connect Talent: The science of structured AI interviews | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Inside Amazon Connect Talent: The science of structured AI interviews
For organizations hiring hundreds or thousands of people, every interview presents the same challenge: How do you give candidates a consistent opportunity to demonstrate their skills while gathering the evidence needed to make informed hiring decisions?
Structured behavioral interviews offer a research-backed approach to this challenge. They use consistent, job-related questions and clear scoring criteria to give candidates an opportunity to demonstrate their skills. Decades of research in industrial-organizational (I-O) psychology have shown that structured interviews help organizations evaluate candidates and predict job performance (Schmidt & Hunter, 1998; Sackett et al., 2022). Yet delivering structured interviews at scale requires significant time and expertise to develop competencies, create questions, train interviewers, and evaluate responses consistently.
Amazon Connect Talent brings established hiring science to AI-led interviews at scale. Connect Talent uses structured questions, adaptive follow-ups, and evidence-based scoring to help organizations gather consistent, job-related information while giving more candidates the opportunity to demonstrate their strengths.
We built Connect Talent around three core design principles and evaluated how well the service applies them through a combination of internal research and independent expert review. The findings offer a closer look at the science behind Connect Talent’s AI-led, structured interviewing.
Three core design principles
1. Build interviews around job-related evidence
Connect Talent builds each interview around the competencies required for the role. The service uses job requirements and established occupational frameworks to create behaviorally anchored scorecards. Each scorecard defines specific strength and concern signals, and every interview question targets the behaviors it aims to uncover.
The AI interviewer also adapts to each response. After every answer, it checks whether the candidate has provided enough evidence for the competency being assessed. When details are missing, it asks targeted follow-up questions. This approach preserves the structure of the interview while giving candidates more opportunities to explain their experience.
2. Separate interviewing from scoring
Connect Talent separates the interview conversation from the evaluation. The AI interviewer gathers evidence but does not assign scores. Afterward, a separate evaluation process identifies which behaviors the candidate demonstrated and cites the supporting transcript passages.
The service calculates each competency score from 1 to 5 using a fixed formula. When the transcript lacks sufficient evidence, Connect Talent flags the competency instead of producing a score. Hiring teams can review the evidence behind each rating, and missing evidence does not automatically count against the candidate.
3. Build fairness protections into the design
Connect Talent evaluates transcribed candidate responses without using video, voice tone, or physical appearance to calculate competency scores. The service also excludes candidate identity information from scoring and evaluates each competency separately. These safeguards help focus assessments on job-related behaviors and limit the influence of unrelated information.
What the research shows
To understand how well these design principles work in practice, we combined independent I-O psychology evaluations with internal research. We examined whether the service generates job-relevant interview content, identifies behavioral evidence in line with expert assessments, gathers more complete responses through follow-up questions, and distinguishes between levels of demonstrated competency.
Connect Talent keeps interview questions focused on job-relevant skills
The quality of a structured interview starts with the skills it measures. Candidates need questions that reflect the requirements of the role, and hiring teams need confidence that the interview assesses those skills.
Amazon engaged an independent I-O psychology firm to evaluate Connect Talent’s AI-generated interview content. The firm reviewed the service’s baseline output before human editing and examined how well its competencies, questions, and rubrics aligned with job requirements. The evaluation found that Connect Talent retained critical job information in 100% of the job descriptions reviewed. Of the competencies generated, 91% were clearly traceable to the job description. The firm’s psychologists also found that 98% of interview questions targeted the intended competencies, and 94% of rubric signals clearly measured the intended competency.
These findings show that Connect Talent generated job-relevant interview content that met independent expert criteria in a vast majority of cases. Hiring teams can then review, select, and edit the competencies, scorecards, and questions before using them. This human oversight gives organizations control over the interview process while helping them apply structured hiring practices at scale.
Connect Talent’s candidate scoring matched independent expert decisions more than 89% of the time
Relevant questions provide the foundation for a structured interview. The next challenge is evaluating the evidence candidates provide with consistency.
To examine this, an independent I-O psychology firm reviewed 36 interviews assessing whether candidates demonstrated specific strengths and concerns, creating 252 rubric signals.
Connect Talent evaluated the same transcripts, reviewed hundreds of rubric signals, and aligned with expert scoring decisions in 89.3% of cases. Scoring alignment reached 97.6% when candidates provided clear evidence and 92.9% when only considering candidate concern signals, which identify behaviors that may indicate a poor fit for the intended role.
The evaluation also produced a Cohen’s kappa of 0.79, a statistical measure that eliminates random chance coincidence. A Cohen’s kappa of 0.79 is just under the standard of 0.81 for almost perfect agreement. This outcome indicates substantial agreement between Connect Talent and the independent expert candidate scoring.
Follow-up questions give candidates more opportunities to demonstrate their strengths
Candidates may have relevant experience but leave important details out of their first response. In a traditional one-way video interview, a candidate may receive a fixed question and have only one opportunity to answer it. Hiring teams must then evaluate the information available, even when the response leaves many important questions unanswered.
Connect Talent uses adaptive follow-ups to gather more complete evidence. For example, a candidate might describe improving a slow system. The AI interviewer can ask what changed, which actions the candidate took, and how they measured the improvement. These questions help candidates explain their contributions and results in greater detail.
We studied the impact of follow-up questions by comparing assessments based on a candidate’s first response with assessments based on the full interview conversation. In a preliminary evaluation, scores based only on the first response were up to 1.14 points lower on a five-point scale than scores based on the full conversation. Assessments using the full conversation also came closer to expert evaluations.
Without follow-up questions, the scoring process identified fewer strength signals and more concern signals. In some cases, the candidate’s initial response simply lacked the information needed to demonstrate a relevant behavior. The full conversation captured more of what candidates demonstrated and gave hiring teams a more complete record of their experience.
Structured scoring helps hiring teams recognize meaningful differences
Hiring teams need scores that reflect meaningful differences in demonstrated skills. Yet research has found that some AI scoring approaches concentrate ratings within a narrow range, making those differences harder to recognize (Zhu et al., 2026).
Connect Talent uses behaviorally anchored scorecards to evaluate specific strength and concern signals. Rather than asking an AI model to assign an overall rating, the service identifies evidence for each behavior and calculates the competency score using a predefined formula.
Consider the competency “collaboration”. A general AI scoring approach might evaluate a candidate’s overall collaboration skills based on the interview transcript. Connect Talent examines specific behaviors, such as whether the candidate sought input from colleagues before making a decision. Each finding contributes to the final score.
We evaluated this approach across hundreds of expert-rated interview assessments. Connect Talent’s structured scoring used all five points of the rating scale, while holistic LLM-as-judge scoring concentrated its ratings within the middle three points.
This wider distribution allows the scoring system to represent more levels of demonstrated competency. The behaviorally anchored scorecards also help hiring teams understand the evidence behind each rating.
Bringing hiring science to AI-led interviews
Connect Talent brings the rigor of structured interviewing to more people while giving each candidate a meaningful chance to demonstrate their skills. The result is a new opportunity for organizations hiring at scale: more candidates can show what they can do, and more hiring teams can make decisions grounded in the evidence that matters.
Learn More at AWS re:Invent 2026
Join us at AWS re:Invent 2026 for BIZ332: Every Candidate, Every Time: AI-Led Structured Interviews with Amazon Connect Talent, an interactive Chalk Talk led by Sunitha Srivatsa and Gerald Friedland.
The session will explore the science behind Connect Talent, including structured interviewing, adaptive follow-up questions, and evidence-based scoring.
Session 1: Monday, November 30, 2026, 10:00–11:00 AM, Caesars Forum – Level 1, Academy 409.
Repeat session: Thursday, December 3, 2026, 3:00–4:00 PM, MGM Grand, Premier 309.

Proceedings of the 2021 International Conference on Multimodal Interaction, 268–277. https://doi.org/10.1145/3462244.3479897

articles.title: PHP anuncia parches de seguridad críticos: qué deben revisar quienes administran sitios web
articles.text:
PHP, el lenguaje que funciona detrás de muchos sitios web y plataformas como WordPress, anunció una nueva ronda de actualizaciones de seguridad. Los parches están programados para el jueves 19 de noviembre. El equipo de PHP indicó que corregirían fallos en todas las versiones con soporte y que algunos alcanzarían el nivel de gravedad más alto, llamado “crítico”. El aviso oficial precisó que esos casos requerirían configuraciones especiales o poco comunes.
La advertencia está dirigida sobre todo a quienes administran sitios, servidores o aplicaciones hechas con PHP. Para el visitante de una página, no significa que deba instalar algo en su teléfono o computadora. La tarea corresponde a las personas o empresas responsables de mantener el sistema que hace funcionar el sitio.
Los nombres de las vulnerabilidades y las versiones exactas que las corregirán se publicarán junto con los parches. Hasta entonces, no se podrá confirmar qué instalaciones estarán expuestas ni si el aviso estará relacionado con fallos anteriores. El equipo recomienda que los usuarios se preparen para actualizar cuanto antes cuando estén disponibles las correcciones.
Qué deben revisar quienes administran sitios
El primer paso es averiguar qué versión de PHP utiliza cada sitio y quién la actualiza. A veces el servicio de alojamiento web —la empresa que mantiene el sitio disponible en internet— instala los parches. En otros casos, la actualización depende del equipo técnico, del proveedor de Linux o de la imagen utilizada para ejecutar el programa.
También conviene comprobar que se está revisando la versión que usa el sitio público. Una computadora puede tener una versión de PHP para ejecutar tareas propias y otra distinta para atender la página. Si el responsable no gestiona directamente el servidor, puede consultar al proveedor de alojamiento si aplicará las correcciones y cuándo estarán disponibles.
El anuncio abarcaba las ramas PHP 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 y 8.5, que eran las versiones con soporte de seguridad. La rama 8.2 se acercaba al fin de ese soporte, previsto para el 31 de diciembre de 2026. Esto significa que, después de esa fecha, el proyecto ya no garantizaría nuevas correcciones de seguridad para esa versión.
PHP también tenía previsto publicar la versión 8.6.0 ese mismo día. Sin embargo, el aviso no aclaraba si incluiría las mismas correcciones. La nota consultada recomienda no cambiar un sitio en producción a una versión recién estrenada solo para intentar resolver el problema: lo indicado es instalar el parche correspondiente a la rama que ya se utiliza, una vez confirmados los detalles oficiales.
Una medida preventiva y una advertencia anterior
Mientras esperan la actualización, los administradores podrán mantener desactivada una función de PHP relacionada con el seguimiento de la carga de archivos. El equipo ya habrá recomendado esa medida para reducir el riesgo de un fallo poco probable, identificado como CVE-2026-115560. La vulnerabilidad requerirá una combinación inusual de ajustes y código, por lo que la recomendación no significará que todos los sitios estarán expuestos.
La nueva alerta tampoco confirma que se trate de otro ataque como PHP2Shell, un conjunto de fallos críticos que se corrigió en octubre. El anuncio de noviembre no incluye identificadores ni puntuaciones técnicas para comparar ambos casos. Cualquier relación con la vulnerabilidad anterior seguirá siendo una posibilidad, no una confirmación.
Cuando los parches estén disponibles, los responsables deberán leer el aviso técnico y comprobar si la configuración de sus sitios coincide con las condiciones descritas. Después tendrán que actualizar PHP mediante el canal que gestione el servidor, reiniciar los servicios afectados y verificar que el sitio funcione con la versión corregida.

articles.title: Groundcover launches Agent Investigations, a shared workspace for AI agents and engineers - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Groundcover launches Agent Investigations, a shared workspace for AI agents and engineers
Observability company groundcover Inc. today announced the launch of Agent Investigations, a shared workspace designed to allow groundcover’s artificial intelligence agents, a team’s own coding agents and on-call engineers to work production incidents together.
Agent Investigations is aimed at the problem of scattered findings as AI agents take on a bigger role in incident response. When production goes down, several engineers often point their own agents at the same issue, with each agent working in isolation, according to the company. What those agents conclude, it says, is end up in private chats, tickets or Slack messages out of view of the rest of the team.
Investigations in the new workspace are started automatically by groundcover once a monitor issue opens. Engineers also have the option to launch one manually from the groundcover interface or from a button in Slack.
On groundcover’s side, the work is split between two agents. The first, known as the Investigator agent, is said to build a graph of questions and hypotheses before testing each one against groundcover’s logs, metrics, traces and Kubernetes data. Supporting graphs are attached to each of its findings.
Reviewing every proposed conclusion is the job of the second, a Moderator agent. The Moderator, which is the only agent allowed to close a hypothesis, sends back any claim that lacks supporting findings. Doing so is said to separate generating a possible explanation from validating whether the evidence actually supports it.
Ending each hypothesis is a structured assessment that either supports or refutes it. The company claims teams get a set of tested answers to read through instead of pages of generated text.
Agent Investigations also offers access for outside agents, including Anthropic PBC’s Claude Code and OpenAI Group PBC’s Codex, through groundcover’s Model Context Protocol server. Connected agents can read from and contribute to the same investigation, with agents used for business intelligence and product roadmapping also able to take part. In October, groundcover launched agent-to-agent observability tools that let outside coding agents hand production investigations to its own agent.
Hypothesis status and assessments post to the Slack thread tied to the original alert. With replies posted in that thread also fed back into the investigation, engineers are able to steer the work from inside the incident conversation.
“Every engineer now has an agent, but each of those agents investigates on its own and findings end up in a chat window,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Shahar Azulay, who started groundcover in 2021 with Yechezkel Rabinovich. “Agent Investigations gives humans and agents one place to work an incident, where every hypothesis is tested against production data and every conclusion has to be backed by evidence.”
Omer Mayer, senior product manager at groundcover, said the wait while agents are working and the on-call engineer has nothing to look at is often “the hardest stretch of an incident.” Engineers using Agent Investigations instead get to watch, he said, as each hypothesis is supported or ruled out in real time.
The graph the Investigator builds also serves as the record, said to show how a team reached the root cause, including the hypotheses that were ruled out along the way. According to the company, keeping the monitor, Slack thread, investigation and conclusion linked means nobody has to piece the history back together from separate tools after an incident closes.
Powering the investigations is the full-fidelity telemetry collected by groundcover’s sensor. Because groundcover uses a bring-your-own-cloud architecture, the data remains in the customer’s own cloud account even while agents are querying it.
Agent Investigations is available to groundcover customers whose backends have AI enabled. The company will demonstrate it at Amazon Web Services Inc.’s re:Invent conference in Las Vegas Nov. 30-Dec. 4.
Groundcover has raised $160 million to date, including a $100 million Series C round led by One Peak in July.

articles.title: Supermicro sued by shareholders over claims Nvidia executive’s wife knew about illicit China sales — former Chief Growth Officer Cenly Chen is married to outgoing Nvidia VP Jay Puri
articles.text:
Supermicro sued by shareholders over claims Nvidia executive’s wife knew about illicit China sales — former Chief Growth Officer Cenly Chen is married to outgoing Nvidia VP Jay Puri
Shareholders are implying that she turned a blind eye to the alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips.
More information about the alleged knowledge of chip diversion by a Supermicro executive is being revealed as shareholders’ civil lawsuit against the company progresses. According to The Telegraph, the investors alleged that there was “no way Cenly Chen lacked knowledge about the company’s illicit sales.” Chen, the former Chief Growth Officer at Supermicro and described by a colleague as the company’s sales leader, resigned from her position in April of this year — about a month after the three Supermicro employees, including its co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, were arrested for a $2.5-billion AI GPU smuggling scheme.
Cenly Chen is married to former Nvidia Executive Vice President of Worldwide Field Operations Jay Puri, who is also described as the company’s sales chief. The Information also called him Jensen Huang’s right-hand man and said he was the person that Nvidia’s customers turned to if they wanted to buy chips or had other pressing concerns. The shareholders’ accusations and her relationship with Puri have put the former Supermicro executive in the spotlight, especially after Huang’s sudden departure from the AI chipmaker amid a flurry of affairs and smuggling accusations.
Sources say that Puri controlled the AI chip allocations to server manufacturers, including Supermicro, while the lawsuit claims that Chen decided how many Nvidia racks each Supermicro customer could get. A former Supermicro employee was also quoted in the complaint saying that it was “widely known within the Company that Chen had to leave because she had sent emails requesting that Nvidia release chips with serial numbers associated with the GPUs illegally diverted to customers in China.” This apparently refers to the serial numbers that were moved from real to dummy servers using a hairdryer.
Supermicro has said multiple times that it has cooperated with the U.S. government regarding the smuggling investigation and that it has not been included in the lawsuit against the three defendants. Furthermore, the company has denied her involvement regarding Nvidia GPU allocations. “Chen did not manage Supermicro’s relationship with Nvidia and did not decide how Nvidia GPUs were distributed to customers,” a Supermicro spokesperson told The Information. They also said that she left voluntarily and that her LinkedIn profile now reads her current position as CEO of ChronoScale, an Nvidia cloud partner based in Silicon Valley. As for Puri, he stepped away from his position at Nvidia in late August, about two months before the Jensen Huang scandal blew up, although he remains as an advisor to the AI chipmaker.

Geekom A9 Max mini PC deal: Black Friday sale drops our favorite Mac mini alternative to $1269
One of our favorite Windows mini PCs gets a major discount for office and creative professionals
We're big fans of Geekom's A9 Max mini PC, which scored 4.5 stars in our review, earning a Highly Recommended award. The combination of AMD’s latest Ryzen AI processor, expandable memory, and extensive connectivity makes ideal for users who need workstation-level power in a compact chassis.
Now, as part of its big Black Friday sale, the Geekom A9 Max is down to $1269 (was $2079) when you use code BFA9M230. That model comes equipped with the AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 chip, 32GB DDR5 RAM, and 2TB SSD. However, you can bump that up to a HX 470 processor $1369.
For my money, this is a clear Mac mini alternative for Windows - it comes with Windows 11 Pro installed, but Geekom notes it's compatible with Linux, too. Not everyone will need a mini PC that delivers this level of performance, but it will easily handle office tasks and content creation without breaking a sweat.
Today's best Geekom A9 Max mini PC deal
We found the A9 Max 2026 Edition a "high-performance mini PC" during our tests. With a focus on AI, it's capable of hitting up to 86 TOPS. Internally, you can expand up to 256GB of DDR5 memory and 8TB storage. Connectivity is excellent, too, equipped with dual 40Gbps USB4 ports, dual HDMI 2.1, dual 2.5GbE, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4, and an SD Card reader. For the full discount, use code BFA9M230.
Why we recommend the GEEKOM A9 Max
In our review, we awarded the A9 Max a lofty 4.5 stars, and we loved its capability in demanding productivity and creative applications. It zoomed through Photoshop, Lightroom, and video editing, and its NPU means it can run local AI models without relying entirely on cloud services.
There are compromises. The integrated graphics aren’t a substitute for a dedicated GPU, so you won’t have as much capability in gaming or creative applications that use a proper GPU - although you can connect an external graphics card via the USB4 port. The standard 32GB of RAM can also feel restrictive for more demanding video production, so we'd recommend upgrading that if you need extra headroom.
Price context and historical value
This is firmly premium mini PC territory, but it's also one of the cheapest prices we've seen on this 2026 Edition of the Geekom A9 Max. That promo code is doing a lot of heavy lifting to make this deal more attractive.
The compact metal chassis, powerful processor, and extensive connectivity make it appealing if desk space or portability matters more than getting maximum value from your next purchase.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Geekom A9 Max if… you need powerful processing in a compact package for creative applications, productivity, and local AI workloads.
❌ Skip the Geekom A9 Max if… You just want a mini PC for general day-to-day tasks like running Microsoft Office and streaming.
