articles.title: Open-Source-KI verliert ihren mächtigsten Fürsprecher – und das hat Gründe
articles.text:
Nvidia: Warum gerade die Open-Source-Szene Jensen Huangs Rücktritt bedauert
Inzwischen scheint klar, dass der Verwaltungsrat von Nvidia eine Rückkehr von Jensen Huang an die Konzernspitze ausschließt. Dies bestätigte die Interimschefin Colette Kress dem Sender CNBC. Die Petition, die in den vergangenen Tagen in den sozialen Medien die Runde machte, und mehr als 115.000 Unterzeichner:innen einsammeln konnte, konnte an diesem Schritt somit nicht rütteln.
Dennoch lohnt ein genauerer Blick auf diese Liste, denn ein bedeutender Teil von Huangs Unterstützer:innen stammt aus einem bestimmten Bereich der Tech-Welt. Die Personen, darunter Führungskräfte von Hugging Face, einer Plattform zum Austausch von Sprachmodellen, die mittlerweile Nvidia gehört, sowie der Risikokapitalfirmen Andreessen Horowitz und Sequoia Capital sind Verfechter einer bestimmten Art von KI.
Jensen Huang galt als eine Art Anführer der Open-Source-Bewegung
Der Personenkreis interessiert sich für die Weiterentwicklung quelloffener Modelle, also solcher, die im Gegensatz zu ChatGPT oder Claude von Nutzer:innen heruntergeladen und unabhängig von großen Tech-Unternehmen ausgeführt werden können. Befürworter:innen solcher KI-Systeme argumentieren, dass eine Konzentration von KI in den Händen einiger weniger mächtiger Unternehmen für alle anderen Nachteile mit sich bringt. Das klingt erst einmal nach grundsätzlicher KI‑Kritik. Doch viele Open-Source-Befürworter:innen sind gleichzeitig Risikokapitalgeber, die davon profitieren, wenn Startups auf kostengünstigere KI zurückgreifen können, ohne „Big Tech“ bezahlen zu müssen, also etwa OpenAI oder Anthropic.
Huang war zuletzt zu einer Art Anführer derjenigen geworden, die gegenüber politischen Entscheidungsträger:innen in den USA Open Source verteidigten. Dabei sollte Bedenken entgegengewirkt werden, dass solche Modelle keine Sicherheitsvorkehrungen bieten und sie dazu führen könnten, die Führungsposition im KI-Bereich an China abzutreten, wo die leistungsstärksten und beliebtesten Open-Source-Modelle entwickelt werden. Diese Gruppe will nun, dass Huang mit seiner einflussreichen Stimme wieder Gehör findet.
Doch es sind nicht nur Huangs außereheliche Affären, die seine (und Nvidias) Glaubwürdigkeit als Verfechter von Open-Source-KI gefährden. Neue Untersuchungen zu chinesischen Startups, die Nvidias Chips nutzen, sowie eine am 16.11.26 angekündigte neue Regelung des US-Handelsministeriums könnten sowohl dem Ruf der Bewegung als auch ihrem weiteren Voranschreiten einen Schlag versetzen.
Mehr fortschrittliche Chips in China
Als Huang in der vergangenen Woche zurücktrat, veröffentlichte der ehemalige OpenAI-Forscher Will DePue online Erkenntnisse, die darauf hindeuten, dass Chinas KI-Unternehmen weitaus mehr Zugang zu Nvidias fortschrittlichen Blackwell-Chips hatten als bisher angenommen. China ist der Zugang zu Nvidias modernsten Chips eigentlich untersagt, um Amerikas Vorsprung im Bereich der KI zu sichern.
Es ist unklar, wie die chinesischen Firmen Zugang zu den Chips erlangt haben könnten. DePue behauptet, die Ergebnisse seien von leitenden Forschern bei OpenAI und Anthropic verifiziert worden, doch eine unabhängige Analyse hat die Ergebnisse bislang nicht bestätigt. (DePue reagierte nicht auf eine Anfrage für ein Interview der US-Ausgabe von MIT Technology Review. Nvidia meldete sich ebenfalls nicht mit einer Stellungnahme zurück.) Die neuen Erkenntnisse belegen zwar nicht, dass Nvidia chinesischen Unternehmen dabei half, an die Chips zu gelangen. Allerdings zeigen sie, wie umfassend der Chipschmuggel war – und Nvidia offenbar zu wenig dagegen tat.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (November 19, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (November 19, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, November 19, 2026.
YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured stories
Meet the women breaking barriers in deeptech, building technologies for tomorrow
On Women’s Entrepreneurship Day, we look at women founders pushing the boundaries of Indian deeptech, building frontier technologies, and opening new possibilities for innovation and entrepreneurship.
Anthropic raises $81.3B in IPO, surpasses SpaceX's record offering
Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic has raised $81.3 billion through its initial public offering (IPO), making it the largest stock market offering on record and surpassing Elon Musk-led space company SpaceX's $75 billion IPO. Anthropic priced its shares at $83 apiece, above the previously indicated range of $70-78 per share. The company is set to make its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, November 19, at a valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion.
Six Indian startups selected for Hub71's Immersion Programme in Abu Dhabi
Six Indian startups have been selected for Hub71's Immersion Programme in Abu Dhabi, following the UAE-India Start-Up Series 2.0 finale in Bengaluru. Hub71, Abu Dhabi's global tech ecosystem, is the cross-border partner which will connect the startups with investors, corporate and government partners, regulators, and prospective customers.
Funding news
Style Union raises Rs 485 Cr to expand beyond southern India
Nexon Omniverse Limited, the parent company of value-fashion retailer Style Union, has raised Rs 485 crore in a Series E round led by Venturi Partners, a consumer-focused investment firm, and co-led by Elev8 Venture Partners, a growth-stage investor.
Quick service restaurant chain Boba Bhai raises $18M in Series B round
Boba Bhai, an Indian bubble tea and Korean street food brand, has raised $18 million in a Series B funding round with participation from Left Lane Capital and BIG Capital, alongside existing investors including Titan Capital.
InPrime Finserv raises Rs 101 Cr in Series B round led by FMO
InPrime Finserv, a tech-led NBFC, has raised Rs 101 crore in a Series B funding round led by FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank. This round also saw participation from existing investors Z47 and Pravega Ventures.
Disseqt AI raises $8M to build enterprise AI safeguards
Disseqt AI, a Dublin-headquartered AI assurance company with a significant presence in India, has raised $8 million in a round led by Gresham House Ventures, the growth equity arm of investment manager Gresham House.
VitusCare raises $3 million in Series B funding
VitusCare, a dialysis care provider, has raised $3 million in a Series B funding round led by Singapore-based healthcare growth equity firm Liberty Ridge Capital, with participation from HDFC Bank, Equentis, NAFA Capital Advisors, existing investors 1Crowd and 3i Partners, and angel investors. The company said its revenue has nearly tripled since its previous funding round in late 2024. Its network has expanded from 22 to over 60 dialysis centres across nine states and more than 50 cities.
VitusCare has treated over 35,000 patients and delivered 8 lakh dialysis sessions. It reported positive corporate EBITDA in FY26. It plans to expand to over 100 centres by FY27, besides investing in technology, AI-powered solutions and workforce training.
Other news
Intuit inaugurates new technology campus in Bengaluru
Global financial technology company Intuit has inaugurated its new Bengaluru office at Embassy Tech Village, strengthening its investment in India as a strategic hub for technology and AI innovation. The two-tower campus houses the company's second-largest engineering centre and nearly a quarter of its global technology talent is based in Bengaluru. Intuit has maintained a presence in the city since 2005. The new facility features collaborative workspaces, focus zones and locally inspired artwork and design.
The company said the campus would support the development of AI-powered products and financial technology solutions for customers worldwide. Alex Balazs, Chief Technology Officer, Intuit, said Bengaluru teams were central to building AI-driven experiences that help customers prosper.
CoinDCX-backed Digital Suraksha Network partners Karnataka government
Digital Suraksha Network (DSN), a non-profit platform focused on combating digital financial fraud, has signed an MoU with the Centre of Excellence for Cybersecurity (CySecK), an initiative of the Karnataka government. The partnership will strengthen cybersecurity awareness, skills development and industry collaboration across the state. The organisations plan to conduct Kannada-language cyber safety campaigns targeting one crore citizens by 2027. They will also provide training resources and mentorship to students, government officials and cybersecurity startups.
DSN was launched by CoinDCX's co-founders in March 2026. According to the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, over 65.89 lakh financial fraud complaints were registered between 2021 and 2025, involving reported losses exceeding Rs 55,050 crore.
Zurich Insurance Group to expand Hyderabad GCC to 1,000 employees by 2028
Zurich Insurance Group plans to expand its India Capability Centre in Hyderabad to approximately 1,000 employees by mid-2028, strengthening its global technology, engineering, data and AI operations. The centre forms part of the insurer's global operating model, with teams in India working alongside colleagues across international markets.
Zurich plans to recruit specialists in cloud and platform engineering, data and AI, application development, cybersecurity and quality engineering. The company also intends to increase the centre's responsibility for end-to-end ownership of projects, from defining business requirements to developing and implementing solutions. Amit Kalra, Global Head of Zurich Capability Centres, will lead the development of additional leadership and decision-making capabilities in India.
Cognizant launches immersive learning centre in Chennai
Cognizant has unveiled the first phase of its Cognizant Immersive Learning Center at its Siruseri campus in Chennai, reinforcing its focus on developing technology and AI capabilities among employees. The facility is designed to provide associates with opportunities to explore emerging technologies, acquire new skills and prepare for changing business requirements.
The initiative forms part of the company's broader workforce transformation strategy as AI adoption reshapes technology services and enterprise operations. Rajesh Varrier, President – Global Operations and Chairman and Managing Director, Cognizant India, said the company's focus was on harnessing AI to transform businesses while developing the skills employees need to lead that transformation. The centre is expected to support continuous learning and innovation.
InMobi launches agentic AI advertising platform for businesses
InMobi has launched InMobi Accelerate, a self-service agentic AI advertising platform designed to plan, build, launch and measure campaigns across multiple advertising channels through a single dashboard.
Targeted at small and medium-sized businesses and advertising agencies, the platform uses seven specialised AI agents covering business analysis, audience strategy, media planning, copywriting, creative design, campaign launch and optimisation. It supports Google Ads, Meta Ads, Microsoft Advertising, TikTok Ads and ChatGPT Ads, among other platforms. Advertisers can approve campaign plans, budgets and creatives before launch and subsequently manage campaigns through plain-English instructions.
InMobi said the platform also provides a consolidated cross-channel view of advertising performance, helping businesses measure returns and optimise spending.
Pine Labs launches stablecoin-linked payment infrastructure platform
Pine Labs has launched Staq Web3 Orchestrator, a technology platform designed to connect stablecoin balances with conventional card payment infrastructure. The platform aims to simplify the development and operation of stablecoin-linked card programmes by bringing together regulated card issuance, payment processing and programme management. It is being deployed in a stablecoin-linked card programme, with Reap serving as the issuer and BIN sponsorship partner.
Pine Labs will manage the customer proposition, programme operations, technology stack and ecosystem integration, while Reap provides card-issuing infrastructure. The platform supports virtual and physical prepaid cards and online and offline payment experiences. The launch marks Pine Labs' expansion beyond traditional merchant payments into digital assets and mainstream payment infrastructure.
Cashify reports Rs 6.49 Cr net profit in FY26
Cashify has reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 6.49 crore for FY26, compared with a net loss of Rs 10.56 crore in the previous financial year. Revenue from operations increased 50% to Rs 1,641.19 crore, while consolidated EBITDA rose to Rs 22.7 crore from Rs 1.98 crore in FY25.
The recommerce platform attributed its performance to growth in smartphone buybacks, refurbishment and sales, alongside improved operating efficiencies. Employee costs declined to 9% of revenue from 10.5%, even as total expenses increased 45.7%. Cashify now plans to expand beyond smartphones into laptops, tablets, smartwatches, gaming consoles and audio devices, extending its buyback and refurbishment model across consumer electronics.
IBM partners Axis Max Life to strengthen database security
IBM has partnered with Axis Max Life Insurance to strengthen database security across the insurer's hybrid technology infrastructure. The collaboration aims to improve oversight of sensitive customer and financial information distributed across on-premises and cloud environments.
IBM Professional Services delivered the implementation, which is designed to enhance data protection and security controls while supporting the insurer's digital transformation initiatives. The project is expected to help Axis Max Life strengthen its ability to monitor and protect critical databases as it modernises its technology environment. Mukul Jain, Chief Technology Officer at Axis Max Life Insurance, said building a robust data security foundation was important as the company continued to strengthen its technology and digital capabilities.
Siemens launches AI engineering agent in India
Siemens has launched its Eigen Engineering Agent in India, an AI-powered solution designed to automate industrial engineering tasks. Unlike generic AI tools, the platform operates within engineering systems and understands project-specific context and constraints. It can support tasks such as programmable logic controller (PLC) coding, human-machine interface development and engineering documentation.
Siemens said the solution completes AI-powered workflows two to five times faster than manual alternatives, with up to 80% higher solution quality. Sixteen Indian customers are already using the platform, including Pelican Rotoflex and Z System Intelligent Controls. The technology was among more than 20 industrial AI innovations showcased at Siemens India's seventh Transform Innovation Day, attended by around 500 industry leaders.
BharatPe launches digital ledger to help merchants manage festive business
BharatPe has introduced Udhaar Khata, a digital ledger designed to help merchants manage customer credit, payment collections and bookkeeping during the festive business season. The platform digitises the traditional bahi-khata system, allowing businesses to record customer dues, set payment deadlines and track outstanding amounts through a dashboard. Merchants can also send payment reminders through WhatsApp and SMS, accompanied by UPI-enabled payment links.
The company said the solution aims to simplify bookkeeping and improve collections for small businesses handling higher transaction volumes during festive periods. Udhaar Khata is part of BharatPe's broader strategy to offer technology-led services beyond payment acceptance, including its recently introduced Agentic AI Suite.
Cloud.in joins OpenAI Partner Network as Select Partner
Cloud.in, the cloud, AI, quantum computing and cybersecurity business of Hostin Services, has been named an OpenAI Select Partner within the OpenAI Partner Network. The recognition will support its efforts to help enterprises develop, integrate and operationalise AI solutions.
The company plans to combine OpenAI capabilities with AWS Bedrock to offer model-agnostic enterprise AI services, focusing on security, governance, performance and cost considerations. Its areas of focus include enterprise AI transformation, intelligent automation and governed generative AI adoption. Cloud.in said it would pay particular attention to data governance, security and regulatory requirements for sectors such as BFSI and the public sector. The company has more than 27 years of experience in enterprise technology services.
Naxatra Labs appoints Naveen Deepak Veeramaneni as CPO
Indian deep-tech company Naxatra Labs has appointed Naveen Deepak Veeramaneni as its Chief Product Officer. He will lead the company's product development, engineering and manufacturing functions as it expands its electric motor and propulsion technology portfolio. Naveen brings experience in electric motor engineering and powertrain development, having spent nearly five years at Ather Energy, where he led motor engineering and subsequently the E-Powertrain team. At Naxatra Labs, he will focus on executing the product roadmap, strengthening design and development processes and improving integration between engineering and manufacturing.
Bank of India joins government's Bharatkosh non-tax receipt portal
Bank of India has announced its association with the Government of India's Non-Tax Receipt Portal (NTRP), also known as Bharatkosh, as an acquiring bank and payment gateway provider. The association will facilitate the collection of non-tax revenues through the government's integrated online platform. The arrangement is aimed at supporting digital payment transactions and providing users with an additional banking channel for making payments through the portal.
Bharatkosh enables the collection of various government non-tax receipts through an online mechanism. Bank of India's participation expands its role in digital payment infrastructure for government services and supports the government's efforts to make revenue collection more accessible and efficient.
Nupur Recyclers reports record Q2 FY27 performance
Nupur Recyclers reported its strongest-ever quarterly performance in Q2 FY27, with consolidated revenue rising 124.86% year-on-year to Rs 116.21 crore. EBITDA increased 148.48% to Rs 15.73 crore, while profit after tax grew 103.06% to Rs 8.80 crore. For the first half of FY27, revenue increased 90.27% to Rs 199.24 crore, EBITDA rose 130.34% to Rs 28.59 crore and PAT grew 93.19% to Rs 16.18 crore.
The company attributed the performance to improved production and capacity utilisation across its manufacturing and processing operations. Nupur Recyclers, which operates in ferrous and non-ferrous metal scrap processing, plans to strengthen capacity, improve operational efficiency and diversify across the recycling value chain.
Visage Lines appoints Vinod Nambiar as senior operating partner
Visage Lines, the parent company of Bombay Shaving Company, Bombae, The Mom's Co, rE and 100 Days, has appointed Vinod Nambiar as senior operating partner. Nambiar brings over three decades of experience in consumer businesses, brand building, retail and business transformation, including leadership roles at Hindustan Unilever and Colgate-Palmolive. He will work with the leadership team on manufacturing, product development, design and engineering, besides supporting the company's next phase of growth.
Indeed integrates employer services across Glassdoor and Indeed
Indeed has begun rolling out a unified login for employers across its job platform and Glassdoor, aiming to simplify recruitment and employer branding. The integration will allow businesses to manage their employer presence through a single account, access job listings across both platforms and use Indeed Smart Sourcing to identify candidates.
The companies will continue operating their respective websites independently. Job seekers will also be able to move between the platforms using one login, with shared information helping personalise their experience. Glassdoor reviews and conversations posted anonymously will remain unlinked to users' profiles. The development follows Glassdoor becoming part of Indeed earlier this year, as the companies seek to combine workplace insights with recruitment capabilities.
Apex Opinion launches independent medical advisory platform in India
US-based health technology company Krivox has launched Apex Opinion, an independent medical advisory platform for patients and families in India seeking specialist second opinions. Founded by Dr Saurabh Sanon, the platform connects patients with US board-certified specialists across medical disciplines. Patients can securely submit medical records and diagnostic reports for review and receive written second opinions, video consultations or multidisciplinary assessments through specialised panels. These include Heart Teams and Solid Tumor Boards.
Each opinion is signed by the reviewing physician, with a target turnaround time of seven business days after receiving complete medical records. Apex Opinion is accessible through its website and mobile applications. The company also plans to establish partnerships with hospitals and clinics in India.
Straive expands Microsoft partnership with 700-plus AI accelerators
Straive is deepening its partnership with Microsoft to help enterprises accelerate AI adoption and deployment. The company showcased its capabilities at Microsoft Ignite 2026, highlighting a portfolio of more than 700 data, analytics and AI solution accelerators. Its agent library brings together reusable workflows, AI agents and specialised tools designed to help businesses move beyond experimentation towards enterprise-wide implementation. Straive said customer-specific proofs of concept could be developed using customer data within seven to 14 days. The company recently achieved Microsoft's AI Platform specialisation and works across its Data and AI, Digital and Application Innovation, and Azure Infrastructure portfolios.
Hexnode adds native IT asset management to UEM platform
Hexnode has introduced native IT Asset Management (ITAM) within its Unified Endpoint Management platform, expanding its capabilities beyond enrolled devices to cover the broader workplace equipment lifecycle. The new functionality allows organisations to track laptops, monitors, accessories, furniture and other assets, alongside their assignments, purchase details, warranties and depreciation. It also includes QR-based physical audits and checkout records to help businesses manage equipment allocation and recovery.
The company has additionally introduced dedicated shared-device policies for Android and remote BIOS management for supported Windows PCs. The IT asset management capability is available to customers on Hexnode UEM's Enterprise plan and above, helping IT teams consolidate asset tracking and endpoint management.
Truecaller partners Bolna to bring transparency to enterprise voice AI calls
Truecaller has partnered with Indian voice AI platform Bolna to bring greater transparency and trust to AI-powered enterprise calls. The integration will allow Bolna's enterprise customers to use Truecaller for Business features without changing how their AI agents are developed. Businesses can display their name and logo during calls, provide personalised information about the purpose of each call and identify calls as AI-assisted.
The partnership also introduces post-call features that allow recipients to schedule callbacks when calls are missed or unanswered. The companies said the integration would benefit enterprises using voice AI for collections, renewals, KYC follow-ups and customer service. Bolna will manage conversations, while Truecaller will provide identity and contextual information.
Aurionpro secures additional order worth nearly Rs 100 crore
Aurionpro Solutions has secured an additional order worth nearly Rs 100 crore from a global hyperscaler for data centre infrastructure solutions. With the latest order, the aggregate value of engagements with the customer has exceeded Rs 400 crore, reflecting the expanding relationship between the two companies. The project is expected to strengthen Aurionpro's position in the data centre infrastructure segment as demand for AI-ready computing facilities accelerates. The company provides enterprise technology and data centre solutions, with capabilities spanning infrastructure, engineering and digital transformation.
Bhaskar Bhattacharya, Executive Vice-President and Head of Enterprise Business at Aurionpro, said the company appreciated the customer's continued confidence as it expanded its presence in the growing data centre market.
Mitra FMCG, Tanvi Foods announce Rs 600-crore strategic integration
Mitra FMCG and BSE-listed Tanvi Foods (India) have announced a strategic integration valued at ₹600 crore, aimed at strengthening their food processing, sourcing, procurement and distribution capabilities. The integration, exclusively advised by Bestvantage Investments, is expected to support expansion across domestic and international markets. The partnership will help Mitra leverage Tanvi Foods' export presence to enter high-value markets, including the US, UK and UAE. Mitra's distribution network will support Tanvi Foods' expansion in Northern India, while Tanvi Foods will help Mitra strengthen its presence in Southern India, particularly in household essentials. The arrangement will also provide Tanvi Foods access to raw materials such as flour, maida and edible oils through Mitra's sourcing ecosystem, improving procurement efficiencies and supply-chain operations.
UpTik crosses Rs 100 crore in cumulative investments
UpTik, an invoice financing startup, has crossed Rs 100 crore in cumulative investments. The platform recorded approximately Rs 21 crore in investments during FY26, followed by Rs 79 crore between April and October 2026. Notably, October alone contributed Rs 21.38 crore in investments, exceeding the platform's entire investment volume for the previous financial year.
Alongside this growth, UpTik has maintained an investor retention rate of 80%+, indicating sustained participation and confidence among its investor base. Founded with the aim of connecting investors with businesses seeking working capital, UpTik operates in the invoice financing space, enabling investors to participate in financing business invoices while helping enterprises address cash flow requirements.
OVH Group unveils 55 new cloud and AI products
The OVH Group has unveiled 55 new products across cloud and artificial intelligence at its OVHcloud AI Summit, marking an acceleration of its AI strategy. The offerings span infrastructure, orchestration, inference and AI-augmented platform-as-a-service solutions. The company is expanding its cloud portfolio with NVIDIA RTX 6000 Pro, Blackwell B300 and Rubin R200 GPUs, alongside new virtual private cloud networking services. Its AI portfolio includes AI Fabric, serverless computing, AI Endpoints and enterprise-focused AI Agents and AI Search services. Through a partnership with Gladia, OVHcloud is also extending speech transcription and voice generation capabilities across more than 100 languages. The services will be available across public cloud, private cloud and on-premises deployment models, supported by three dedicated AI research laboratories.
Taboola completes acquisition of digital advertising firm Dianomi
Global performance advertising company Taboola has completed its acquisition of Dianomi, a digital advertising services provider focused on premium business, finance and lifestyle publishers. The acquisition strengthens Taboola's ability to offer specialised financial advertising solutions through its Realize performance advertising platform, which uses proprietary publisher inventory, first-party data and artificial intelligence. Dianomi connects leading advertisers, including with audiences across premium publishers. With a network of more than 600 advertisers and publishers, the acquisition is expected to expand Taboola's reach among high-value business and finance audiences.
Scalefusion wins Platinum award at 2026 MarCom Awards
Unified endpoint management platform Scalefusion has won the Platinum Level distinction at the 2026 MarCom Awards for its brand film, “One Platform. One Agent. We are Scalefusion.” The award recognises the creative execution of the film and its presentation of the company's unified IT platform vision. The film showcases Scalefusion's core offerings, including Endpoint Management, OneIdP and Veltar, highlighting how device management, identity access and endpoint security work together within an integrated IT environment.
Bansi Astro crosses 15,000 users within two weeks of launch
Bansi Astro, an AI-powered astrology platform founded by Writesonic CEO Samanyou Garg, has crossed 15,000 users within two weeks of launching its Android application. The platform combines traditional Vedic astrology with artificial intelligence to offer personalised readings, Kundli analysis and voice-based consultations in English, Hindi and Hinglish. Its proprietary astrology engine uses classical systems, including Parashari and Krishnamurti Paddhati, to calculate planetary positions and generate interpretations.

articles.title: Windows 11 : vos logiciels pourront refuser de se lancer si votre PC ne coche pas ces 8 cases de sécurité
articles.text:
Windows Baseline Protection : comment vérifier si votre PC respecte les exigences de sécurité de Windows 11
Dans quelque temps, avec Windows baseline protection, Windows 11 cherchera à mieux protéger ses utilisateurs, quitte à les empêcher de pleinement pouvoir profiter de leurs applications.
Microsoft Windows 11 Professionnel
En ce mois de novembre 2026, Microsoft poursuit activement son travail sur Windows 11. Outre des nouveautés et une optimisation des performances, la firme pense également à la sécurité. C'est pour améliorer ce point que Microsoft vient de présenter lors de la conférence Microsoft Ignite 2026 Windows baseline protection, une nouvelle fonctionnalité qui risque de compliquer la vie de bien des utilisateurs en cherchant à mieux les protéger.
Huit critères à respecter pour pouvoir lancer certaines applications sur Windows 11
Prévue pour un lancement auprès du grand public en 2027 sans plus de précisions, Windows baseline protection peut déjà être essayé via le programme Windows Insider. L'objectif de Microsoft avec cet outil est de rendre les mesures de sécurité de Windows plus simples et plus faciles à vérifier, aussi bien pour les utilisateurs que les admins ou les développeurs d'applications.
Avec Windows baseline protection, les applications installées pourront vérifier que huit conditions de sécurité sont bien remplies par le PC pour se lancer pleinement, ou de manière bridée. Des éditeurs comme Adobe, Blizzard (Battle.net), Epic Games, 1Password et Dropbox travaillent déjà en collaboration avec Microsoft.
Les huit conditions à respecter, jusqu'à présent répandues un peu partout dans l'OS et qui seront désormais visibles via un panneau dédié dans la rubrique Sécurité des Paramètres, sont les suivantes : protection du processeur (TPM 2.0), Secure Boot, intégrité de la mémoire, pilotes certifiés et certifiés par Windows uniquement, sécurité fondée sur la virtualisation (VBS) et protections contre le débogage du noyau et les pilotes vulnérables.
Plus de sécurité, mais moins de souplesse
Sur le papier, pourquoi pas. Cependant, bien des utilisateurs, notamment les bidouilleurs et les joueurs qui désactivent certaines de ces fonctionnalités pour des raisons de compatibilité ou de performances, risquent d'avoir des problèmes pour lancer certaines applications. D'autant que les huit conditions actuelles peuvent être amenées à évoluer pour renforcer davantage la sécurité au prix de la flexibilité.
L'interface de Windows baseline protection devrait au moins faciliter l'activation des fonctionnalités nécessaires, vérifiée à chaque démarrage. Des guides seront proposés dans certains cas, comme pour activer Secure Boot dans le BIOS.

articles.title: Nous ne pouvons plus dépendre de SpaceX : ce rachat doit donner vie à un géant spatial made in europe
articles.text:
Le fabricant de satellites finlandais ICEYE veut racheter Avio, qui construit la fusée européenne Vega C. Un mariage qui pourrait changer la donne pour le spatial européen.
L’industrie des satellites panique : la retraite programmée du Falcon 9 de SpaceX suggère une pénurie prochaine de fusées, alors que ses rivales américaines subissent anomalie sur anomalie. Dans ce contexte, ICEYE, fleuron finlandais qui a déjà mis 84 satellites en orbite, a décidé de prendre les choses en main.
Une constellation de satellites d'observation
Et si son nom vous dit quelque chose, ce n’est pas pour rien. Car la start-up développe des engins radar, capables d’observer la Terre de jour comme de nuit. Des images prisées, qui lui sont achetées par des entreprises, mais aussi par des États, dont l’Ukraine, qui les exploite pour suivre les mouvements des troupes russes.
Leur valeur stratégique est telle qu’en octobre, le satellite russe Kosmos 2612 s’est suspicieusement approché de l’appareil ICEYE-X36, suscitant de vives inquiétudes. Pas de quoi freiner la société. Ce mardi 17 novembre, elle a lancé une offre pour mettre la main sur la société italienne Avio, cotée à Milan.
Surtout, elle construit Vega-C, l’un des deux lanceurs européens aujourd’hui en service aux côtés d’une certaine Ariane 6. Cette petite fusée, dotée d’une capacité de charge utile entre 2,5 et 3,3 tonnes pour l’orbite basse, a réussi 7 de ses 8 vols depuis 2022. Vous l’aurez compris : elle vole peu, moins de trois fois par an, et dispose avant tout de clients institutionnels à l’image de l’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA).
Accès garanti à l’orbite
Mais l’intérêt pour ICEYE est évident, alors que quasiment tous ses satellites ont été acheminés dans l’espace sur Falcon 9. Mettre la main sur Avio lui garantirait un accès à l’orbite, tandis que le groupe italien gagnerait un client fidèle et surtout, les moyens pour produire davantage et voler plus souvent. Car le mois dernier, la firme nordique a en plus signé un partenariat avec Nokia pour bâtir une constellation de connectivité pour l’Europe, incluant 50 satellites lancés chaque année dès 2028.
Cette annonce intervient alors qu’AST SpaceMobile, autre opérateur de satellites, a présenté son projet de fusée maison, baptisée Blacklift. Elle vise un lancement dès 2028, sans la moindre expérience dans les lanceurs. Un calendrier qui peut donc paraître extrêmement optimiste, d’autant plus lorsque l’on prend en compte les difficultés rencontrées par les acteurs déjà établis, à l’instar de Rocket Lab avec Neutron.
Dans cette optique, le pari d’ICEYE semble bien plus malin. Encore faut-il que l’opération aboutisse : les conseils d’administration d’Avio et de Leonardo, son premier actionnaire avec 18 % du capital, doivent encore examiner l’offre. L’accord des autorités italiennes sera également nécessaire, celles-ci pouvant bloquer le rachat d’entreprises jugées stratégiques. « Si j’étais Leonardo, j’y réfléchirais à deux fois avant de quitter Avio », a lancé Guido Crosetto, ministre italien de la Défense.
De son côté, ICEYE espère boucler l’acquisition en quelques mois.
Sources : Ars Technica, Reuters, The Wall Street Journal

articles.title: 138 km/h sur une trottinette électrique : la police saisit deux bolides hors normes
articles.text:
Lors d’un contrôle de routine ciblant la circulation sur les pistes cyclables espagnoles, les forces de l’ordre de Valence sont tombées sur un véhicule « tuné » un peu spécial. Passées sur le dynamomètre de la police, deux trottinettes électriques ont affolé le compteur en grimpant jusqu’à 138 km/h, pulvérisant ainsi de plus de cinq fois la limite légale de 25 km/h.
Un débridage inquiétant des trottinettes
Après analyse, les forces de l’ordre ont constaté que le matériel d’origine de la trottinette avait été profondément modifié. Pour atteindre de telles pointes de vitesse, les propriétaires n’ont pas hésité à greffer sur leurs trottinettes électriques des composants directement issus du monde de la course automobile, totalement inadaptés à une utilisation sécurisée sur la voie publique. Plus inquiétant encore, ces modifications ne sont pas si complexes à effectuer. Certains revendeurs spécialisés commercialisent en effet ces modèles apparemment conformes, mais qui intègrent un système de restriction qu’il est possible de désactiver à distance en quelques secondes via une simple télécommande ou une application sur son smartphone.
 Voir cette publication sur Instagram
À une telle vitesse sur un châssis léger et dépourvu d’équipements de protection adéquats, le moindre obstacle ou écart de trajectoire peut avoir de graves conséquences. Les autorités rappellent ainsi qu’à 138 km/h, ces véhicules ne représentent pas seulement un danger pour leur conducteur, mais constituent également une menace directe pour les piétons, les cyclistes et les autres usagers de la route.
Des amendes salées pour les conducteurs
Les deux engins ont été confisqués et retirés de la circulation sur-le-champ, et leurs conducteurs devront régler des contraventions pouvant atteindre 500 euros chacun. À cette somme déjà conséquente viendront s’ajouter des sanctions financières complémentaires spécifiquement liées aux modifications apportées aux véhicules.
À lire : Test Xiaomi Electric Scooter 6 Ultra : la trottinette électrique ultime à moins de 800 euros ?
Mais les autorités ne s’arrêtent pas seulement aux utilisateurs croisés sur la route. Une enquête a en effet été ouverte contre les commerces et boutiques spécialisées qui vendent ces modèles modifiés et fournissent les outils de déverrouillage. Les forces de l’ordre suspectent ces établissements de violer la réglementation relative à la protection des consommateurs en distribuant du matériel dangereux pour leurs utilisateurs.

articles.title: Amazon Polly launches voice cloning: A unique voice for your brand | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Amazon Polly launches voice cloning: A unique voice for your brand
Voice cloning in Amazon Polly is now generally available as a gated release. Give Amazon Polly a few minutes of audio recordings from a speaker who has agreed to have their voice cloned, and Amazon Polly builds your own cloned voice in that speaker’s voice. The cloned voices run on the Amazon Polly generative engine, which delivers similar naturalness and accuracy as the rest of the generative voices. Amazon Polly voice cloning launches with seven languages: English, Spanish, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, and Hindi. Each cloned voice speaks the language it was recorded in. The cloned voices are automatically encrypted and access-controlled: only you can access your cloned voices.
Amazon Polly voice cloning is available in all the AWS Regions supported by the Amazon Polly generative engine, including the AWS GovCloud (US) Region. Access is already enabled for select Amazon Polly customers. Others can reach out to their AWS account team or apply for access to get access.
With this new feature addition, you can build the cloning lifecycle into AWS applications. Building a cloned voice is free for Amazon Polly customers, and Amazon Polly charges for cloned voice usage on a pay-as-you-go basis, see Amazon Polly Pricing page for details.
Hear it for yourself
Press play: the first few seconds are a real recording of the speaker, and then their cloned voice takes over with words they never recorded.
- From recordings to TTS voice. A few minutes of our science lead Trevor’s source audio, and the resulting generative voice. 
         
  - Recorded: “Hello, I’m Trevor, from Science.” Cloned voice: “That first sentence was my real voice. This is my cloned voice, created from a few minutes of my recordings. It can read any text you give it.”
- Supports seven languages. Hear Jonas, one of the authors, speaking German in his recording and then in his cloned voice: 
         
  - Recorded: “Hallo, ich bin Jonas. Das ist meine echte Stimme.” (Hi, I’m Jonas. This is my real voice.) Cloned voice: “Und das ist meine geklonte Stimme! Gleiche Stimme, neue Worte: Diesen Satz habe ich geschrieben, aber nie aufgenommen.” (And this is my cloned voice! Same voice, new words: I wrote this sentence, but never recorded it.)
- Use in a variety of applications. Here’s Trevor in a new job he hasn’t had: a non-player character in a game. 
         
  - “Who’s that crossing my bridge? Oh, it’s you again. Same deal as last time: answer my riddle, or hand over the sandwich.”
- Expand your voice library with voice cloning. Hear this audio sample from AWS Chief Evangelist Jeff Barr: a real recording, then his cloned voice.
         
  - Recorded: “Hi, I’m Jeff, and this is how I really sound.” Cloned voice: “And this is how my cloned voice sounds, reading a sentence I never recorded.”
- Hannah: a real recording, then her cloned voice on a support line.
         
  - Recorded: “Hello, I’m Hannah. This is my real voice.” Cloned voice: “Thanks for calling AnyCompany. Your order 4471 9902 ships today and should arrive on Thursday between 9 AM and 1 PM. Your confirmation code is K-7-Q-2-X-9.”
- Joely: a real recording, then her cloned voice narrating a lesson.
         
  - Recorded: “Hi, I’m Joely, and this is how I really sound.” Cloned voice: “In this module, we’ll look at how a neural network learns. First, it makes a guess. Then it measures how far off that guess was, and adjusts, a little at a time.”
What you can build
A consistent brand voice across channels
Establish one recognizable voice and use it across your interactive voice response (IVR) system, cascaded voice agents, mobile app, in-store announcements, advertising, and connected devices. Rather than relying on a generic stock voice or re-booking a recording session each time a script changes, you can generate on-brand audio on demand, with a consistent sound in every channel.
Contact centers
Deliver a distinctive, on-brand voice across self-service flows, and update prompts as offers and policies change without a new studio session. You can create prompts from source text, test them before rollout, and use the same voice across greeting, routing, and notification experiences.
Media and content at scale
Creators, publishers, and studios can create audiobooks, courses, podcasts, game characters, and videos in multiple custom voices to enhance the listening experience, and produce subsequent chapters or updates quickly.
Localization with a consistent persona
Maintain a recognizable voice identity across a content library, so narration remains coherent across titles and updates. Each cloned voice speaks only the language it was recorded in. For multilingual experiences, create and review approved voices per supported language.
Accessibility and personalization
Offer a natural, human-sounding voice for reading experiences, assistive tools, and personalized interactions. You confirm the speaker’s consent each time you create a voice.
How voice cloning works
With voice cloning, you can build a custom Amazon Polly voice from recordings of a single speaker and then synthesize speech in that voice through the Amazon Polly generative engine. The voice moves through four steps, from recording the speaker to using the finished voice:
A cloned voice goes through four steps:
- Record. You record one speaker (see the following recording tips). You can send the recordings directly in the CreateVoice request or upload them on the console. You can also store them in an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket in the AWS Region where you want the voice and point Amazon Polly to them.
- Create. You call CreateVoice with 1-10 recordings, the language they are spoken in, and TermsAccepted=True, your confirmation that you have the speaker’s consent. Amazon Polly returns a voice ID (vc-…) right away and builds the voice in the background.
- Wait. Creation is asynchronous and typically takes 5-10 minutes. During that time, Amazon Polly also checks the quality of your text-to-speech (TTS) voice for speaker similarity. You call GetVoice until the status changes from pending to active or failed.
- Use. You pass the voice ID to SynthesizeSpeech for real-time audio or to StartSpeechSynthesisTask for long-form audio written to S3, with Engine="generative", the same way you call the other generative voices in Amazon Polly. When you no longer need the voice, you call DeleteVoice.
Consent and control
A cloned voice is made from one person’s recordings. You confirm that you have the speaker’s consent for all recordings and that you control who can use the voice and when it’s deleted.
- You confirm consent for each voice you create. When you create a voice, on the console or with TermsAccepted=True in the API, you confirm that you have obtained all rights and consents necessary to create and use the cloned voice. Your use of voice cloning is subject to the AWS Service Terms, the Biometric Notice and Consent Terms, the AWS Responsible AI Policy, and the AWS Acceptable Use Policy.
- Generated speech carries a watermark. Amazon Polly adds a watermark to text-to-speech audio generated with the cloned voice.
- Only your account can use it. A cloned voice is scoped to the AWS account that created it, and you control access with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). You can encrypt voices with your own AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key and tag them.
- You decide when it goes away. Delete a voice with one DeleteVoice call or on the console, once it’s active or its creation has failed.
- Amazon Polly does not retain a copy of your voice recordings once the voice is created and doesn’t use them to train Amazon Polly models. It keeps only the voice data it needs to synthesize speech, and stores it encrypted. You can use your own AWS KMS key for that encryption, and DeleteVoice removes the data immediately.
We recommend that you:
- Keep a record of each speaker’s consent.
- Delete the voice if the speaker withdraws consent.
- Tell listeners when they’re hearing a synthetic voice where that’s appropriate.
- Grant voice permissions only to the people and systems that need them.
For details on intended uses and limitations, see the Amazon Polly AI Service Card and the AWS Responsible Use of AI guidance.
Best practices for recordings
Your cloned voice learns from the recording, including the parts you’d rather it didn’t: the laptop fan, the room echo, the meeting app’s noise filter.
- Record two to ten minutes of natural speech, split into takes of up to a minute. You can send up to 10 recordings per voice, and up to 15 minutes of audio in total. Quality matters more than length: more audio might not change how the voice sounds.
- One speaker, a quiet room, the same distance from the mic. Use a USB microphone, or a phone app that can record WAV. Record in mono WAV, 16-bit, at 24 kHz from the start, so there’s nothing to convert later. Amazon Polly accepts other audio formats, but we recommend WAV. See the Amazon Polly Developer Guide for supported formats and limits.
- Avoid using meeting apps and browser recorders. Their echo cancellation and noise suppression change the voice, and the clone learns those changes too.
- Record every take in the style you want the voice to have. The cloned voice takes its style from the recordings and can’t blend several, so upbeat, sad, and angry takes won’t give you a voice that can do all three.
- Record in the language the voice should speak. Voice cloning is tested with recordings in US English, German, US Spanish, French, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese, and Hindi. Recordings in other accents of these languages, such as British English or Canadian French, also work but are less tested, so check the voice with your own content.
Getting started
On the console: once voice cloning is enabled for your account (see Availability), expand the left panel and choose Voice cloning, upload up to 10 recordings or select them from Amazon S3, confirm the terms, and choose Create. Each upload can be up to 5 MB. When the voice is ready, try it out on its details page.
In code, you need:
- The latest version of boto3 (pip install --upgrade boto3).
- IAM permissions for polly:CreateVoice, polly:GetVoice, polly:DescribeVoices, polly:SynthesizeSpeech and polly:DeleteVoice. For long-form audio, also polly:StartSpeechSynthesisTask, polly:GetSpeechSynthesisTask and s3:PutObject on the output bucket.
- For the following Amazon S3 example: your recordings in a bucket in the Region where you create the voice, with s3:GetObject permission for the IAM role or user that calls CreateVoice.
If Python reports that the Polly object has no attribute create_voice, upgrade boto3.
For long texts such as audiobook chapters or course modules, use an asynchronous synthesis task that writes the audio to S3:
For additional end-to-end Speech AI applications you can build with Amazon Polly, including the voice cloning feature, such as cascaded voice agents and live speech translators, go to the Amazon Polly GitHub repo.
Production considerations
Create voices ahead of time
Voice creation takes minutes, so treat it as a provisioning step, not part of a user request. A small workflow (for example, AWS Step Functions or a job queue) can call CreateVoice, check GetVoice every 30 seconds until the voice is active, and then store the voice ID in your configuration. CreateVoice and DeleteVoice share a limit of 1 request per second, so queue bulk creations and deletions.
Keep an inventory
DescribeVoices lists your cloned voices alongside the voices built into Amazon Polly. Cloned voices have Origin set to customer. Store the voice ID, Region, language, consent reference, and owner for each voice, and give each voice a unique Name. If a CreateVoice call times out or returns a server error, the voice might already exist, and the SDK’s automatic retries can create a second one. Check DescribeVoices for that name before you try again.
Plan for errors
CreateVoice returns ThrottlingException when you exceed the 1-request-per-second limit it shares with DeleteVoice, and ServiceQuotaExceededException when the account has reached its cloned-voice quota in that Region. Synthesizing with, or deleting, a voice that is still being created returns ConflictException. If a voice uses your own KMS key, callers without access to the key get an access-denied error. When creation fails, StatusReason gives only a general message, so check the recordings against the preceding recording best practices, then delete the failed voice and create a new one.
Scope permissions to voices
Cloned voices are IAM resources, so you can give the role that serves traffic permission to synthesize with one voice of choice. If the voice uses your own KMS key, that role also needs access to the key. Keep polly:CreateVoice and polly:DeleteVoice for a separate provisioning role. Here’s an example policy for the serving role:
With tags, you can write the same rule once for a whole group of voices using aws:ResourceTag conditions. Review your existing policies too: a statement that allows polly:SynthesizeSpeech on all resources ("Resource": "*") also covers every cloned voice in the account.
Plan for quotas and Regions
Each account has an initial quota of 10 cloned voices per Region. To request an increase, contact your account team or AWS Support. A voice exists only in the account and Region where you created it. To serve another Region or account, create the voice again in that Region from the same recordings, and make sure the speaker’s consent covers every copy.
Test with your real scripts
Before a voice goes live, listen to it reading your own content: product names, numbers, addresses, and the longest sentences you have. The same text can come out slightly differently from one request to the next. For fixed prompts such as phone-line greetings, generate the audio once, approve it with the speaker and your brand team, and serve the stored file. If a name or term comes out wrong, spell it differently in the text or use a Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) <phoneme> tag. Phoneme tags work with cloned voices in English, French, Italian, German, and Spanish. See Supported SSML tags.
Things to know
| Availability | Access is enabled per AWS account. If you see Voice cloning in the Amazon Polly console (expand the left panel and see if Voice cloning is listed), it’s enabled for your account. If not, you can reach out to your AWS account team or apply for access to request access. Supported AWS Regions are the same as the generative engine: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Zurich), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), and AWS GovCloud (US-West). A cloned voice lives in the AWS Region where you created it. | 
| Languages | English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, and Hindi. Tested recording locales: US English ( en-US), German (de-DE), US Spanish (es-US), French (fr-FR), Italian (it-IT), Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR), and Hindi (hi-IN). Other accents of these languages also work but are less tested. Each voice speaks the language it was recorded in. | 
| Recordings | 1-10 recordings per voice, up to 15 minutes in total. WAV is recommended: mono, 16-bit, at 24 kHz or 44.1/48 kHz. Amazon Polly accepts other audio formats too. Console uploads are limited to 5 MB per file. For larger files, use Amazon S3. | 
| Data handling | Amazon Polly deletes its copy of your recordings once the voice is created and doesn’t use them to train Amazon Polly models. It keeps only the voice data needed for synthesis, stored encrypted (you can use your own AWS KMS key), until you call DeleteVoice. | 
| Creation time | Typically takes 5-10 minutes to build a TTS voice, asynchronous. | 
| Synthesis latency | Same as Generative voices in Amazon Polly. | 
| Quotas | 10 cloned voices per account per AWS Region initially. To request an increase, contact AWS Support. CreateVoice and DeleteVoice share a limit of 1 request per second. | 
| Synthesis | Cloned voices follow the Amazon Polly quotas for generative voices, including the text limits per request and per synthesis task. See Amazon Polly quotas. | 
| Pricing | Creating a cloned voice is free. Amazon Polly charges for cloned voice usage on a pay-as-you-go basis. See Amazon Polly pricing. | 
| APIs | CreateVoice, GetVoice, DeleteVoice and DescribeVoices to manage voices. SynthesizeSpeech and StartSpeechSynthesisTask with Engine="generative" to use them. See the Amazon Polly API reference. | 
Conclusion
Voice cloning in Amazon Polly gives your application a voice people recognize: recorded once, with the speaker’s consent, and ready to use through the Amazon Polly APIs. To get started on the console, make sure Voice cloning is enabled for your account, prepare a recording and the required consent, open the Amazon Polly console, and create your first cloned voice. If you are a new customer and would like to enable voice cloning, reach out to your AWS account team or apply for access to get access.
For the developer guide, refer to the Amazon Polly documentation. For pricing, see the Amazon Polly Pricing Page. For additional speech AI use cases you can build with Amazon Polly, including voice cloning, check out the GitHub repo.
We can’t wait to hear what you build.
Thanks to Trevor Wood, Jonas Rohnke, Suyin Wang, Hannah Barrett, Nikie Xiong, Jeff Barr, and Joely Huang for lending us their voices.

articles.title: Lenovo Delivers Record Q2 Performance, Confident in Long-term Hybrid AI Opportunities
articles.text:
Thursday, November 19th 2026
Lenovo Delivers Record Q2 Performance, Confident in Long-term Hybrid AI Opportunities
Lenovo Group Limited (HKSE: 992) (ADR: LNVGY), together with its subsidiaries ('the Group'), today reported second quarter results for fiscal year 2026/27, demonstrating strong growth, a leap forward in profitability, and structural enhancements to the Group's business fundamentals.
Overall Group revenue for the second quarter reached an all-time high of US$30.2 billion, up 48% year-on-year. All business groups delivered record second-fiscal-quarter revenue while demonstrating strong profitability, with the Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) becoming an engine of hyper-growth with operating profit surpassing US$1 billion for the first time. Adjusted net income was up 166% year-on-year to US$1.4 billion, with adjusted net margin improvements of two percentage points year-on-year. AI-related revenue grew 79% year-on-year, surpassing the US$10 billion mark for the first time and accounting for 36% of total Group revenue in Q2.Performance was underpinned by broad-based momentum across the Group's diversified portfolio and balanced growth across all sales geographies. Business fundamentals continued to strengthen as faster growth in higher-value segments reshaped the Group's profit mix. This diversification helps mitigate industry-wide cost pressures and exposure to device-demand cycles, supporting a more resilient and sustainable profitability profile.
The Group continues to maintain disciplined cash and capital management, balancing strong revenue growth and industry-wide higher component costs with controlled capital expenditure and credit risk controls for large AI infrastructure projects. In this quarter, it generated US$1.6 billion in operating cash flow and US$1.2 billion in free cash flow.
Market Outlook
Lenovo remains highly confident in the long-term growth opportunities across both infrastructure and devices. As AI shifts from training to inferencing, rapidly expanding real-world use cases are driving sustained compute demand across cloud, edge, and enterprise environments. Cloud Service Provider revenue for the Group grew nearly 170% year-on-year, and Enterprise & SMB infrastructure revenue was up 200% year-on-year. At the same time, AI democratization is creating new demand for intelligent, agent-enabled devices as well as new form factors, as more AI data and workloads are generated at the edge. With a full-stack Hybrid AI portfolio spanning devices, edge, infrastructure, solutions and services, Lenovo is uniquely positioned as a full-stack player to capture opportunities and value across the market, as well as extend its leadership.
Lenovo's Board of Directors declared an interim dividend of 9.0 HK cents per share.
Yuanqing Yang, Chairman and CEO"Lenovo delivered another exceptional quarter, where we have sustained strong growth, made a leap forward in profitability, and structurally enhanced our business fundamentals, together demonstrating the success of our transformation from a PC leader into a global full-stack compute leader. Now, the real-world AI adoption is booming, which will not only drive sustained growth in infrastructure demand but also unlock tremendous growth potential in the device market. With our Hybrid AI strategy, full-stack portfolio across Client-Edge-Cloud, as well as strong financial discipline and operational resilience, we are confident in sustaining this strong momentum and reaching US$100 billion in annual revenue as early as this fiscal year."
Winston Cheng, CFO"Our results this quarter demonstrate the strength of Lenovo's geographically diverse business and balanced customer mix, while marking further progress toward our long-term net-margin ambitions of more than 5%. This, combined with disciplined working-capital management and controlled capital expenditure, gives us the flexibility to invest in organic growth while maintaining strong liquidity, a resilient balance sheet and our investment-grade credit profile. Together, our operational excellence and financial discipline position Lenovo to capture long-term demand for AI compute and deliver sustainable, profitable growth."
Financial Highlights: Q2 results:
Intelligent Devices Group (IDG):
- Revenue for IDG increased 15% year-on-year to record second fiscal quarter revenue of US$17.4 billion, with double-digit year-on-year revenue growth from PCs and smart devices.
- IDG's industry-leading operating margin was well maintained at 7.1%, despite a challenging market environment, reflecting the Group's operational excellence, supply chain resilience, and continued innovation.
- Global PC market share leadership was further strengthened, reaching 23.8% and extending Lenovo's lead over the #2 player to an all-time high of more than seven percentage points.
- The smartphone business delivered record second-quarter revenue, with double-digit year-on-year growth.
Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG):
- ISG delivered the strongest quarter in its history in terms of both revenue and profit, with revenue reaching US$11.3 billion, up 178% year-on-year, and operating profit exceeding US$1 billion for the first time. Operating margin expanded to a record 9.6%.
- ISG strengthened its global market leadership in traditional server, ranking number one in global x86 server shipments for the first time with 16%[3]market share, up six percentage points year-on-year.
- Enterprise & SMB revenue grew 200% year-on-year. GPU server revenue grew more than 300% year-on-year, supported by a pipeline that grew 48% quarter-on-quarter to US$80 billion.
- In the first full quarter as part of the Lenovo Group, Infinidat delivered its best quarter ever - with the high-end storage portfolio expanding ISG's enterprise storage capabilities.
Solutions and Services Group (SSG):
- SSG delivered record quarterly revenue of US$3.1 billion, up 20% year-on-year, and surpassing US$3 billion for the first time. Operating margin expanded 3.7 percentage points to a record 26%.
- SSG is growing nearly 2x faster than the broader services market, an outperformance increasingly being driven by higher-value segments as enterprise AI-led offerings accelerate. Managed Services, Projects & Solutions reached a record 63% of SSG revenue, demonstrating the strength of SSG's tech-led, labor-light model.
- AI Services continued to deliver triple-digit year-on-year revenue growth, as SSG scaled repeatable AI-powered solutions and Lenovo IP across industries, with momentum in areas including retail, manufacturing and sports.
- AI Library is also scaling proven, validated use cases across industries and functions, helping customers move from AI experimentation to measurable business outcomes up to 24 times faster.
Corporate highlights
Achievements, announcements, and notable commitments over the past quarter include:
- Lenovo climbed 43 places to #153 on Fortune's annual Global 500 List, making it the highest ranking in the company's history and one of the most significant advances in recent years. The recognition underscores Lenovo's position as one of the world's 500 largest companies by revenue.
- Lenovo received the highest possible rating by Hang Seng Indexes company advancing from its AA+ rating of last year to AAA this year, as well as the highest Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) scores for any company within the technology industry.
- The Group was named to TIME's World's Best Companies 2026 list for the first time, ranking no. 51 globally among leading companies worldwide. The ranking, developed by TIME in partnership with Statista, recognizes top-performing companies around the world based on three primary dimensions: employee satisfaction, revenue growth, and sustainability transparency. Lenovo achieved an overall score of 87.51, with its growth performance categorized as "Very High."
- For the third year in a row, Fast Company recognized Lenovo among its annual Best Workplaces for Innovators list. The Group was named as a finalist in both the Best Workplaces for Innovators: AI, Automation and Machine Learning Excellence and Best Workplaces for Innovators: North America categories.
- Lenovo has been recognized as a World's Top Disability Inclusive business through the Disability Index, the world's leading benchmarking tool for measuring and advancing disability inclusion in business.
- Tech World, Lenovo's annual global innovation event, will return to CES 2027 in Las Vegas. Hosted at Sphere and part of the CES Keynote lineup, Tech World will bring together a visionary lineup of speakers and breakthrough innovations with a first-of-its-kind immersive technology and music experience.
Source:
				Lenovo Investor Relations

articles.title: El precio de ethereum para este día
articles.text:
Ether, comúnmente llamada como ethereum, es la moneda virtual #2 en cuanto a términos de capitalización de mercado, por lo que se trata de una de las divisas digitales que más despierta el interés entre los mineros (creadores de las criptodivisas).
Ethereum es una plataforma de blockchain de código abierto que se ejecuta con el uso de su moneda nativa, llamada ether o ETH, por lo que a pesar de que la gente usa estos nombres como sinónimos son cosas distintas.
Ether es un token que se utiliza específicamente en la blockchain ethereum para pagar transacciones. Este token es responsable de impulsar casi todo lo que ocurre en la red, misma que puede ser usada por cualquier persona para crear y ejecutar contratos inteligentes, que son programas de software que se ejecutan de manera autónoma y sin la intervención del usuario.
De acuerdo con el portal de Binance, la moneda digital solana actualmente cuenta con 122.2M de unidades creadas.
La cotización de ethereum para este día a las 14:05 horas (UTC) es de 1805.95 dólares, lo que significa que la criptomoneda reportó un cambio de 0.69 % en el último día.
Por otro lado, registró un cambio de 0.0 % con respecto a su valor hace una hora. En cuanto a su popularidad, se ubica en la posición #2.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Ethereum
La nueva era de Ether
Tras varios meses de retraso y con el temor de que ya nunca pasaría, finalmente el 15 de septiembre de 2022 Ethereum llevó a cabo su tan ansiada fusión o actualización al nuevo nivel 2.0 con la promesa de mejorar la experiencia de los usuarios de esta criptomoneda.
“The Merge”, inglés para “La Fusión”, es una transformación en la forma en que Ethereum procesa las transacciones y en cómo se crean nuevos tokens de Ether.
Esta fusión se trata de la combinación de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum con una nueva cadena de bloques separada conocido como proof-of-stake, el cual reduce el consumo de energía de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum en un 99,9 %, según sus propios desarrolladores, lo que la vuelve más “amigable” con el ambiente al tiempo que las transacciones serían más baratas.
Sus defensores creen que la fusión hará que Ethereum resulte favorecido con respecto al máximo rival, Bitcoin, pues podría aumentar su uso.
En el proceso Proof Stake los propietarios de Ether bloquearán cantidades establecidas de sus criptomonedas para verificar nuevos registros en la cadena de bloques, ganando nuevas monedas además de su criptografía “participada”.

articles.title: Google will launch Android app verification requirement globally in January 2027
articles.text:
Google announced Android developer verification last year, and despite numerous objections from developers and users, the company is forging ahead. It began blocking the installation of unregistered apps in some countries this fall, and the system is expanding globally soon. Google says it will start rolling out the requirement in all regions in January 2027, and it urges devs who still haven’t registered their apps to do so soon.
The apps you download from the Play Store all come from verified developers, and Google’s new requirement expands that requirement to apps from third-party sources. Once developer verification is live in your region, you won’t be able to sideload apps unless the developer has registered with Google, which is framed as a security measure. Verification requires providing government identification and paying a $25 fee, which will allegedly make it harder for nefarious actors to distribute malware and scammy apps.
In September, Google launched verification in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. Apparently, nothing exploded, so the company is now ready to expand. It previously said verification would go global in 2027, and it’s not wasting any time with the January start. It says that verification will reach all devices within “several months.”
So far, Google is getting what it wanted from this initiative, with “millions” of non-Play apps already registered. The company says this accounts for more than 99 percent of global Android app installs.
The verifier system service has already been rolled out to Google-certified devices running Android 8 Oreo or higher, which accounts for just about every Android device in the world outside of China and Russia. Google has also partnered with the biggest third-party app stores to enforce verification: Galaxy Store, Honor, Oppo, Xiaomi, Transsion, and Vivo. The system-level verifier is responsible for blocking installs, but these stores will only list verified apps once Google flips the switch.

articles.title: « On choisit la plus difficile » : comment Xiaomi prépare l’arrivée de ses voitures en Europe — Frandroid
articles.text:
Lundi dernier, la veille du lancement mondial des Xiaomi 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max à Paris, une poignée de médias européens se retrouvent autour d’une table près de la gare Montparnasse, sous une pluie battante.
Face à nous, Xu Fei, présentée comme l’employée numéro 14 de Xiaomi, passée par Google avant de rejoindre Lei Jun en 2010. Elle est aujourd’hui vice-présidente et directrice marketing du groupe, et fait partie des dirigeants chargés d’emmener l’automobile hors de Chine. Pas de PowerPoint, un seul graphique, et beaucoup d’histoires. J’ai pu échanger longuement avec elle, et elle a notamment reconnu qu’il serait « vraiment difficile » de faire des smartphones très bon marché.
Sur la voiture, elle commence par raconter un refus. Bien avant de se lancer, Lei Jun, le fondateur de Xiaomi, investissait déjà dans de jeunes constructeurs électriques chinois, mais repoussait l’idée d’en devenir un : « Nos fondations ne sont pas assez solides. Je ne peux pas me lancer dans tout. La voiture, c’est trop sérieux. Je ne suis pas prêt ». Le déclic arrive en 2020, lors des dix ans de l’entreprise, au fil de tables rondes qui duraient parfois de 20 heures à 5 heures du matin.
Selon Xu Fei, Lei Jun en ressort convaincu que la voiture, après être devenue électrique, va devenir intelligente, et donc un appareil connecté comme un autre, « à condition qu’il soit sûr, parce que des vies sont en jeu ». Xiaomi annonce son entrée dans l’automobile l’année suivante.
    Pour aller plus loin
Nous avons testé le Xiaomi 18 Pro Max : il fait le plein de nouveautés
            
    Pour aller plus loin
Xiaomi, roi du petit prix, l’avoue : des smartphones très bon marché ? « Vraiment difficile »
            
En Chine, une gamme qui s’étoffe vite
Depuis, Xiaomi a avancé à un rythme que les constructeurs historiques lui envient. La berline SU7 est lancée en mars 2024, le SUV YU7 suit en juin 2025 avec 200 000 précommandes en quelques minutes, puis la SU7 restylée arrive en mars 2026.
En septembre, la marque a ouvert un nouveau front avec les Sky Nomad N70 et N90, des SUV à prolongateur d’autonomie, c’est-à-dire électriques mais équipés d’un petit moteur thermique qui recharge la batterie. Xu Fei parle de plus de 800 000 voitures livrées, uniquement en Chine continentale, et les chiffres publiés par Xiaomi donnent même 887 966 exemplaires à fin octobre.
Le tableau a pourtant ses zones grises. En octobre, les Sky Nomad ont représenté plus de la moitié des livraisons, alors que la SU7 enchaînait un treizième mois de baisse sur un an et que le YU7 chutait de 70 %. Avec 336 658 voitures livrées de janvier à octobre, l’objectif de 550 000 pour 2026 paraît hors de portée. Autrement dit, la croissance chinoise vient désormais de l’hybride, alors que c’est l’électrique pur qui doit partir en Europe.
L’équipe de Xiaomi nous a surtout beaucoup parlé de son usine de Yizhuang, en banlieue de Pékin, devenue selon elle une attraction qui accueille des centaines de milliers de visiteurs par an.
Xiaomi revendique 91 % de fabrication automatisée et une voiture qui sort de chaîne toutes les 76 secondes, avec plus de 700 robots. Des robots humanoïdes y sont même testés sur la chaîne, que Lu Weibing, président de Xiaomi, qualifie lui-même de « stagiaires ». Xu Fei tempère l’image d’une usine 100 % maison : « On investit beaucoup dans la fabrication intelligente, parce que certaines catégories de produits exigent les lignes les plus avancées. Mais on ne produit pas tout nous-mêmes. »
L’Europe d’abord, et pas par hasard
Pour comprendre le choix européen, Xu Fei revient sur les débuts de Xiaomi hors de Chine, avec pas mal de franchise. « Il y a dix ans, quand on est partis à l’étranger, c’était un peu : on a un tas de téléphones difficiles à vendre en Chine, est-ce qu’il y a un endroit où on pourrait les vendre ? C’est comme ça qu’a commencé le business hors de Chine ».
Pour la voiture, Xiaomi prend le chemin inverse. Là où la plupart des constructeurs chinois testent d’abord l’Asie du Sud-Est, la marque vise directement l’Europe : « Comme l’a dit notre fondateur, c’est une décision très simple. On choisit la plus difficile ». Elle compare ce choix aux essais de la SU7 sur le Nürburgring, « la piste la plus difficile du monde ». Record qui a été depuis battu par Porsche.
Le calendrier, lui, n’est pas une surprise. En septembre, Xiaomi Auto confirmait l’Europe pour 2027, avec l’Allemagne comme porte d’entrée et huit groupes de distribution déjà signés. Xu Fei ne va pas plus loin : « On commencera évidemment par l’Allemagne, mais plusieurs autres pays suivront. On a une feuille de route, mais on ne peut pas la partager, c’est encore en discussion. Désolée ». Pour la France, toujours espérée mais pas datée, il faudra patienter. Elle-même dit avoir passé cinq séjours en Europe l’an dernier et quatre cette année, d’au moins dix jours chacun.
Pas de blitz façon BYD
La méthode tranche aussi avec celle de BYD, très présent en Europe en publicité et en sponsoring.
« Je ne pense pas qu’on suivra le modèle BYD. Pour Xiaomi, l’important est de se faire des amis parmi les utilisateurs », tranche Xu Fei.
Elle veut d’abord convaincre les clients qui comprennent la voiture, puis compter sur leur bouche-à-oreille, car en Europe, la confiance « compte plus que tout, surtout pour une voiture ». Elle n’entend pas non plus miser sur la figure de Lei Jun, star absolue en Chine : « Si on veut une entreprise saine, on ne peut pas trop dépendre d’un seul homme. […] Ici c’est l’Europe, ce n’est pas la Chine. »
En Chine, Xiaomi gère lui-même ses points de vente, à la manière de Tesla. En Europe, il passera par des concessionnaires, et Xu Fei dit en avoir rencontré près d’une centaine, dont certains centenaires qui ont commencé par vendre des vélos.
Le tri reste délicat : « Certains partenaires sont bons. Mais ce n’est pas parce que le gars est bien que je vais l’épouser ». Voir les voitures dans les boutiques Xiaomi, en revanche, « pourrait prendre du temps ».
L’ambition et résumé en une phrase : « Ce Xiaomi n’est pas le Xiaomi que vous connaissiez ». La voiture doit rejoindre l’écosystème « Human x Car x Home », aux côtés du frigo, des aspirateurs et du lave-linge de la marque, de sa machine à laver star, de la Watch S5 en petit format ou du Smart Band 11.
La conduite autonome peut attendre
La discussion a pris un tour inattendu quand l’équipe de Xiaomi a retourné la question aux journalistes : en Europe, faut-il présenter ces voitures comme des autos autonomes, ou d’abord comme des électriques ? « C’est une bonne question. Quelle est votre suggestion ? », nous a-t-on lancé. Autour de la table, les avis ont plutôt convergé. Une électrique très connectée, bien dessinée et dotée de vrais boutons parlera davantage aux Européens qu’une autonomie encore perçue comme de la science-fiction, et un confrère a rappelé que les automobilistes français pensent d’abord à leur pouvoir d’achat, alors qu’une électrique reste chère.
Côté Xiaomi, on a rappelé que la Chine elle-même reste très prudente. La réglementation y plafonne largement au niveau 2, où la voiture gère direction et vitesse mais où le conducteur doit surveiller en permanence, le niveau 3, qui autorise à lâcher la route des yeux dans certaines conditions, restant très encadré.
L’Europe n’est pas plus permissive, et les aides à la conduite de Xiaomi devront de toute façon y être homologuées. Le message qui se dessine est donc celui d’une voiture électrique intelligente, plutôt que d’une promesse d’autonomie.
La SU7 en éclaireur
Xu Fei n’a pas dit quel modèle ouvrirait le bal. Au lancement parisien du lendemain, j’ai pourtant compté trois SU7 exposées et pas un seul YU7.
Selon nos informations, le SUV devrait bien arriver, mais la berline SU7 restylée serait la première à débarquer. Elle passe entièrement sur une architecture 800 volts, qui accélère la recharge sur borne rapide, et reçoit de série un lidar, un capteur laser qui cartographie l’environnement pour les aides à la conduite.
Le changement le plus symbolique concerne les poignées de porte. En octobre 2025, à Chengdu, le conducteur d’une SU7 accidentée est mort dans l’incendie de son véhicule, faute d’avoir pu être extrait par les témoins.
La Chine interdira les poignées affleurantes sur les nouveaux modèles dès janvier 2027, et la nouvelle SU7 adopte une ouverture à triple redondance, avec un secours mécanique qui fonctionne sans courant. En Chine, elle démarre à 219 900 yuans, soit environ 27 000 euros hors taxes, avant les droits de douane européens.
Ce qu’il manque encore
Prix européen, date précise, liste des pays : rien n’est officiel. Pour l’instant, les Européens connaissent surtout chez Xiaomi des smartphones de moins en moins bon marché, un 18 Pro Max, un bracelet, une montre et un lave-linge. Passer de l’électroménager à une berline vendue chez un concessionnaire allemand, c’est un pari autrement plus lourd qu’un lancement de smartphone.
    Pour aller plus loin
Xiaomi Auto confirme l’Europe en 2027 : l’Allemagne citée, la France espérée
            
    Pour aller plus loin
Xiaomi lance son Smart Band 11 en France : écran plus lumineux, capteur plus précis et prix en nette hausse
            
    Pour aller plus loin
