articles.title: "Be ready for change": AAIF’s CTO on why the agent stack won’t settle
articles.text:
“Be ready for change”: AAIF’s CTO on why the agent stack won’t settle
If you’ve spent any time over the past year trying to get AI agents to talk to each other without tearing your architecture apart, you know the struggle: vendor lock-in, fragmented protocols, and context that definitely vanishes the second you attempt to make a cross-framework handoff.
It’s astounding how fast developers’ needs have changed just in 10 months since the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) was formed to help solve those problems.
The Linux Foundation-backed AAIF gives shared agent infrastructure a home outside any one vendor’s control. It launched in December 2025 with three projects, including the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which connects AI applications to external tools and data.
On October 22, Anthropic contributed Agent Skills, and OpenAI contributed Open Responses to the foundation, alongside projects from Hugging Face and Alibaba. The additions brought AAIF to 10 hosted projects.
The New Stack Editor-in-Chief Nick Lucchesi sat down with Manik Surtani, AAIF’s co-founder and CTO, for The New Stack podcast at AGNTCon + MCPCon in San Jose, shortly after Surtani announced the additions in his October 22 keynote. The news was still fresh — the problems behind it, though, were all too familiar.
“I think that’s always been there,” Surtani said of the needs these projects address. “We’ve always known that sandboxes are really important.” Agent Skills, too, was already in use before joining the foundation. What had changed was where these projects would be governed.
“…having a standardized way to speak to a model is super important.”
“I’m really happy [Agent Skills] is here. And Open Responses as well. I mean, having a standardized way to speak to a model is super important. And I’m glad to see that it’s now happening in a way that is vendor-neutral, in a neutral governance and everything else.”
Four giant projects join the foundation
The big news from Surtani was this: Four heavy-hitting projects had joined the AAIF. Here’s what each brings to the table:
- Agent Skills (Anthropic): An open format for bundling instructions, scripts, and reference materials that an agent can load when it needs to perform a particular task. Write those instructions once, and use them across agents that support the format.
- Open Responses (OpenAI): An open specification, based on OpenAI’s Responses API, for how applications send requests to language models and receive results. A shared format means less translation work when developers switch between compatible model providers.
- OpenEnv (Hugging Face): A framework for building and sharing reinforcement learning environments, where agents practice tasks and receive feedback that can be used to train them.
- OpenSandbox (Alibaba): A platform for running agent-generated code and other work in isolated environments, separating that execution from the surrounding system.
While Anthropic, OpenAI, Hugging Face, and Alibaba rallying around a neutral foundation sounds like an AI miracle, Surtani noted that developer demand for open governance has existed from Day 1.
“More than faster, I think people are going to be able to build on top of things that they can trust more.”
“More than faster, I think people are going to be able to build on top of things that they can trust more,” Surtani said. “It’s not like you couldn’t trust open responses before. Of course you could. But now everyone has a say in how it’s going to grow and how it’s going to get shaped.”
Developers learned this lesson the hard way during the early cloud-native boom. Nobody wants to build core enterprise infrastructure on tech they can’t help steer.
Tackling the real pain points: Agent memory and portability
What problem keeps Surtani up at night? In the near term, it’s agent memory and context management — the information an agent needs to keep working on a task, including what’s already happened. A harness is the software around a model that manages its tools and workflow. Carrying that context from one model or harness to another remains difficult, Surtani said; he wants teams to be able to share it across the agents and people working on the same problem.
Beyond context portability, Surtani emphasized that software engineering teams should design for model independence right now using abstractions, proxies, and standardized interfaces. In practical terms, that means keeping the application from being tied too tightly to one model provider: A proxy or router sits between the application and the model, letting a team switch the model behind the scenes. It doesn’t solve everything, he cautioned, but it handles much of the heavy lifting.
Unlike the cloud stack associated with the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) — which Surtani described as already well-defined — the agentic AI stack is inherently fluid.
“My advice to people is just be ready for change. Change is going to happen.”
“My advice to people is just be ready for change. Change is going to happen,” Surtani told The New Stack. “Now, the good thing in all of this is that change is actually easy as well. With agents actually building themselves and writing code, it’s not going to be that expensive or that hard to migrate from one thing to the other.”
A sandbox for early-stage projects
With more than 300 member organizations signing on in just 10 months (ranging from fintechs to non-tech giants such as the Gates Foundation), AAIF realized its initial high barrier to entry — borrowed from the mature CNCF template — was ill-suited for a space evolving at warp speed.
To adapt, the foundation launched a new Sandbox lifecycle phase on September 1 to bring in early-stage, high-momentum community tools before they hit massive enterprise scale.
This Sandbox phase is a project maturity category, separate from the isolated execution environments provided by OpenSandbox. It gives promising young projects a place to develop under neutral governance, even before they have widespread production use.
Surtani’s main call-to-action for developers? Push your vendors for open standards, transparent specs, and true longevity.
Watch the full interview
Watch our full interview with Surtani to get his take on agentic commerce, agent permissions, advertising without human eyes, and why an AI stack might never fully solidify. Subscribe to The New Stack‘s YouTube channel to keep up with our new episodes as they are released.

articles.title: Google ajoute un mode privé à sa recherche IA : voici ce qu’il garde pendant 24 heures
articles.text:
Le Mode IA de Google permet désormais d’ouvrir une conversation qui n’apparaîtra pas dans votre historique et n’influencera pas vos prochaines recherches. Vous en perdez l’accès dès que vous la quittez, mais Google conserve le fil pendant 24 heures.
Toutes les recherches ne sont pas bonnes à partager, et cela vaut aussi pour le Mode IA de Google. Depuis le 17 novembre, Google déploie les fils de discussion temporaires dans le Mode IA de son moteur de recherche. Comme l’indique TechCrunch, un bouton permet de mettre la personnalisation de côté le temps d’une conversation, sans toucher aux réglages de son compte.
Un bouton pour poser une question hors de son historique
Si vous avez déjà utilisé les discussions temporaires de l’application Gemini, le principe est familier. Cette fois, le bouton se trouve dans le Mode IA du moteur de recherche, qui vient d’adopter Gemini 4 Hydrogen. Il suffit de cliquer sur l’icône en haut à droite avant de saisir sa question. Aucun réglage du compte Google n’est à modifier.
Une fois dans le fil, vous pouvez relancer l’IA, joindre une image ou poser une question à l’oral. Google répond sans s’appuyer sur votre activité passée, et ce que vous lui dites ne viendra pas modifier la personnalisation de vos prochaines réponses. En contrepartie, certaines fonctions sont indisponibles, dont les applications reliées à votre compte, le partage d’une réponse et la génération d’images.
Ce qui disparaît tout de suite, et ce qui reste 24 heures
Quand vous quittez la conversation, vous revenez à la recherche habituelle. Même si vous changez d’avis dans la minute, vous ne pourrez plus rouvrir le fil depuis l’historique de Google ou celui du Mode IA. Google précise que la conversation n’est pas enregistrée dans votre compte et qu’elle disparaît au bout de 24 heures.
Google indique que ces échanges ne servent pas à entraîner ses modèles d’IA générative, sauf si vous envoyez des commentaires ou si leur utilisation est nécessaire pour des raisons de sécurité. L’entreprise dit aussi continuer à collecter certaines données dissociées de votre compte pour faire fonctionner ses services et soutenir ses activités commerciales. Elle ne précise pas dans sa documentation si ces données servent au ciblage publicitaire.
Le fil temporaire s’arrête aux portes du moteur de recherche. Dès que vous ouvrez un résultat, le site consulté et les services qu’il utilise peuvent collecter des données, et votre navigateur peut enregistrer la visite. On peut donc demander des idées de cadeaux à Google sans les retrouver dans son historique de recherche, sans gâcher la surprise en laissant le nom de la boutique dans les suggestions de la barre d’adresse.
Autrement dit, le mode protège surtout de vos propres traces et de la personnalisation, pas d’un éventuel regard extérieur. Dans un contexte où Google pousse son IA au cœur de la recherche, ce qui alimente une grogne que le moteur de recherche DuckDuckGo cherche à capitaliser, le geste ressemble à un gage de confiance bienvenu, mais limité.

articles.title: Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis cuts a third of its workforce
articles.text:
Rumor mill: Firaxis Games, the studio behind the Civilization and XCOM strategy franchises, eliminated about 60 jobs on Tuesday, representing roughly a third of its workforce, according to people familiar with the cuts. The Maryland-based developer says the smaller team will focus on design, technology, and the player experience – areas that have defined its games for three decades.
Studio head Heather Hazen is also leaving as part of the restructuring. Meanwhile, people familiar with the matter say a new XCOM game, which is already behind schedule, could face further changes as a result of the overhaul.
Firaxis is owned by Take-Two Interactive Software Inc. and operates under 2K Games, one of Take-Two's publishing labels. A 2K Games spokesperson confirmed Hazen's departure. The people who provided details about the scale of the layoffs asked not to be identified because they were not authorized to speak to the press.
The spokesperson described the cuts as a restructuring intended to refocus Firaxis on what it does best: develop strategy games that have set the genre's standards for 30 years. The studio is being downsized so it can concentrate on design, technology, and the player experience, the spokesperson added. That means parting ways with talented colleagues who helped build the studio.
The rep acknowledged that the decisions were difficult but described them as "essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis."
By highlighting technology alongside design and player experience as areas of continued focus, Firaxis is signaling that its engine and systems development will remain central to the studio's work despite the downsizing. The company did not disclose which departments were affected by the layoffs. If the sources' figures are accurate, and 60 employees represent roughly a third of the workforce, Firaxis had approximately 180 employees before Tuesday's cuts and will continue operating with around 120.
That reduced workforce is responsible for two technically demanding franchises. Civilization VII, the studio's most recent release, launched last year to mixed reviews. Since then, Firaxis has released a steady stream of updates, requiring designers and engineers to continue working on the game well beyond its initial launch.
The new XCOM game has reportedly faced greater difficulties, according to people familiar with the project. They said development ran into problems and the game missed a significant milestone over the summer. Work on the project will continue, they added, but the layoffs could lead to further changes. Firaxis has not publicly commented on the game's status.
The timing puts the layoffs in sharp relief across Take-Two. They come right as Grand Theft Auto VI drops, which is expected to rank among the most lucrative entertainment launches of all time. Rockstar, another Take-Two publishing label, is responsible for developing and publishing the game.
The contrast highlights two very different sides of the same publisher. One label is preparing for a record-breaking open-world launch, while another is scaling back to a smaller core team that it says will continue developing the technology behind its strategy games. How effectively Firaxis's reduced workforce can support Civilization VII while getting the next XCOM game back on track will help determine whether the restructuring pays off.

articles.title: Optimize AI economics on Amazon Bedrock with Accenture’s sequenced approach | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Optimize AI economics on Amazon Bedrock with Accenture’s sequenced approach
As enterprises scale AI on Amazon Bedrock, token spend often grows even as per-token prices fall. Without cost allocation tags in place, your cloud invoice shows AI spend as a single line item rather than by team, workload, agent, or model. Cheaper tokens expand adoption, and agentic workloads multiply invocations. As successful AI use cases scale, consumption can rise faster than unit prices drop. The economic question is whether the business value generated grows faster than the cost of the intelligence required to produce it. The Linux Foundation has launched the Tokenomics Foundation to develop open standards for AI cost economics, a sign that managing the economics of AI is now an industry discipline.
In this post, you will learn about six levers for optimizing token spend, how Accenture applied them in production, and how to apply them using Amazon Bedrock.
Accenture applied these levers in four client engagements across telecom, insurance, mining, and a large enterprise deployment. The same levers are available natively on Amazon Bedrock as described in this post. Where savings were measured, token spend fell by about 40–85 percent. Results are specific to each client’s workload and may vary. Client names are withheld by Accenture to protect client confidentiality.
Attribution first: Measuring cost at the business level
Before you optimize anything, you need to see where consumption is occurring, who owns it, and what business value it produces. Cost allocation tags at the team, workload, and agent level are the prerequisite for connecting consumption to accountable owners and, ultimately, to business outcomes. You apply them through Amazon Bedrock application inference profiles, one profile per application or workload, tagged by team, cost center, and environment. After you activate them as cost allocation tags in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console, you can use these tags to trace which teams, applications, and agents are driving spend. They also make it possible to measure the impact of each change you introduce.
Three AWS services provide the underlying telemetry. AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR 2.0), delivered through AWS Data Exports, handle financial attribution, breaking down billed inference cost by workload and team after your cost allocation tags are active. Amazon CloudWatch captures operational signals such as invocation counts and latency. Amazon Bedrock model invocation logging records request-level detail, including the model used and the input and output token counts for each call.
Telemetry alone isn’t enough. Engineers can read cost per invocation on a dashboard, but product owners and program leaders need a metric expressed in business terms. Accenture’s Cost per Business Transaction (CpBT) framework bridges this gap. CpBT aggregates all the model invocations, retries, tool calls, and agent handoffs that contribute to one successful business output into a single fully loaded cost figure. It surfaces the true cost of producing a result, including the failed attempts that raw token pricing hides. Tracked against the business value each workflow delivers, CpBT distinguishes a growing bill that reflects scaling success from one that reflects waste.
The six optimization levers
The goal of these six levers isn’t to minimize tokens at all costs. It’s to use the right amount and level of intelligence to deliver each business outcome at the appropriate cost, quality, and risk. The levers are organized into three phases based on the complexity of the change and the investment it requires. AWS and Accenture recommend working through the phases in order, and you can apply each phase independently to the workloads where it will have the most impact.
Phase 1: Configuration only, no infrastructure change
With Amazon Bedrock prompt caching, the model reuses the parts of a prompt that repeat across requests, such as system instructions, tool definitions, and reference documents, so you stop paying full price to process the same content again. Amazon Bedrock stores the key-value state of previously computed prompt prefixes and is designed to skip recomputation on later requests. This is designed to reduce cached input token costs by up to 90 percent for supported models (see Amazon Bedrock Prompt Caching).
Amazon Bedrock batch inference processes non-urgent workloads asynchronously as a group at 50 percent lower cost than on-demand pricing for select models (see Amazon Bedrock Pricing). You submit inference requests as a batch job, and results are written to Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) when processing completes. Batch inference suits nightly reports, document processing pipelines, and evaluation runs that don’t need an immediate response.
Both levers add configuration to your existing setup. Prompt caching requires cache checkpoint markers in your prompts, and batch inference requires submitting eligible requests as a batch job instead of calling the on-demand API. Apply caching to interactive, on-demand traffic and batch inference to asynchronous work. Neither requires new infrastructure or architecture changes.
Phase 2: Architectural changes
Amazon Bedrock intelligent prompt routing directs requests across models within the same family, matching each task to the level of intelligence its business value, complexity, and risk require, rather than defaulting every request to the most powerful model. Intelligent prompt routing can reduce costs by up to 30 percent without compromising accuracy (see Amazon Bedrock intelligent prompt routing). Check Amazon Bedrock Pricing for any routing charges. In the following engagements, Accenture’s model tiering and triage routing apply this same routing lever.
Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) optimization tunes the retrieval step in the RAG process so that fewer unnecessary context tokens reach the model. Techniques such as hierarchical chunking, metadata-based filtering, and reranking narrow the retrieved context to the most relevant chunks, so you pay primarily for content that improves the answer.
Two complementary Accenture patterns work alongside these AWS native levers. Context scoping limits the data each agent receives to the document slice relevant to its step of the workflow, rather than passing the full case context at every handoff. Context compression summarizes or filters documents before they reach the model. Both reduce input token volume, especially across multi-agent chains.
Phase 3: Infrastructure and training investment
Semantic caching stores responses and reuses them when a new request is semantically similar to one already answered, even if the wording differs. This avoids redundant model invocations and reduces both cost and latency. On AWS, you can implement it with a vector store such as Amazon ElastiCache in front of the model. In an AWS benchmark on 63,796 real chatbot queries, a 0.90 similarity threshold produced a 74.5 percent cache hit rate, 92.3 percent accuracy, and 72.5 percent cost savings (see ElastiCache semantic caching benchmarks). As you apply routing and semantic caching, keep Amazon Bedrock Guardrails on every route, and set semantic cache expiry so that users don’t receive outdated answers.
Model distillation transfers knowledge from a large teacher model to a smaller, faster student model. Distilled models in Amazon Bedrock are up to 500 percent faster and up to 75 percent less expensive than original models, with less than 2 percent accuracy loss for use cases such as RAG. Distillation is best suited to stable, high-volume workloads where the transaction volume justifies the training investment.
In production: Four client engagements
Accenture applied these levers in four client engagements. Each engagement targeted a different cost pattern. In two of them, Accenture applied several changes together, so those results reflect the combined effect rather than any single lever.
The first engagement was a large enterprise deployment where every request went to a frontier model, with no caching, model tiering, or batching. Accenture applied three changes together: model tiering to match each task to the smallest model that could handle it well, prompt caching for repeated context, and batch processing for overnight and non-urgent jobs. Together they cut monthly token cost by 85 percent, and the saving was not separated by change. About 15 percent of tasks still needed the top model for hard, open-ended reasoning, and the rest ran on lighter models. Your split will depend on your workload composition.
The second engagement was a telecom operator with $12 million in annual token spend. Most of that spend came from agents fanning out requests without limits and from every request going to a frontier model regardless of complexity. Accenture applied triage routing, semantic caching, and context compression together. Input tokens fell by 70 percent, and annual token spend fell from $12 million to $3.8 million, a 68 percent reduction. Accenture validated output quality against the operator’s pre-change performance benchmarks.
The third and fourth engagements each applied a single cache layer. An insurer used model-layer prefix caching, reusing the static portions of its prompts across invocations. A mining operator used an application-layer semantic cache, returning stored responses for repeated queries before they reached the model. Across the two engagements, token spend fell by about 40 percent combined, without model routing changes or training investment.
Results
Outcomes ranged from about 40 percent to about 85 percent, reflecting each client’s starting point. The large enterprise deployment began with no optimization in place and reached 85 percent. The telecom operator reached 68 percent on $12 million in annual token spend, and the insurer and mining operator reached about 40 percent combined with one caching lever each. Results are specific to each client’s workload and may vary.
These savings aren’t the end goal. They create capacity to scale AI workloads, reinvest in higher-value use cases, and improve the return generated by each dollar of AI consumption. Two of these engagements applied several changes at once. When you apply one lever at a time, you can attribute each result to a specific change. AWS and Accenture recommend this sequence for your own workloads: connect consumption to owners and outcomes, apply one lever at a time, measure cost, quality, and business value, and build on what works.
Production governance: Four operating tenets
Optimizing AI economics in production requires an ongoing governance cycle spanning cost, quality, risk, and business value, not a one-time technical change. Before you apply any lever, establish a quantitative baseline for both cost and quality so that you can measure the impact of each change against a known starting point. When you validate output quality, use held-out evaluation sets drawn from your actual production traffic rather than synthetic benchmarks. Apply one lever at a time per workload so that you can attribute results to a specific change and roll back cleanly if quality drops below your acceptable thresholds. If you operate in a regulated industry such as financial services, insurance, or healthcare, document your quality test results and rollback procedures as part of your standard change management record.
These four tenets apply regardless of which levers you are using or what phase of the sequencing you are in. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is an environment where you can build, connect, and optimize agents at scale with any framework or model. It includes AgentCore Evaluations, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that provides batch evaluation to support your quality validation cycle as you progress through more advanced levers.
Getting started
You can begin with three steps. First, turn on cost attribution for Amazon Bedrock by applying cost allocation tags at the team and workload level so that your spend is traceable from day one. Second, activate those tags in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console. Then use CUR 2.0 and model invocation logging to identify high-consumption workloads, and assess each one based on spend, business value, quality requirements, risk, volume, and optimization potential. Third, apply Amazon Bedrock prompt caching to that workload’s interactive traffic and Amazon Bedrock batch inference to its asynchronous jobs as configuration-only changes, and measure the result before you move to architectural changes in Phase 2.
The AWS Well-Architected Agentic AI Lens includes model invocation and token cost optimization (AGENTCOST02), a focus area within the cost optimization pillar for agentic workloads. This focus area provides a structured framework you can use to apply these levers at scale across your organization.

articles.title: Google gives Gemini the ability to use your Mac for you | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google on Thursday announced that it is bringing computer use to its Gemini desktop application on macOS, allowing its AI to complete tasks on users’ behalf, navigating native Mac apps, and browsing websites in the background.
The tech giant is a little late to the game with this launch, as other leading AI model makers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta have already been offering agentic features in their desktop applications for some time. Meanwhile, Google only this week announced the broader rollout of Gemini’s “Tasks,” the in-app feature that allows the AI to work more as an agent, helping users sign into websites, make online purchases, or book appointments.
Google also only recently began admitting early testers to try its revamped “CC” AI agent, announced in September, which is designed to help families stay organized across email, calendars, chats, and tasks.
Computer use is another type of agentic offering that allows an AI agent to take actions directly on the user’s computer — in Gemini’s case, a Mac. This allows the AI to complete multistep tasks that involve getting things done across local files, apps, and the web. After the user instructs the AI what they want to do, they’ll see the agent working in a live preview in their chat, while still keeping their screen and cursor free to continue working on other things.
As with other AI agents offering computer use, users can pause, stop, and approve Gemini’s actions before they happen.
Google suggests the feature could be useful for tedious tasks and other workflows, like filling out forms, repeating the same task over and over across a batch of files, organizing files into folders based on specific criteria, creating slideshows from files or information in online dashboards, and more.
The feature is initially available in English in the U.S. and requires the Gemini app for Mac and a Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscription. The company didn’t say when it would expand to other markets or platforms.

articles.title: Anthropic: dona do Claude estreia na bolsa valendo US$ 1,5 trilhão • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Anthropic: dona do Claude estreia na bolsa valendo US$ 1,5 trilhão
Famosa pelo Claude, empresa de inteligência artificial chega à bolsa dos EUA com ações cotadas a US$ 83, um valor notável.
Esta quinta-feira (19/11) registra um momento histórico para a Anthropic: a empresa especializada em inteligência artificial realiza, hoje, a sua oferta pública inicial de ações (IPO, na sigla em inglês). A estreia na bolsa (Nasdaq) ocorre com a companhia tendo um valor de mercado estimado em US$ 1,5 trilhão (R$ 8,86 trilhões).
Um número tão grande é efeito, em parte, da valorização do preço por ação. Inicialmente, esperava-se que cada papel custasse algo entre US$ 70 e US$ 78, mas o preço individual ficou em US$ 83 na estreia. Tamanho ajuste na precificação inicial indica que há mais investidores interessados em comprar as ações da Anthropic do que o previsto.
980 milhões de ações foram oferecidas nesta IPO. Considerando o preço individual de US$ 83, isso representa um montante de US$ 81,3 bilhões em valor bruto. Desse total, cerca de US$ 80 bilhões irão para os cofres da Anthropic, enquanto o restante ficará com acionistas anteriores que aproveitaram a estreia para vender parte de suas ações.
Não termina aí. A Anthropic também está realizando uma operação fechada de venda de ações, esta direcionada a investidores institucionais e parceiros estratégicos, que incluem big techs como Google, Nvidia e Microsoft. A arrecadação desta operação é estimada em US$ 26 bilhões.
Se somarmos a IPO e a operação fechada, a arrecadação bruta com a venda de ações chega a notáveis US$ 107,3 bilhões.
É curioso pensarmos no valor de mercado de US$ 1,5 trilhão porque ele vem de uma empresa que tem custos operacionais elevados. E, pelo menos até o momento, a Anthropic não dá lucro. Para você ter ideia, a companhia encerrou o terceiro trimestre de 2026 com prejuízo operacional de US$ 567 milhões.
Por outro lado, a empresa registra receitas expressivas. Ainda considerando apenas o terceiro trimestre do ano, a receita da Anthropic ficou em quase US$ 17 bilhões. Isso se deve ao interesse cada vez maior de usuários individuais e organizações por soluções de IA da família Claude.
Em linhas gerais, os investidores veem potencial para que a Anthropic ganhe ainda mais destaque no mercado e, finalmente, se torne lucrativa.

articles.title: Nodal Networks raises $11.3M to solve global shipping bottlenecks - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Nodal Networks raises $11.3M to solve global shipping bottlenecks
Nodal Networks Inc., a company that builds artificial intelligence decision networks to manage the world’s shipping container terminals, announced today that it has raised $11.3 million in seed funding to help port and rail hubs reduce congestion and move more cargo.
Freight networks move more than a billion shipping containers per year. They carry everything from clothing, electronics, furniture, raw materials for construction and perishable goods – the things that people rely on every day.
However, according to Sea-Intelligence Pte. Ltd., a Copenhagen-based shipping consulting and data analytics company, in September only half of the world’s container ships arrived on time and the late ones were a week behind. Oftentimes, ships can spend nearly half their time at port not working cargo.
Nodal Networks believes the solution is better management, not new infrastructure, which will be key to providing better terminal capacity.
“Watching ports through Earth-observation satellites, I started to see transport as a physical internet: Containers are the data packets, ports and rail yards are the routers, and congestion is the lag,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Paul Albert-Lebrun. “So, we went looking for the routers. We spent eight months in ports, terminals and rail yards, and even sailed the North Sea aboard a container ship, learning the work from the people who do it.”
Albert-Lebrun worked in satellite operations and later led product at Kepler Communications Inc., a space telecom company. Co-founder and Chief Commercial Officer Nic Westgate, by contrast, comes from mining engineering, approaching the problem from the opposite end.
Together, they combined their expertise in Malcom, the company’s AI-powered platform for improving terminal operations, named after Malcom McLean, a North Carolina truck driver turned entrepreneur who pioneered modern container shipping.
The AI platform combines agents with specialized forecasting models that can see, understand and predict incoming shipments, timing and offloading metrics to follow congestion, track lost productivity and make better-informed decisions about container placement, equipment allocation and loading operations. The company said it’s already deployed in terminals across three continents but did not provide details on which locations.
“There’s a lot of noise about AI in our industry right now, and I see a new company pitching terminals almost every week,” said Peter Levesque, an adviser to Nodal and former president of Ports America Inc. and CEO of CMA CGM North America LLC. “Most bring a general-purpose tool and look for somewhere to apply it, and few can answer the question every operator asks: what’s the return? Nodal got into the details, surrounded itself with the right people and kept the customer’s bottom line at the center of everything.”
Levesque added that Nodal has proven itself in terminal after terminal by showing measurable results.
According to Nodal, Malcom has already reduced truck time by one-half in one terminal after operators reassigned yard equipment. At another terminal, ship loading and unloading speeded up by 5% after the team pinpointed what kept cranes waiting for containers. In both cases, the company said Malcom helped operators identify which decisions would have the greatest impact.
The company said it would use the new funding to expand Malcom’s reach to more terminals within the groups Nodal already works with, support new customers and advance product development. It also intends to extend Malcom beyond the terminal, adding planning for shipping lines, railroads and trucking companies, becoming support for transportation networks where operators work together to exchange information.

articles.title: Karnataka emerges as India's GCC powerhouse with 1,088 centres, says Kharge
articles.text:
Karnataka emerges as India's GCC powerhouse with 1,088 centres, says Kharge
Karnataka hosts 51% of India's GCCs and 43% of its GCC AI talent. Minister Priyank Kharge unveiled a new Zinnov-KDEM report at the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026.
Global companies are increasingly looking to their India offices to do more than support business operations. In Karnataka, these centres are taking on a larger role in building and deploying artificial intelligence for their global businesses.
The State is home to 1,088 Global Capability Centres (GCCs), accounting for 51% of India's total. It also hosts 111,000 AI and machine learning professionals, representing 43% of the country's GCC AI/ML talent.
These findings are part of a new report, GCCs in Karnataka: Shaping the Future of Enterprise AI, released by Karnataka IT and BT Minister Priyank M. Kharge on November 19 at the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026.
Prepared by Zinnov in collaboration with the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM), the report examines how GCCs in the State are building AI capabilities, hiring specialised talent and taking on larger technology mandates.
Karnataka leads in AI maturity
The report finds that surveyed Karnataka GCCs score 1.12 times the national average in overall AI maturity. Around 66% have reached the Portfolio Hub stage, compared with approximately 43% across India.
The findings also point to stronger AI adoption within these centres. Around 69% of surveyed Karnataka GCCs have dedicated AI budgets, against 57% nationally. Similarly, 69% conduct role-specific AI training, compared with 53% across the country.
Around 83% reuse in-house AI platforms across business units, while 66% follow Responsible AI practices. The corresponding national figures are 57% and 49%, respectively.
Karnataka's position is also reflected in its AI infrastructure. More than 660 GCCs in the State have AI and machine learning capabilities, while over 120 dedicated AI and ML Centres of Excellence operate in the region. This represents around 48% of India's total.
Bengaluru attracts AI leadership talent
Beyond infrastructure and adoption, Bengaluru has emerged as a major destination for senior AI talent.
The city accounts for 44% of India's senior AI leadership job postings within GCCs, 6.4 times the average of other tier-I cities. It also accounts for up to 63% of Distinguished and Principal AI Engineer openings.
In 2026, AI skills featured in 13.6% of GCC job postings in Bengaluru, compared with 9.8% at the same companies' offices outside Karnataka.
The State's wider technology ecosystem supports this demand. Karnataka hosts more than 29% of India's AI startups and has over 5,000 active technology investors. It also produces more than 130,000 STEM graduates annually.
GCCs move beyond support roles
The report outlines five priorities for Karnataka's GCC ecosystem through 2030. These include attracting advanced GCC mandates, increasing global ownership of AI development, building AI leadership talent, scaling AI with measurable business outcomes and moving research into enterprise adoption.
The State currently hosts 1,088 GCCs, including 320 centres belonging to Global 2000 companies. Between FY2021 and FY2026, it attracted 217 of India's 510 new GCCs.
Launching the report, Kharge said Karnataka's GCCs were becoming key drivers of the State's technology leadership.
"With 1,088 GCCs and 111,000 AI and machine learning professionals, Karnataka is where global enterprises come to build AI," he said.
He added that the State would continue strengthening AI capabilities, research and skills through its dedicated GCC Policy and IT Policy 2025-30, while extending opportunities to other regions through the Beyond Bengaluru initiative.
Dr Manjula N, Secretary of the Department of Electronics, IT and BT, said Karnataka had embedded AI and deep technology across six State technology policies. She pointed to the higher adoption of role-specific AI training and Responsible AI practices among surveyed GCCs as evidence of this progress.
Nitika Goel, CMO and Managing Partner at Zinnov, said GCCs were entering a new phase in which their value would be measured by AI deployed in production rather than pilots and proofs of concept.
"The contest now is for talent, and Karnataka holds a rare advantage, with over a thousand GCCs, tier-1 academic institutions and the country's largest cohort of start-ups," she said.
The report also points to the State's efforts to build its talent pipeline through Nipuna Karnataka, a Rs 300 crore industry-driven programme focused on AI, deep tech and cybersecurity.
The report, GCCs in Karnataka: Shaping the Future of Enterprise AI, is available on the KDEM website.

articles.title: Youtube Premium pour moins cher : Google lance une nouvelle façon de s’abonner
articles.text:
Alors que le prix de YouTube Premium n’en finit plus de grimper, voilà un possible bon plan qui se profile à l’horizon. Pour peu que vous ayez besoin de l’abonnement le plus cher de Google pour son IA Gemini et le stockage en cloud, vous pourrez alors faire d’une pierre deux coups et obtenir la plateforme de streaming musicale non seulement pour vous, mais aussi pour votre famille.
Dans le détail, cette nouveauté s’applique à l’abonnement Google AI Ultra à 99,99 euros par mois. Auparavant, cette offre permettait d’obtenir un compte Youtube Premium individuel. Désormais, elle débloque un compte famille, ce qui permet de partager l’abonnement avec jusqu’à cinq personnes supplémentaires.
Une montée en gamme plus cohérente
Ce changement permet de mieux appuyer la montée en gamme entre le tiers Google AI Pro et AI Ultra. Le premier, coûtant tout de même 49,99 euros par mois, offre 10 To de stockage et Youtube Premium Lite en individuel. L’abonnement Ultra à 99,99 euros, en plus de ses 20 To de stockage des limites d’utilisations de Gemini cinq fois plus élevé, permet donc de passer deux tiers sur son abonnement Youtube Premium.
Pour une fois, le changement n’est pas disponible uniquement aux États-Unis. La page Google One qui résumes les différents tiers des abonnements à Google Cloud a été mise à jour pour affiche le changement.

articles.title: En 2008, Steve Jobs sacó el primer MacBook Air de un sobre: Richard Yu, de Huawei, sube la apuesta metiendo dos ordenadores
articles.text:
El 15 de enero de 2008, Steve Jobs subió al escenario de la Macworld, abrió un sobre de oficina normal y corriente y sacó de él un MacBook Air. El truco dejó claro que podían construir un portátil lo bastante fino y ligero para que el usuario pudiera llevárselo cómodamente a cualquier lugar. Casi dos décadas después, Richard Yu, director ejecutivo de Huawei, quiso tomar prestado el chiste para presentar el MateBook Fold S.
Lo que ha cambiado todo. En 2008 el remate era un portátil fino. Ahora el remate son dos PC plegables, uno sacado del otro. El perfecto ejemplo de cómo la tecnología y las pantallas han evolucionado a lo largo de estas últimas dos décadas. Ahora los ordenadores, tablets y dispositivos móviles se presentan en múltiples formatos, con pantallas plegables, y con hardware sobrado para nuestras tareas del día a día.
Qué ha pasado. Yu publicó un teaser en redes el pasado 10 de noviembre en el que aparece metiendo en un sobre el MateBook Fold Ultimate Design de 18 pulgadas, dobla el sobre por la mitad y saca una máquina más pequeña, en este caso el nuevo MateBook Fold S. El modelo original de 18 pulgadas se pliega hasta ocupar el espacio de 13 pulgadas, mientras que el Fold S se despliega hasta las 14,7 pulgadas. Cerrado tiene aproximadamente el tamaño de un cuaderno.
Los detalles. El Fold S tiene una pantalla exterior en la tapa que Huawei llama “Live display”, situada junto a su sistema de triple cámara. Esto permite mostrar información de todo tipo como, por ejemplo, la hora mientras el PC está cerrado. Una vez abierto, el dispositivo se parece a las tabletas MatePad Pro de la compañía y funciona con un lápiz óptico, un teclado magnético o un teclado dividido en pantalla.
Viene en colores azul, blanco y negro y las reservas anticipadas en China se abrieron el pasado 14 de noviembre. Todavía no hay información sobre si llegaremos a ver este producto en España, así que tendremos que esperar para conocer más detalles al respecto.
Entre líneas. Huawei aún no ha confirmado precio ni muchas de sus especificaciones técnicas, como chip, batería o peso, aunque se espera un dispositivo de unos 600 gramos. Desde Huawei Central apuntan a HarmonyOS PC como sistema operativo en lugar de Windows o Linux. Sería un paso en la estrategia para adaptarse a las restricciones impuestas por EEUU, con chips Kirin propios y software independiente de firmas estadounidenses.
¿Y el precio? Como referencia, el MateBook Fold de 18 pulgadas se puso a la venta en China desde 24.999 yuanes (unos 3.410 euros al cambio). Incluso si el Fold S es más barato, es poco probable que sea una ganga. Tampoco lo fue el MacBook Air de primera generación con los 1.649 euros de la época.

articles.title: GTA 6 : être un furry est strictement illégal à Leonida et les chasseurs tirent à vue
articles.text:
Rockstar Games a beau avoir assagi certains réflexes historiques de sa licence comme la présence de prostituées dans GTA 6 pour servir la crédibilité de Jason et Lucia, sa plume satirique n’a rien perdu de son mordant dès qu’il s’agit de caricaturer les paniques morales américaines.
Dans sa version parodique de la Floride, les autorités locales ont ainsi trouvé leur ennemi public numéro un : les furries, ces fans d’animaux anthropomorphes dont certains se déguisent en costume intégral.
Propagande télévisée, presse locale et société secrète dans GTA 6
Rockstar décline cette interdiction dans tous les médias du jeu, de la télévision à la presse locale. En allumant la télévision dans leur planque, les joueurs peuvent tomber sur un spot publicitaire financé par une mystérieuse Anti-Furry Association. Sur le ton d’une campagne de sécurité publique paranoïaque, la vidéo sur GTA 6 rappelle que toute « activité furry » est illégale à Leonida et avertit les touristes que « la saison de chasse est ouverte ». Elle demande aux habitants de signaler tout comportement suspect, comme un « animal » qui dirait « uwu », « rawr xD » ou « hewwo ». Le dernier carton autorise même les chasseurs munis d’un permis à abattre à vue tout furry.
Sur le téléphone des héros, un article du Vice City Horn, le quotidien local, titre sans détour : « Le gouverneur déclare Leonida furry-free ». Poussant le vice jusqu’au bout, les scénaristes ont même imaginé un groupe clandestin baptisé les Furverts (contraction de furry et perverts), contraint d’opérer dans l’ombre face à la répression. La même télévision qui diffuse les spots anti-furry programme d’ailleurs un dessin animé dont la vedette est un alligator anthropomorphe, Macca the Gator.
Une traque jusque dans les rencontres aléatoires
Fidèle à sa philosophie de monde ouvert réactif héritée de Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar a également traduit cette loi absurde en mécanique de gameplay. Au détour d’une rue, un événement dynamique permet aux joueurs de croiser un individu en fursuit, un costume intégral d’animal, poursuivi par les forces de l’ordre. Libre alors à Jason ou Lucia d’ignorer la scène ou d’intervenir pour aider le fugitif à semer la police.

articles.title: Nasa-Teleskop beobachtet Sternenfusion nur 47 Tage nach der Eruption – ein Novum
articles.text:
James Webb: Nasa-Teleskop beobachtet Sternenfusion nur 47 Tage nach der Eruption – ein Novum
In Doppelsternsystemen, in denen die Wechselwirkungen zwischen den Himmelskörpern über reine Gravitationskräfte hinausgehen, kann es schon mal passieren. Der größere Partner verschluckt sozusagen seinen kleineren Begleiter.
Common Envelope: Kurze Phase bei Fusion zweier Sterne
Bei diesem Prozess kommt es zu einem Stadium, das als Common Envelope (CE) bekannt ist, auf Deutsch also so viel wie „Gemeinsame Hülle“. Dabei kreisen die Sterne in einer lose gebundenen gemeinsamen Hülle umeinander, eben der Common Envelope.
Durch den Reibungswiderstand verengt sich die Umlaufbahn des kleineren Sterns spiralförmig. Dann verleibt sich der große Partner den kleineren Partner ein.
Die CE-Phase dauert in der Regel nur kurz, ein paar Monate bis zu wenigen Jahren. In kosmischen Dimensionen also einen Wimpernschlag lang. Deswegen ist es noch nie gelungen, sie von Anfang bis Ende zu beobachten.
Forschende verfolgten erstmals vollständige CE
Dies haben Forschende nun geschafft. Sie verfolgten die vollständige CE-Phase der Fusion zweier Sterne in der Andromedagalaxie. Das Resultat ergab eine Rote Nova, die AT 2025abao getauft wurde. Ihr Spitzname lautet Bao.
Das Team um Viraj Karambelkar, Nasa Hubble Fellow an der Columbia University, hat seine Erkenntnisse in einer Studie dargestellt, die gerade in der Zeitschrift Nature erschienen ist. Die Forscher:innen griffen unter anderem auf Daten des Nasa-Weltraumteleskops James Webb zurück.
So stießen die Forschenden auf das Doppelsternsystem
„Sternverschmelzungen sind in Echtzeit sehr, sehr schwer zu beobachten, da sie kaum vorhersagbar sind“, sagte Viraj Karambelkar in einer Mitteilung der Nasa.
Im Jahr 2023 bemerkten Karambelkar und sein Team, dass am Rande der Andromedagalaxie etwas „Ungewöhnliches vor sich ging“. Das Objekt, das später Bao genannt wurde, wies untypische Merkmale für einen Roten Riesen auf. Die Forschenden bekamen den Verdacht, dass es sich um ein Doppelsystem handeln könnte.
Roter Riese und ein kleiner Begleiter
Die Auswertung der Daten von James Webb und anderen Teleskopen ergab, dass es sich bei dem größeren Stern des Systems um einen Roten Riesen handelt, der sieben Mal schwerer ist als unsere Sonne.
Das Licht des kleinen, mittlerweile verschwundenen Begleiters ging aufgrund der Strahlkraft seines größeren Partners unter. Nur durch Modellrechnungen kamen die Wissenschaftler:innen zu dem Schluss, dass seine Größe 0,7 Sonnenmassen betrug.
James Webb beobachtete Nova nur 47 Tage nach Eruption
2025 kam es dann zu einer Eruption. Innerhalb von 25 Tagen wurde AT 2025abao um ein Hundertfaches heller. Seine äußere Hülle dehnte sich mit einer Geschwindigkeit von 330 Kilometern in der Stunde aus. Laut den Forschenden resultierte dies daraus, dass der kleinere Begleiter mit dem Heliumkern des Roten Riesen kollidierte. Damit endete die Phase der Common Envelope.
James Webb durchleuchtete das Sternensystem 47 Tage danach. So früh wurde der Vorgang einer solchen Fusion noch nie beobachtet. „Die Daten des Teleskops halfen uns dabei, zu charakterisieren, wie das System vor, während und unmittelbar nach der Verschmelzung aussah, was absolut atemberaubend ist“, gab Karambelkar zu Protokoll.

articles.title: Con un tubo y botellas de plástico, un estudiante chino de 14 años crea la solución perfecta para “fabricar” agua en el desierto
articles.text:
En las zonas áridas de Mongolia Interior (norte de China) es complicado que puedan sobrevivir los nuevos árboles debido a la escasez de agua. A Jia Mingxuan no le era ajeno este problema. De ahí que quisiera desarrollar un dispositivo que ayudara a regar. Con él ha ganado una medalla de oro juvenil en la feria de inventos de Núremberg con solo 14 años.
Tiene su origen en un momento en el que su madre estaba cocinando. Vio cómo el vapor formaba gotas de agua en los azulejos. Recordó lo que había estudiado en física sobre condensación y decidió aplicarlo para extraer humedad del aire y llevarla a la raíz de los árboles. Empezó con unos tubos de acero (de una ferretería) y unas botellas de plástico (que tenía usadas).
El tubo necesitó algo más que aire
Por medio de una caperuza situada en la parte superior, se dirigía el aire al interior de un tubo enterrado. El objetivo era aprovechar la diferencia de temperatura entre la superficie y el subsuelo para que se produjera la condensación de vapor y así llegara agua a la tierra. No se necesitaba ningún tipo de entrada de agua externa.
Sin embargo, en los primeros test no funcionó como esperaba. Tras cuatro intentos fallidos, añadió un dispositivo de condensación (recargable) para ayudar a generar esa diferencia de temperatura. Jia contó que entonces consiguió que se acumulase agua en el fondo.
Jia era interno y tenía que ir a 30 kilómetros de distancia a su casa para probar los prototipos. En alguna ocasión se tuvo que levantar a las 4 de la mañana para comprobar su dispositivo antes de volver a clase.
El objetivo es ayudar en la lucha contra la desertificación (en su región es importante ayudar a que sobrevivan los nuevos árboles en el proceso de reforestación). Una vez que obtuvo el premio, comenzó a trabajar con un equipo de Shanghái para seguir mejorándolo y hacerlo útil en zonas áridas.

articles.title: Mouse fight club might explain why we like to watch violent things
articles.text:
There’s something about watching violent events that broadly appeals to us, whether it’s the latest John Wick movie, a video game, or a live UFC bout. Scientists have debated whether watching violent things could make us more aggressive, but it could also be an adaptive survival strategy. Male mice, for instance, who watched other mice fighting learned enough about how to fight to better protect themselves (compared to mice who didn’t watch fights) when pitted against stronger, more aggressive opponents, according to a paper published in the journal Nature.
The team randomly assigned male mice to three groups—fighters, spectators, or novices—and then subjected each group to eight days of training with three 10-minute sessions per day. The novices played with stuffed mice in isolation, while the spectators watched various pairs of fighter mice battle from a raised platform behind a transparent barrier—a set-up chosen to let them smell and listen to the fights as well as observe them.
The ninth day was “fight night,” when all the mice had to face a daunting opponent in three 4-minute rounds. Each fight was filmed from above so that the mouse behavior could be analyzed. To monitor corresponding changes in brain activity, the team engineered the rodents’ excitatory brain cells to glow green whenever they were activated, while inhibitory brain cells glowed red. They also implanted tiny optical fibers into 12 interconnected brain regions so they could track changing activity in every brain region simultaneously.
How did they get the mice to fight? “Mice are naturally territorial,” co-author Jorge Iravedra-Garcia of Princeton University told Ars. “A traditional behavioral assay that experimenters use is called resident intruder. You just drop mice that are bred to be slightly weaker, and a little bit more docile, into the home cage of strains we know are more on the aggressive side. Those strains are typically very good at just naturally evoking that behavior.”

articles.title: Intel 18A yields hit 70% as company signs Microsoft as EMIB customer — the first company to publicly commit to Intel's new packaging technology
articles.text:
Intel 18A yields hit 70% as company signs Microsoft as EMIB customer — the first company to publicly commit to Intel's new packaging technology
And inks long-term supply agreement with Microsoft.
Lip-Bu Tan, chief executive of Intel, said on Thursday that yields of chips made using the company's latest 18A (1.8nm-class) fabrication process have achieved 70%, which is more or less in line with what one would expect from an all-new manufacturing technology at this stage of its ramp. In addition, Intel and Microsoft have signed an agreement under which Microsoft will secure Intel Xeon supply capacity for years to come and will use Intel's EMIB advanced packaging technology for in-house silicon.
"When I took over [as CEO in March, 2025], 18A yield was horrible; now we are at 70%," Lip-Bu Tan said at the TomorrowX conference (via @firesidealpha).
Lip-Bu Tan did not specify whether he meant functional yield, parametric yield, or percentage of sellable silicon. However, it is reasonable to expect a CEO of a semiconductor company to talk about functional die yield, the percentage of dies that pass basic electrical and functional testing.
Intel began volume production of compute tiles of its Core Ultra 300-series CPUs codenamed Panther Lake using 18A in the second half of 2025, so a 70% functional yield seems decent at this stage of the product ramp, though for Intel's economics a lot depends on parametric yield and how many advanced SKUs of Core Ultra 300-series 'Panther Lake' processors Intel can supply to customers at a premium. The same applies to Intel's Xeon 6+ Clearwater Forest processors with up to 288 cores that are in high-volume production now and which use 18A-based compute chiplets along with Foveros Direct 3D stacking.
In addition to announcing an important 18A milestone, Intel also signed a long-term agreement with Microsoft, under which the latter will secure multi-year Intel Xeon supply capacity, including supply of next-generation Xeon processors codenamed Diamond Rapids, and will use Intel's EMIB advanced packaging technology for multi-chiplet data center solutions developed in-house.
The EMIB agreement is arguably the biggest news. Microsoft is the first company to publicly commit to Intel's advanced packaging technology for its own silicon (i.e., it does not mean that Microsoft is the first third party to use EMIB; it is the first party to confirm usage of EMIB), which represents a significant commercial development for Intel Foundry in terms of publicity. However, the announcement does not identify the processors involved, their manufacturing process, production volumes, or deployment schedule. Microsoft was the first company to commit to use Intel's 18A for its data center silicon in 2024, though it is unclear whether the newly announced EMIB packaging agreement relates to the same solution or not. As the majority of high-end data center solutions tend to use multi-chiplet design, it is reasonable to expect Microsoft's future solutions for data centers to use EMIB for multi-die processors.
"Through use of our advanced packaging capabilities with EMIB to scale future generations of Azure infrastructure, Intel and Microsoft can combine the flexibility of heterogeneous integration with the manufacturing scale required for the AI era — giving customers new levels of performance and economics when interacting with Azure," said Naga Chandrasekaran, EVP, Chief Technology and Operations Officer and General Manager of Intel Foundry.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The Xeon agreement provides Intel with greater visibility into future server CPU demand. Importantly, Microsoft has committed to using Intel's next-generation Xeon 'Diamond Rapids,' although the announcement does not disclose purchase volumes or financial terms.
The collaboration extends beyond processor procurement and EMIB. Specifically, Intel and Microsoft are jointly developing infrastructure capabilities that encompass processor architecture, heterogeneous integration, CXL memory expansion, QuickAssist Technology (QAT) acceleration, and Trust Domain Extensions (TDX) security.

articles.title: IDrive wants to back up your coding agents, too
articles.text:
IDrive wants to back up your coding agents, too
Coding agents need backups, too, or at least that’s what IDrive is arguing.
Backup and storage service IDrive on Thursday announced AI Agents Backup, a feature in its desktop app that finds the data these agents store locally for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Cline and copies it to the user’s IDrive account.
By default, agents tend to keep a lot of their state on a developer’s machine, including session transcripts, instruction files, and MCP server configurations. The problem is that most of this sits in hidden folders that developers rarely look at.
Thing is, some of this data is actually valuable. A session transcript, after all, is a record of how a developer and an agent got to a fix, and this local data also helps agents like Claude Code and Codex pick up from old sessions to continue a task days later. Then, there are the AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files and things like MCP configurations that involve some setup work that few developers will want to have to redo when something goes awry.
As IDrive CEO Raghu Kulkarni notes in the announcement, “Most of that data lives only on the local machine and has been left out of backup plans.” The history and configuration these agents build up, he says, is “a real work product.”
Session history is easily lost
Some of this data is also easy to lose. By default, Claude Code deletes session transcripts older than 30 days. Users have actually filed a long list of GitHub issues about history that disappeared without warning and Cursor’s forum has plenty of threads from users whose chat history disappeared after an update.
What IDrive backs up
For Claude, the new backup feature covers Claude Code history from both the terminal and the desktop app, plus settings, instruction files, and local MCP server configurations. It also picks up Cowork scheduled tasks that Team and Enterprise users chose to keep on their own machine.
The Cursor backup includes chat history, workspace data, keybindings, extensions, and the Cursor Agent CLI’s sessions. Codex and Cline get similar treatment.
It’s worth noting that IDrive skips caches and temporary files. It also doesn’t back up source code and repositories, because the company expects users to protect them with its regular file backup. Any chats that live on a provider’s servers are also out of bounds.
When a user wants to restore these files, IDrive puts them back into their original location. One thing to note is that, for Claude, IDrive’s documentation says it replaces whatever is there. Restoring also only works between machines that run the same operating system, which means a Windows setup can’t be restored to a Mac, for example.
Open source backup alternatives
This idea, of course, isn’t entirely new. Developers can already use a plethora of open source tools to sync and back up their agent’s state.
There are tools like bak, which syncs agent configurations, and commercial services like Agent Bak. Agent-archive, meanwhile, ships session transcripts to an S3 or R2 bucket and backup specialist Backblaze’s labs team has published an open source engine for backing up agent state to its B2 storage service.
IDrive’s version is built into a consumer backup app and can automatically detect the four agents on its own. It also comes with a restore flow that is meant for moving to a new computer.
AI Agents Backup is available now in the IDrive desktop app for all users, the company says. Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, and Windsurf aren’t on the supported list.

articles.title: Xiaomi 18 Pro Max : à peine sorti, ce smartphone premium avec un écran dorsal s'allège déjà de 300 € pendant le Black Friday — Frandroid
articles.text:
Jusqu’à présent, les smartphones Xiaomi Pro équipés d’un écran dorsal étaient réservés au marché chinois. Mais le 17 novembre dernier, la marque a commercialisé pour la première fois en France des modèles dotés de cette particularité, les Xiaomi 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max. À l’approche du Black Friday, c’est le modèle Pro Max, lequel a obtenu la note de 9/10 lors de notre test, qui nous intéresse davantage. Et pour cause : son prix n’est plus aussi élevé grâce à une remise de 300 euros.
Les points forts du Xiaomi 18 Pro Max
- Un petit écran Amoled LTPO au dos
- Une puissante puce Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6
- Une excellente autonomie
Initialement affiché à 1 803 euros, le Xiaomi 18 Pro Max (12 + 512 Go) peut aujourd’hui vous revenir à 1 503 euros sur Amazon grâce à un coupon valable jusqu’au 30 novembre 2026, à minuit. Sans le coupon, le smartphone est proposé à 1 603 euros.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant le Xiaomi 18 Pro Max. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Le Black Friday est lancé sur l’univers Apple. Sur Back Market, profitez de promotions sur les iPhone, MacBook, iPad, AirPods et Apple Watch. Chaque appareil est soumis à jusqu’à 100 points de contrôle qualité et est livré avec une garantie de 12 mois. De quoi profiter de performances comparables à celles d’un produit neuf.
Deux écrans pour le prix d’un
Le Xiaomi 18 Pro Max est un smartphone haut de gamme arborant un châssis en alliage d’aluminium aux bords arrondis, dont la prise en main est très agréable. Sur sa tranche, on trouve un bouton IA dédié, qui ne peut malheureusement pas être utilisé pour lancer une application, une autre fonction ou un autre chatbot. Ce modèle est par ailleurs bien robuste : il est certifié IP68 et sa face avant est protégée par un verre Xiaomi Shield Glass 3.0. Sachez que ce 18 Pro Max est aussi assez massif : il pèse 229 g et mesure 8,4 mm d’épaisseur.
Un format volumineux qui s’explique, entre autres, par la présence d’un mini-écran dorsal, qui est évidemment l’un de ses plus gros atouts. Il s’agit ici d’une petite dalle AMOLED et tactile de 2,9 pouces, qui supporte une fréquence de 120 Hz et exploite la technologie LTPO pour économiser la batterie. Ce petit écran affiche les notifications, la musique ou encore une livraison en cours. Mais on préfère clairement l’utiliser comme viseur pour prendre des selfies avec le capteur photo dorsal. Testé et approuvé ! Les vlogueurs apprécieront de leur côté de pouvoir utiliser cet écran dorsal comme retour vidéo pour se filmer jusqu’en 8K à 30 ips en Dolby Vision.
À l’avant, c’est un grand écran Amoled de 6,9 pouces, LTPO lui aussi, qui se dévoile. Il est entouré de bordures très fines de 0,99 mm et affiche une définition QHD (2 624 x 1 208 pixels). Il s’avère aussi lumineux : il peut monter jusqu’à 3 300 nits d’après nos relevés. L’écran principal embarque en prime un filtre de confidentialité, comme le Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, mais son efficacité reste malheureusement limitée.
Une autonomie ultra-rassurante
Le Xiaomi 18 Pro Max tourne sous HyperOS 4, une surcouche qui complète avantageusement Android 17. Les outils IA sont nombreux, même si peu originaux. Et bonne nouvelle, le fabricant garantit des mises à jour du système d’exploitation pendant 5 ans (donc jusqu’à Android 22) et jusqu’à 6 ans pour les patchs de sécurité. Certes, Samsung et Google font mieux sur ce point, mais cela reste largement rassurant. Côté performances, le 18 Pro Max embarque la dernière puce Qualcomm haut de gamme, la Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, gravée en 2 nm. Un SoC très puissant, mais qui voit rapidement ses performances bridées pour limiter la montée en température.
Concernant la partie photo, le Xiaomi 18 Pro Max intègre un capteur grand-angle de 200 Mpx, un téléobjectif 3,2x de 200 Mpx et un ultra grand-angle de 50 Mpx. L’efficacité des deux premiers est indéniable. L’ultra grand-angle est aussi convaincant, sauf de nuit. Mention spéciale également pour les capacités vidéo de ce smartphone, qui propose notamment un mode 4K à 120 ips et du Dolby Vision. Enfin, le Xiaomi 18 Pro Max renferme une batterie lithium-ion Si/C de 7 050 mAh ; la version chinoise, elle, grimpe à 8 500 mAh. Mais rassurez-vous, le 18 Pro Max vendu en France fait de l’ombre à beaucoup de concurrents, puisqu’il peut fonctionner deux jours, voire plus, avant de devoir être rechargé. D’ailleurs, le plein se fait ici rapidement, puisque le port USB-C accepte un adaptateur secteur (compatible PPS) d’une puissance maximale de 100 W. La charge sans fil 50 W et la charge inversée sont aussi au programme.
Pour en savoir encore plus, n’hésitez pas à lire notre test complet du Xiaomi 18 Pro Max.

articles.title: Una herramienta de Microsoft escondía malware capaz de robar claves de GitHub y Azure
articles.text:
Una herramienta oficial de Microsoft para Python fue modificada para robar datos de las personas que la instalaran. El problema afectó a las versiones 1.26.1 y 1.26.2 de agent-framework, un programa que ayuda a crear asistentes de inteligencia artificial. Ambas versiones se publicaron en PyPI, un sitio donde los programadores descargan herramientas para sus proyectos.
El malware podía buscar contraseñas, archivos de acceso y otros datos guardados en la computadora. También apuntaba a cuentas y servicios usados por desarrolladores, como GitHub y Azure. GitHub permite guardar y compartir código; Azure es una plataforma de Microsoft para alojar programas y manejar servicios en internet. The Register informó que investigadores de seguridad descubrieron el problema y que Microsoft puso algunos repositorios en privado mientras investigaba.
No hacía falta abrir la herramienta para que actuara
Según los investigadores citados por The Register, el malware podía empezar a funcionar cuando se iniciaba Python en una computadora que tuviera instalada una de las versiones afectadas. Python es el lenguaje con el que se escriben ciertos programas. Por eso, el usuario no necesitaba abrir agent-framework ni pedirle que hiciera algo: bastaba con tener la versión peligrosa instalada en ese entorno.
Mientras buscaba información, el paquete también cargaba una versión legítima de la herramienta de Microsoft. Eso podía hacer que siguiera funcionando con normalidad y que el usuario no notara que algo ocurría en segundo plano.
El malware no solo revisaba los datos que ya estaban guardados. También pedía nuevos códigos de acceso a servicios como GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps y Azure. Esos códigos, llamados tokens, permiten que una persona o un programa demuestre que tiene permiso para entrar a una cuenta. Algunos duran poco tiempo, pero los investigadores señalaron que aun así pueden ser útiles para un atacante si los obtiene enseguida.
El riesgo era mayor para quienes usan estas herramientas en su trabajo: una contraseña o un código robado podría abrir el acceso a proyectos de programación o a servicios de una empresa. OX Security, una de las firmas que investigó el caso, indicó que el paquete tenía cerca de 200.000 descargas mensuales. Esa cifra no permite saber cuántas personas instalaron las versiones afectadas.
Cómo llegaron las versiones peligrosas a PyPI
Los investigadores sospechan que alguien obtuvo acceso a una cuenta con permiso para publicar el paquete. La empresa OX Security reportó que la versión 1.26.1 fue reemplazada por una versión segura, pero después apareció la 1.26.2 en PyPI, publicada desde la cuenta oficial asociada al proyecto de Microsoft. Esto hizo pensar que el acceso no autorizado podría no haberse cerrado de inmediato.
Microsoft dijo a The Register que puso algunos repositorios en privado mientras revisaba el contenido y que estaba tomando medidas para proteger a sus clientes y a otros usuarios. El repositorio de agent-framework también dejó de estar disponible durante la investigación.
De acuerdo con los reportes citados por el medio, el malware no instalaba un programa permanente que siguiera activo para siempre. Su actividad dependía de que los archivos de la versión peligrosa continuaran en la computadora. Sin embargo, borrar el paquete no garantiza que las contraseñas o los códigos de acceso robados ya no puedan usarse.
Qué hacer si se instaló una versión afectada
Quienes hayan instalado agent-framework 1.26.1 o 1.26.2 deben considerar que las contraseñas y los códigos disponibles en ese entorno pudieron quedar expuestos. Se recomienda eliminar la versión afectada, crear de nuevo el entorno de trabajo con archivos verificados y cambiar las claves que se usaban allí.
También es importante cerrar o revocar los códigos de acceso que sigan activos y revisar el historial de actividad de GitHub, Azure y otros servicios conectados. Si aparecen accesos o cambios que nadie reconoce, podrían ser una señal de que alguien más entró a esas cuentas.
El caso muestra que incluso una herramienta publicada desde una cuenta oficial puede verse comprometida. Por eso, cuando se descubre una versión peligrosa, no basta con esperar a que deje de estar disponible: quienes la instalaron deben revisar sus cuentas y renovar los accesos que pudieron quedar en riesgo.

articles.title: NAND flash prices fell 20% in the last two weeks, and are predicted to fall further in 2027
articles.text:
Forward-looking: NAND flash spot prices fell by around 20% over the past two weeks and could decline by a further 5% by Q2 2027 amid "a reversal in supply-demand dynamics." Contract prices were previously expected to decline in Q3 2027, but TrendForce, a market intelligence and research firm, now believes the decline could begin as early as Q2 2027. The revised outlook is driven by slowing enterprise demand in China and weakness in the global consumer electronics market.
While NAND flash prices have risen rapidly over the past year, 2027 could finally bring some relief to customers. According to TrendForce, the anticipated price correction could be attributed to two main factors: a large-scale reduction in enterprise SSD orders from Chinese cloud service providers and a marked downturn in the consumer electronics market.
The report notes that demand for enterprise SSDs from AI data centers and cloud service providers in North America will remain robust through 2027, despite the changing political landscape in the US. However, steady demand in North America will be offset by a pullback among Chinese technology companies due to GPU shortages, elevated inventories, and slower-than-expected AI monetization.
Adding to the slowdown in China, NAND flash manufacturers are also grappling with sluggish consumer demand worldwide, as steep prices have prompted many retail buyers to postpone their upgrade plans. Negative consumer sentiment and softening enterprise demand have created challenging market conditions for hardware manufacturers, resulting in oversupply and a likely price correction.
Curiously, most suppliers appear to be continuing their investments in new process nodes and increasing their use of QLC technology despite the gloomy market outlook. One of the few major exceptions is Yangtze Memory Technologies Co. (YMTC), the world's third-largest NAND flash supplier by bit shipments, which has "slightly trimmed" its expansion plans in response to changing market conditions.
The predicted price correction also appears to have already begun, with NAND spot prices reportedly declining by an average of 20% in just two weeks amid weak consumer demand. According to a Bank of America study cited by Seoul Economic Daily, prices for 512Gb wafers fell by as much as 32% quarter over quarter (QoQ) to $14.30, while 1Tb products declined by 19% to $24.90.
TrendForce states that the extent and pace of the correction in NAND flash contract prices will depend on how quickly Chinese cloud service providers can reduce their inventories and how long OEMs continue producing laptops, smartphones, and other consumer electronics with downgraded hardware specifications.
The report also notes that the speed of approvals for new data centers in the US will influence the NAND flash market outlook. However, with bipartisan opposition to data center development growing across the country, it remains unclear whether all proposed projects will receive approval from local, state, and federal authorities.

articles.title: Exclusive: Fig Security partners with Elastic to show how data changes affect detection coverage - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: Fig Security partners with Elastic to show how data changes affect detection coverage
Security operations startup Fig Security Inc. today announced an integration partnership with Elastic N.V. that it says gives security teams visibility into how data changes affect their detection coverage.
The partnership sees Fig’s capabilities for mapping detection dependencies now integrating with Elastic Security, the open security operations platform from Elastic. The platform offers prebuilt integrations and detection rules to establish coverage from day one, with Fig claimed to help security operations engineers safeguard that coverage as their environments evolve.
Detection rules are dependent on data arriving in the structure they expect, including the fields and values needed to identify suspicious activity. According to Fig, those dependencies can break when changes are made in tools that the security team does not own. The resulting problem, which Fig calls drift, leaves rules active while the data feeding them is missing the information needed to catch an attack.
Once connected through a read-only application programming interface key, Fig’s Security Data Lineage feature maps an Elastic environment’s sources through pipelines, mappings and fields to the detection rules that use them. Any change to a source, pipeline or mapping is said to have Fig identify the affected detections, along with a suggested repair.
“Elastic gives security teams control over their data, and Fig gives them control over the engineering around it,” said Gal Shafir, co-founder and chief executive of Fig, who previously led global security architecture for Google Cloud Security. Teams are able to test each change against their own environment, he said, before shipping it as code.
Environments “never stop changing,” according to Jamie Hynds, director of product at Elastic, who said Fig traces those changes to the detection rules that depend on them so that SecOps teams can maintain their coverage.
Fig also works alongside Elastic’s Automatic Import and AI Agent, two features designed to help teams build new integrations and custom rules as their requirements grow. Changes tested in Fig against the organization’s own data can then be shipped as code using continuous integration and continuous delivery, with version control and one-click rollback included.
The integration is also aimed at organizations moving to Elastic Security from another security information and event management platform. After Elastic’s Automatic Migration has translated their existing detection rules, Fig checks each translated rule against the data available in Elastic ahead of cutover. Rules that need rework are flagged, with a recommended fix for each.
Founded in 2025 by Shafir, Nir Loya Dahan and Roy Haimof, Fig launched in March with $38 million in seed and Series A funding from Team8 and Ten Eleven Ventures. The company added an AI agent and software-style deployment tools to its platform in July.
The Fig and Elastic integration is available now, with demonstrations offered through Fig’s website.
