articles.title: Nvidia's latest drivers may be wearing out your SSD with tens of gigabytes of unnecessary writes
articles.text:
TL;DR: Users who have recently updated their Nvidia display drivers should check the Resource Monitor's Disk tab to see whether an executable called NVDisplay.Container.exe is writing excessively to the disk. Nvidia had not acknowledged the issue at the time of writing, but reports claim that it now writes tens of gigabytes per day, which might shorten an SSD's lifespan. Until Nvidia provides a fix, rolling back to driver version 621.01 is the only foolproof remedy.
TroubleGrid recently published a summary of the issue, which impacts driver versions 621.14 and 621.24, both released in November. Besides rolling back drivers, users can restart the affected service or change the display container settings, but neither solution is perfect.
The problem occurs because the display container service now rewrites its log instead of appending to it, exponentially increasing the amount of data written to the SSD. Users can confirm whether they are experiencing the issue by opening the Resource Monitor app, clicking the Disk tab, and searching for a process called "NVDisplay.Container.exe" to see how much data it is writing in bytes.
While some users report the figure holding steady at around 20 MB, others report it writing dozens of gigabytes each day, even while idle. SSDs start breaking down after writing a certain amount of data, usually measured in hundreds of terabytes, so it's best to monitor how much each program writes.
The simplest countermeasure is to stop the service, delete the log, and restart it. To do this, press Windows + R, type "services.msc," press Enter, find "NVIDIA Display Container LS," and select Stop from the right-click menu. Then, delete the file at "C:\ProgramData\NVIDIA Corporation\nvtopps\nct\nvlog.nvlgstg," return to the display container service, and click Start. While this might reduce data usage by up to 91%, the solution is only temporary, as the file will grow back.
A more permanent but still problematic solution is to set the service to manual. Find it in services.msc again, double-click it, change "Startup type" from Automatic to Manual, click Stop, and click OK. Unfortunately, this prevents the Nvidia Control Panel and Nvidia App from working properly, so users should only try this if they don't need to change resolution or graphics settings via those menus.
Finally, as the issue has not been reported in driver version 621.01, users can safely revert to it. It is available via the Nvidia app, on the company's website, or on third-party sites like TechSpot.
AMD recently fixed a similar problem that caused the External Events Utility service to create a process that could write more than 400GB per day. To resolve the issue, install AMD Radeon Adrenalin hotfix version 26.11.1.

articles.title: Nigeria gives crypto firms November 30 tax deadline
articles.text:
Nigeria’s tax authority has given cryptocurrency exchanges and other virtual asset service providers until November 30, 2026, to register on a new portal, adding a compliance deadline to an industry facing tighter regulatory oversight.
In a public notice seen by TechCabal, the Nigerian Revenue Service (NRS) said providers operating in Nigeria serving Nigerian residents must submit registration forms through its newly deployed VASP Tax Portal by that date. They must then integrate their systems with the portal by December 31, 2026, to complete the process.
The move is the latest effort by Nigeria’s tax authority to bring the crypto industry further into the tax net, giving the sector a formal registration and reporting framework as the government tightens oversight of virtual asset transactions. New virtual asset tax guidelines released in August impose a 1.5% stamp duty on token-to-fiat and fiat-to-token transfers.
The new rules apply to Nigerian and foreign businesses providing virtual asset services in Nigeria or to people resident in the country, regardless of their physical presence in Nigeria. It covers crypto exchanges, peer-to-peer platforms, brokers, custodial wallet providers, payment and remittance companies, and businesses involved in the transfer, exchange or safekeeping of digital assets.
Missing either deadline could attract statutory penalties and other enforcement measures, the NRS said in response to questions from TechCabal.
The NRS said the requirement applies regardless of a provider’s business name or regulatory status. Individuals using virtual assets for personal purposes are excluded, as are businesses that simply accept cryptocurrency as payment for their own goods and services. Their existing tax obligations remain unchanged.
The registration requirement follows provisions in the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025, and the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025. The NRS said Section 79 of the administration law and its Fifth Schedule subject persons engaged in virtual asset activities to tax obligations covering registration, record-keeping, reporting, filing, and payment.
It said it deployed the portal under Section 71 of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, which provides for the use of technology to automate tax administration. It will also facilitate registration for anti-money laundering, counter-terrorist financing and counter-proliferation financing (AML/CFT/CPF), in line with the Financial Action Task Force’s Recommendation 15.
Two steps to registration
The NRS has split registration into two stages. First, crypto providers must submit their business details, Tax Identification Number, contact information, virtual asset activities, and relevant AML/CFT/CPF registration information by November 30.
The second stage requires providers to integrate their systems with the portal. The NRS said detailed reporting requirements and application programming interface (API) specifications would be provided during the technical integration process.
The integration is intended to support transaction reporting, tax assessment, and the remittance of taxes collected in tokens. The NRS said a provider would only be considered registered after completing both the registration form and the integration process.
“A VASP is deemed registered only after completing both steps,” the tax authority said.
The portal will also support the administration of existing tax obligations, including Value Added Tax (VAT), Stamp Duty and Withholding Tax (WHT) payable in tokens. These functions will be introduced in phases, while taxes payable in fiat currency will continue to be administered through the NRS’s existing Rev360 platform and other channels.
The NRS said the portal does not introduce new taxes or create additional tax obligations. Providers remain responsible for taxes on their own taxable activities and, where applicable, for collecting or withholding taxes on customer transactions.
“The VASP Tax Portal introduces no new taxes,” it said, adding that existing Nigerian tax laws would continue to apply.
Not a crypto operating licence
The NRS clarified that registration on its portal does not authorise a business to provide virtual asset services.
The process is separate from licencing and approval requirements administered by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and other relevant regulators. Providers may register with the NRS while awaiting regulatory approval, but must still obtain any licence required for their activities.
The service said the relevant authorities would continue to supervise and enforce AML/CFT/CPF obligations. It added that it could share information collected through the portal with regulators and law enforcement agencies when the law permits.
It added that information collected, processed, or stored through the platform would be subject to applicable data protection laws and the NRS Data Protection Policy, including confidentiality and information security controls.

articles.title: NetWasm 0.10 Speeds Up C# on WebAssembly, Now Faster Than Mono AOT
articles.text:
The team behind NetWasm has published a write-up of its 0.10 optimisation work, spanning releases 0.10.1 to 0.10.8. The changes touch exception handling, array bounds checks, WebAssembly SIMD and integer division. On the project’s own benchmark set, NetWasm now comes out ahead of Mono AOT and gets close to desktop .NET on some workloads.
NetWasm is a compiler and runtime that compiles C# programs ahead of time into small, standalone WebAssembly files. It takes the IL that Roslyn produces and emits Wasm, using its own runtime and a CoreLib ported from .NET. The yardstick is the Mono AOT build for WASI, which runs .NET on the same engine. A new garbage collector had already put NetWasm in front on allocation-heavy code, but plain loops were still slower: a quicksort of 100,000 integers took 77.2 ms, against 58.0 ms for Mono AOT.
Much of the early gain came from exception handling in 0.10.1. Wasmtime adds extra register save-and-restore code around any function that can throw or catch, floating-point registers included. Methods with null, bounds or checked-arithmetic checks paid that price on every call. Throws now go through a shared function and the catching handler releases the frames, which cut UI churn from 17.6 to 7.9 ms.
Version 0.10.2 inlines small straight-line methods in loops, tuple swaps included, and skips checks already performed on the same array and index. The quicksort fell to 54.0 ms. DoomSharp, a C# software renderer for Doom that ships a NetWasm build, served as a second test case. Value-type accessors now compile to plain field loads, and at O3 small branching helpers are inlined inside loops. Together these brought a 120-frame render from 3,595 down to 1,934 ms.
SIMD arrived in 0.10.7. Vector128, Vector<T> and PackedSimd lower to 128-bit Wasm instructions, and element-wise array loops handle four or more elements per iteration, with a scalar fallback. Hoisting loop-invariant Math calls allowed a solver for Burgers’ equation, a fundamental partial differential equation from fluid mechanics, to vectorise: its first test dropped from 497 ms to 71 ms, against 186 ms for Mono AOT and 93 ms for desktop .NET.
Version 0.10.8 targets division and range-checked arithmetic. A remainder that follows a division now reuses the quotient and skips repeated zero-divisor and int.MinValue / -1 checks. A trial-division test fell from 1,376 to 765 ms, while Mono AOT needed 862 ms.
Across the 2,213 cases, 0.10.8 at O3 with NetWasmGC takes 0.41 times Mono AOT’s time as a geometric mean, excluding five cases where Mono’s LLVM removes the work. Against desktop .NET 11 RC3 JIT the ratio is 0.87, down from 2.15 for 0.10.6. By family, the ratio to Mono AOT runs from 0.34 for intrinsics to 0.81 for math. The 120-frame DoomSharp render takes 1,623 ms on NetWasmGC, compared with 2,371 ms for Mono AOT and 1,053 ms for desktop .NET JIT.
Those figures come from Wasmtime 49.0.3 on an Apple M1 Max, using cases from dotnet/performance plus five NetWasm workloads. The authors also found that identical loops at different addresses could differ by up to 15 per cent, so their A/B tests align every function to 4 KiB.
The article is open about what is left. Desktop .NET is about 3.1 times faster on vector benchmarks, because it can use host SIMD directly while Wasm is limited to fixed 128-bit operations. Math.Pow is 1.4 times slower than on Mono AOT, and CopyBlock64 is 3.3 times slower. One workload, NewtR, regressed to 1.9 times slower than in 0.10.6, which the authors blame on Wasmtime’s register allocator keeping a value in a stack slot around the loop.
Since the numbers are self-reported and come from one machine and one runtime, results elsewhere may differ. NetWasm can be tried in the online playground, and local setup is covered in the compile and publish guide. Developers can find the documentation is in the official GitHub repository.

articles.title: Nimble enters the item-tracking market with eco-friendly luggage tags and keychains | TechCrunch
articles.text:
As Google steps up its competition with Apple in the item-tracking market, smaller brands are also looking to carve out a piece of the category. The latest entrant is Nimble, the sustainable accessories brand best known for its charging products.
Founded in 2018 by former Mophie executives, the California-based company announced Thursday that it’s expanding into the category with “Trace,” a seven-product collection of item trackers designed to blend tracking technology into everyday accessories.
Nimble’s new collection arrives as competition in the Bluetooth tracking market continues to heat up. Apple’s AirTag helped popularize the category, while Google recently introduced its first-party tracker, the $29 Pixel Tag, powered by its Find Hub network. Meanwhile, established third-party players, such as Chipolo and Pebblebee, continue to expand their lineups.
Nimble is taking a slightly different approach. Rather than introducing another stand-alone tracker to attach to a set of keys or slip into a bag, the company has integrated tracking technology directly into practical accessories, including wallets, keychains, luggage tags, and passport covers.
The lineup includes seven products, ranging from the $14.95 Trace Tag, which features a replaceable coin-cell battery, to the $49.95 Trace Folio, a passport cover with built-in rechargeable tracking. Other options include the Trace Keyfob ($19.95), Trace Slim Wallet Card ($29.95), Trace Keychain ($29.95), Trace Luggage Tag ($39.95), and Trace Wallet ($39.95).
The entire collection is compatible with both Apple’s Find My and Google’s Find Hub networks.
Ross Howe, co-founder and CEO of Nimble, told us that the company’s approach is designed to differentiate its products from traditional trackers.
“Most locators are built as utility gadgets, not as things you want to own. Few were asking why the locator couldn’t just be the nice object itself. So, for example, we made a wallet findable instead of making a tracker that fits a wallet. We also thought more options should be rechargeable.”
The Trace Luggage Tag and Trace Folio are arguably the most interesting products in the collection. Dedicated luggage tags and passport covers with built-in tracking remain relatively uncommon, giving Nimble an opportunity to stand out in a market. There are only a few alternatives, including Spotminder’s $59 passport cover with Apple Find My support, which is $10 more than Nimble’s option. Knog Scout offers a luggage tag, although I find its design a little too bulky.
Rechargeability is another appealing aspect of Nimble’s new collection. Several models support USB-C or wireless charging, offering an alternative to the disposable batteries found in many traditional trackers. Howe says battery life lasts for “months,” with the Trace Keyfob, for example, rated for approximately six months on a charge.
Sustainability is another major part of Nimble’s pitch. Staying true to its roots, the company has incorporated eco-friendly materials throughout the collection, including recycled plastics and plant-based, vegan aloe leather. The products have also undergone third-party testing for chemicals of concern.
“We’ve spent the last two years going through the chemistry of our products line by line to remove or limit as many harmful ingredients as possible. Trace is the first collection designed specifically to meet these higher standards. We’re not 100% yet, but the independent labs checking our work will help us get there,” Howe said.
The collection is available now through its website and Amazon. All seven products come in five color options: Black, Stone, Tangerine, Plum, and Teal.

articles.title: AI Accelerators Drive Changes In Power Delivery Networks
articles.text:
Moving voltage regulators closer to processors can reduce power loss, but adds challenges for advanced packaging, thermal management, and system-level design.
Key Takeaways:
Power delivery is now a significant performance limiter in data center chips. The demands of AI and high-performance computing chips running near 0.7 V for a 600W GPU are forcing current to rise to 1,000 amps and beyond, compounding resistive losses and voltage droop across the PDN. Multi-chiplet constructions only compound these issues by further increasing current density and signal congestion.
To solve these challenges, designers are turning to vertical power delivery networks, where the voltage regulator modules are relocated much closer to the processors from their position on the device periphery — to the PCB landside (under the PCB), inside the accelerator package, or inside the silicon interposer. Together with the growing customization of AI accelerator modules, there are many approaches on offer with varying design and manufacturing complexity.
The vertical PDN trend began nearly a decade ago with the integration of backside power delivery networks (BPDNs) on the wafer backside, enabling fine-tuned power delivery more directly to the transistors while reducing IR drop across the tens of interconnect levels on-chip. That approach is being extended with increasingly sophisticated on-die decoupling capacitors (DCaps) formed in deep trenches as part of the BPDN. While this addresses high-frequency decoupling at the chip level, recent changes inside packages, interposers, substrates, and across data center racks are becoming just as important.
Add to that recent developments in the design of compact passive devices, like high-performance inductors, and new architectural solutions become possible, moving the VRMs and DC-DC converters into the interposer or package.
But these architectural changes are neither straightforward nor simple because they involve system co-design of the PDN, interposer, power management ICs (PMICs), integrated voltage regulators (IVRs), DC-DC converters, capacitors, and other passive devices, alongside custom HPC, memory devices, and interconnects that perform today’s elaborate AI tasks.
“In the most advanced semiconductors, people are moving from discrete PMICs to distributed IVRs. Those IVRs are great because they are placed much closer to the chip, which reduces the IR drop to the chip’s own power delivery network, so it is way more efficient. In addition, closed and fast control loops between the chip power management unit to the IVR reduce the reaction time to voltage droop events from milliseconds to microseconds. Because this reaction is so fast you can tune voltage very accurately, with a high degree of granularity even on different areas of a chip,” said Nir Sever, senior director of business development at proteanTecs.
Reconfiguring the PDN is part of a much larger drive to improve energy use. “Energy efficiency becomes the most important performance index for AI-infused platforms moving forward,” said Lipen Yuan, senior director of TSMC’s Advanced Technology Business Development, during a 2024 IEDM short course.
Power delivery challenges are most important at points of load. “AI systems are placing unprecedented demands on board-to-chip power delivery, making the final stage of voltage regulation increasingly important,” said CP Hung, vice president of corporate R&D at ASE.
Fig. 1: By regulating voltage at the point of load, OSATs enable fine-tuned voltage control. Source: ASE
“The move to multi-die architectures is bringing power integrity to the forefront, alongside thermal, stress, and warpage challenges. But the underlying power-delivery problem already existed in advanced single-die designs,” said Sojan Philips, principal product manager of Redhawk-SC at Synopsys. “AI accelerators are now operating at currents approaching the kiloampere range, where even milliohm-level resistance in the power-delivery network can result in significant IR drop. That loss of voltage margin can directly affect performance and power targets, particularly maximum operating frequency and Vmin.”
Several developments illustrate these trends:
As a result, OSATs are playing an increasing role in system co-design, electrical validation, and power integrity (PI) simulation. “The OSAT sits where die, substrate or interposer, passives, and board meet, so we are brought in earlier to model the package-level PDN and co-simulate it with the customer’s die power data,” said Alex Kizeev, technical director of signal and power integrity at Amkor’s design optimization team.
Kizeev breaks down the supply chain and responsibilities among different companies. “The best results come from a PDN budget partitioned across the die, package, and board. The foundry and fabless teams own the on-die PDN, including the die power map and the bump-map allocation. The substrate supplier defines what stackup and via/plane technology is possible. The OSAT optimizes the package-level pieces, including stackup choice, via and ball assignment, DCap selection and placement, warpage and reliability, and validation.”
“Backside power delivery can significantly improve power delivery by reducing IR drop and freeing up frontside routing resources for signals, but it doesn’t eliminate power-integrity challenges,” said Philips. “It also changes the thermal landscape. As power delivery and other structures move to the backside, the paths available for heat removal become more complex. This makes co-optimization of power integrity and thermal management increasingly important.
The overall trend is moving toward closer integration in advanced packages and dies, including the integration of inductors, capacitors, and power-conversion components into substrates and interposers.
Why power losses scale with increasing power
A simple illustration shows how the power efficiency drops as the industry scales from a 1kW GPU to a 5kW GPU (see figure 2). While losses from the voltage regulator itself stay constant at around 13%, resistive losses jump from 8% to 31%, and voltage droop rises from 17% to 31%. As a result, increasing power levels must be supplied to meet all the chip-level needs.
Fig. 2: At higher power levels, the PDN efficiency using motherboard voltage regulators degrades significantly due to VR losses, resistive losses, and droop. Source: Intel Foundry
With this lateral power delivery approach, power integrity (PI) becomes increasingly difficult to maintain as compute loads rise. As AI accelerators integrate increasing levels of compute, HBM, and interconnects between devices, the low supply voltage (0.7-0.9V) of devices means multiple kiloamp levels of current are needed to meet the high-power needs of modern GPUs. As if managing kiloamp currents is not enough, fast workload transients tend to magnify voltage droop, so designers apply voltage guardbands that further increase power consumption and reduce system efficiency. [1]
Next-gen data centers pull in 800V
For next-generation data centers built to meet AI demands, 800V DC power delivery is starting to replace traditional AC power distribution. The 800V DC power distribution coexists with multiple distributed regulators located much closer to individual loads.
To lower transmission losses from the grid to the microprocessor, next-generation PDNs begin at 800V DC and are stepped down in stages using DC-to-DC converters to 48V, 12V, and then 0.7V, for instance. One of the most critical junctures occurs at the point of load, where integrated voltage regulators supply the AI multi-chiplet package. By limiting the number of power conversions, system-level efficiency can improve while reducing thermal cooling requirements.
The voltage regulator module can be positioned underneath the PCB, a logical first step that is commonly referred to as vertical power delivery. However, chipmakers are embracing recent developments that shrink the size of various voltage regulator components, especially capacitors and inductors, to move voltage regulation inside the main processor package and below the SoC, called integrated power delivery. Finally, integrating voltage regulator components into the interposer itself is called fully integrated power delivery.
One step at a time
The approach companies take to voltage regulation integration depends on the company’s expertise, its partners, and the complexity of the system involved.
For this reason, companies are introducing suites of solutions. For example, ASE is offering a range of power delivery capabilities to enable PCB backside integration, which considers the limited space inside computer trays. [2] The company’s PowerSiP options can include double-sided connected capacitors sandwiched between coreless substrates; substrateless designs, solder-free cap array modules with exposed terminals for embedded substrate or PCB solutions; high-aspect-ratio 4:1 copper pin integration for lower packaging impedance; and high-density active and passive component integration using single- or double-sided molding.
“Power efficiency is becoming a defining challenge for next-generation AI systems,” said Harrison Chang, vice president of corporate R&D at ASE. “By shortening the high-current transmission path, our solution can reduce parasitic routing losses by 50% or more, translating directly into meaningful power savings at the system level,” he said in the release.
In June 2025, Marvell introduced its Package Integrated Voltage Regulator (PIVR) technology for AI and HPC. The PIVR replaces the conventional arrangement of discrete voltage-regulator components, often several inches away on the PCB, with compact silicon power converters and passive components tightly coupled to the processor. It’s designed to reduce the amount of low-voltage, high-current routing between the regulator and the processor. The PIVR can sit on the underside of the processor package, shortening the path from voltage conversion to the processor’s power connections. It also can sit next to the processor’s package or inside the advanced package.
Marvell is partnering with multiple companies on integration, including Infineon, which makes power semiconductors and packaged devices; Ferric, which specializes in designing integrated voltage regulators using thin-film magnetic inductors; Monolithic Power Systems, a developer of high-current-density power modules; and Empower Semiconductor, a developer of compact integrated power converters.
In July of this year, Analog Devices completed the acquisition of Empower Semiconductor, expanding ADI’s AI compute power delivery capabilities with integrated voltage regulators and silicon capacitors. “By enabling power conversion closer to the processor, the combined solution shortens the power delivery path and improves efficiency to support higher-performance, higher-density systems. Building on its leadership in high-performance power management, ADI is investing in its system-level platform to deliver a step-change in performance, density, and efficiency from grid to core.” [3]
In addition, on Nov. 2, onsemi announced it will acquire the assets of Ferric, which develops integrated voltage regulators, for up to $775 million. [4]
To understand these important acquisitions, it helps to take a closer look at IVRs.
What is an IVR?
An integrated voltage regulator is typically a 3D stack arrangement that replaces off-chip voltage regulator modules and bulky capacitors and inductors on the PCB with integrated magnetics and passives mounted onto the silicon or package using thin-film technology.
“The IVR is implemented as a 3D stack, bringing together the deep-trench capacitor, PMIC, and inductor, and embedding them directly into the substrate or interposer,” said Veshal Sridhar, product engineering architect, 3D IC at Synopsys. “Companies are moving it closer to the SOC for obvious reasons such as reduced signal parasitics between IVR and SOC die, but that introduces new thermal effects and stress effects because you’re bringing another 3D stack in and embedding it inside an interposer. There’s also potential noise coupling into the other dies from the IVR, because even for a simple 3D stack you are going to have noise coupling.”
In what Intel Foundry refers to as a Super High Density MIM (metal-insulator-metal), capacitance density can be improved by 10× compared to conventional MIM capacitors. [5] This may offer response times on the order of nanoseconds. As part of Intel’s collaboration with UMC for 12nm finFETs, the capacitors feature three metal layers for routing in a scalable design. “This broad adaptability highlights the HDMIM as a universal, highly scalable passive component, capable of heterogeneous integration with logic and power chips manufactured across diverse process nodes from various foundries.” [5]
Inductors have traditionally been one of the greatest passive bottlenecks due to their large footprint, but by integrating them into the package using copper-plated through-hole technology and advanced magnetic materials (see Figure 3), Intel is touting a high resistance-to-capacitance ratio while minimizing stray magnetic fields that could adversely affect surrounding circuits. [5]
Fig. 3: This in-package inductor uses copper-plated through holes embedded with high-permeability magnetics to improve the resistance-to-capacitance ratio and limit magnetic parasitic effects. Source: Intel Foundry
Intel’s FIVR platform uses switched-capacitor voltage regulators and hybrid buck converters to accommodate nanosecond transient spikes by computing cores without exacerbating voltage droop. FIVRs that allow a continuous switching range are superior to fixed SCVRs when it comes to delivering low-voltage inputs (e.g., 1.8 to 3V).
Finally, Intel’s low-voltage GaN MOSHEMT-on-CMOS devices are designed for >12V applications, where high density and high efficiency are essential, while minimizing the overall number of power conversions. By integrating both low voltage and high voltage MIM capacitors with active devices, it minimizes PDN impedance from VR to load. By monolithically integrating the GaN power switches with GaN nMOS drivers, the company can achieve even faster response to transients along with aggressive power density.
“Integrated voltage regulators provide unprecedented speed and granularity in voltage control, but realizing their full power-saving potential requires equally precise visibility into the silicon itself,” said proteanTecs’ Sever. “Traditional power management methods leave significant timing margin untapped. By continuously measuring timing margins across the full chip, cycle by cycle, under actual operating conditions, our embedded monitoring technology identifies where performance is truly limited and where voltage can be safely reduced. Combined with the fine-grained control of IVRs, this enables more aggressive power optimization without compromising performance or reliability.”
Can the system handle the power?
Multiphysics simulation plays an important role in power delivery planning. “A designer may have a simple stack in mind, interposer, base die, top die, and substrate. And it starts with a prototype grid and listing the power required for each die,” explained Synopsys’ Sridhar. “So there is a power budget that comes from the devices, and number of C4 bumps, number of microbumps, TSVs, etc. You want to determine whether your power delivery system can deliver the power needed from the C4 bumps through the top of the stack. Starting with a simple static IR-drop analysis, we can then leverage 3DIC Compiler together with signoff solutions like RedHawk-SC to help bridge the gap between early bump planning and PSE (power sourcing equipment) planning.”
In cases where the PDN cannot handle the power required of the system, design changes such as increasing the interposer size may come into play.
Sridhar noted how one customer brought system-level PI (power integrity) analysis into the early architecture stage, closing the loop between implementation and system analysis using 3DICC plus RHSC, turning iterations that once took days into hours and giving designers more freedom to explore before the architecture is frozen.
At the same time, the package assembly design kits that OSATs compile are becoming more detailed. “Kits are moving beyond geometric design rules to include electrical models, material properties, and validated reference designs. Teams now must consider bump pitch against current density, metal layers against cost, and DCap placement against thermal path early in the design,” said Amkor’s Kizeev.
Conclusion 
Power integrity and power efficiency have already become key differentiators in advanced AI accelerator-based data center designs. Companies are racing to incorporate leading power delivery solutions, including integrated voltage regulators, in positions closer to the GPU or AI accelerator modules where they can be most effective. Advanced power delivery began with the integration of wafer backside PDNs, but package-level and interposer-level solutions are coming fast.
Coordination among major companies in the supply chain is critical during early-stage PDN design. “Some of these design houses are not building the entire system, for instance, like HBM, where even the base die and the stack may be coming in from other design houses,” noted Synopsys’ Phillips. They want to make sure that the grid they’re designing in-house works with the other models. So they want a model exchange between these two, which is performed as part of a feasibility analysis.”

articles.title: Ojo con el autoguardado de 'GTA 6': no es tan frecuente como crees y puedes perder tu progreso
articles.text:
GTA 6 ya está definitivamente entre nosotros y tanto el público como la prensa especializada lo están amando. Lo nuevo de Rockstar Games ha logrado estar a la altura del hype, cosechando calificaciones inmejorables, pero hay un apartado que está dando algunos dolores de cabeza: el autoguardado.
La función de autoguardado de GTA 6 cumple la misma finalidad que en cualquier otro videojuego: salvar el avance que has logrado en una misión o campaña sin que tengas que hacerlo de forma manual. Sin embargo, su implementación en la más reciente entrega de la saga Grand Theft Auto tiene sus bemoles.
Se supone que GTA 6 guarda automáticamente el progreso cuando terminas una misión principal o ciertas tareas secundarias. Pero han aparecido reportes de jugadores aseverando que el sistema no se ha disparado de forma consistente siguiendo esos parámetros. ¿Esto qué significa? Que tal vez al finalizar una misión sí se ha guardado el avance de forma automática, pero que al culminar otras no ha sucedido lo msimo.
Esto conlleva un riesgo bastante evidente, pues si das por hecho que GTA 6 va a guardar tu progreso al completar cada misión principal que se te presente, es posible que te equivoques. Y si por algún motivo el uso del juego se interrumpe de forma repentina (si se va la luz, por ejemplo), tal vez te topes con que debes repetir algo que ya habías cumplido.
El autoguardado de GTA 6 presenta inconsistencias
Todavía no está claro si la inconsistencia del autoguardado de GTA 6 es un bug o una característica. Es un hecho que Rockstar Games tiene medidas bastante concretas sobre cuándo se puede o no guardar el progreso de una sesión. Si estás en una pelea o te persiguen pandilleros o la policía, no puedes guardar tu partida de ninguna manera, sea manual o automática. Asimismo, los desarrolladores no permiten salvar el avance mientras estás en medio de una misión con Jason y/o Lucía.
Dicho todo esto, lo más recomendable es no confiar a ciegas en el guardado automático de GTA 6. El juego es tan vasto y lleno de posibilidades que puedes pasar horas y horas recorriéndolo, independientemente de cuánto progreses en tu carrera criminal o en la relación entre los protagonistas. Así que no está bueno dedicarle tanto tiempo para luego perder lo poco o mucho que consigas por culpa de un imponderable.
Si quieres evitar sorpresas desagradables, lo más saludable es guardar tu progreso de GTA 6 de forma manual cada vez que te sea posible. Grand Theft Auto VI tiene 15 ranuras para almacenar el progreso de tus sesiones frente a la consola, de las cuales una está dedicada exclusivamente al autoguardado. Si optas por guardar tus avances de forma manual puedes hacerlo en Juego > Guardar juego, ingresando desde el menú de opciones.
GTA 6 es, sin dudas, de esas propuestas que se ven una sola vez en una generación. De acuerdo con el seguimiento que lleva Sensor Tower, lo nuevo de Rockstar ha vendido más de 19 millones de copias. Una cifra que se espera que siga en alza con el correr de los días.

articles.title: Natural Products Canada to open $25-million food systems scale-up fund |
articles.text:
A new fund is looking to cut $1-million to $5-million cheques to companies contributing to Canada’s food production and supply chain capacity.
The news: Spearheaded by Natural Products Canada (NPC), the Capacity Building Fund is a $25-million fund launching next month. Announced on Thursday, the fund will back Canadian companies as they scale production capacity with non-dilutive funding. Intake opens on Dec. 9, with companies considered on a continuous basis.
From the source: The capacity-building fund is offering $1 million to $5 million in funding, up to 50 percent of eligible project costs. Projects can be up to three years in length and must be a minimum of $2 million in overall size. Applicants also need to match 50 percent of funds from private financing or non-dilutive government funding.
The context: The Capacity Building Fund was announced in conjunction with NPC’s second economic impact assessment report. The report, which outlines the more than $1 billion in GDP contributions generated from NPC’s portfolio over five years, affirmed continued growth among the portfolio since its last assessment in January. It also outlined a renewed $50-million investment from the federal government’s Strategic Response Fund, a portion of which is being used to supply capital to NPC’s new fund.
The fund is looking for early-stage companies that are majority Canadian-owned, have 150 employees or less, and less than $15 million in annual revenue. A full list of criteria is available here.
RELATED: Canadian companies are generating massive returns in the “bioeconomy”
Final thought: NPC’s portfolio companies generated a whopping $294 million in GDP contributions in 2026, according to the impact assessment. That’s nearly a third of the nearly $900 million in GDP generated by the portfolio between 2021 and 2025. NPC’s assessment cites growth among existing portfolio companies, more pre-commercial companies reaching market, and a robust set of new innovators entering the commercialization pipeline as reasons for the returns, underscoring the value of scale-up supports like the Capacity Building Fund. 
BetaKit’s Prairies reporting is funded in part by YEGAF, a not-for-profit dedicated to amplifying business stories in Alberta.

articles.title: What employee adoption of Shadow AI is telling the enterprise
articles.text:
What employee adoption of Shadow AI is telling the enterprise
Many employees are already choosing their own AI tools
Across industries, businesses are putting approved AI tools into the hands of employees, but many employees are already choosing their own.
Microsoft research found that 71% of UK employees have used unapproved consumer AI tools at work, and more than half use them every week.
For 41%, these are tools they already use in their personal lives, while more than a quarter say their employer offers no approved alternative.
Chief Evangelist at Kore.ai
This is the Shadow AI economy. It creates an obvious security challenge, but it also shows where demand already exists.
Employees are choosing these tools because they are finding practical value in them, often before their employers have caught up.
Why Shadow AI persists
Providing an approved AI tool doesn't automatically change the habits employees have already formed. Consumer AI has set expectations around speed, flexibility and ease of experimentation. Employees can try different approaches, move between tasks and use the technology for whatever they need to get done.
Approved enterprise AI has to meet a different set of requirements. It needs to protect company data, respect access controls, integrate with existing systems and operate within governance requirements. But employees still expect it to be just as useful and easy to use.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
If the sanctioned option is more restrictive, harder to use or less suited to the way work gets done, employees are likely to return to the tools that work better for them. Blocking those tools may reduce the immediate risk, but it doesn't make the approved alternative any more useful or address why employees chose unapproved tools in the first place.
Shadow AI can therefore show businesses where their approved tools are falling short of what employees actually need.
Shadow AI is a signal of where demand already exists
We can't overlook the risks that come with Shadow AI. When employees use personal accounts or unapproved tools, organizations can lose visibility into what company information is being shared, how it is being processed and where it may go. But if employees are choosing these tools despite those restrictions, businesses should pay attention to what they are using them for.
If employees repeatedly turn to AI to analyze information, create content or speed up work that would otherwise take them hours, they are already showing where AI is useful in their day-to-day work.
We saw this in our own organization. Employees were already using tools such as ChatGPT and Claude to create presentations, draft content and produce other everyday assets. We looked at where they were saving time and brought those tools into an approved enterprise environment.
We also created shared skills that employees across the organization could use. Presentations are a good example. A shared skill in ChatGPT or Claude can include our enterprise messaging, brand language and the context employees need to talk about the company accurately. Anybody across the organization can create a presentation deck with standard brand guidelines and style.
For us, this has been the balance to get right. Employees can continue using tools they find useful, with company context and shared skills built in. At the same time, we have visibility into how those tools are being used and how company data is flowing through them, with enterprise security and access controls around that activity.
Businesses can take a similar cue from their own employees. Rather than trying to predict every AI use case centrally, look at where employees are already turning to AI and bring what is working into an approved environment.
Build beyond today’s AI tools
Employees may favor tools like ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini today, but that will change. New tools will come along, and existing ones will get better. Businesses cannot start again every time employees find something new that works for them.
The controls need to outlast the tools. Access to company data, what employees can do with it and the visibility the business needs should not depend on which model someone uses. Put those controls across the AI environment, and the business can introduce or replace tools as employee needs change without having to rebuild everything around them.
Also, businesses do not need to predict which tool employees will choose next. They need to get better at recognizing what is useful, bringing it into the business and making it safe to use. That way, the next tool employees discover does not have to become the next Shadow AI problem.

articles.title: Applications open for Kora Collective’s Spring 2027 founder cohort - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Applications are now open for the Spring 2027 cohort of the Kora Collective, a private network for seed-to-Series A founders building for emerging markets.
The Kora Collective is aimed at founders who are past day zero, have found traction, and are now focused on scaling, whether through bigger teams, new markets or better products. Its members are backed by investors including Coinbase, Digital Currency Group, Kraken, Hustle Fund, Jump and Cadenza.
The Spring 2027 cohort will bring together 15 founders, and will kick off in London in April. Members are placed in a small peer group of founders at a similar stage and in the same vertical across markets, and are paired with a coach.
They also take part in off-the-record sessions with operators who have built category-defining companies, reached US$1 billion-plus valuations and exited, and are connected one-on-one with senior venture capitalists matched to them based on fit.
For now, the collective is focused on two areas – payments and money movement, and credit, but an artificial intelligence (AI) track, covering agents, automation and intelligent infrastructure, is set to be added in future.
According to the Kora Collective, its existing members have processed more than US2.7 billion in combined volume, raised an average of US$6 million, and serve more than 10 countries across Africa, Asia and Latin America.
Founders have until December 18 to apply here.

articles.title: Instagram vous laisse enfin éditer vos stories
articles.text:
Qui n’a jamais publié un peu trop rapidement une story sur Instagram avant de le regretter, quelques secondes plus tard, à cause d’un oubli ou d’une vilaine faute ? Jusqu’à présent, Instagram n’offrait aucune solution permettant de corriger ce que vous aviez publié en story, vous obligeant ainsi à supprimer votre publication pour la recommencer ensuite. Mais les choses sont sur le point de changer.
Un délai de 15 minutes pour éditer vos stories
La bonne nouvelle a été annoncée officiellement par Adam Mosseri, le patron d’Instagram en personne sur son compte.
 Voir cette publication sur Instagram
 « Si vous avez déjà remarqué une faute de frappe juste après avoir posté une story, celle-ci est pour vous. Vous pouvez maintenant éditer du texte, de la musique, des autocollants et des dessins pendant 15 minutes maximum après le partage, sans perdre vos vues, vos likes ou vos réponses. » a-t-il ainsi expliqué en commentaire de sa publication.
Cette option d’édition, attendue de longue date par les utilisateurs, est accessible en tapotant le bouton Plus affiché en bas de la story, puis en sélectionnant Éditer la story. Attention toutefois, la possibilité de modifier une story n’est possible que dans les 15 minutes après la publication de celle-ci. Passé ce délai, vous n’aurez donc pas d’autre choix que d’adopter l’ancienne méthode, c’est-à-dire supprimer votre publication pour en refaire une nouvelle.

articles.title: Adieu le volant et les pédales : Elon Musk veut transformer le Tesla Model Y en robotaxi pour toute la famille
articles.text:
Tesla Model Y sans volant ni pédales : Elon Musk annonce un robotaxi familial jusqu’à 7 places
Après le Cybercab biplace, Tesla s'attaque à son SUV vedette. Elon Musk annonce un Model Y sans volant ni pédales, conçu pour emmener six ou sept passagers sans personne aux commandes. Il n'a donné ni date ni prix, et le précédent du Cybercab fait déjà grincer des dents.
Le 18 novembre, Andrew Ross Sorkin interrogeait Elon Musk en visioconférence lors du DealBook Summit du New York Times. Le patron de Tesla y a confirmé que la marque travaille sur une version du Model Y sans volant ni pédales. Le SUV familial reprendrait la recette du Cybercab, le taxi autonome sans commandes que Tesla fait déjà rouler à Austin, au Texas.
Pour Musk, la suite coule de source : "Il va être logique pour nous de fabriquer des voitures capables d'accueillir un nombre variable de passagers. Nous avons encore besoin de véhicules autonomes pour quatre ou six personnes, ou pour toute une famille."
Pourquoi Tesla veut un Model Y sans volant après le Cybercab
Musk a sorti sa calculette. Une voiture transporte en moyenne 1,2 personne, et un biplace couvre donc selon lui 90 % des kilomètres parcourus par des passagers. Les 10 % restants reviennent aux familles et aux groupes, qui ne tiennent pas dans l'habitacle exigu du Cybercab. D'où ce Model Y autonome, pensé pour six ou sept occupants.
	
Nous avons encore besoin de véhicules autonomes pour quatre ou six personnes, ou pour toute une famille.
Tesla fait déjà circuler des Model Y dans sa flotte de robotaxis, mais ils gardent leur volant et leur pédalier. Cette fois, les commandes disparaîtraient dès l'usine. Au détour de l'échange, Sorkin a confié qu'il attendait un Model Y L, la version allongée à six places, pour sa famille de cinq. Musk lui a répondu que Tesla devrait sans doute basculer toute la production du Model Y vers cette variante.
Elon on the @Tesla Model Y L:
"It's certainly our most popular car. We should just change all of the Model Y production to the Y L because it's what most people seem to want." pic.twitter.com/FVcBjZavOD
— Sawyer Merritt (@SawyerMerritt) November 18, 2026
Musk n'a donné ni calendrier ni tarif, et pas un mot sur une éventuelle vente aux particuliers.
Un abonnement obligatoire et une sécurité sous surveillance
Le Cybercab donne déjà une idée de la facture. Depuis le 13 novembre, des clients invités peuvent le commander pour un usage personnel à 29 990 dollars hors taxes, avec un acompte de 1 000 dollars non remboursable et des livraisons prévues en décembre à Austin. La voiture reste limitée aux zones du service Robotaxi et exige un abonnement mensuel de 299 dollars, sans lequel elle ne bouge pas. Musk lui-même a jugé ce tarif trop élevé en répondant sur X au youtubeur Marques Brownlee. Il l'imagine "plutôt autour de 115 dollars par mois", mais aucune baisse n'a été annoncée.
Les autorités ne lâchent pas Tesla d'une semelle. Le 3 septembre, la NHTSA, l'agence fédérale américaine de la sécurité routière, a ouvert un audit sur la façon dont Tesla a autocertifié le Cybercab, qui n'a ni volant, ni pédales, ni rétroviseurs. Le passif de la marque pèse lourd : des accidents de robotaxis passés sous silence, une communication très approximative sur leur fréquence et une conduite autonome accusée de malmener le code de la route. Un Model Y sans commandes devrait passer le même examen.
Fabriqué en Europe, interdit d'y rouler
En Europe, Tesla vient d'annoncer 3 milliards d'euros pour une nouvelle usine à Grünheide, près de Berlin, un site qui n'assemble aujourd'hui que des Model Y. L'objectif est d'y produire jusqu'à un million de Cybercab par an à partir de 2029, alors que le robotaxi n'a pas le droit de rouler sur le continent. Les règles européennes plafonnent chaque modèle de véhicule sans conducteur à 1 500 immatriculations par an, rappelle Electrek. Un Model Y sans volant se heurterait au même plafond.

articles.title: Scarlett Johansson, sobre su película con Robert Redford en 1998: “Antes de cada escena, él me contaba la historia para ayudarme a encontrar mi lugar en la película”
articles.text:
Scarlett Johansson pasó un largo proceso de audiciones para trabajar junto a Robert Redford en la película “El hombre que susurraba a los caballos”. Esta película (estrenada en 1998) es anterior incluso a que Scarlett haya trabajado con Sofia Coppola o haya encarnado al personaje de Viuda Negra.
Además de dirigir la película, Robert Redford también participó en ella como actor. Antes de rodar cada secuencia, le contaba a Scarlett cuál era la situación de su personaje en la historia. En palabras de la propia actriz: “Antes de cada escena, él me contaba la historia para ayudarme a encontrar mi lugar en la película”.
Su personaje se llamaba Grace Maclean y era una adolescente que pierde una pierna en un accidente de caballo. En este sentido, la actriz encontró un punto de partida en el hecho de que su personaje era una adolescente y siente que sus padres no le hacen caso. “Fue fácil para mí meterme en el papel. Lo que fue más difícil fue crearlo”.
Preparar la escena antes de actuar
La noticia le sorprendió y supuso un alivio tras todo el proceso de audiciones. “No podía creerlo. Estaba impactada”, recordaba en una entrevista. Además de contarle la historia antes de cada escena, Robert Redford le aconsejó a Scarlett “no actuar”. Es decir, que controlase su interpretación.
Cuando la película llegó a los cines, Scarlett Johansson tenía 13 años. En realidad, cuando rodaron la película (cuyo rodaje empezó en 1997), la actriz tenía 12 años.
En estas conversaciones con el director estaba también presente el hecho de que tenía que reflejar los efectos de este accidente y el alejamiento de su madre (Kristin Scott Thomas).
También influyó que apenas se conocían cuando empezaron a trabajar juntas. Se presentaron y en un par de horas ya estaban rodando una escena. Esto ayudó a transmitir el desapego y la incomodidad que hay entre Annie y Grace.
La actriz lo recordaba así: “Fue muy rápido y ayudó con ese desapego entre los personajes de Annie y Grace y esa especie de sensación de incomodidad”.

articles.title: Six Indian startups selected for Hub71's Immersion Programme in Abu Dhabi
articles.text:
Six Indian startups selected for Hub71's Immersion Programme in Abu Dhabi
The winners were chosen from among ten finalists in the areas of AI, clean energy, advanced manufacturing and digital finance.
Six Indian startups have been selected for Hub71's Immersion Programme in Abu Dhabi, following the UAE-India Start-Up Series 2.0 finale in Bengaluru.
Hub71, Abu Dhabi's global tech ecosystem, is the cross-border partner which will connect the startups with investors, corporate and government partners, regulators, and prospective customers.
Convened by the UAE Embassy in New Delhi, the series drew more than 11,000 applications this year. The winners were chosen from among ten finalists in the areas of artificial intelligence, clean energy, advanced manufacturing and digital finance.
Since the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement came into force in 2022, bilateral trade between India and the UAE has grown from about $73 billion to more than $101 billion, it added. Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, President of UAE, and Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India, have set a target of $200 billion by 2032.
According to a statement, the series seeks to help Indian companies expand globally, with the UAE as their gateway to investment and growth, said a statement.
H.E. Abdulla Saif Al Nuaimi, Ambassador of the UAE to India, announced the winners. Three of them will be shortlisted for Hub71's Access Programme; one startup will join the programme and receive AED 250,000 in in-kind incentives and AED 250,000 in cash through a SAFE note, the statement said.
Al Nuaimi said, “The UAE and India have set themselves the goal of doubling bilateral trade to $200 billion by 2032. Innovative companies like the ones we celebrate tonight will be central to reaching it. The UAE offers Indian founders a gateway to new markets, capital, and partnerships, and we will support these winners as they grow there. I congratulate all ten finalists on the standard they set.”
Ahmad Ali Alwan, CEO of Hub71, said, “India is an important source of technology innovation and entrepreneurial talent, and our collaboration with the UAE-India Start-Up Series is helping more ambitious founders connect with investors, partners, and market opportunities through Hub71.
"Through Hub71's Immersion Programme, startups can deepen their understanding of the market, build meaningful relationships, and access opportunities that support their growth in the UAE and internationally.”
The finale in Bengaluru brought together 10 startups for two days of investor meetings, mentorship and live pitching: CYRAN AI Solutions, Nawgati, KoinX, Onsite, Forthcode, Flo Mobility, Pointo, Econovus, XYMA Analytics, and Sustvest.
The jury comprised Al Nuaimi; Tushar Ved, President of Apparel Group; and members of the UAE-India business community. Al Nuaimi also unveiled a Top 50 Investment Dossier profiling 50 leading applicants.
The six winners will take part in a two-week hybrid programme, comprising a week of virtual preparation, followed by a one-week in-person session at Hub71 in Abu Dhabi from December 7. The programme includes mentorship, curated introductions, and knowledge sessions on Abu Dhabi's business and regulatory environment.
The first edition in 2025 opened a pathway for Indian startups to explore the UAE through Hub71. Endimension, an AI-powered radiology platform, later joined Hub71's Access Programme as part of Cohort 18. BioReform, Docket Run, Data Sutram and SBNRI are the other startups that have completed the Immersion Programme.
Here's a look at the six winning startups this year.
CYRAN AI Solutions (New Delhi, NCR)
The deeptech company uses AI to help aerospace and precision manufacturers catch defects before a part ships, an engine returns to service, or a satellite launches. Founded by IIT Delhi professor Manan Suri, it also builds edge AI for Industry 4.0 and geospatial customers.
Nawgati (Noida, Uttar Pradesh)
The AI and IoT platform helps fuel companies, dealers and governments monitor and run fuel stations from one real-time view. Founded by Aalaap Nair, Vaibhav Kaushik and Aryan Sisodia, the startup raised $2.5 million in a pre-Series A round led by Ajay Upadhyaya, and has deployments in Sri Lanka and the UAE.
KoinX (Bhubaneswar, Odisha)
This crypto tax and accounting platform helps investors and businesses calculate their tax, track their holdings, and keep compliant books. Founded in 2022 by Punit Agarwal, its CEO, the startup raised $1.5 million in seed funding from investors including Polygon founder Sandeep Nailwal, and later attracted investment from CoinDCX Ventures.
KoinX Founder and CEO Punit Agarwal, told YourStory that he has been active in crypto for about 10 years and had previously led the Crypto Relief Fund, a UAE-domiciled fund of close to $500 million. He said India has the most stringent crypto tax regime in the world, and the crypto market would grow in the country with regulations.
Agarwal said KoinX first earned revenue in the June-July 2023 tax season. Revenue grew from about $140,000 in its first year to about $700,000 in the third. He expects about $1.5 million this financial year, aided by B2B contracts.
In the UAE, KoinX sells B2B software to businesses. Agarwal said a local presence, through Hub71's Immersion Programme, would help build trust.
Onsite (New Delhi, NCR)
The AI-powered construction management platform helps contractors and developers control cost and time from site to office. Founded in March 2021 by Sumit Garg, Dheeraj Anand, and Akshansh Agarwal, the startup raised $1.5 million in 2022 in a round led by Foundamental.
Forthcode (Bengaluru, Karnataka)
The aviation technology company helps airlines grow ancillary revenue and automate operations at the airport, on board, and after the flight. Its platform automates inflight retail, services, and catering management. It has partnered with Worldline for inflight payments in India.
Founder and CEO Ajith Balakumar, told YourStory that Forthcode has built an AI model for aviation on Core42's sovereign AI models. Core42 is an Abu Dhabi-based technology company.
On seatback screens in planes, passengers can search for films or ask advanced questions, such as what a city they are flying over looked like 2,000 years ago. He said the software is isolated from avionics and flight controls, and guardrails limit questions to movies, food and the destination.
Balakumar said AI can also answer queries from ground staff on matters such as dangerous goods compliance and support ancillary revenue and disruption management.
Forthcode is a winner of AviationX Labs by Emirates, Thales, Collins, GE and Airbus, has completed a paid pilot with Emirates, and works with Thales as its go-to-market partner.
Flo Mobility (Bengaluru, Karnataka)
Founded by Manesh Jain and Pratik Patel, the construction robotics company helps builders and contractors move materials across large sites using autonomous electric vehicles.
The startup's Flo Hauler robot can carry up to 1.5 tonnes. More than 60 of its robots are deployed across 10 states for developers including L&T and Godrej Properties. Flo Mobility raised $2.5 million in a pre-Series A round co-led by Mela Ventures and Arali Ventures.

articles.title: Ce pionnier du fatbike électrique est en faillite
articles.text:
Aux Pays-Bas, le fatbike électrique est au cœur d’un débat public depuis plusieurs années déjà, notamment parce qu’il se débriderait trop facilement aux yeux des autorités. Knaap Bikes, l’une des marques néerlandaises les plus connues du segment, en a fait les frais selon sa direction : l’entreprise installée à Ter Aar a été déclarée en faillite mardi 17 novembre par le tribunal de La Haye.
Plusieurs causes évoquées
La chaîne économique néerlandaise RTL Z a révélé l’information, à partir des éléments fournis par le syndic de faillite, Wouter Vlasveld. En janvier, la marque cherchait pourtant encore à se diversifier avec son premier vélo cargo électrique, le longtail PAR X26 à 3 300 euros.
Du 19 au 30 novembre, le Plaud Note Pro passe à 149 € au lieu de 189 € ! Il enregistre vos réunions, les transcrit et les synthétise pour vous, il suffit d’appuyer sur un bouton. Les Plaud Note, NotePin et NotePin S sont aussi à -20 %. Bref, c’est le moment d’arrêter de perdre du temps au travail !
Les entrepreneurs Robin Cats et Michael Fiering ont fondé Knaap en 2019. L’entreprise est vite devenue l’un des premiers importateurs et vendeurs de fatbikes du pays. Dans le dernier rapport financier de l’entreprise, que RTL Z dit avoir consulté, Robin Cats explique que l’image du fatbike a été très abîmée par les comportements de certains utilisateurs : excès de vitesse, circulation dans les zones piétonnes, agressivité envers les autres usagers, voire implication dans des délits.
Il cite aussi la facilité avec laquelle ces vélos se débrident pour rouler plus vite, et le retrait des assureurs, qui a encore compliqué la situation.
Concurrence chinoise et 1,1 million d’euros dans le rouge
Knaap range également la concurrence des fatbikes chinois bon marché parmi les causes principales. D’après Robin Cats, ces fournisseurs étrangers ont pu dégager des marges en contournant les droits d’importation et en ignorant les normes de sécurité, ce qui revient selon lui à une concurrence déloyale pour les marques néerlandaises. La direction reproche aussi aux autorités leur manque de fermeté. Knaap faisait en effet partie des fabricants qui avaient demandé au gouvernement, en 2024, de bloquer l’importation et la vente des vélos débridés. Elle estime aujourd’hui que l’absence de règles et de contrôles a pesé dans la faillite.
De son côté, la marque avait essayé de prendre les devants. En juin, elle a lancé une campagne nationale de reprise, ouverte jusqu’au 31 juillet : les clients pouvaient échanger un fatbike ou un vélo électrique débridé illégalement contre un modèle légal de la gamme Knaap, avec une prime allant jusqu’à 1 000 euros selon le vélo rendu. L’entreprise était déjà mal en point avant cette opération. Le dernier rapport financier montre que Knaap Bikes a terminé 2025 avec des capitaux propres négatifs de plus de 1,1 million d’euros.
Une reprise reste envisageable
L’entreprise a cherché de nouveaux investisseurs pour redresser la barre, sans succès. Le syndic Wouter Vlasveld enquête maintenant sur les causes précises de la faillite et étudie en parallèle une reprise de l’activité. D’après lui, des pistes existent : la réputation de qualité de la marque, les stocks de vélos, les livraisons en cours et les droits sur ses propres modèles pourraient intéresser un acteur qui veut se lancer sur le marché du fatbike. Une faillite ne signe donc pas toujours la fin d’une marque de vélo électrique.

articles.title: Où trouver la maison de GTA San Andreas dans GTA 6 ?
articles.text:
Les théories étaient donc vraies. Dans Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy – The Definitive Edition, Rockstar Games s’est amusé à ajouter des photos dans GTA San Andreas, photos renvoyant à différents lieux apparus dans ses jeux à l’exception d’une mystérieuse maison au style très floridien. Quand la trilogie est sortie, en novembre 2021, GTA 6 n’avait pas encore été officialisé. Difficile, dès lors, de relier cette demeure au jeu de Rockstar Games sorti ce jeudi 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5, Xbox Series S et Xbox Series X.
La photo en question était accrochée au mur du Lil’ Probe’Inn, le bar de San Andreas consacré aux ovnis. On y voyait un pavillon de banlieue entouré de palmiers, avec une soucoupe volante dans le ciel.
La maison de la photo de GTA San Andreas figure bel et bien dans GTA 6. Numerama a pu se rendre sur le lieu où elle se trouve pour confirmer qu’il s’agit du même design. Les développeurs ont donc glissé un indice sur GTA 6 dès novembre 2021, moins de trois mois avant que Rockstar ne confirme son développement, en février 2022.
Où trouver la maison de GTA San Andreas dans GTA 6
Pour trouver la maison en question, il faut se rendre à Belville, dans le sud de Leonard County, au nord de la maison de Jason (mais assez loin de celle-ci). Elle se trouve dans un quartier résidentiel, avec un voisinage très ressemblant. Vous trouverez ci-dessous le point à marquer sur votre carte pour que le GPS intégré au jeu vous y emmène.
La maison ressemble exactement à la photo de GTA San Andreas, jusque dans les décorations extérieures. Rockstar Games s’est contenté d’ajouter un panneau « à vendre », juste devant. Impossible, d’ailleurs, d’entrer dans la maison. En revanche, le garage renferme quelques secrets.
On peut forcer la porte (via un QTE, une action rapide à réussir au stick) pour entrer dans le garage et découvrir un lieu habité, avec un canapé, un téléviseur, un bureau ou encore un frigo. Le garage est jonché de messages à tendance conspirationniste. Des phrases comme « We don’t die », « We are in a loop », « It’s a simulation » ou encore « Why can’t I leave ? » peuvent être lues. Un clin d’œil savoureux pour une maison qui alimente les théories des fans depuis cinq ans.
Les notes vont plus loin que ces slogans. Leur auteur explique ne pas pouvoir acheter de billet d’avion pour Los Santos ni quitter l’État en voiture, allant jusqu’à songer au bateau. Il désigne aussi deux personnes, J et L, qui échapperaient aux limites de son monde. Difficile de ne pas y voir Jason et Lucia, les deux héros du jeu.
Dans le garage, on trouve aussi deux éléments utiles pour la progression : une carte à collectionner et un magazine, lui aussi à tendance conspirationniste.

articles.title: Un retraité a acheté 32 panneaux solaires à quatre entreprises en un an, sa famille dénonce un acharnement
articles.text:
À Aix-en-Provence, un retraité s'est vu vendre 32 panneaux solaires par quatre entreprises différentes, pour 100 600 euros au total. Cette affaire de démarchage photovoltaïque, mise au jour par une association, pourrait bientôt se régler devant la justice.
En un peu plus d'un an, Paul, retraité aixois de 71 ans qui vit seul et se chauffe au gaz, a accumulé trente-deux panneaux solaires, quatre installateurs et 100 600 euros de factures. L'UFC-Que Choisir, qui a enquêté sur son cas, relève des prix très au-dessus du marché, des aides gonflées et des crédits empilés jusqu'à dépasser 1 000 euros de mensualités cumulées. « Je n'avais jamais vu un tel acharnement », commente Joël Mercy, président du Groupement des particuliers producteurs d'électricité photovoltaïque (GPPEP). Si les installateurs défendent leurs pratiques, la famille du septuagénaire veut faire annuler l'ensemble des contrats.
Black Friday Roborock
Profitez du meilleur du nettoyage et bénéficiez de meilleures offres et services : plus de points Cadeau, réductions sur les packs, assurance transport gratuite, paiement en plusieurs fois sans frais, prix garantis pendant 30 jours
Des panneaux solaires vendus au prix fort, encore et encore
Le premier contrat mis en cause date de novembre 2024. À cette époque, Eco Habitat Energie vend à Paul (les prénoms ont été modifiés pour respecter l'anonymat des intervenants) pas moins de 8 panneaux photovoltaïques (4 kWc) pour 24 900 euros. C'est déjà une belle puissance pour un homme seul aux consommations ordinaires, et surtout un prix élevé, car à ce moment-là, rappelle Joël Mercy, on trouvait la même puissance « autour de 8 000 euros ». On assure pourtant à Paul que l'installation s'autofinancera grâce à l'autoconsommation et à la revente du surplus.
« Mon père est tombé dans le panneau, attiré par l'appât du gain », soupire Marie, sa fille, auprès de l'UFC-Que Choisir. Le doute apparaît un an plus tard. Le 4 novembre 2025, Paul écrit au commercial d'Eco Habitat Energie, en lui disant que les 4 910 euros d'aides promises ne sont toujours pas arrivés, et que ses mensualités atteignent 301,77 euros, au lieu des 261,71 euros prévus au contrat. « Dans la quasi-totalité des cas, ça s'arrête là », note Joël Mercy. Pas pour Paul.
Six jours plus tard, il signe avec le Groupe Solar Renov pour 7 panneaux DualSun (3,5 kWc) à 20 900 euros, soit 17 136 euros après aides. DualSun situe pourtant une installation de 3 kWc posée par ses installateurs agréés entre 6 500 et 8 500 euros, aides déduites. Le commercial indépendant qui a démarché Paul pour Solar Renov lui fait ensuite signer avec HM Environnement 9 panneaux à 29 900 euros, financés par un crédit Sofinco d'un coût total de 46 751 euros. À la même période, Heliora Home lui en vend 8 autres pour 24 900 euros. Vous le constatez, les factures s'enchaînent pour notre retraité.
La famille veut faire annuler les contrats
Au total, Paul a acheté 16 kWc, plus de trois fois la puissance d'une installation résidentielle moyenne en France. Et son toit ne suffit même plus à tout accueillir. Les panneaux d'Eco Habitat Energie ont été démontés et sont stockés dans le jardin, et ceux d'Heliora Home ont été posés sur le versant nord, contre les recommandations d'usage. L'installation électrique disjoncte sans cesse : « Dès que mon père s'absentait trop longtemps de chez lui, les denrées dans son frigo étaient à jeter », raconte Marie. Depuis juin, à la demande de ses proches, Paul est carrément sous curatelle.
L'association de consommateurs relève que dans au moins trois des quatre bons de commande, les aides promises sont très élevées, jusqu'à 4 470 euros chez Heliora Home. Elles comprennent un remboursement de la TVA, qui oblige pourtant à créer son entreprise et à déclarer chaque année son chiffre d'affaires. Le 11 janvier 2026, Paul reçoit le courrier d'une société qui se dit mandatée par l'installateur pour récupérer cette TVA. Selon lui, le mandat joint porte déjà « une pâle imitation » de sa signature. Le retraité a par ailleurs porté plainte pour escroquerie contre le commercial de Solar Renov, qu'il accuse de lui avoir soutiré deux fois 3 500 euros.
Les installateurs, eux, ne voient pas le problème. « Nous sommes libres sur la tarification », rappelle le Groupe Solar Renov. « Si le client nous en demande, nous exauçons son souhait », assume le responsable d'Heliora Home. Karine Leboucher, l'avocate de la famille, leur répond qu'« une entreprise a évidemment un devoir de conseil. » Début novembre, elle s'apprêtait à saisir le tribunal judiciaire d'Aix-en-Provence pour faire annuler les quatre bons de commande, selon elle « tous illégaux » au regard de la loi sur le démarchage à domicile.

articles.title: Unbemannter Drogenschmuggel: Wie Kartelle ihre U-Boote mit Starlink und Hardware von Amazon steuern lassen
articles.text:
Keine Crew an Bord: Wie Drogenkartelle mit Standard-Hardware autonome U-Boote bauen
An einem strahlenden Morgen im vergangenen April entdeckte ein Überwachungsflugzeug des kolumbianischen Militärs eine 12 Meter lange, haifischähnliche Silhouette. Sie trieb direkt vor dem Tayrona-Nationalpark im Meer. Es handelte sich zweifellos um ein „Drogen-U-Boot“, ein getarntes Glasfaserboot, dessen Rumpf fast vollständig unter Wasser liegt und das von Drogenkartellen zum Transport von Kokain in Richtung Norden genutzt wird. Die Besatzung des Flugzeugs meldete den Vorfall per Funk, und schließlich erhielten nahegelegene Boote der Küstenwache den Befehl – routinemäßig, aber dringend: Abfangen.
Dieser Text stammt aus der Ausgabe 8/2026 von MIT Technology Review. Darin beschäftigen wir uns mit den Folgen des Klimawandels und wie wir uns an Hitze, Dürre und Überschwemmungen anpassen sollten. Das Heft ist ab sofort im Zeitschriftenhandel erhältlich und in unserem Online-Shop bestellbar.
Kolumbianische Küstenwache fängt U-Boot ab
In Cartagena, etwa 250 Kilometer von diesen Geschehnissen entfernt, setzte sich der Kommandant der regionalen Küstenwache, Kapitän Jaime González Zamudio, an seinen Schreibtisch und verfolgte von dort, was nun passierte. Auf seinem Bildschirm rasten die Symbole für seine Patrouillenboote auf die Koordinaten des U-Boots zu, während er über Funk mit den Besatzungen in Kontakt stand. Ein ganz normaler Tag in kolumbianischen Gewässern.
Kolumbien ist der weltweit größte Kokainproduzent, und seine Marine beschlagnahmt seit Jahrzehnten Schmuggel-U-Boote. Und so war sich der Kapitän ziemlich sicher, wie diese Aktion ausgehen würde: Seine Mannschaft würde das U-Boot einholen, von dem ein kleiner Teil aus dem Wasser ragte. Sie würden es anhalten, entern und die Luke aufbrechen. Im Inneren würden sie zwei, drei, vielleicht auch vier erschöpfte Männer vorfinden, die kurz davor waren, an den feuchten Dieselabgasen zu ersticken. Im Laderaum würden sie mehrere Tonnen Kokain finden.
Der erste Teil verlief wie geplant: Die Boote holten das U-Boot ein. Eine Besatzung der Patrouillenboote enterte es, brach die Luke auf und stellte fest, dass das Schiff sicher war. Doch ab diesem Moment verliefen die Dinge anders.
Starlink, Amazon-Autopilot und Überwachungskamera
Zunächst kam über Funk die unerwartete Info, es befände sich kein Kokain an Bord. Und auch keine Besatzung. Noch nicht einmal ein Steuerrad. Und auch nicht genügend Platz für eine Person, um sich hinzulegen. Stattdessen fanden die Männer der Küstenwache einen Treibstofftank, ein Autopilotsystem und Steuerelektronik sowie eine ferngesteuerte Überwachungskamera. Das Team von González Zamudio schickte Bilder nach Cartagena: Am Rumpf waren eine weitere Kamera sowie zwei rechteckige Kunststoffteile, jedes etwa so groß wie ein Backblech, festgeschraubt – Antennen für die Verbindung zum Starlink-Satelliteninternet.
Die Behörden schleppten das Boot nach Cartagena, wo Militärtechniker es genauer unter die Lupe nahmen. Wochen später lieferten sie die beunruhigenden Ergebnisse: Sie hatten das erste unbemannte Drogen-U-Boot Kolumbiens auseinandergenommen. Es konnte ferngesteuert werden, war aber auch zu einem gewissen Grad in der Lage, autonom zu fahren. Die Techniker schlossen daraus, dass es sich bei dem U-Boot wahrscheinlich um einen Prototyp des „Clan del Golfo“ handelte, einer mächtigen kriminellen Vereinigung, die an der Karibikküste operiert.

articles.title: PHP security updates fix 18 flaws, including critical RCE bugs
articles.text:
The PHP dev team released security updates for 18 vulnerabilities, including critical flaws that could allow unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute code on vulnerable servers.
The updates were released Thursday, November 19, for all supported PHP branches, with PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, and 8.2.36 now available.
Security firm Aikido reports that the updates address 18 CVEs affecting PHP's core engine, session handling, PHP-FPM, CGI, and other components.
One of the most serious flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-129289, is a critical PHP-FPM request smuggling vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.2.
According to Aikido, the flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to execute PHP code remotely on vulnerable servers that reuse connections to PHP-FPM under certain conditions.
The vulnerability affects certain nginx, Apache, HAProxy, and LSAPI configurations that reuse backend connections to PHP-FPM.
Standard nginx and Apache configurations that do not reuse backend connections are not affected by the attack.
Other important vulnerabilities fixed in the updates include:
- CVE-2026-129474: A use-after-free vulnerability involving magic method backtraces that could lead to remote code execution.
- CVE-2026-129496: A timezone cache use-after-free vulnerability that could lead to remote code execution.
- CVE-2026-126714: A vulnerability involving partially overwritten session files that could lead to remote code execution.
- CVE-2026-115560: A session serializer mismatch vulnerability that could lead to remote code execution.
- CVE-2026-129291: A PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free vulnerability that could lead to local privilege escalation.
- CVE-2026-128090: A PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass vulnerability involving an algorithm downgrade.
Additional fixes address memory corruption, information disclosure, cross-site scripting, denial-of-service issues, and potentially unsafe handling of HTTPS and FTPS URLs.
The releases follow a warning issued Wednesday by the PHP security team that the upcoming updates would address vulnerabilities affecting all supported PHP versions, with the highest severity rated critical.
"The issues rated CRITICAL require either non-default configuration or uncommon setups," the PHP security team warned.
One of the vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-115560, was already disclosed in an October 23 informational advisory and relates to how PHP handles session data under certain configurations, potentially leading to remote code execution.
As a temporary mitigation, PHP recommended disabling session upload progress by setting session.upload_progress.enabled=0 and restarting PHP workers. This setting was also recommended to mitigate the recent PHP2Shell flaws.
For CVE-2026-129289, administrators who cannot immediately install the security updates can mitigate the vulnerability by disabling persistent backend connections between their web servers and PHP-FPM, ensuring connections are closed after each request.
Aikido warns that these mitigations do not address all vulnerabilities fixed in the November updates and recommends ensuring PHP-FPM and LSAPI listeners are not directly exposed to untrusted networks.
Although the official security updates are limited to supported PHP branches, third-party maintainer Ondrej Surý has also released patched packages for unsupported PHP versions dating back to PHP 5.6.
Aikido has similarly released hardened PHP container images containing backported security fixes for unsupported versions, including PHP 5.6, 7.0, 7.1, 7.2, 7.4, and 8.1.
PHP administrators are urged to upgrade to PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, or 8.2.36, depending on their supported branch, to address the newly disclosed vulnerabilities.
