articles.title: How Nigerian startup PeoplePulse is helping SMEs digitise HR with AI - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nigerian startup PeoplePulse has developed an affordable, AI-powered workforce management platform designed to help African small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) manage their people and automate routine HR processes.
Founded in June 2025, PeoplePulse grew out of HR and business consultancy Bridgemead Consulting, which has worked with SMEs on recruitment, HR outsourcing, employee management and training.
The platform brings employee records, onboarding, leave and attendance management, payroll support, performance management, workforce analytics and compliance into one place.
“Many growing African businesses still manage their HR operations using spreadsheets, WhatsApp, paper records and disconnected tools. At the other end of the market, enterprise HR platforms can be too expensive or complicated for smaller organisations,” Adetola Abolarinwa, co-founder and chief product officer, told Disrupt Africa. “PeoplePulse is designed to bridge that gap: it is accessible enough for an SME but robust enough to support a growing workforce.”
The startup, which has an 11-strong team, competes with the likes of SeamlessHR and BambooHR, but believes its combination of affordability, simplicity, localisation and AI-powered automation sets it apart.
“We did not begin by making assumptions about what SMEs needed; we had already spent years working directly with them and understanding their operational problems,” Abolarinwa said.
Funded by its founders and a friends-and-family round, PeoplePulse piloted its platform with around 280 employees across eight companies between May and July 2026, with all eight converting into paying customers. It was also selected as one of the top 11 finalists for Cycle 7 of the Women in Tech Accelerator Nigeria.
The startup charges between NGN2,000 (US$1.5) and NGN3,500 (US$2.5) per employee per month across three subscription tiers.
“Our focus is not simply on acquiring registrations. We are concentrating on successful onboarding, active usage, retention and expanding adoption within each customer organisation,” Abolarinwa said.
PeoplePulse is focused on building a strong customer base in Nigeria, with Bridgemead’s network of more than 80 businesses providing a warm pipeline, before expanding into other African markets.
“We see PeoplePulse as a pan-African opportunity, but we intend to build a strong foundation in Nigeria before expanding aggressively,” said Abolarinwa.

articles.title: AI can write code, but knowing what to build still matters
articles.text:
AI can write code, but knowing what to build still matters
At TechSparks 2026, Srinivas Chamarthy of Diligent India, Madhusudan N. Murthy of EY GDS, and Arun Kalyanaraman of Target discussed why domain expertise, engineering skills, and human judgement remain important as AI makes software development more accessible.
AI is making it easier to build software. Product managers, designers, and domain experts can now turn ideas into prototypes without necessarily knowing how to code. But turning those prototypes into reliable products that solve real problems remains a challenge.
At TechSparks 2026, Srinivas Chamarthy, Senior Vice President of Engineering, Site Lead and Country Head at Diligent India; Madhusudan N. Murthy, Digital Engineering and Tech Strategy Leader at EY GDS; and Arun Kalyanaraman, VP of Engineering at Target in India, discussed these changes during a panel titled ‘From Who Can Code to Who Can Build’.
The discussion was moderated by Chhavi Mahajan, Chief Content Officer at YourStory.
From prototypes to production
AI-assisted development allows business teams to test ideas, demonstrate concepts, and gather feedback much earlier. However, a prototype that shows an idea can work is not necessarily ready for production. Applications still need to meet security, scalability, and reliability requirements.
Murthy said that AI is making experimentation easier, but companies must distinguish between a proof of concept and a production-ready application. Engineering teams still need to identify vulnerabilities, put safeguards in place, and ensure systems can handle real-world use.
“It's good, it's a very positive development, but it also has to have its guardrails,” he stated.
Kalyanaraman said AI can do more than help developers write code faster. It can also speed up the entire development process, from defining a problem and testing a solution to getting stakeholder approval. However, strong engineering fundamentals, architectural thinking, and technical depth will remain essential, even as AI changes how solutions are built.
He gave the example of a product owner, an engineer, and a UX professional who used AI tools and large language models to prototype a complex concept and present it to leadership within a week. Without these tools, the process could have taken six weeks to two months.
The benefit was not just faster coding, but the ability to test an idea and make a decision sooner.
Chamarthy said coding is becoming a commodity in the generative AI era, shortening the path from prototype to customer feedback to production, with a nine-month cycle potentially coming down to a month or two. As speed increases, he said, knowing what not to build becomes more valuable, so ideas should be tested in a sandbox while experienced engineers harden them for security, scalability, and privacy.
Deciding where human oversight is needed
As companies move from using AI to assist developers to deploying agents that can complete tasks with limited supervision, they must decide how much autonomy to allow.
Chamarthy said this should depend on the risks involved, the potential impact of a decision, and whether its outcome can be reversed.
He suggested organizations consider whether a decision is a two-way-door or a one-way-door call, with significant financial or strategic decisions needing human oversight and contextual judgment.
Chamarthy cautioned that access to AI coding tools cannot replace engineering experience. Experienced engineers understand the architectural decisions that affect security, scalability, and long-term maintenance, including risks that may not be apparent in a prototype.
His advice was to encourage experimentation, but within controlled environments.
“Don't stop the code. Sandbox it.”
This allows more employees to test ideas while giving engineering teams the opportunity to review the applications, address weaknesses, and prepare them for production.
Why domain expertise matters
As AI makes it easier to generate code and find answers, knowing which problems to solve becomes more important.
Kalyanaraman compared using AI to consulting a genie that grants only three wishes. Getting a useful result depends on asking the right questions and understanding the constraints.
“In a world where maybe getting answers are easy, asking the right questions is going to be a really, really critical skill,” he said.
People who understand customers, business processes, and operational requirements are better placed to identify solutions that create value.
Engineering teams will also need systems thinking and platform expertise to help non-engineers develop applications without putting production systems at risk.
The shift also has implications for workforce development.
Murthy said EY GDS is preparing employees for an AI-driven workplace by bringing experienced professionals and younger talent together. Existing employees bring knowledge of customers and systems, while newer team members contribute fresh approaches and develop emerging technical skills.
Chamarthy said teams need a mix of strengths: organizations should upskill existing employees, who understand their products and customers, while bringing in fresh graduates who can work with AI tools.
He also added that engineering performance should be measured by the problems teams solve for customers, rather than only by metrics such as lines of code written or tickets closed.
As AI takes over more routine work, the outcomes delivered by engineering teams become a more useful measure of their contribution.
A workforce of people and AI agents
The panellists expect employees and AI agents to work increasingly closely together.
As agents take on more complex tasks, companies will need to rethink workflows, accountability and performance expectations. They will also need to ensure safeguards keep pace with what the technology can do.
Murthy described a future in which managers will oversee AI agents alongside human employees.
“The future I see is getting used to agents reporting to you and not just humans,” he said.
Kalyanaraman added that The New Tech Order is not just about what AI can do for us. It is about how we evolve our thinking, engineering practices, and decision-making to make the most of it.
While AI is making software easier to build, companies will still need engineering expertise, domain knowledge, and human judgement to decide which ideas are worth pursuing and which prototypes are ready for production.

articles.title: How Virtual Twins And Machine Learning Optimize DRAM Yield
articles.text:
Model process variation, detect multiple failure modes, and evaluate solutions with less wafer experimentation.
As memory technologies continue to scale, manufacturing processes are becoming increasingly complex.
Additional process steps, tighter process windows, and new sources of variation are making it progressively more challenging to reach acceptable yield.
Systemic failures are emerging as a source of yield loss during yield ramp. Unlike random defects, these failures are often driven by complex interactions between multiple process modules.
Rapid root-cause identification of these systemic defects is critical to quickly improving yield and accelerating time-to-market.1 But conventional failure analysis relies heavily on wafer experimentation and statistical analysis, which can be slow and costly as manufacturing complexity increases.
That’s where calibrated virtual twins and machine-learning optimization can help.
Fig. 1: Systemic failures are a key bottleneck during yield ramp. Faster identification and reduction of these failures can accelerate the yield ramp and shorten the time required to reach a targeted manufacturing yield.
Process engineers use virtual manufacturing models (SEMulator3D) with machine learning (ML) optimization (Fabtex Yield Optimizer) to predict process failures.
Using this technique, engineers can evaluate potential yield improvements, all with limited need for wafer-based experimentation.
As an example of this technique, we built a SEMulator3D model (virtual twin) of a DRAM manufacturing process sequence. During this model-building, we established virtual metrology measurements throughout the process sequence (Figure 2).
Fig. 2: Building and calibrating a DRAM virtual twin using process integration, virtual metrology, and silicon data.
ML was then used to calibrate the model against silicon data, enabling the virtual environment to better reproduce observed manufacturing behavior and serve as the foundation for downstream failure analysis and optimization.
For our specific case study, we built a calibrated virtual twin for our DRAM memory device that contained eight known systemic failure mechanisms.
Figure 3 displays examples of these failure mechanisms, including shorts, opens, and overlap-related defects between critical DRAM structures.
Fig. 3: Reproducing systemic DRAM failure modes and detecting them using virtual metrology.
We also specified (in the virtual twin) the virtual metrology needed to detect these failures. By translating each failure into a measurable geometric condition and monitoring it through virtual metrology, we were able to automatically detect and simultaneously analyze multiple failure mechanisms within a single study.
Using the calibrated virtual twin, ML was then applied to help us understand the impact of process and structural variations on the eight predefined failure modes.
We then searched for an optimized manufacturing solution (specific process changes) that provided the lowest failure rate across our eight predefined failure modes. Instead of addressing each failure mode independently, the optimization routine evaluated the impact of multiple process changes simultaneously and searched for process targets that improved the overall pass ratio.
As shown in Figure 4, the optimized process settings significantly reduced all eight systemic failure modes.
Fig. 4: Simultaneous reduction of multiple systemic failures through ML-based optimization and retargeting analysis. A sample retargeting plot for SNLP (storage node landing pad) open/short failures is highlighted.
Under the nominal process conditions used in the study, the predicted total yield was 0.1%. Following optimization, the predicted yield increased to 78.5%, with lower failure rates across all eight failure mechanisms.
This analysis also translated the optimized solution into actionable inline fab targets that can be directly applied in the real process, helping engineers identify which process and structural parameters should be adjusted to further reduce systemic failures.
This work demonstrates how the combination of process models and ML can be used to accelerate yield improvement during DRAM device development. By reproducing process variability in a calibrated virtual environment, and performing simultaneous optimization and retargeting, engineers can detect multiple device failures and investigate a broad solution space without the time and cost of extensive silicon experimentation.
1 I. Tirkel, “Yield Learning Curve Models in Semiconductor Manufacturing,” IEEE Transactions on Semiconductor Manufacturing, vol. 26, no. 4, pp. 564-571, Nov. 2013.
Leave a Reply

articles.title: Oppo Reno 17: Price, release date and full specs
articles.text:
Table of contents
Oppo launched the Reno 17 in China on November 16, 2026, alongside the Reno 17 Pro. It packs an 8,000mAh battery, the biggest Oppo has ever put in a Reno phone, and four 50MP cameras. This time, the standard model is bigger, while the Pro is the compact one.
Prices start at CNY 3,599, which is about ₦728,330. Oppo has not said when the phone will come to Nigeria. This guide covers the release date, price, full specs, and how the phone compares with the Reno 16, so you know what to expect.
Oppo Reno 17 release date
Oppo announced the Reno 17 at a launch event in China on November 16, 2026. Oppo also launched the Watch 5 and Pad Air 6 at the same event. Pre-orders are now open in China, and sales start on November 20, 2026.
Oppo has not announced a launch outside China yet. Here is what we know so far:
- Global version: A global Reno 17 (model CPH2975) and a cheaper Reno 17 F (CPH3013) have appeared on certification databases in Thailand and India. This usually means a global launch is close.
- India: Tipsters expect the phone in India between December 2026 and early 2027. Oppo has not confirmed either date.
- Nigeria: Oppo Nigeria launched the Reno 15 and Reno 15 F on March 10, 2026, about 113 days after their China debut. If the Reno 17 follows that pattern, it could reach Nigeria around March 2027. Treat this as a guess based on past launches.
- The Reno 16 gap: We found no official Nigerian launch for the Reno 16, so the Reno 17 could skip Nigeria too.
Keep one more thing in mind. For the last two Reno series, Oppo sold different phones under the same name in China and in global markets. Leaks point to a global Reno 17 with a smaller 6.32-inch screen and a 7,000mAh battery. If that is true, the phone that reaches Nigeria may not match the China model in this guide.
Oppo Reno 17 price
The Reno 17 comes in four versions in China. Here is what each one costs:
| Version | China price | US dollars (approx.) | Naira (conversion) | 
|---|---|---|---|
| 8GB + 256GB | CNY3,599 | $533 | ₦728,330 | 
| 12GB + 256GB | CNY3,799 | $563 | ₦768,804 | 
| 12GB + 512GB | CNY3,999 | $592 | ₦809,278 | 
| 12GB + 1TB | CNY4,899 | $726 | ₦991,411 | 
The naira figures are straight conversions at ₦202.37 per yuan (XE, November 17, 2026). They are not Nigerian prices. They leave out shipping, import duty, VAT, and dealer margins, and the naira rate changes daily.
Buyers in China can also use the national subsidy program to get the base model for CNY3,099. That offer only works in China.
What could it cost in Nigeria? Slot sells the Reno 15 (12GB + 512GB) for ₦949,900. If Oppo Nigeria launches the Reno 17, we estimate the 12GB + 512GB model could land between ₦850,000 and ₦1,000,000. This is our estimate, not an official price.
For context, the global Reno 16 launched at €899 in Europe and Rs 61,999 in India. Expect the global Reno 17 to cost more than it does in China.
Detailed specs
1. Display
- 6.56-inch flat OLED screen with 2,624 x 1,208 resolution (1.5K) and 440ppi
- Up to 120Hz refresh rate and 240Hz touch sampling
- 10-bit color with full DCI-P3 coverage
- 800 nits in normal use and 1,800 nits in high-brightness mode
- Up to 6,000 nits at its local peak
- Oppo Crystal Shield glass on top
2. Processor and performance
- Qualcomm Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 (4nm, up to 2.8GHz) with an Adreno 722 GPU
- LPDDR5X RAM and UFS 3.1 storage
- A 5,000 sq mm vapor chamber to keep the phone cool
- Oppo’s own touch chip and network chip working alongside the Snapdragon
The Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 is the same chip inside the global Reno 16 and the Reno 15 sold in Nigeria. It is slower than the Dimensity 8550 Super in the China Reno 16. Early chip-level scores put it about 45% behind on AnTuTu. Reno 17 benchmark tests are still to come, so wait for reviews before you judge it.
3. Memory and storage
- 8GB RAM + 256GB storage
- 12GB RAM + 256GB storage
- 12GB RAM + 512GB storage
- 12GB RAM + 1TB storage
There is no microSD slot, so pick the storage you need on day one.
4. Cameras
All four cameras use 50MP sensors:
- Main: 50MP, f/1.8, with optical image stabilization (OIS). Notebookcheck reports it is a Sony LYT-600 sensor.
- Ultrawide: 50MP, f/2.0, with a 116-degree view
- Periscope telephoto: 50MP, f/2.8, with OIS, 3.5x optical zoom and up to 120x digital zoom
- Selfie: 50MP, f/2.0, with autofocus
You also get these camera extras:
- 4K video at 60fps on both the front and back cameras
- 4K Live Photos at every zoom level, with clips that now last six seconds instead of three
- Oppo’s Natural Tone 3.0 engine for better skin tones in portraits
- Support for the OPPO Bubble, a small magnetic screen that lets you frame selfies with the rear cameras. It costs CNY 399 in China.
5. Battery and charging
- 8,000mAh battery (7,765mAh rated), the largest ever in a Reno phone
- Silicon-carbon cell with 15% silicon, which packs more power into a slim body
- 80W SuperVOOC and 80W UFCS wired charging
- Works with other fast chargers too, including 55W PPS and 44W UFCS
Charging is wired only. Oppo does not list wireless or reverse charging, and it has not shared an official full-charge time.
6. Design and durability
- Size: 157.64 x 75.27 x 8.28mm
- Weight: 206g (the cat edition is 8.47mm thick and weighs 208g)
- Metal frame with a glass back
- IP66, IP68, IP69, and IP69K ratings for dust and water protection
The Reno 17 comes in Ice Moon White and Cocoa Brown. It also comes in a light blue special edition called Qiyu Miao (some outlets call it Encounter Cat), with a cat design that floats inside the glass back.
Other features include an under-display fingerprint sensor, face unlock, an IR blaster for controlling your TV or AC, NFC, and stereo speakers.
7. Connectivity
- 5G with dual nano-SIM support
- Wi-Fi 6
- Bluetooth 5.4
- USB-C 2.0
8. Software
The Reno 17 runs ColorOS 17 based on Android 17. You can read what Android 17 brings to your phone and check which phones are getting it.
Oppo has not shared an update promise for the China model. For comparison, the global Reno 16 gets five years of Android updates and six years of security patches.
Oppo Reno 17 vs Oppo Reno 16
Oppo launched the China Reno 16 on May 25, 2026. Here is how the two China models compare:
| Spec | Oppo Reno 17 (China) | Oppo Reno 16 (China) | 
|---|---|---|
| China launch | November 16, 2026 | May 25, 2026 | 
| Starting price | CNY3,599 (8GB + 256GB) | CNY3,499 (12GB + 256GB) | 
| Display | 6.56-inch OLED, 120Hz, 6,000 nits peak | 6.32-inch OLED, 120Hz, 3,600 nits peak | 
| Chipset | Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 | Dimensity 8550 Super | 
| RAM | 8GB or 12GB | 12GB or 16GB | 
| Main camera | 50MP with OIS | 200MP with OIS | 
| Telephoto | 50MP periscope, 3.5x | 50MP periscope, 3.5x | 
| Battery | 8,000mAh | 6,700mAh | 
| Charging | 80W wired | 80W wired | 
| Weight | 206g | 188g | 
| IP rating | IP66, IP68, IP69, IP69K | IP68, IP69K | 
| Software at launch | ColorOS 17, Android 17 | ColorOS 16, Android 16 | 
What you gain with the Reno 17:
- 1,300mAh more battery, about 19% more than the Reno 16
- A bigger screen with a much brighter peak
- More water and dust ratings
- Android 17 out of the box and 4K Live Photos at every zoom level
What you give up:
- The 200MP main camera
- The smaller, lighter body (the Reno 17 is 18g heavier)
- Speed, since the Dimensity 8550 Super scores much higher in chip tests
- Some RAM on the base model, which drops to 8GB while the price goes up by CNY100
For you in Nigeria, the more useful comparison is the global version of the Reno 16. It already uses the Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 and a 50MP main camera. That makes the China Reno 17 a global Reno 16 with a bigger screen and battery.
Pick the Reno 17 if battery life and a big screen matter most. Pick the Reno 16 if you want a smaller phone with a sharper main camera and more speed. If you want a compact phone with a 200MP camera on the newer generation, look at the Reno 17 Pro.
Where you can buy the Oppo Reno 17
- China: Oppo Mall, JD.com, Tmall, and Oppo’s other authorized stores, from November 20, 2026
- Nigeria: Oppo has not started sales here. As of November 18, 2026, we found no Reno 17 listing on Oppo Nigeria, Jumia, Slot, Konga, or Jiji. Watch Oppo Nigeria’s official pages for launch news.
If a Reno 17 shows up in Nigeria before Oppo launches it here, it is a grey import of the China model. Check these before you pay:
- Network bands: The China model lacks 4G bands 7 and 20. Industry data shows MTN uses these bands for 4G in Nigeria, so you may get a weaker MTN signal. The phone does support band 3 and 5G on n78. Check with your network before you buy.
- Google apps: China models ship without Google apps. Users report that you can switch on Google services in settings, but features like Google Wallet may not work.
- Software: The China software comes with Chinese apps first, though you can set English as your language.
- Warranty: Expect no local warranty. Ask Oppo Nigeria before you buy.
If you can wait, your best move is to hold on for Oppo Nigeria’s official launch. You get a phone set up for Nigerian networks, with a local warranty.

articles.title: Microsoft thinks it can make agentic AI work for the whole company, not just you
articles.text:
While there's been a tremendous amount of excitement surrounding agentic AI over the last year or two, the vast majority of the attention has focused on individual use of these tools. Everywhere you look, it seems, you can find stories of people who have done amazing work on their own with agentic AI.
Scaling the technology to groups and large companies, on the other hand, hasn't always been as easy. In fact, a number of stories have circulated lately about companies that haven't seen the return they expected on their agentic AI investments.
At the same time, much of the popular press on agentic AI has focused on high-profile model providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic and the tools they make, as well as others like Perplexity, Muse, and OpenClaw that tend to be seen primarily as tools for individuals.
When it comes to the enterprise, however, there's little doubt that Microsoft is still king of the hill – a fact that was dramatically reinforced last week when Outlook, Teams and other Microsoft services broke down and essentially halted productivity for businesses of all sizes for about an entire day.
Perhaps appropriately, then, at this year's Microsoft Ignite event in San Francisco, the company intentionally brought the agentic AI story to the enterprise, with the specific goal of addressing the key issues that arise when you try to scale a personal productivity tool to a group-focused enterprise level.
Through a wide-ranging set of announcements, the company tackled group co-working, specialized tools for different departments, leveraging corporate data and context to improve the quality of AI output and, most importantly, cost.
At a core level, Microsoft has expanded Copilot with several new modes and broader capabilities for both individuals and groups. In fact, the company even went so far as to call Copilot the new operating system for work, which certainly raises some interesting questions for the future.
Copilot Workspaces, for example, lets individuals and groups create long-running agentic workflows that can be used and edited by multiple people. If a group within a department wants to work collectively on a project, they can integrate Office documents (which are now directly editable in Copilot), Teams threads and more into a dynamic project that agents can modify and update.
The new Today option in Copilot, which just entered private preview, brings a proactive agent to individuals, reminding them of tasks they need to complete, documents to edit, emails to send and more. Both of these modes also have new auto-routing tools that can automatically send different tasks to the most appropriate model. For frontier-level clients, a new Autopilot will take these kinds of proactive steps even further.
To deliver these capabilities, the company has built an increasingly sophisticated and complex set of software layers and interconnection tools that let organizations customize and optimize agentic tools for their specific needs.
The newly announced Microsoft IQ, for example, brings together Work IQ, Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ and Web IQ into a comprehensive contextual layer that off-the-shelf and custom-built agents can tap into to create new business workflows, enhance existing processes and more. Though it sounds similar, it does not replace the Microsoft Graph. Instead, it adds an abstraction layer above Graph that's specifically designed for interactions with agentic tools.
Another critical capability of Microsoft IQ is a set of more than 350 "plug-ins" that serve as connectors between a wide variety of applications and data types. These matter because they help ease the seemingly insurmountable challenge of cleaning and prepping data stores for use with AI tools.
Virtually every organization that has had success with agentic AI, as well as many creators of agentic AI tools, has talked about how critical clean, custom data is to getting the most value from these tools.
Doing that work, however, has often proven more challenging than many organizations expected. With well-constructed plug-ins, many of those challenges can be removed because the import process can automatically put data into the proper formats for ingestion. On top of these connection tools, Microsoft also announced a new partnership with Salesforce called Copilotforce, which can integrate data and skills into the Microsoft IQ environment via MCP connections to Salesforce. For many organizations, these types of connector plug-ins could be a significant game changer.
Equally important to Microsoft's enterprise-wide agentic story is an extended range of its own smaller, specialized models in the MAI (Microsoft AI) family. The new MAI-Code-2 model, now available through GitHub, is claimed to offer 90% of the coding capabilities of today's latest frontier models at a fraction of the size. This, in turn, means lower token costs and the potential to move more workloads on-prem.
Even more important was the launch of the new Microsoft-Decision-1.1 tool, an intelligent model router that takes requests from an agent, breaks them into smaller pieces and sends each piece to the most appropriate and cost-effective model. This capability is an absolutely essential element of a hybrid AI environment that can work across the cloud, on-prem data centers and edge/client devices. While multiple other companies are working on similar routing capabilities, and there's still more work to be done, Microsoft's massive presence in the enterprise is bound to make this a very important tool moving forward.
In addition to software, Microsoft made a few AI infrastructure announcements on the hardware side. Notably, the company debuted its new Arm-based Cobalt 200 CPUs, which power Cobalt 200 virtual machines that offer 50% better performance on agentic workloads than the first-generation chips.
Microsoft also made an array of important security announcements, including additions to its Perception security stack, an integrated Security Operations Center and a new AI transparency initiative designed to give organizations more insight into how AI tools function and are governed.
The key takeaway from it all is that Microsoft is starting to fully leverage its privileged position within businesses around the world to extend agentic AI from the individual to the organization. It's not a transition that's going to occur overnight, but it's clear that an increasingly wide range of the tools needed to scale these efforts are starting to come into place.
Bob O'Donnell is the founder and chief analyst of TECHnalysis Research, LLC a technology consulting firm that provides strategic consulting and market research services to the technology industry and professional financial community. You can follow him on Twitter @bobodtech

articles.title: From voice cloning to “digital eugenics”: disability leaders unpack how AI is improving and damaging accessibility | BetaKit
articles.text:
In many ways, AI has made things better for people living with disabilities. In others, the technology has exacerbated existing problems.
Speakers at Access to Success’ inaugural Canadian Disability Tech Summit in Toronto on Wednesday afternoon unpacked some of the most interesting ways that AI is improving accessibility, how its underlying nature is deepening existing divides, and how we ought to leverage this tech to build a more inclusive world.
“Disability has always been a driver of innovation.”
Pete Horsley, Remarkable
Panellist Max Lemmens, general manager of Canada at the UK-founded, US-based voice AI firm ElevenLabs, noted that AI has made it easier to not only create but restore things. Some of ElevenLabs’ work has focused on giving a voice to people living with permanent voice loss.
“Historically, people who’ve lost their voice have been stuck with what I’ll call the Stephen Hawking effect, where it’s a very robotic voice that’s not really theirs,” Lemmens said. “For many people, their voice is their identity.”
To help address this problem, Lemmens claimed that, to date, ElevenLabs has helped more than 11,000 people regain access to their voice by applying AI to old recordings.
Fellow panellist Pete Horsley, founder of Australian disability tech accelerator Remarkable, highlighted some of the capabilities that Calgary-based brain-computer interface startup Possibility Neurotechnologies has demonstrated in his country as another helpful use-case. Possibility aims to allow users to control devices using their thoughts.
RELATED: Accessibility isn’t “a niche problem,” says organizer of inaugural assistive tech conference
“For one child that we tested the technology [on] within Australia, they only [previously] had a signal for yes … [Possibility was] able to give this child the ability to say no, and they actually said no a whole lot more after that,” Horsley said to audience laughter.
Tom Butcher is a senior advisor and ambassador at Austrian disability research organization Zero Project. He said the World Institute on Disability’s work using AI to compile resources on where to find wheelchairs, interpreters, and accessible shelters during times of crisis is an example of how AI can break down barriers.
However, as panellist Jutta Treviranus pointed out, one of the biggest underlying challenges is that AI is “statistically representative.” Modern AI and large language models rely on statistical pattern recognition, often amplifying the biases and trends present in their training data.
Treviranus, professor at OCAD University and director of the Inclusive Design Research Centre, said that since AI chooses “the average, the middle, the majority, [of] the most popular … many of [its] determinations regarding people with disabilities are wrong right from the get-go.”
“What we’re creating is this almost digital eugenics.”
Jutta Treviranus,
OCAD and IDRC
“Disability is a universal condition,” Treviranus added. “We will all experience it, and we all know that within this room. But, for whatever reason, we haven’t considered that. What we’re creating is this almost digital eugenics where we’re removing difference, we’re removing comfort with difference, and we’re not addressing that diversity that is the key to our human survival.”
Treviranus is particularly frustrated that “we are now going into what is the disruption of our lifetime, or this generation, but we’re not disrupting; we are basically automating, accelerating, and amplifying past patterns.”
People in the disability community are often told to just use these AI tools. But in practice, they can “work the worst for people [who] need them the most” due to their algorithms and often limited data on users with disabilities, Treviranus said.
Treviranus believes the solution involves re-engineering those algorithms and enabling on-device AI that can make use of individual data to better serve members of the disability community. Lemmens thinks that AI trained on synthetic data based on disability-focused datasets like the one Treviranus has spent years collecting could also help fill this need.
RELATED: Toronto gets a new hub for accessibility innovation
Lemmens does not see avoiding AI as an option. He believes the best approach involves pushing things forward, recognizing the tech’s shortcomings, and addressing them “head on.”
Horsley stressed that “disability is not about some of us; it’s about all of us,” and encouraged people living with disabilities to play an active role in building the world they’d like to inhabit. “Disability has always been a driver of innovation,” he said. “When you don’t have a world that’s creative for your needs, you’re always thinking about, what is the solution for that?”
Given where we now sit in the AI era, Horsley sees a unique chance to build better systems “from the bottom up,” rather than retrofit for accessibility, which is typically costlier. Horsley said Remarkable has seen “a massive, massive uptick” in the number of founders with disabilities launching businesses using AI tools, and urged attendees to follow suit. “There are huge opportunities here to create your future in [this] space, so go ahead and do it.”
Feature image courtesy Access to Success. Photo by Tim Fraser of KITE Studio.

articles.title: Hackers expõem dados de clientes de Visa, Mastercard e JPMorgan
articles.text:
O JPMorgan Chase, a Visa e a Mastercard confirmaram que fornecedores terceirizados foram alvo de incidentes de cibersegurança. As declarações foram divulgadas após o grupo de ransomware n0n ameaçar publicar dados que afirma ter roubado das instituições financeiras. A Visa reconheceu o problema envolvendo um prestador de serviços na região da Ásia-Pacífico, mas ressaltou que seus próprios sistemas não foram afetados.
No caso do JPMorgan, o banco informou que os invasores podem ter acessado dados de marketing armazenados nos sistemas de fornecedores. As informações eventualmente expostas incluem nomes e endereços de e-mail de clientes. A instituição afirmou que entrará em contato diretamente com as pessoas afetadas.
A confirmação das empresas dá novos contornos às alegações do n0n, que publicou nomes das instituições em seu site de vazamento na rede Tor. O grupo ameaça divulgar os arquivos caso não receba um resgate, mas a autenticidade de todo o material ainda não foi comprovada de forma independente.
JPMorgan confirma ataque a fornecedores terceirizados
- Em declaração à Reuters, um porta-voz do JPMorgan Chase afirmou que prestadores de serviços da instituição foram alvo de ataque cibernético. Segundo a investigação inicial do banco, os invasores acessaram determinados dados de marketing mantidos por essas empresas;
- O material pode incluir nomes e endereços de e-mail de alguns clientes. O JPMorgan disse que notificará diretamente as pessoas afetadas, mas não detalhou quantos fornecedores foram atingidos nem quantos clientes podem ter tido informações expostas;
- A instituição também esclareceu que o incidente não tem relação com a instabilidade registrada em seus serviços no início da semana. Na ocasião, um erro de software provocou problemas no processamento de transações e também afetou outros bancos;
- O esclarecimento é importante porque, após a interrupção, o JPMorgan havia atribuído os problemas a uma falha técnica e não a uma ação criminosa. Agora, o banco confirma um incidente distinto, envolvendo empresas terceirizadas.
Leia mais:
- Ataque com IA leva Comissão Europeia a tirar aplicativos do ar
- Brasil concentra ataque que roubou dados de um milhão de cartões
- iFood sofre ataque hacker, que expõe dados de clientes e entregadores
Visa e Mastercard também relatam problemas com fornecedores
A Visa afirmou estar ciente das alegações do grupo n0n e confirmou incidente envolvendo um prestador de serviços terceirizado na região da Ásia-Pacífico.
Em declaração reproduzida pela Reuters, a empresa disse que seus sistemas não foram envolvidos nem afetados. Também afirmou que nenhum dado de pagamento, como números de cartões, foi comprometido.
A análise da Reuters sobre os arquivos publicados pelo grupo identificou planilhas com milhares de supostos endereços de e-mail, números de telefone e informações relacionadas a campanhas de marketing da Visa. Os registros parecem se concentrar em mercados da Ásia-Pacífico, incluindo Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japão, Filipinas, Singapura e Austrália. A agência, porém, não conseguiu verificar a autenticidade dos dados.
A Mastercard também confirmou ter sido informada sobre incidente em fornecedor terceirizado. Segundo a empresa, uma quantidade limitada de endereços de e-mail de clientes inscritos em um programa específico de benefícios foi exposta.
A companhia classificou as informações como dados que não envolvem pagamentos e afirmou que não houve impacto na rede de transações nem na possibilidade de os clientes utilizarem seus cartões.
O que o grupo n0n diz ter roubado?
O grupo de extorsão cibernética n0n reivindicou os ataques na segunda-feira (16). Em uma das mensagens, afirmou ter obtido registros de relacionamento com clientes de cartões, incluindo centenas de milhares de interações de campanhas e endereços de e-mail de dezenas de milhares de pessoas.
Uma análise da Reuters identificou no material publicado pelo grupo o que parecem ser 124 endereços de e-mail de funcionários de bancos e mais de 16 mil endereços de clientes. Alguns registros também contêm números de telefone e códigos postais.
A agência ressalta, entretanto, que não conseguiu confirmar a autenticidade dessas informações. O JPMorgan também não comentou especificamente os dados divulgados pelos criminosos.
O n0n ameaçou publicar o material caso não recebesse o pagamento exigido dentro de 48 horas. Até o momento, não há confirmação independente de que o grupo tenha conseguido acessar diretamente os sistemas das três instituições ou de que todos os arquivos apresentados sejam legítimos.
Quem está por trás do grupo n0n?
O n0n é um grupo relativamente novo, identificado pela primeira vez em setembro. Sua atuação combina roubo de informações e ransomware, estratégia conhecida como dupla extorsão: os criminosos extraem dados das vítimas e também podem criptografar sistemas para pressionar pelo pagamento de um resgate.
Pesquisadores da empresa de inteligência de ameaças SOCRadar identificaram possíveis métodos utilizados pelo grupo para invadir organizações. Entre eles, estão credenciais comprometidas, chaves de acesso à nuvem expostas e infraestruturas vulneráveis de acesso remoto.
A investigação também aponta para o uso frequente de ferramentas de inteligência artificial (IA). Segundo os pesquisadores, há indícios de que agentes de programação com IA foram empregados no desenvolvimento e na manutenção de ferramentas utilizadas nos ataques.
Já a empresa de segurança ZeroFox classifica o n0n como um agente de ameaças oportunista, motivado financeiramente e com sofisticação técnica entre baixa e moderada. Ainda não se sabe qual é o tamanho da operação, onde o grupo atua ou quem são seus responsáveis.
De acordo com registros da Ransomnews, o n0n já contabiliza 365 vítimas. Entre as organizações mencionadas estão CarNow, Patagonia e Wise Advisory Group. O grupo também apresenta concentração de ataques contra o setor farmacêutico, com dezenas de vítimas dessa indústria registradas pelos analistas.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Meta now sells 3D movies on Quest VR headsets
articles.text:
Meta now offers more than 150 3D movies that you can buy or rent to watch in VR on its Quest 3 and 3S headsets, the company announced today. The movies are available in Meta’s TV app and include titles like Avatar, Spider-Man: Far From Home, Jurassic World Rebirth, Wicked: For Good, and a Billie Eilish concert film co-directed by Eilish and James Cameron.
Meta now sells 3D movies on Quest VR headsets
Use your Quest 3 to catch films like Avatar and Jurassic World Rebirth in 3D.
The company suggests watching movies in a Theater view that’s rolling out with a new Meta Quest update. Theater view “provides a big screen and dims your surroundings to create a cozy, personal cinema experience,” Meta says.
Meta promises that the library will “keep growing, with thousands of titles and international availability coming” when it launches its VR Glasses next spring. If you’re a Disney Plus subscriber, you can also watch 3D movies on Meta Quest hardware in the Disney Plus app thanks to an update rolled out earlier this month.

articles.title: Mehr als ein Jahrzehnt unerkannt: Gravierende Sicherheitslücke in Nginx entdeckt
articles.text:
Mehr als ein Jahrzehnt unerkannt: Gravierende Sicherheitslücke in Nginx entdeckt
Eine Reihe von Cybersecurity-Unternehmen hat eine Sicherheitslücke in Nginx entdeckt. Dabei handelt es sich um die Webserver-Software, die von zahlreichen Webseiten genutzt wird. Laut „Built with it“ sind es mittlerweile mehr als 65 Millionen Seiten, darunter die Webauftritte von Mastercard, Morgan Stanley und Logitech.
Wie gravierend ist die Nginx-Sicherheitslücke?
Zu den Sicherheitsforscher:innen, die den Fehler gefunden haben, zählen unter anderem die Expert:innen von Wiz Research, Ikotas Labs und Metnir. Wie Wiz schreibt, handelt es sich im Grunde um zwei kritische Sicherheitslücken, die aber dieselben Auswirkungen haben. Werden sie ausgenutzt, können Server kompromittiert werden. Angreifer:innen haben dann die Möglichkeit, Schadcode aus der Ferne auszuführen, Daten zu stehlen, die betriebenen Webseiten zu verändern oder deren Betrieb zu stören.
Eine der Sicherheitslücken mit der Kennung CVE-2026-123633 soll sich schon mehr als sechs Jahre unbemerkt in Nginx verbergen, die andere sogar zehn Jahre (CVE-2026-123007). Wiz schreibt dazu: „Beide Fehler sind Speichersicherheitsfehler bei Nginx Handhabung von HTTP/2-Traffic. Bei CVE-2026-123633 wird der für eine Verbindung benötigte Speicher schon freigegeben, obwohl er noch genutzt wird, wodurch ein Use-after-Free entsteht. Bei CVE-2026-123007 sorgt eine falsche Flow-Kontrolle für eine ungültige Speicherkopierung.“
Laut Wiz wurden die Fehler in Nginx nicht allein von den Sicherheitsforscher:innen gefunden. Sie haben zunächst ihren eigenen KI-Harness Wiz Atlas genutzt, um die Probleme aufzuspüren. Im Anschluss nutzten sie Gemini 4 Carbon und ChatGPT 5.6 Sol, um die Auswirkungen der beiden Sicherheitslücken zu validieren. Erst im Anschluss wurden die Erkenntnisse an F5, das Unternehmen hinter Nginx, weitergeleitet.
F5 hat eng mit den Sicherheitsforscher:innen zusammengearbeitet, um Lösungen für beide Probleme zu finden. Nicht einmal einen Monat nach der Entdeckung stehen jetzt für beide Lücken Patches bereit. Dementsprechend sollten alle Nginx-Betreiber:innen ein Update der Webserver-Software anstoßen. Andernfalls steigt mit fortlaufender Zeit das Risiko, dass Angreifer:innen die ungepatchten Lücken ausnutzen.

articles.title: Horizon Zero Dawn Remastered sur PS5 tombe à un prix difficile à ignorer
articles.text:
Horizon Zero Dawn Remastered est actuellement proposé à 18,74 € sur PS5 chez Cdiscount. Affiché 49,99 € à sa sortie, il se trouve en général entre 30 et 40 € dans le commerce.
Bienvenue dans un monde dominé par les machines
Dans un futur lointain, l’humanité a régressé à l’état de tribus, et la Terre est peuplée d’immenses machines qui ressemblent à des animaux. C’est dans ce monde qu’on suit Aloy, une jeune chasseuse rejetée par les siens, partie à la recherche de ses origines. Sorti en 2017, le jeu de Guerrilla s’est imposé comme l’une des grandes réussites de PlayStation, avec plus de 24 millions d’exemplaires vendus.
Cette version Remastered, confiée à Nixxes avec Guerrilla, offre une vraie cure de jouvence au jeu original. Végétation plus dense, visages retravaillés, nouvelles animations pour les dialogues et plus de dix heures de répliques réenregistrées, l’ensemble se rapproche beaucoup de ce qu’on a pu voir dans Horizon Forbidden West. La manette DualSense est aussi mieux exploitée, avec des gâchettes adaptatives qui donnent plus de corps au tir à l’arc. Et l’extension The Frozen Wilds est incluse.
Le bon moment pour partir à la chasse ?
Le jeu était sorti à 49,99 € fin octobre 2024. À 18,74 €, il coûte donc près de trois fois moins cher qu’à son lancement. En comparaison, il est actuellement affiché à 33,08 € chez Carrefour.
Avec un 8/10, notre test salue surtout le travail de Nixxes Software, qui donne au jeu l’allure d’une vraie production PS5. Textures, végétation, éclairages, visages, tout a été repris dans la lignée d’Horizon Forbidden West, et le mode Performance assure 60 images par seconde sans sacrifier le rendu. Le gameplay est un peu moins riche que dans la suite, mais il reste efficace, et la beauté du monde d’Aloy donne envie d’explorer chaque recoin. Si vous possédez déjà la version PS4, sachez qu’une mise à niveau vers le Remastered est proposée à 10 €.

articles.title: Physical AI startup Humyn Labs raises $47M in Series A
articles.text:
Physical AI startup Humyn Labs raises $47M in Series A
Humyn Labs said it will use the funds across three areas: building deployment-readiness infrastructure in Brazil, South Korea and India; and expanding its R&D and market presence in San Francisco, London and Seoul.
Humyn Labs, a physical AI research and deployment startup, has raised $47 million in a Series A funding round comprising equity and debt.
The Bengaluru-headquartered startup raised $26 million in equity funding led by Accel, with participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Finserv Intelligence (through Bajaj Finance), Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, Jump Trading LLC and angel investor Anita Pramoda, former CFO of Epic.
The $21 million venture debt round was led by Lighthouse Canton, with participation from Trifecta Capital.
Founded in February 2026 by Manish Agarwal and Ishank Gupta, Humyn Labs prepares physical AI systems for real-world deployment by translating human experience into physical understanding for robots. The startup's proprietary capture devices record how people perform specific tasks across factories, warehouses, farms and homes. Its end-to-end data engine then converts these recordings into labelled, training-ready datasets with verified provenance across sight, sound, motion and touch.
Humyn Labs will use the funds across three areas: building deployment-readiness infrastructure in Brazil, South Korea and India; and expanding its R&D and market presence in San Francisco, London and Seoul.
“Physical AI will only be as good as the real-world data it learns from. This funding will help us strengthen our research, build trust with labs and enterprises, and expand our global presence. With a $10 billion opportunity emerging in data infrastructure, we aim to build a $1 billion annual revenue business and establish ourselves as a global leader in the space,” said Manish Agarwal, Co-founder, Humyn Labs.
According to Humyn Labs, it has surpassed $50 million in annualised revenue within six months of operations. It works with frontier AI labs, robotics companies and world-model developers, and runs its own capture and enrichment operations across 20+ countries in Latin America, East Asia, and South and Southeast Asia.
“A robot does not learn a job from the internet. It learns it from the person who has done it for twenty years, on the floor where it will be done. We bring the model lab and the site operator onto that floor together, so every deployment teaches the next model, and the world’s factories, farms and warehouses become the training se,” said Ishank Gupta, Co-founder, Humyn Labs.

articles.title: Five warning signs of ransomware breach before encryption or data theft
articles.text:
Ask many IT teams how they would recognize ransomware, and the answer is still “when files start changing extensions.” By then, the intrusion may already include credential theft, privilege escalation, defense evasion, recovery sabotage, lateral movement and data exfiltration.
Encryption is often a late-stage action, not the beginning of the attack. In data-extortion attacks it never happens at all: the operators steal data and threaten to leak it without encrypting anything.
Recent attacks against on-premises SharePoint servers illustrate that sequence. After exploiting internet-facing systems, operators used stolen credentials and legitimate administration tools to move through victim environments before deploying ransomware.
The practical lesson is simple: defenders need to detect the behaviors that precede encryption, not only the encryptor itself.
Acronis Cyber Platform (formerly Acronis Cyber Protect Cloud) natively integrates cybersecurity, data protection and endpoint management through a single agent, console and policy framework.
When the relevant capabilities are licensed and enabled, Acronis Active Protection, EDR, MDR and XDR can help detect, contain and recover from ransomware-related activity before widespread encryption occurs.
Five high-value signals deserve immediate attention:
- Defense tampering: Attempts to stop security services, modify protection agents, load vulnerable drivers or clear event logs.
- Privilege escalation and lateral movement: Unexpected privileged accounts, remote-execution tools spreading across hosts or unusual server-to-server remote access.
- Data exfiltration: Unusual outbound transfers from systems that do not normally upload large volumes of data.
- Recovery sabotage: Deletion of shadow copies, backup catalogs or recovery options with tools such as vssadmin.exe, wbadmin.exe or bcdedit.exe.
- Pre-encryption file behavior: Rapid file enumeration, repeated read-write-rename activity and encryption-like changes across local or network locations.
How do ransomware gangs typically gain initial access to corporate networks?
Ransomware attacks rarely begin with the ransomware payload itself. Operators first need an initial foothold, and common entry paths include exploitation of vulnerable internet-facing systems, abuse of stolen credentials, and social engineering.
An unpatched externally accessible service can provide a route into the environment, while compromised credentials can allow an attacker to enter through legitimate remote-access or cloud services.
Social engineering adds another path by targeting users and the processes around identity and access.
Once attackers establish access, the initial compromise can become the starting point for credential theft, privilege escalation, defense evasion and lateral movement.
Organizations should reduce unnecessary internet exposure, prioritize patching of high-risk systems, strengthen identity and access controls, and protect email and collaboration channels.
Monitoring endpoints for suspicious post-compromise behavior provides another layer when preventive controls do not stop the initial intrusion.
The article already establishes these pre-encryption stages as important signals defenders should detect.
Acronis Cyber Platform supports this layered approach from one platform.
On the detection and response side, endpoint protection, built on Acronis Active Protection and EDR, identifies and contains malicious activity once an attacker gains a foothold, while email security and XDR extend that detection to the attack surface beyond the endpoint.
On the prevention side, vulnerability assessment and patch management reduce exploitable exposure, security posture management and security policy management close configuration gaps, and data loss prevention limits what an intruder can take.
Together these create a progression from reducing opportunities for initial compromise to detecting and responding to activity after one occurs.
What are the warning signs of ransomware before encryption or data theft?
Encryption happens late in a ransomware attack, and data-extortion attacks may skip it entirely. Earlier warning signs include defense tampering, privilege escalation, data exfiltration, recovery sabotage and pre-encryption file activity.
Learn how to detect each signal, respond quickly and recover.
Try for Free
How does ransomware protection prevent an attack instead of only detecting it?
Stopping ransomware is rarely about a single control. Organizations need to reduce the opportunities attackers have to get in, detect and contain malicious activity when they do, and have a reliable way to recover if systems or data are affected.
That makes prevention, detection and response, and recovery different parts of the same ransomware defense strategy.
Acronis brings those layers together in one platform.
On the prevention side, patch management reduces exploitable exposure, security posture management and unified endpoint and security policy management close configuration gaps before an attacker can use them, data loss prevention limits what can leave the environment, and data protection with immutable backups removes the leverage that recovery sabotage depends on.
On the detection and response side, Active Protection, EDR, XDR and email security identify and contain malicious activity across endpoints, email and the wider environment. Integrated backup and recovery then provide the path to restoring affected systems and data.
That last layer is critical for getting operations back online, but it does not undo data theft, an important distinction in double-extortion attacks.
How do detection tools stop ransomware before it encrypts files?
Ransomware rarely goes straight to encryption. Endpoint detection tools can spot the suspicious activity that comes first, from attempts to disable defenses to lateral movement and unusual file activity. The table below breaks down five signals worth watching, the controls that can address them and how Acronis supports each response.
| Signal | Recommended control | Acronis implementation | 
| Recovery sabotage | Alert on recovery-tool abuse; stop the malicious process; maintain off-host, immutable recovery points. | Active Protection blocks ransomware behavior and restores affected files. Self-protection helps defend Acronis components and backups. Immutable Acronis Cloud Storage protects eligible recovery points. | 
| Defense tampering | Use agent self-protection, exploit prevention, vulnerable-driver controls and off-host logging. | Self-protection helps prevent unauthorized changes to the Acronis agent. EDR/XDR and SIEM integrations add incident visibility, subject to configuration. | 
| Privilege and lateral movement | Monitor privileged-account changes and remote-execution activity; isolate affected endpoints. | EDR/XDR correlates activity across workloads, presents the attack chain and supports endpoint isolation and response actions. | 
| Data exfiltration | Monitor unusual data flows and apply controls appropriate to systems and users, based on least-privilege principle. | XDR correlates endpoint activity with supported telemetry sources. Acronis DLP controls sensitive-data transfers on supported endpoints. | 
| Pre-encryption file behavior | Use behavioral detection and automated rollback; protect local data, network folders and servers. | Active Protection uses behavioral and AI/ML-based detection to stop ransomware and restore affected files. Network folder and server-side protection extend coverage where supported. | 
What should an organization do immediately after detecting ransomware?
The first actions should limit spread, preserve evidence and create a safe path to recovery. Organizations should pre-authorize automated actions for clearly defined, high-severity conditions and test them before an incident.
- Isolate the affected workload while preserving the management channel needed for investigation.
- Stop malicious processes and quarantine confirmed malicious files.
- Protect evidence, including process trees, command lines, network connections and relevant logs.
- Identify and disable the compromised account, token or remote-access path.
- Patch the exploited vulnerability or close the exposed service after containment.
- Restore affected files or workloads from a known-good recovery point, then validate the recovered environment before reconnecting it.
- Escalate to incident-response, legal, privacy, insurance and communications stakeholders according to the organization’s response plan.
Acronis EDR and XDR support investigation, isolation and response actions from the incident view. Recovery actions depend on the applicable backup and recovery licenses, available recovery points and configuration.
Acronis MDR by Acronis TRU adds 24/7 expert monitoring, investigation and response; managed remediation and recovery are included in the Advanced service tier within the agreed scope and permissions.
Turn pre-encryption signals into tested controls
The value of an early ransomware warning depends on what happens next. The five signals above can give defenders an opportunity to contain an attack before encryption spreads, but only if the response is already defined and tested.
Whether it is an attempt to delete shadow copies, data exfiltration, unexpected remote execution or a sudden burst of encryption-like file activity, suspicious behavior should trigger a clear containment and recovery plan.
Acronis Cyber Platform can connect prevention, detection, response and recovery through one integrated platform. Capabilities vary by edition, deployment model, configuration and licensing.
See how Acronis Cyber Platform helps detect and contain ransomware, protect recovery points, and restore client operations faster.

Iliyan Gerov is a cybersecurity product marketing leader at Acronis, where he focuses on EDR, XDR, MDR, emerging AI-driven security technologies, email and collaboration app security, DLP, and security awareness. He works at the intersection of cybersecurity, product strategy, and go-to-market, translating complex security challenges and technology trends into practical insights for businesses and service providers.

articles.title: Black Friday CyberGhost à 1,99 €/mois : quel montant prévoir au moment de payer ?
articles.text:
CyberGhost sort son offre Black Friday, mais un détail mérite votre attention
CyberGhost affiche son abonnement VPN à 1,99 €/mois pour le Black Friday. Mais derrière ce prix d'appel, la formule impose un paiement en une fois dont le montant mérite attention.
CyberGhost à 1,99 €/mois : une facture de 55,72 € pour 28 mois
Le VPN CyberGhostest proposé à 1,99 €/mois dans le cadre de son offre de fin d'année. Mais attention, ce montant ne correspond pas à un prélèvement mensuel. Pour bénéficier de ce tarif, il faut souscrire un abonnement de deux ans, auquel s'ajoutent quatre mois offerts. La durée totale atteint ainsi 28 mois, pour un paiement initial affiché de 55,72 €.
C'est précisément ce détail qui mérite d'être vérifié avant de valider la commande. Le prix mensuel annoncé correspond à une moyenne calculée sur toute la période, et non à la somme réellement débitée chaque mois. Le règlement s'effectue en une seule fois. Par ailleurs, le montant final peut dépendre de la TVA applicable dans le pays de facturation et des éventuelles options ajoutées au panier.
Sept appareils protégés et 45 jours pour demander un remboursement
Au-delà du prix, CyberGhost propose un ensemble de fonctionnalités destinées à sécuriser les connexions quotidiennes. Son réseau couvre plus de 100 pays, ce qui permet de choisir une localisation différente selon les besoins. Le service masque l'adresse IP réelle et chiffre le trafic internet pour limiter l'exposition des données personnelles, notamment sur les réseaux Wi-Fi publics.
L'abonnement autorise jusqu'à sept connexions simultanées. Il peut ainsi couvrir plusieurs équipements sans devoir souscrire un contrat pour chaque appareil. Les applications sont compatibles avec les principaux systèmes d'exploitation et navigateurs.
CyberGhost met également en avant plusieurs possibilités :
- Des serveurs dédiés à certaines activités, notamment le streaming et le téléchargement P2P ;
- Une sélection automatique du meilleur emplacement ;
- Une politique de confidentialité sans journalisation de l'activité en ligne ;
- Une assistance disponible 24 h/24 et 7 j/7.
Certaines protections supplémentaires restent toutefois payantes. L'adresse IP dédiée et la Windows Security Suite, qui comprend notamment un antivirus et des outils anti-malware, sont proposées sous forme d'options.
Un dernier point concerne la garantie de remboursement de 45 jours, applicable à cette formule longue durée selon les conditions du fournisseur. Elle permet de tester le service, mais ne transforme pas l'abonnement en essai gratuit : le montant est bien réglé au moment de la souscription.
Au final, CyberGhost affiche un tarif mensuel attractif, mais les 61,32 € à régler d'avance constituent le véritable prix à prendre en compte. La durée de 28 mois et les sept connexions simultanées rendent cette formule intéressante pour un usage régulier, à condition d'accepter cet engagement financier.

articles.title: « Improbable et grave » : l’IA a découvert une faille planétaire dans un langage informatique « dont nous dépendons tous »
articles.text:
Une nouvelle faille critique fait trembler le monde de l’informatique. Ce 17 novembre, la start-up californienne Calif a dévoilé une brèche dans le cœur du code de Java, un langage de programmation omniprésent dans le monde entier. Baptisée Java4Shell, la faille permet à un pirate de prendre le contrôle de certains serveurs à distance. Elle touche surtout les serveurs des entreprises équipés de processeurs Intel ou AMD récents. Les puces ARM, présentes dans la plupart des smartphones, ne sont pas concernées.
À lire aussi : « Un faux sentiment de secret » – face à l’IA, Google prend une décision qui divise le monde de la cybersécurité
Une faille découverte par l’IA… en une heure
L’affaire a commencé il y a quelques semaines quand Quang Luong, chercheur chez Calif, a décidé de se pencher sur le code de Java. Conscient de la difficulté de la tâche, il s’est tourné vers Codex, l’assistant d’OpenAI propulsé par GPT-6 Cyber, un modèle d’IA spécialisé dans la recherche de failles.
 Since the vulnerability has leaked: Calif discovered and reported Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938).
We’re publishing technical details by 1 PM Pacific today, after Oracle releases a patch.
Stay tuned!
— Calif (@calif_io) November 17, 2026
Au début, l’IA n’a proposé que des pistes inutiles. Moins d’une heure après le début des recherches, l’intelligence artificielle a mis le doigt sur une vraie faille de sécurité, bien plus préoccupante que prévu. Selon Calif, il n’a fallu qu’une heure pour trouver la faille, puis deux heures pour mettre au point une attaque, le tout pour moins de 200 dollars de frais de calcul.
« Je suis venu chercher du cuivre et j’ai trouvé de l’or », résume le chercheur.
64 lettres « A » pour pirater un serveur
La faille se cache dans une fonction très banale de Java qui sert à décoder du texte au format Base64. Ce format sert à transformer des données en suites de lettres et de chiffres pour qu’elles circulent facilement sur Internet. La fonction est notamment utilisée pour envoyer des identifiants de connexion ou des fichiers. Sur les processeurs récents, Java utilise une version accélérée de cette fonction. C’est dans cette fonctionnalité que l’IA a déniché une faille de sécurité.
Pour déclencher la brèche, il suffit d’envoyer 64 lettres « A » suivies d’un signe « = » à la fonction. Celle-ci se met alors à déborder et à écraser certaines des données de sa mémoire. Un pirate peut alors en profiter pour lire des informations secrètes, comme des mots de passe ou des clés de chiffrement, explique Calif. C’est la porte ouverte à des vols de données sensibles, susceptibles de compromettre des comptes en banque. Un attaquant peut aussi en profiter pour envoyer ses propres commandes par le biais de la fonction. Lors de ses tests, Calif a piraté plusieurs logiciels très utilisés en entreprise, comme Jira, Confluence ou Jenkins.
« Corriger immédiatement » la faille Java4Shell
L’annonce devait rester secrète jusqu’à la publication du correctif, conformément aux meilleures pratiques du monde de la cybersécurité. Selon Calif, l’information a été divulguée quelques heures trop tôt, alors qu’aucun correctif n’avait encore été annoncé. Le 17 novembre, la start-up a donc publié le résultat de ses travaux.
Le jour même, le géant américain Oracle, propriétaire de Java ,et OpenJDK, la version libre de Java, mettent en ligne un correctif pour colmater la vulnérabilité dans l’urgence. Dans la foulée, la CISA, l’agence américaine de cybersécurité, a appelé toutes les organisations à « corriger immédiatement » la faille pour éviter une explosion des cyberattaques.
 🚨We urge orgs to immediately patch the recently disclosed Oracle Java vuln CVE-2026-114938. This critical memory-corruption vulnerability, known as “Java4Shell,” affects the Base64 decoder of the x86-64 HotSpot JVM, part of the Java Development Kit. 🔗https://t.co/SwrhdPFlZF pic.twitter.com/3QGldeAerV
— CISA Cyber (@CISACyber) November 17, 2026
L’alerte fait rapidement le tour du monde. En Allemagne, le BSI (Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik), l’agence fédérale de cybersécurité, met lui aussi en garde contre les attaques exploitant la faille de Java, rapporte Reuters. Le Canada et l’Inde ont rapidement publié des avis similaires, exhortant toutes les entreprises à agir dans les plus brefs délais.
Une faille jugée « improbable et grave »
Interrogé par la BBC, le chercheur Toby Walsh juge la faille « improbable et grave ». Il rappelle que Java est justement conçu pour protéger la mémoire à l’encontre de ce genre d’erreur. Selon Walsh, « l’IA met désormais au jour davantage de failles, bien plus rapidement ». Le chercheur Pedram Hayati ne cache pas son inquiétude. Il estime que la brèche dans Java pourrait compromettre « des systèmes financiers critiques ».
Pour Fouad Matin, le responsable de la préparation aux cybermenaces chez OpenAI, les travaux de Calif montrent que l’IA peut aider les chercheurs à débusquer des failles graves « dans des logiciels dont nous dépendons tous », selon des propos rapportés par le New York Times.
Bonne nouvelle, aucune cyberattaque n’a encore été détectée. Dans une réaction envoyée à 01net, les chercheurs de Group-IB révèlent n’avoir « trouvé aucune preuve d’exploitation » pour le moment. Comme le souligne le Centre canadien pour la cybersécurité, « cela peut changer rapidement ». C’est également l’avis de Cisco Talos, qui s’attend à voir les tentatives d’attaque se multiplier prochainement.
Avant Java, le chaos PHP
L’histoire de Java4Shell rappelle celle de PHP2Shell. En octobre, Calif avait déjà utilisé l’IA pour dénicher deux failles critiques dans PHP, un autre langage très répandu, plongeant une partie d’Internet dans le chaos. La faille a aussi été divulguée un peu trop tôt, ouvrant la porte à des tentatives d’intrusion. Des pirates chinois se sont rapidement servis de la faille pour mener des attaques. Les versions touchées sont Java 17 (à partir de la 17.0.6), 21, 25 et 27. Comme pour PHP, le plus dur sera de retrouver toutes les copies de Java cachées dans les logiciels et les machines à travers le monde. De facto, des systèmes risquent de rester vulnérables pendant un long moment…

articles.title: Así es la casita autosuficiente de esta familia de Karrantza: “El techo está hecho de tierra y la hierba que va creciendo funciona como aislante y nos protege del sol en el verano y del frío en el invierno”
articles.text:
Erika decidió irse al campo, dejar atrás la ciudad y mudarse con su familia a Karrantza (Bizkaia). Han optado por construir en armonía con el entorno.
“El tejado de la casa es un tejado verde”. Construyeron la casa con materiales locales. De esta manera consiguieron que la mayor parte de su consumo estuviese relacionado con su propio espacio y los productores de la zona. Según explica Erika, son totalmente autónomos en electricidad, tienen su propia producción y son semiautónomos en alimentación.
Paredes de paja y un tejado con hierba
Los cerramientos están realizados con fardos de paja de centeno. Los fardos se hacen con la paja que queda tras la recolección de este cereal. “Lo que queda de cosechar el centeno es la paja. Con esos fardos es con lo que está construida la casa”, explica Erika.
En cuanto al tejado, eligieron una cubrición de tierra vegetal. Sobre esta capa va creciendo la hierba. “No tiene tejas ni nada que se le parezca”.
Erika explica que de esta manera consiguen que haya un aislamiento térmico respecto al exterior. En sus palabras, “Es una forma de construir para que haga de aislante y nos proteja del sol en el verano y del frío en invierno”.
Además, también utilizan el sol para calentar la casa. En una de las fachadas existe una superficie de cristal que deja pasar la radiación solar en invierno. Erika explica que permite que el sol entre y “haga de calefacción pasiva”.
En los meses más fríos también utilizan una chapa de leña. Esta sirve tanto para cocinar como para calefaccionar. “La chapa es con lo que cocinamos en invierno y con lo que calefactamos la casa”.
Electricidad propia, con una inversión inicial
Los paneles solares cubren el consumo de electricidad de la vivienda y de un obrador que tienen junto a ella. En este edificio elaboran parte de los productos que posteriormente comercializan.
Explican que no tienen que pagar la factura de la luz. Sin embargo, tuvieron que hacer una inversión inicial. “No tenemos factura de la luz, pero sí que hemos hecho una inversión grande para tener la instalación de placas fotovoltaicas”.
Esta inversión la consideran a largo plazo. Una vez amortizados los paneles y demás equipamiento, consideran que el sistema es más barato que tener que pagar a una compañía de luz.
Una huerta que exige planificar las compras
Por otra parte, tienen una huerta de subsistencia. En ella planifican qué es lo que tienen que sembrar para que tengan determinados productos durante el año. Por ejemplo, es el caso de las cebollas y puerros, así como de las verduras de temporada. Además, en la parcela tienen árboles frutales.
Los productos que no pueden obtener los buscan básicamente en los agricultores y ganaderos de la zona. En el caso de la carne, miel o lácteos, aprovechan los de productores de la zona. Para otros productos como lentejas o garbanzos, los adquieren a granel (en sacos que les duran muchos meses).
También tienen que recibir suministros externos en el caso del obrador. En este utilizan harina de trigo ecológica. Explican que en Euskadi no hay suficiente producción para cubrir todas sus necesidades. Por ello tienen que traer parte de la materia prima de otros territorios.
