For that, you get a swish new remote and 4K TV output, although if you want the likes of Dolby Atmos you can always pay slightly more for the Fire TV Stick Plus (£34.99) or Max (£46.99).
Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K: was £69.99 now £31.99 at Amazon
The vinyl countdown
Shout out to any Europe fans who saw what I did there…
Anyway, quick PSA: vinyl is not a durable format — you need to store it properly and treat it with care.
That's why I love this compact little record player stand: yes, it's small, but you get four vinyl storage cubby-holes — because we never ever stack records flat like coasters, one on top of the other — and it gives your turntable what it needs.
And in case you're new to this (that's OK, we're all here to learn) what a turntable requires is its own dedicated, low resonance stand. Vibrations are the enemy of analogue audio and your turntable's delicate needle tracking through its ever decreasing circle, you see. Don't be putting your plate-spinner on the coffee table upon which you regularly eat toast and then expect smooth playback, OK?
Also, this chic-looking vinyl stand is 15% off, which is a tidy little saving.
Costway Record Player Stand: was £64.95 now £55.19 at Amazon
Oh, this may also be my 'vinyl' post of the day (sorry) as I hand back over to a responsible adult, but catch you later deals lovers — and remember, always enjoy the music!
The darling buds of Black Friday
What if you want earbuds? I've got you too — and although they're more expensive, I have to tell you they're so worth it. I tested them, I've written odes to them and now, I need you to know about them.
Technics makes one of the only pairs of earbuds that will allow you to connect to three devices simultaneously. And these are my daily-use buds, so believe me when I tell you that I cannot go back to two now — not when the Technics EAH-AZ100 will stay hooked up to my iPhone, my MacBook and my tablet without bumping me off one. Also, the call-handling is excellent thanks to Sidetone, a great little feature that amplifies your voice just a little, so you can hear yourself and won't shout in calls (or on the bus, say).
The fit is sublime, the audio is detailed and divine and the build-quality is incredibly premium. Honestly, I have been recommending them at full price, but they're an excellent buy at this lowest-seen price.
Technics EAH-AZ100: was £259.99 now £179.99 at Amazon
You can can-can!
They say write about what you know, and since my encyclopaedic knowledge of ballet, contemporary dance and musical theatre is perhaps irrelevant right now, I need to tell you about my deep, deep love for these inexpensive CMF by Nothing headphones (or 'cans' as we say in the business).
I reviewed them at their full RRP of £79 and said — in my actual header — that "CMF Headphone Pro could easily cost twice as much".
And now, they're actually 38% cheaper! There's ANC, great on-ear controls, a whacking great battery life and full-throttle, zealous audio. This is easily my cheap headphones deal of Black Friday (and I test headphones for a living now — you know, since my body won't let me dance like it did in my 20s… or even my 30s… *sigh*).
CMF BY NOTHING Headphone Pro: was £79 now £49 at Amazon
Welcome to my turntable TED talk
Howdy! I'm TechRadar's Audio Editor Becky, just clocking on for an hour or so (until my boss comes back from "other work") and while I'm on the mic, you'll be getting some top hi-fi and headphone savings. So strap in!
First up, let's talk turkey turntables. This excellent Bluetooth-enabled Sony deck had big shoes to fill when it landed earlier this year, and it only went and filled them. It reviewed beautifully, as did the powered speakers I'm pairing it with — that's right, no separate amp stack needed here. Just hook 'em up and get to spinning. Or simply snap up the turntable and use your Bluetooth speakers at home, if you're fine with Bluetooth audio.
Two products + two discounts = a complete cheap vinyl system. That's what I bring to the table.
This is the first time I've seen either product discounted too, and won't they both look delightful in your budget-savvy, hi-fi happy home? (No, you cannot have the cat. She is not for sale and anyway, she has very specific music tastes…)
Sony PS-LX5BT: was £399 now £291 at Amazon
Edifier MR5 (3-Way Active Speakers): was £279.99 now £189.99 at Amazon
Shoot for the stars
Smart telescopes are truly awesome devices that make it easy to take photos of galaxies and nebulae without needing to spend hours setting it all up — or a fortune buying all the kit.
I've owned and tested several of these brilliant devices, such as the Seestar S30 Pro, and I'm currently putting the new Seestar S30 Plus through its paces. This is a well-priced model that's ideal for beginners but that still produces superb results — and right now its on sale at Amazon.
Seestar S30 Plus smart telescope: was £449 now £426 at Amazon
A must for cat lovers
One of my daughters is pretty much obsessed by cats, so this might have just made it on to my Christmas gift guide list. With 1710 bricks it'll be quite the undertaking to make it — but that's great, because it means it'll keep her busy for days. When finished, it stands more than 32cm tall, thus reducing the need for her to have an actual kitten any time soon.
LEGO Ideas Tuxedo Cat: was £90 now £65 at Argos
Sonos deals are starting
Looking for a soundbar? Two highly rated Sonos soundbars have early discounts. The Arc Ultra is the company's biggest and best soundbar, and really impressed our Acting Editor in Chief Matt Bolton when he reviewed it. But the Beam 2 is half the size, half the price, and super-impressive in its own right if you want something not quite so imposing.
Sonos Beam Gen 2: was £449 now £339 at Amazon
Sonos Arc Ultra Soundbar: was £999 now £799 at Amazon
The laptop deal to beat so far
Currys has come out strong with one of the best laptop deals in the early Black Friday sales.
This Acer Swift Air 14 is an excellent all-around modern machine, powered by an Intel Core 5 CPU, 8GB of RAM, and a 512GB SSD. Seeing 16GB of RAM would have been nice to bump up the performance, but this is still a strong everyday laptop for home, work or college use — especially with the battery life of up to 21 hours. We scored it 4.5 stars in our Acer Swift Air 14 review.
Acer Swift Air 14: was £699 now £499 at Currys
£100 off Amazon's Kids Tablet 11
Need a babysitter? My go-to was always one of Amazon's Fire Kids tablets. I joke, of course (sort of), but the Fire tablets have always been a great way to keep young'uns entertained without a risk that they will access things they shouldn't.
Fire Tablets are dead now — and instead you have the Amazon Kids Tablet 11, which adds Google Play Store access and upgraded tech to make the whole experience faster and a bit more premium. But you still get the very handy colourful bumper case, 1-year subscription to the Amazon Kids+ service and in-built parental control software. There's also a cheaper 8.7-inch version, plus different designs for older and younger kids. Great, eh? And right now it's £100 off for Black Friday.
Amazon Kids Tablet 11: was £289 now £199 at Amazon
The Nintendo Switch 2 bundle to beat
Hi all, Marc here on this live blog for a few hours.
While half the world is obsessed with a certain PS5 and Xbox game right now, that doesn't mean Nintendo Switch fans have nothing to be excited about. The official Nintendo Store has already come in strong with some excellent Switch 2 bundles for Black Friday, but there are plenty of others popping up now too. Play that chest-opening jingle.
This latest one is over at Very, where you can get a Nintendo Switch 2 console with Nintendo Switch Sports Resort and Ocarina of Time for £449.99. Essentially, you're getting the five-star remake of the Legend of Zelda classic for free in this bundle, which is a huge steal.
Nintendo Switch 2 + Nintendo Switch Sports Resort + Ocarina of Time: was £509.98 now £449.99 at Very
A fantastic price on one of the best OLED TVs
We love the LG C6. How much? Well, we crowned it our TV of the year last month. The fact that it's on sale for a record-low price at Amazon (and also Currys) in its 65-inch guise is therefore cause for celebration.
It has a ton of great features, an amazing picture that's a lot brighter than last year's model and it's available for a bargain price (relatively speaking) — what more could you want from a premium TV?
LG C6 65-inch OLED TV: was £1,899 now £1,699.99 at Amazon
A big deal for physical media fans
The Panasonic DP-UB820 is the best 4K Blu-ray player on the market, and its price rose this year. Currys has a deal that brings it back down to the price it was before, roughly.
With Blu-rays really having a renaissance at the moment (and with The Odyssey out now on disc too), this will be very popular over Black Friday.
Panasonic DP-UB820 4K Blu-ray player: was £429 now £379 at Currys
A top toothbrush
I was always put off by the thought of dropping lots of money on an electric toothbrush when most of the cheaper alternatives were fine. But when I finally picked up the original Suri about a year or so ago, I didn't regret my purchase at all.
The newer 2.0 version is now on sale for Black Friday, featuring an impressive 40-day battery life, fast wireless charging over USB-C, a useful pressure sensor, and comes with handy extras like a magnetic wall mount and UV cleaning travel case.

Black Friday isn't all about giant TVs and game consoles, it's also become a great time of the year to stock up on some essentials for the home. articles.title: Sony’s WH-1000XM5 are cheaper than ever for Black Friday
articles.text:
Back in my day, the only “Doorbuster” sales were at physical retail stores. But now, you can get ultra-low prices before Black Friday whether you want to shop in-store or online. One that stands out is the previous-generation Sony WH-1000XM5 noise-canceling headphones, which are marked down to their lowest price ever, just $169.99 at Best Buy. While their MSRP is $399.99, they’ve been spotted as low as $198 in the last few months.
Sony’s WH-1000XM5 are cheaper than ever for Black Friday
Last-generation noise-cancelling headphones are still a great option for traveling or staying focused.
The WH-1000XM5 launched in 2022, and despite having been succeeded by the WH-1000XM6, they’re still an excellent set of headphones. Their active noise cancellation effect is one of the best out there — competitive with the latest models from Bose and Apple — and the sound profile is tighter and more balanced than the older Sony headphones. There are some minor downsides, like a bulky case and all-plastic design, but those seem easier to overlook at this lower price point.
The newer Sony WH-1000XM6 improve the sound and noise cancellation, with quality of life upgrades not present in the XM5, like a folding design and more comfortable headband. However, they’re significantly more expensive, currently discounted to $348 during Black Friday (Amazon, Best Buy), down from their MSRP of $450.
To make shopping a little more confusing, the newer WH-1000XM4C sit between the XM5 and XM6 in terms of price, and are a slightly updated version of the older XM4 model with its foldable design. Our reviewer John Higgins thinks the XM4C’s noise cancellation lags behind, so I’d opt for the XM5 over them, especially at the sale price.

articles.title: Simulation of Plasma Chambers for Predictive Simulation of Semiconductor Manufacturing
articles.text:
Home >
                                                                    Manufacturing, Packaging & Materials >
                                                                Simulation of Plasma Chambers for Predictive Simulation of Semiconductor Manu...                                                    
Manufacturing, Packaging & Materials
                        WHITEPAPERS
		
Linking plasma chamber simulation with feature-scale process modeling to predict etch profiles, evaluate wafer uniformity, and optimize plasma etching processes.
								November 19th, 2026 - 
								By: Silvaco
								
							
Plasma etching and deposition processes increasingly determine the manufacturability of advanced semiconductor devices, where smaller features, more complex geometries, stricter wafer-uniformity requirements, and new chemistries demand predictive control of ion fluxes at the wafer surface. Kinetic plasma simulation provides a physics-based route to this control by resolving sheath dynamics, ion-neutral transport, and ion angular and energy distributions that cannot be captured reliably with bulk fluid approximations alone. VSim Plasma applies Particle-in-Cell modeling with Monte Carlo collisions to compute self-consistent electromagnetic fields, charged-particle motion, collisions, and current deposition. Validation against inductively coupled plasma measurements shows strong agreement for electron temperature and plasma potential, reasonable density agreement, and consistent electron energy probability function behavior. Coupling plasma-derived ion angular and energy distributions into Victory Process enables feature-scale etch simulation, linking chamber conditions and waveform design to process variability and profile evolution.
Read more here.

articles.title: Enabling Real-Time AI for Scientific Instruments with GPU-Native Data Acquisition | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
In science and industry, analyzing sensor measurements in real time can enable AI to adjust processes, guide experiments, and search for better operating conditions. Yet limits on how quickly the measured data can be moved and processed often shape how an instrument is designed, from readout electronics to acquisition timing. What could scientific instrument makers simplify—or make possible—if processing could keep pace with their sensors?
NVIDIA DAQIRI is a software-defined data acquisition library that moves high-bandwidth instrument and sensor data into GPU-ready workflows. It enables developers to process measurements during acquisition without first writing them to disk. An NVIDIA Holoscan platform library, DAQIRI bridges sensors optimized for measurement with programmable GPU platforms for scientific analysis, AI inference, and feedback applications.
For existing Ethernet-capable instruments, this opens opportunities to add processing and feedback capabilities, as described in the previous post, Enable Real-Time AI for High-Speed Data Acquisition with NVIDIA DAQIRI. For new instruments, it allows opportunities for reconsidering acquisition constraints from the start.
This post explores how a new electron microscopy camera and GPU processing enable analysis during acquisition. It then introduces new DAQIRI features, including hardware packet reordering, performance and throughput improvements in the library, and a low-latency NIC polling mode for time-sensitive packet processing.
Case study: Connecting high-dynamic-range imaging to GPU processing
A high-dynamic-range electron microscopy camera developed at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory’s Molecular Foundry illustrates what becomes possible when advanced detectors and GPU processing are designed to work together.
Electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) measures the energy electrons lose as they interact with a sample, helping scientists identify which elements are present and how they are bonded together. These measurements contain both strong and faint signals. To capture those differences in intensity, the conventional approach uses two separately optimized acquisition processes in rapid succession.
This requires precise coordination of the electron optics, exposure timing, and detector readout. The resulting measurements then need to be aligned and combined, adding complexity to both acquisition and processing. The new high-dynamic-range camera developed at the Molecular Foundry captures strong and faint signals together.
This advancement simplifies the experimental setup and microscope optics, but generates more than 500 gigabits of data per second (Gbps)—a stream that must be received and processed to make those measurements useful during acquisition. This is over 500x faster than conventional EELS data streams, which greatly enhances the raw detector information available for further processing and analysis.
Handling that stream requires an acquisition and processing pipeline designed to keep pace with the camera. This is where the collaboration between Berkeley Lab and NVIDIA brings together the camera, DAQIRI, and GPU-accelerated processing. FPGA readout electronics transmit detector data over Ethernet, DAQIRI receives the packets directly into GPU memory, and GPU processing assembles and corrects detector frames before reducing them to energy-loss spectra.
Computation also improves the spatial information recovered from the detector, enabling submicron spatial resolution from sensor pixels measuring 5 micrometers across. Through this pipeline, the team enables inspection of the data during the measurement and adjusting the acquisition parameters and regions of interest in real time, all while processing high bandwidth data incoming at more than 500 Gbps.
The benefits of this approach extend beyond electron microscopy. Connecting sensors to GPU processing can extract more information from measurements and give instrument makers greater flexibility in how they acquire, analyze, and act on data. Realizing those benefits requires efficient data movement, ordered payloads ready for processing, and low-latency communication for feedback.
Designing acquisition paths for intelligent instruments
The latest DAQIRI release adds hardware packet reordering, an optimized library backend for improved throughput, and direct polling for low-latency packet transmission and reception.
Reorder data as it arrives with NIC hardware
Most networks rely on protocol processing or receive-side buffering to handle out-of-order packets, which can add latency and memory overhead. DAQIRI can now offload packet reordering tasks to supported NVIDIA ConnectX-7 or newer NICs, preserving CPU and GPU resources for analysis. For compatible sequence formats, the NIC parses sequence fields and places each payload directly into its ordered position in memory. The application receives the assembled, ordered data without requiring a separate software reorder copy step.
Hardware-based reordering is defined here for a specific receive queue. The configuration dictates how to parse the sequence number from the packet header, which reordering method to use, and how missing packets should be handled.
- name: "rx_reorder_seq_1024"
  reorder_engine: "hw"          # NIC places payloads in order
  cyclic_sequence: true         # Confirm compatible cyclic numbering
  missing_action: “drop”        # Drop partial batches on RX timeout
  reorder_type: "gpu"           # Deliver packets to GPU memory
  memory_region: "Reorder_RX_GPU"
  payload_byte_offset: 42       # Skip 42-byte Ethernet/IPv4/UDP header
  packet_size: 8192             # Payload bytes per output slot
  flow_ids: [201]               # Apply reorder to RX flow 201
  method:
    seq_packets_per_batch:      # Reorder by one sequence field
      sequence_number:
        bit_offset: 336         # Sequence starts at bit 336
        bit_width: 32           # 32-bit sequence field
      packets_per_batch: 1024   # 1024 packets per output buffer
Use the ibverbs engine for efficient acquisition
DAQIRI introduces an ibverbs engine for high-rate receive and transmit of raw Ethernet packets. Built on libibverbs and NVIDIA DevX, the engine is selected by default for raw Ethernet streams. Developers can also select it explicitly by adding engine: “ibverbs” to their DAQIRI configuration, without changing how they use the application API. By reducing per-packet CPU overhead, the ibverbs engine delivers approximately twice the per-core throughput of the previous default DPDK backend at small packet sizes (up to 1024 bytes) and extreme data rates (greater than 200 Gbps), based on benchmark tests performed on the NVIDIA DGX Spark, NVIDIA IGX Thor, and NVIDIA RTX PRO server platforms.
Reduce feedback latency with direct polling
Intelligent instruments may require latency-sensitive feedback from GPU analysis to adjust acquisition or control settings. The DAQIRI direct polling mode reduces communication latency by letting the application thread receive and submit packets directly, eliminating the handoff to a separate I/O worker. In cabled loopback benchmark tests, application send-to-receive latency on the order of 2-4 µs has been demonstrated in direct polling mode. When using the ibverbs engine, developers can select direct polling for control queues while retaining batched processing for high-throughput data streams.
Set poll_mode: "direct" on the latency-sensitive TX and RX control queues so the application thread submits and receives packets directly.
# TX/RX queue settings in example configuration file
tx:
  queues:
  - name: "control_tx"
    id: 0
    poll_mode: "direct"         # App thread submits packets
    memory_regions: ["Control_TX"]
rx:
  queues:
  - name: "control_rx"
    id: 0
    poll_mode: "direct"         # App thread polls received packets
    memory_regions: ["Control_RX"]
Run the direct-polling latency benchmark using a cabled loopback between TX and RX ports on the same host.
First, replace the configuration’s hardware address placeholders and other system-specific settings with values for your system:
sudo ./build/examples/daqiri_bench_raw_latency 
examples/daqiri_bench_raw_latency_ibverbs.yaml --samples 
10000 --warmup 1000 --csv latency.csv
Get started with GPU-native data acquisition
During the process of making scientific instruments, GPU-native data acquisition enables you to design around what will be measured and your desired means of response. Advanced detectors and GPU processing can work together for reconsidering acquisition constraints.
The latest DAQIRI capabilities extend the options for moving and organizing measurements efficiently and connecting analysis to experimental control. That means more engineering effort can focus on measurement quality and scientific insight.
To explore these capabilities, start with the DAQIRI documentation and DAQIRI configuration examples. Then use the DAQIRI benchmarks to evaluate throughput and communication latency on your hardware.
To learn more, check out these related resources:
- Explore the NVIDIA/daqiri GitHub repo
- Browse the DAQIRI plus TensorRT Streaming Inference Reference Application
- Generate DAQIRI Configurations for your hardware

articles.title: “Tienes una racha ganadora y echas a Michael Jordan del equipo”: Elon Musk sobre la salida de Jensen Huang de Nvidia
articles.text:
Elon Musk cuestionó la salida de Jensen Huang como CEO de Nvidia tras denuncias sobre una relación extramatrimonial y vínculos con una mujer presuntamente sospechosa de espionaje chino.
“Tienes una racha ganadora y de repente echas a Michael Jordan de tu equipo”, le dijo Musk a Andrew Ross Sorkin en la cumbre DealBook. “No me parece una decisión inteligente”, mencionó.
El director ejecutivo de SpaceX y Tesla había afirmado previamente que sería un “honor” contratar a Huang. Ambos se conocen desde hace años por la colaboración de Nvidia con Tesla y OpenAI.
Tesla fue un cliente relevante del fabricante de chips de inteligencia artificial, mientras que Huang destacó en reiteradas ocasiones la estrategia de inteligencia artificial de Musk, incluidos los vehículos autónomos, xAI y el robot Optimus.
Qué otros líderes apoyan el regreso de Jensen Huang a Nvidia
Musk aseguró haber escuchado la misma postura de otras personas, incluido el presidente Donald Trump. “Creo que el presidente ha expresado públicamente que piensa que Jensen debería haberse quedado como director ejecutivo, y todos los que conozco piensan lo mismo. El empresario añadió: “Nosotros no formamos parte de la junta, ¿verdad?”.
La posición de Musk coincide con una carta abierta firmada junto con Tim Sweeney, director ejecutivo de Epic Games, y Garry Tan, presidente de Y Combinator, para pedir el regreso de Huang a la conducción de Nvidia.
La petición reunió más de 165.000 firmas, entre ellas las de más de 7.500 empleados de Nvidia, una cifra equivalente a más del 15% de la plantilla. Travis Kalanick, cofundador de Uber, escribió: “Huang erró, sí, errar es humano, pero no creo que nada de lo que hizo alcance el umbral para separarlo de su compañía”.
Cuál es la posición de la junta directiva de Nvidia sobre el regreso de Jensen Huang
La junta directiva de Nvidia aceptó por unanimidad la renuncia de Huang y no contempla reincorporarlo como director ejecutivo. Su presidente, Harvey Jones, atribuyó la salida a la conducta personal del empresario y a su “falta de franqueza”.
En una conferencia con inversores celebrada en los últimos días, Jones sostuvo que la empresa busca reemplazantes tanto dentro como fuera de la compañía. “No habrá un clon de Jensen”, afirmó, aunque señaló que Nvidia procura líderes con experiencia técnica y trayectoria probada.
Asimismo, la posibilidad de que Huang vuelva a Nvidia enfrenta objeciones dentro del Gobierno de Estados Unidos. El secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, reclamó una “reorganización drástica” de la conducción de la compañía y sostuvo que el próximo director ejecutivo debería ser elegido fuera de la empresa.
Huang deberá testificar ante el Congreso de Estados Unidos el próximo mes por asuntos vinculados con la seguridad nacional y los controles de exportación. Su dimisión estuvo precedida por informes sobre relaciones con empleadas de Nvidia.
Qué ha pasado en Nvidia luego de la salida de Jensen Huang como CEO
La directora ejecutiva interina de Nvidia, Colette Kress, comunicó que los aumentos salariales y las nuevas acciones para los empleados serán entregados en diciembre de 2026, en lugar de marzo de 2027. El anuncio fue realizado durante la primera reunión general de la empresa desde la renuncia de Huang.
Las consultas sobre salarios fueron las más comunes entre las 700 preguntas enviadas por el personal antes del encuentro. La segunda petición más solicitada fue mayor transparencia de la junta directiva, según Wired.
Recientemente, Huang manifestó que aceptaría volver si la junta concluye que su retorno favorece a los accionistas, los empleados, Nvidia y Estados Unidos. “Me sentiría honrado de atender esa petición y volver a ejercer como director ejecutivo”.
Un aliado de Huang dijo a Financial Times que un grupo de ejecutivos de Silicon Valley organizó un “cuartel de guerra” para impulsar su regreso y reunir respaldo en la Casa Blanca.

articles.title: Cyient Semiconductors bags $10M from GlobalFoundries
articles.text:
Cyient Semiconductors bags $10M from GlobalFoundries
Cyient Semiconductors will use the capital to scale custom-chip development, manufacturing access, and global growth.
Cyient Semiconductors has secured $10 million equity investment from GlobalFoundries, a global semiconductor manufacturer serving the data centre, automotive, and communications markets.
Hyderabad-headquartered Cyient said the investment carries the same pre-money valuation of $490 million as its recent financing led by Edelweiss, taking its combined post-money valuation to $510 million.
However, the announcement does not explain the calculation behind the combined valuation. The Edelweiss round in May involved approximately $10 million in equity from funds managed by EAAA India Alternatives and affiliated co-investors, alongside structured debt.
The freshly raised capital will be used to expand Cyient's turnkey custom application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) capabilities, accelerate custom silicon development, and improve long-term access to wafers, the silicon discs on which chips are manufactured.
Suman Narayan, Chief Executive Officer of Cyient Semiconductors, said the investment would help the company accelerate innovation, strengthen engineering capabilities, and scale global customer engagements. He described the funding as “a strong validation” of the opportunity for semiconductor innovation from India.
Cyient develops ASICs, chips designed for particular products or functions, as well as power-management products. Its capabilities span chip architecture, design, manufacturing coordination, packaging, testing and qualification. Its customers operate across the automotive, industrial, artificial intelligence, communications and data centre markets.
The company follows a fabless model, meaning it designs chips but relies on specialist manufacturers, known as foundries, to produce them. GlobalFoundries' (GF) involvement is significant in this respect. The companies had already established a channel partnership in August 2025 to provide customers with access to GF’s semiconductor manufacturing services and technologies.
Cyient has also been expanding its product portfolio. In April, it completed an $85 million majority investment in Kinetic Technologies, adding more than 250 power-management and related products, alongside established customer relationships and semiconductor intellectual property.
The latest investment comes amid growing interest in India’s chip-design sector. In February, Bengaluru-based C2i Semiconductors raised $15 million in a Series A round led by Peak XV Partners, while Vervesemi Microelectronics secured $10 million from investors including Ashish Kacholia and Unicorn India Ventures. Both companies are developing chips for applications spanning AI infrastructure, power management, and industrial systems.
However, semiconductor businesses typically require substantial research and development spending and longer periods to bring products to commercial scale, making sustained funding important.
Government support is also expanding. In July 2026, the Union Cabinet approved Semicon 2.0, with an outlay of Rs 1.275 lakh crore, covering chip design, manufacturing equipment and materials, fabrication plants, advanced packaging, research, and talent development.
In November, the government opened applications for support covering equipment and materials, new fabrication facilities, and semiconductor assembly and testing. Of the 12 projects approved under the first phase of the India Semiconductor Mission, five had commenced commercial production by October.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Chrome croule sous les failles : Google déploie la troisième mise à jour de sécurité en huit jours
articles.text:
Google a déployé une nouvelle version de Chrome sur Windows, macOS et Linux. Baptisée Chrome 158, la mise à jour corrige pas moins de 204 failles de sécurité, à savoir six brèches critiques, 62 failles de gravité élevée, 82 failles moyennes et 54 failles mineures.
À lire aussi : Ces 319 extensions Chrome ont espionné des millions d’internautes pendant 10 ans
Six failles critiques dans le cœur de Chrome
Les six failles critiques touchent des composants clés du navigateur. La moitié des failles surviennent quand un logiciel continue d’utiliser une zone de mémoire qu’il a déjà libérée. Un pirate peut alors s’engouffrer dans la brèche pour corrompre des données, ou y exécuter du code malveillant. Les trois autres failles touchent le composant GPU et ANGLE, la couche graphique de Chrome, et le module Media. Dans les deux cas, Chrome écrit au-delà de l’espace mémoire prévu, ce qui peut écraser des informations voisines.
Pour l’instant, Google n’a pas découvert le moindre indice qui laisse penser que les failles ont été exploitées dans des cyberattaques. Comme toujours, le géant de Mountain View reste discret et refuse de communiquer davantage d’informations techniques, pour des raisons de sécurité.
IA et explosion des failles de sécurité
C’est déjà la troisième mise à jour de sécurité en l’espace de huit jours. Le 3 novembre, Chrome 157 est arrivé avec 213 correctifs. Six jours plus tard, Google a colmaté en urgence une faille zero-day déjà exploitée par des pirates. Deux jours après, un nouveau correctif est venu combler 83 failles dans le code du navigateur. Au total, plus de 500 failles ont été comblées en seulement deux semaines.
Ce déluge de vulnérabilités découle évidemment de l’essor de l’IA générative. Les notes de Google indiquent d’ailleurs que Claude, l’IA d’Anthropic, est à l’origine de la découverte de huit failles, dont deux des six failles critiques. Google s’appuie aussi sur ses propres outils pour traquer les failles, dont Big Sleep, un agent d’IA conçu par DeepMind et Project Zero.
L’accélération chez Google ne concerne pas que Chrome. La semaine dernière, Project Zero, l’équipe de sécurité d’élite de Google, a annoncé qu’elle allait divulguer les failles trois fois plus vite, qu’à l’accoutumée, en ramenant son délai de 90 à 30 jours. Selon les chercheurs, l’IA permet désormais aux pirates d’analyser un correctif dès sa sortie pour déduire une faille capable de mener à une attaque.
Le correctif est inclus dans la version 158.0.8127.36/.37 pour Windows et Mac, 158.0.8127.36 pour Linux, et 158.0.8127.42 pour Android. Pour installer la mise à jour, cliquez sur les trois points en haut à droite de Chrome, puis allez dans « Aide » et « À propos de Google Chrome ». Le navigateur télécharge alors tout seul la dernière version. Cliquez ensuite sur « Relancer » pour l’appliquer sur le navigateur. Vu la cadence actuelle des mises à jour de Chrome, on vous conseille d’activer les mises à jour automatiques.

articles.title: Microsoft tests new Edge Lockdown Mode that disables GPU APIs
articles.text:
Microsoft is developing a new Edge security feature to reduce the attack surface by disabling the WebGL, WebGL2, and WebGPU APIs.
Inspired by Apple's Lockdown Mode, the new feature shares the same name and builds on Edge Enhanced Security Mode (also known internally as Super Duper Secure Mode), which disables Just-In-Time Compilation (JIT) from the V8 processing pipeline.
The new Edge Lockdown Mode offers optional, extreme protections for users facing highly targeted attacks who are willing to sacrifice website compatibility for stronger defenses.
"Lockdown Mode is designed for users who are at particular risk of being targeted in cybersecurity campaigns. This may include journalists, executives, security researchers, and administrators," said Partner Security Group Manager Gareth Evans.
"Individuals whose threat model justifies accepting reduced compatibility in exchange for stronger protection. It may also apply to devices operating within highly restricted environments."
Evans also warned that websites that use the disabled APIs (especially those with interactive graphics like games or maps) may not work as expected when this security feature is toggled on.
Edge users can test Lockdown Mode by switching to the Canary release channel, enabling the #edge-sdsm-plus flag, restarting the browser, then toggling on Strict mode for "Enhance your security on the web" and blocking WebGL graphics and WebGPU graphics.
After enabling it, users will see a new "Lockdown Enabled" indicator in the address bar when WebGL or WebGPU is blocked on a web page.
While the current Edge Canary Lockdown Mode blocks websites from using WebGL, WebGL2, and WebGPU APIs to stop attacks that try to escalate privileges and escape the sandbox, Microsoft plans to extend the feature in upcoming releases.
"The initial set of Lockdown Mode mitigations focus is the GPU process, a more privileged component that handles complex graphics workloads across browser code, third-party libraries, and device drivers," Evans added.
"Results from this experiment will inform the finished Lockdown Mode experience, including clearer descriptions of restricted capabilities and site-level exceptions that restore trusted sites without weakening protection everywhere else."
According to the company's estimates, this new security feature would have blocked around 60% of privilege escalation attacks targeting Edge users in the wild.
Last year, Microsoft also introduced a new Edge scareware sensor to ensure Defender SmartScreen blocks scam pages faster, and restricted access to Edge's Internet Explorer mode after learning that hackers were leveraging zero-day exploits in the Chakra JavaScript engine to access target devices.

articles.title: GTA 6 : la carte interactive ultime pour découvrir les secrets de Leonida
articles.text:
À chaque nouvel opus, des fans de Rockstar se regroupent sur Discord et GTAForums pour passer chaque image officielle à la loupe. Le site gratuit State of Leonida, développé par Laze, rassemble les relevés de Yanis et de la communauté GTA 6 Mapping.
Plus de 3 800 marqueurs recensés image par image pour GTA 6
Cette carte interactive de GTA 6 est passée par près d’une vingtaine de versions au fil des bandes-annonces et des captures d’écran. Elle repose sur un travail de triangulation minutieux. En croisant les coordonnées issues des fuites de septembre 2022 avec les angles de vue des trois bandes-annonces officielles et des visuels promotionnels ainsi que le contenu final, l’équipe a cartographié les six régions nommées par Rockstar : Vice City, les marécages des Grassrivers, l’archipel des Leonida Keys, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia et le parc national du Mont Kalaga.
L’outil recense 3854 marqueurs répartis par catégories, accompagnés d’une barre de recherche complète :
- Les infrastructures et commerces : magasins, stations-service, lignes de transports en commun, aéroports, ports et bâtiments officiels.
- La géographie et les points d’intérêt : lacs, parcs naturels, plages et axes routiers principaux.
- Les détails insolites : la communauté a même répertorié des éléments anecdotiques aperçus dans les vidéos, à l’image d’un mystérieux piano abandonné sur une plage.
Comparateur de taille et mini-jeu intégré
Le site propose aussi plusieurs outils annexes. Un outil de superposition permet de comparer l’échelle de Leonida avec les anciennes cartes de Rockstar, de Vice City et San Andreas jusqu’à GTA 4, GTA 5 et Red Dead Redemption 2. Ces superpositions restent une estimation de fans. Côté officiel, Aaron Garbut, codirecteur du studio Rockstar North, a indiqué à Game Informer fin septembre que Leonida fait environ deux fois la taille de la carte de GTA 5.
Le site intègre aussi une base de données de plus de 200 entrées, qui relie chaque lieu à la capture d’écran correspondante. Il propose enfin un mini-jeu baptisé « Find the Marker » : à la manière de GeoGuessr, il faut retrouver sur la carte l’endroit où a été pris un extrait de bande-annonce, avec un classement communautaire à la clé.
Cette reconstitution, menée sans aucun lien avec Rockstar Games ou Take-Two, peut désormais être comparée au jeu. GTA 6 est disponible depuis ce jeudi sur PS5 et Xbox Series X/S.

articles.title: Inside Helium Health’s difficult year
articles.text:
On November 4, employees at Helium Health, a Lagos-based healthtech startup, received an email from its People & Culture team thanking them for staying with the company through what the company described as “challenging moments.”
That same day, a picture of Dimeji Sofowora, its current CEO, standing beside Babajide Sanwo-Olu, the governor of Lagos State, and Olumide Balogun, Google’s director for West and East Africa, was published as they announced a ₦3.4 billion ($2.5 million) grant from Google.org, tech giant Google’s philanthropic arm. The funding will finance artificial intelligence tools that flag pregnancy risks and improve maternal care in four Nigerian states.
While Sofowora said the timing of both events was “coincidental,” together they signal a return to normalcy for the startup after a turbulent year marked by a leadership change and months of unpaid staff salaries.
“There were delays to salary payments during a period of the year,” he told TechCabal in an emailed response on Friday.
In the email sent to employees, the startup described the delays as “a difficult experience.”
“The November 4 communication was an internal email from our People & Culture team intended to recognise and thank employees for their commitment and to confirm that outstanding allowances had been settled,” Sofowora said.
For nearly a decade, Helium Health worked to digitise the operations of African hospitals. It raised at least $40 million, said it had worked with over 1,000 healthcare facilities, and lent money to hospitals.
Sofowora, who took over as chief executive in August, said the salary delays came from “temporary cash-flow timing” and that the company kept staff informed. Helium Health declined to disclose the number of affected employees or confirm how long the delays lasted. Former employees say they were owed salaries for at least six months.
Nigeria’s difficult healthtech sector
Helium Health’s troubles show the difficulties of running a healthtech startup in Nigeria’s healthtech sector, which saw 40 startups become inactive between 2020 and 2025. Founders and investors point to infrastructure challenges, the difficulty of making money servicing hospitals, and a funding slowdown as reasons why many early healthtech startups struggle to survive.
Spurred by sudden demand for digital health services after COVID-19, funding into Nigerian healthtech startups grew from about $5.5 million in 2019 to nearly $55 million in 2023, and Helium Health’s $30 million Series B round that June was more than half of 2023’s total. Healthtech funding later fell to about $18 million in 2024 and about $3 million in 2025. Helium Health has not announced an equity round since.
Helium Health pitched that round mainly as fuel for HeliumCredit, its lending arm for hospitals, clinics and pharmacies. These healthcare providers were already under pressure from inflation, which drove up the cost of running a hospital sharply in 2023.
After the 2023 currency float, health inflation rose from 20.5% in May 2023 to 24.1% a year later, according to an analysis of the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) data, and four listed drug makers saw their cost of sales rise 88% between early 2024 and early 2025.
In 2024, the Health Care Providers Association of Nigeria said about one in five small and medium private hospitals had shut down because of operating costs. By 2024, half of all private hospitals had shut down, according to Dr Raymond Kuti, the former president of The Guild of Medical Directors, while existing ones struggled to survive due to operating costs.
Despite this contraction in Nigeria’s health care industry, HeliumCredit’s lending period grew longer, from three to six months in 2020 to 12 to 24 months by 2023, so cash came back more slowly. The currency float also added another layer.
Since its 2023 Series B round, the naira has lost about two-thirds of its value against the dollar. Every naira loan the company facilitated and recovered is worth far fewer dollars than it was when it last raised money. Sofowora did not answer questions about who funds its loans, what Helium Health earns from them, or how they have performed.
“In cases where healthcare facilities default on the payment of loans, we will offer a full cycle of monitoring of the facility and provide support to them, whether it is capacity development through education or financial training,” Olubusi, the former CEO, told TechCabal in 2023.
How Helium Health got here
Founded in 2016 by Adegoke Olubusi, Tito Ovia, and Sofowora, Helium Health launched with an electronic medical records (EMR) system to replace paper records in hospitals. That EMR ended up as the base of everything that followed; the hospital data it collected became the credit-scoring engine for its loan products in 2020.
When Helium Health raised its $10 million Series A in May 2020, it planned to expand beyond digitising hospital records and start lending to healthcare businesses in Nigeria and across Africa. Adegoke Olubusi, then CEO, told TechCabal a week after the round that hospitals struggled to grow because few were run as proper businesses, and most had never raised outside funding.
Helium Credit was meant to fix that with zero-collateral loans, and its 2023 $30 million round used the lending business as the main draw for investors in the second-largest Series B for an African healthtech company.
By 2023, HeliumCredit’s loan book had grown from $250,000 to more than $3.5 million, spread across over 200 Nigerian health facilities. It lent on behalf of financing partners, including banks. In 2023, the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), the American government’s development lender, disclosed a $10 million loan to Helium Health to fund new loans to healthcare businesses at a $46,000 average each.
The following year, as inflation rose and hospitals closed, the customers Helium Health earned from through software and lending were squeezed. That likely shaped the startup’s new direction as it focused more on consumer-facing tools, especially in maternal healthcare, and as more of its funding came from donors like Google.
Delayed salaries, leadership change
From January, Helium Health owed salaries, at least seven months before Olubusi stepped down, one employee said.
Three current and former employees told TechCabal that Helium Health owed them salaries, in some cases for six months. One former employee, who asked not to be named to avoid retaliation, said in June they were owed more than ₦2 million ($1,470).
“At this point, I’m unsure if or when I’ll receive the outstanding amount, as my follow-up emails are no longer being responded to,” they said in August.
“Former employees whose final entitlements were still being processed when we responded in August have since completed their exit processes, as well as received those entitlement payments,” Sofowora told TechCabal.
In August 2026, Olubusi stepped down as chief executive after nearly a decade, leaving Sofowora as the only co-founder still running the company.
“A decade of belief, courage, sacrifice, and turning a simple conviction into reality; healthcare in Africa could work better, and technology would play a meaningful role in making that happen,” Olubusi wrote in a public farewell message.
Sofowora declined to discuss the reasons for his exit, calling them “private personnel matters.” He said the transition “is being managed in an orderly manner and does not change the company’s core strategic priorities.”
For the four states rolling out Helium Health’s maternal health tools with Google, Helium Health’s finances now matter as much as its technology. For now, Helium Health says its business remains on track. The company continues to operate across its markets and business lines and says Olubusi’s departure has not disrupted its daily operations or changed its strategic priorities.
“We remain focused on expanding our healthcare technology business,” Sofowora said.

articles.title: The Governance Gap in Open-Weight AI and What to Do About It
articles.text:
Open-weight AI has gone mainstream. As of September 2026, some estimates suggest 42% of enterprises surveyed were running open-weight models in production, up from 31% just two months earlier. But downloading a model also means taking on responsibilities that a provider might otherwise handle, and many organizations have yet to put clear ownership and controls in place.
Renting Capability Vs. Running Your Own Copy
When you use an AI model through a provider’s app or service, you’re essentially renting its capabilities. The provider controls the model and handles the infrastructure, updates, and safety controls. You access it through an app or a software connection.
An open-weight AI model makes its learned parameters, the ‘weights’ that shape its behavior, available to download and run yourself. You can run the model on your own infrastructure and adapt it for a particular use case using your own data. The license may limit how you can use it, and running it still carries infrastructure and staffing costs.
Open-weight models are becoming more capable. One estimate puts the best open-weight models roughly four months behind leading models.
Open-weight does not necessarily mean open-source. Access to the weights does not guarantee access to the training code or details of the training data.
When Benefits Clash with Risks
Zoey is a bank analyst using a provider-hosted model to summarize a loan application. The model does a good job of delivering an actionable summary, but to do so, her request, loan file included, has to go to the provider’s servers. The customer’s data is no longer solely in the bank’s hands. A few quarters later, the provider raises its prices and changes its policies in ways that force workflow changes. Switching providers would take time and effort, so Zoey and her team have little choice but to go along, even though it hurts both their budget and their operations.
Let’s look at the same scenario from the perspective of an open-weight model that is running on the bank’s server. If the model is configured to run entirely within the bank’s system, the loan file can stay there too. The bank can apply its own access controls to the model and the data.
In the above example, an open-weight model does seem like a good option, but there are risks that are easy to overlook:
- Trojan horses: Some model files can execute malicious code when loaded. Others may contain hidden behavior that a particular input can trigger.
- An origin story with missing chapters: A popular model on a public repository may not be the developer’s original. Someone may have modified and reuploaded it without explaining what changed. That version could contain a hidden backdoor or have weak safety rules.
- The upgrade won’t knock on your door: A developer may release improved versions, but your copy is not updated automatically. Your team must track updates, test them, and decide when to switch.
- Attack surface just got bigger: Running your own model creates new targets for attackers. You are essentially adding to your IT infrastructure. This includes the servers and GPUs that keep the model running and the systems that retrain it.
Controls to Address Risks
If an open-weight AI model makes sense for your organization, governance should walk in lockstep with deployment:
- Set a regular review schedule for updates and security notices. Decide who approves a move to a new version.
- Assign an owner for each model, with clear responsibility for approving its use, reviewing updates, and responding when something goes wrong.
- Record each model’s source, version, license, and every fine-tune. Also record its file hash. It’s a unique fingerprint that changes if anyone alters the file.
- Give teams an approved internal repository to fetch models. Before adding a model, verify its source and check its file fingerprint or digital signature against a trusted reference.
- The rule of thumb should be: ‘trust after testing.’ Test the model as an attacker might. Try to bypass its safety rules and look for unexpected behavior, including whether it produces insecure code.
- If you do choose to download a modified version, run the same tests on the developer’s original. This may help reveal weak safeguards or unexpected behavior.
- Higher-risk models need more control. For example, a model that reads source code should also run in isolation, with no access to passwords or keys, and a person assigned to review its output.
- Run the model on a separate server while giving it only the access it needs. Monitor all requests and outputs for unusual behavior, while protecting sensitive information in the logs. If you think a model is misbehaving, have a backup in the form of an earlier version you can switch back to quickly.
Open-weight models need to be scrutinized like any other software brought inhouse. Their benefits are clearly driving their popularity, but there are tradeoffs to be aware of. It’s wise to put ownership and controls in place before putting them into production.

articles.title: Opinion: Ottawa wants an investment supercycle. Here’s how to make that happen. | BetaKit
articles.text:
Liam Gill leads the Capital Program at MaRS Discovery District, the largest innovation hub in Canada. In 2024, MaRS-supported companies raised 13 percent of all venture capital deployed in Canada.
Earlier this month, the federal government released Budget 2026, which Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne says will kickstart an “investment supercycle.” 
An investment supercycle is exactly what our startup ecosystem needs, and the measures announced will help. But to guarantee Canadian entrepreneurs thrive for generations, we need to truly make Canada the greatest place for entrepreneurs to build. This means not only providing competitive economic conditions but building a private-sector-led venture capital (VC) industry to fund growth and build procurement pathways for the government to buy new technologies.
“To guarantee the benefits of Canada’s investment supercycle last, our startups need more than a short-term boost; they need changes that make Canada the greatest place for entrepreneurs to build in the world.”
According to some estimates, there are more than 500 US technology companies with a Canadian founder worth a combined $414 billion USD ($590 billion CAD); half were founded in the last three years. Since 2024, US visas for Canadians have increased by 142 percent. The US has arguably provided better economic conditions for entrepreneurs, which has allowed it to attract the most talented Canadians. The new Canada Growth Incentive, a $15-million CAD capital gains exemption modelled on the US Qualified Small Business Stock program, is the biggest change in a generation to the incentives our entrepreneurs have to build in Canada. It will help reverse this trend.
A report earlier this year by the National Angel Capital Organization (NACO) found that Canada has a $322-million USD funding gap from the pre-seed to Series A stages. That has cost our economy 133,000 high-paying jobs and $143 billion in value.
In October, Industry Minister Mélanie Joly announced $1 billion for the Venture and Growth Capital Catalyst Initiative (Growth VCCI) to provide more capital for our VC ecosystem. While Growth VCCI is a welcome short-term boost, it shouldn’t be mistaken for a long-term solution to Canada’s capital shortage.
This is the fourth iteration of similar initiatives that followed 2013’s Venture Capital Action Plan and two Venture Capital Catalyst Initiatives in 2017 and 2021. In 2012, before the first of these federal programs, Canadian VCs raised $1.78 billion, equivalent to $2.39 billion in 2025 dollars. In 2025, they raised $2.01 billion. Over a similar period, BDC’s average annual direct investing in startups rose from $75 million in inflation-adjusted terms (2009 to 2012) to $354 million in 2025. In other words, real VC fundraising has declined by 12 percent while direct public investment has increased nearly fivefold.
RELATED: Canada sees rebound in angel investments as industry calls for more federal support
If Growth VCCI’s effects are only temporary, how can we leverage the short-term boost to guarantee capital availability for generations to come?
First, we can create new angel investors. A United Kingdom-style innovation tax credit would activate angel investors, steering capital away from passive investments in real estate and GICs into startups.
Second, we can create more VCs. Ten percent of Growth VCCI is already intended to support emerging managers, with the government matching private funds they raise. This should be made permanent by establishing an evergreen fund-of-funds that invests as a limited partner, matching every dollar emerging fund managers raise, up to $10 million per manager.
Third, Canada can become a natural home for global capital. To support our VCs in attracting foreign capital, Canada should create a dedicated legal structure for venture capital funds, combining the tax neutrality of the Cayman Islands with the sub-fund flexibility of Singapore’s Variable Capital Company.
In August 2025, the Canadian government became a customer of two Canadian ventures, signing a $250-million MOU with Cohere and giving a $4.2-million contract to North Vector Dynamics. Last month, both of those companies raised private capital, with Cohere securing $7 billion and North Vector Dynamics securing $29 million. These ventures prove that when the government is willing to be an early customer, it can validate technologies and make ventures a more attractive investment for private markets.
RELATED: Feds reveal breakdown of $750-million VC funding envelope, open Growth VCCI applications
With provincial governments responsible for healthcare, education, infrastructure, transit, and much more, it is vital that they follow the lead of the federal government by creating clear procurement pathways for startups in these industries to sell to the government. Founders won’t build here if they feel they need to sell outside of Canada before our domestic markets will buy their products.
Canada has tremendous potential, and Budget 2026 shows the government wants to match its ambition, but to guarantee the benefits of Canada’s investment supercycle last for generations, our startup ecosystem needs more than a short-term boost; it needs changes that make Canada the greatest place for entrepreneurs to build in the world with strong economic conditions, abundant capital, and clear procurement pathways.
The opinions and analysis expressed in the above article are those of its author, and do not necessarily reflect the position of BetaKit or its editorial staff. It has been edited for clarity, length, and style.

articles.title: Ubisoft demite 166 funcionários em Montreal e Quebec e fala em ajuste de equipes
articles.text:
A Ubisoft vai eliminar 166 posições em Montreal e na cidade de Quebec, no Canadá, em uma nova rodada de demissões que equivale a menos de 4% da sua força de trabalho no país. Foram 128 cortes em Montreal e 38 em Quebec. O anúncio saiu nesta quinta-feira (19), no mesmo dia em que a empresa divulgou o balanço do primeiro semestre do ano fiscal.
A Ubisoft confirmou as demissões em comunicado e deu a justificativa de sempre: ajustar o tamanho das equipes.
“A Ubisoft está reduzindo sua força de trabalho em 166 posições em suas operações de Montreal e Quebec. À medida que nosso portfólio evolui, nossas necessidades de produção estão mudando, exigindo que ajustemos o tamanho de algumas equipes para garantir que nossos recursos estejam alinhados às prioridades atuais de produção e às necessidades do negócio.”
Quem foi atingido pelas demissões na Ubisoft
A empresa não disse quais jogos foram afetados. Segundo a imprensa especializada, que cita informações de bastidores, as demissões atingem principalmente quem trabalhava em projetos cancelados ou com escopo redefinido, mas isso não foi confirmado oficialmente. Esses relatos indicam ainda que os cortes se concentram em funções de produção e apoio e incluem profissionais da Vantage Studios, a subsidiária que reúne Assassin’s Creed, Far Cry e Rainbow Six e conta com investimento da Tencent.
Os dois estúdios estão no centro da operação da Ubisoft. Montreal, com cerca de 4.000 funcionários, trabalha em franquias como Assassin’s Creed, Rainbow Six, Far Cry e Watch Dogs. Quebec, com cerca de 600, foi o estúdio por trás de Assassin’s Creed Shadows, lançado em 2025.
Os funcionários desligados recebem indenização, plano de saúde estendido e serviços de transição de carreira. No comunicado, a empresa diz reconhecer “o impacto que isso pode ter sobre nossos colegas”.
O balanço da Ubisoft no semestre
O semestre fechou com €644,7 milhões em net bookings, queda de 16,5%. No segundo trimestre, as vendas cresceram 16,8%, mas os net bookings, que medem o valor das vendas efetivamente contabilizadas, caíram 20,8% e somaram €388,9 milhões, acima da projeção de cerca de €370 milhões. O quadro de funcionários encolheu quase 1.100 pessoas no semestre encerrado em 30 de setembro.
Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced foi o destaque. Em julho, a Ubisoft informou 3,5 milhões de cópias distribuídas em 14 dias, o que superou as expectativas anuais da empresa. O balanço desta quinta não trouxe números novos do jogo. A Ubisoft afirma que o novo modelo operacional está totalmente em vigor e que o plano de custos segue firmemente dentro do previsto.
Um ano de cortes e cancelamentos na Ubisoft
Em janeiro, a Ubisoft anunciou o cancelamento de seis jogos, entre eles o remake de Prince of Persia: Sands of Time, o adiamento de outros sete e o fechamento dos estúdios de Halifax e Estocolmo. Em junho, fechou Winnipeg, no Canadá, e Belgrado, na Sérvia, e propôs reestruturar o escritório de Barcelona, com consulta aos funcionários. Segundo relatos da imprensa, o pacote de junho pode atingir até 380 pessoas, incluindo a área de publishing global e a unidade de San Francisco.

articles.title: Why UK biotech innovation struggles to scale into industry
articles.text:
Why UK biotech innovation struggles to scale into industry
The UK has biotech innovation. Why is it struggling to scale?
The UK has a problem with innovation, but it’s not the ability to invent, in fact we’re leaders in the invention side, but the ability to turn invention into industry.
Across British laboratories and businesses, scientists and engineers are developing new ways to manufacture the chemicals and materials that underpin modern life. Using biological resources rather than fossil feedstocks, these technologies could help reduce our dependence on oil and gas while opening up new markets for British industry.
Yet developing a promising technology is only the first step. To build a successful business, companies must be able to manufacture at scale, attract investment and compete in a market that has spent decades optimizing around fossil-based alternatives. This is where the UK risks falling behind.
CEO of the BBIA and BioRevolution Coalition.
Biotechnology is becoming an increasingly important part of the industrial technology landscape. Advances in fermentation, microbial engineering and biomanufacturing are creating new ways to produce chemicals and materials that have traditionally depended on fossil resources.
The next industrial opportunity is biological
The bioeconomy may sound like a niche sustainability concept, but its potential reaches massively beyond just environmental policy. The UK’s bioeconomy is already Europe’s fourth-largest by value added, generating around £325 billion and supporting 6.4 million jobs. Biotechnology can use plants, algae, microorganisms and agricultural or food waste to create chemicals and materials traditionally made from fossil resources. These can find applications in everyday products, from medicine like paracetamol to household cleaning ingredients to packaging and industrial materials.
The distinction matters because it’s still not a quiet topic that fossil resources are not just used for energy. They are also the raw materials for much of the physical economy. As this summer has proven, there is a desperate need to reduce our reliance on them and this ultimately means rethinking how we manufacture the products businesses and consumers use every day.
Bio-based describes a material’s biological origin; biodegradable and compostable describe what can happen to it at the end of its useful life under particular conditions. These properties are not interchangeable, and each product must be assessed on its actual performance and environmental impact.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
It gets frustrating when British companies are already demonstrating what is possible. Celtic Renewables uses fermentation to turn residues from the whisky industry into bio-based chemicals. Biome Bioplastics is developing plant-based bioplastics for packaging and other applications.
These are examples of biotechnology moving beyond research into commercial applications and yet, biotech businesses are being held back from that transition.
Why scaling is harder than inventing
In manufacturing, a successful laboratory process must be translated into reliable and repeatable production. Companies then need facilities, equipment, skilled employees, financing and customers prepared to adopt something new.
For emerging bio-based businesses, those challenges can be compounded by a market in which established fossil-derived products benefit from mature supply chains, existing infrastructure and, vitally important, familiar regulatory frameworks.
This creates a vicious cycle. Companies need capital and predictable demand to scale, but investors and customers often want evidence of commercial scale before committing. The UK must do more to bridge that gap between innovation and industrial deployment.
When policy sends mixed signals
Government support for research and development is important, but it cannot deliver an industrial strategy on its own. At present, responsibility for the bioeconomy is spread across government departments, while some tax and carbon-accounting frameworks can disadvantage bio-based alternatives relative to established fossil-derived products.
That creates uncertainty for businesses making long-term investment decisions. Comparisons between materials need to reflect their actual characteristics and use consistent methodologies. Taxation and procurement also influence whether a new material can compete. Public policy can support innovation in principle while leaving commercial incentives that favor incumbent technologies in practice.
There is a further challenge at the infrastructure level. A successful pilot does not automatically translate into a viable commercial facility. First-of-a-kind manufacturing plants can require substantial capital before a business has a proven record of large-scale production.
Five changes that could unlock growth
The BioRevolution Coalition is calling for practical policy changes through its parliamentary petition.
First, the UK needs clear ministerial responsibility for the bioeconomy, giving businesses a coordinated point of contact and a more consistent long-term direction.
Second, tax and policy frameworks should be reviewed to remove unintended disadvantages for bio-based products, while maintaining appropriate environmental and safety standards.
Third, carbon-accounting methodologies should enable fair, consistent comparisons between bio-based and fossil-based materials.
Fourth, public procurement should help create early demand for credible alternatives. Large public-sector buyers, including the NHS, can play a role in demonstrating that new materials can meet practical requirements and perform in real-world settings.
Finally, the Government should help unlock investment in first-of-a-kind commercial facilities.
These measures are not a substitute for companies building competitive products. Nor should bio-based materials receive preferential treatment regardless of their performance. The objective is to ensure that sound technologies can compete on a fair basis and that policy does not inadvertently obstruct their development.
The cost of failing to scale
The UK has an opportunity to build a stronger industrial base around biotechnology and advanced materials. Doing so could support skilled employment, attract investment, improve supply-chain resilience and help reduce dependence on fossil resources. But that outcome is not guaranteed. If Britain continues to develop innovations without creating the conditions for their commercialization, we risk exporting not just products but the economic value that comes with manufacturing them.
The question is whether we want to remain a place where promising technologies are developed, or become a place where they are manufactured, scaled and turned into globally competitive businesses. Now the UK needs a policy framework that allows its innovators to build the industries of the future here.
That is the change the BioRevolution Coalition is campaigning for, and why we are asking the Government to act.

articles.title: Quiénes son Sam Altman y Greg Brockman, fundadores y creadores de ChatGPT con OpenAI
articles.text:
Sam Altman y Greg Brockman son dos de los nombres más importantes en el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial. Ambos participaron en la creación de OpenAI, la compañía que lanzó ChatGPT en noviembre de 2022 y que transformó la manera en que millones de personas utilizan esta tecnología para estudiar, trabajar, buscar información y crear contenido.
Aunque suelen aparecer juntos cuando se habla de los orígenes de OpenAI, sus trayectorias profesionales son diferentes. Altman construyó su carrera en el mundo de las empresas tecnológicas y las inversiones, mientras que Brockman se especializó en ingeniería de software y desarrollo de productos. Antes de fundar la organización, los dos acumularon experiencias en compañías y proyectos que marcaron sus carreras.
OpenAI nació en diciembre de 2015 como una organización de investigación en inteligencia artificial. Entre sus fundadores también estuvieron Elon Musk, Ilya Sutskever, John Schulman y Wojciech Zaremba, entre otros. Por eso, aunque Altman y Brockman son protagonistas de su historia, no fueron sus únicos creadores.
Sam Altman: de Stanford a la dirección de OpenAI
Sam Altman nació el 22 de abril de 1985 en Chicago, Estados Unidos, y creció en St. Louis, Misuri. Su interés por la informática comenzó durante la infancia, cuando recibió su primera computadora y aprendió a programar.
Estudió en John Burroughs School, una institución privada de Misuri. Después ingresó a la Universidad de Stanford, donde cursó Ciencias de la Computación. Sin embargo, abandonó sus estudios en 2005, cuando tenía 19 años, para dedicarse a desarrollar su primera empresa tecnológica.
Ese proyecto fue Loopt, una aplicación que permitía compartir la ubicación con amigos y contactos mediante teléfonos móviles. Altman fue uno de sus cofundadores y director ejecutivo. La compañía consiguió inversiones superiores a los 30 millones de dólares y fue adquirida por Green Dot Corporation en 2012 por aproximadamente 43,4 millones de dólares. Después de la operación, Altman también tuvo responsabilidades en Green Dot.
Su siguiente etapa profesional estuvo vinculada con Y Combinator, una de las aceleradoras de empresas emergentes más conocidas de Silicon Valley. Se incorporó como socio en 2011 y en 2014 asumió la presidencia de la organización, cargo que mantuvo hasta 2019.
Durante ese período ayudó a impulsar emprendimientos que posteriormente alcanzaron reconocimiento internacional, entre ellos Airbnb, Reddit, DoorDash, Dropbox y Stripe. También desarrolló una trayectoria como inversionista en compañías tecnológicas y proyectos relacionados con energía, biotecnología y transporte autónomo.
Uno de sus principales logros llegó en diciembre de 2015, cuando participó en la fundación de OpenAI. En 2019 asumió como director ejecutivo y se convirtió en la principal figura pública de la compañía.
En noviembre de 2023, la junta directiva lo apartó temporalmente del cargo, pero regresó cinco días después, tras una crisis interna que provocó la salida de varios integrantes de la dirección. Desde entonces, continuó al frente de la empresa.
Greg Brockman: el ingeniero que ayudó a construir OpenAI
Greg Brockman nació en Estados Unidos y desarrolló desde joven habilidades relacionadas con las matemáticas, la programación y las ciencias. A diferencia de Altman, su trayectoria estuvo más concentrada en el desarrollo técnico de productos y la infraestructura informática.
Estudió Matemáticas en la Universidad de Harvard y posteriormente se trasladó al Instituto Tecnológico de Massachusetts (MIT), donde cursó Ciencias de la Computación. Sin embargo, tampoco terminó sus estudios universitarios: abandonó ambas instituciones para incorporarse a una empresa emergente que posteriormente se convertiría en Stripe.
En 2010 se sumó a Stripe como uno de sus primeros integrantes. Allí contribuyó a desarrollar la infraestructura tecnológica de la plataforma de pagos y ayudó a ampliar el equipo de ingeniería de cuatro a aproximadamente 250 trabajadores. En 2013 fue nombrado director de tecnología (CTO), puesto que ocupó hasta 2015.
Ese mismo año dejó Stripe para participar en la creación de OpenAI. Inicialmente asumió como CTO y posteriormente pasó a ocupar la presidencia de la compañía. Su trabajo estuvo relacionado con la estrategia técnica, la programación y el desarrollo de los sistemas de inteligencia artificial.
Entre sus reconocimientos figuran su inclusión en la lista Forbes 30 Under 30 de 2018 y su selección para TIME100 AI en 2023. También obtuvo el sexto puesto en la competencia científica Science Talent Search de 2007, gracias a una investigación matemática que fue publicada en una revista especializada.
Los logros que comparten con OpenAI y ChatGPT
Aunque Altman y Brockman son dos de las figuras centrales de OpenAI, ChatGPT no fue creado exclusivamente por ellos. Su desarrollo fue resultado del trabajo de investigadores, ingenieros y especialistas de distintas áreas.
La compañía presentó avances importantes antes de lanzar el chatbot. Entre ellos estuvieron GPT-2, en 2019; GPT-3, en 2020; y DALL-E 2, un sistema capaz de generar imágenes a partir de instrucciones escritas, presentado en 2022. El 30 de noviembre de ese año llegó ChatGPT, inicialmente como una versión de prueba pública basada en GPT-3.5.
Posteriormente, OpenAI presentó GPT-4 en marzo de 2023, amplió las capacidades de ChatGPT y desarrolló herramientas para generar imágenes, analizar información y ayudar en tareas de programación.

articles.title: La Ley de Propiedad Horizontal lo confirma: si un propietario aparca dos vehículos en una plaza de garaje, puedes apelar al artículo 9.1
articles.text:
Puede haber problemas entre vecinos por aparcar dos vehículos en una plaza de garaje. Esto puede ocurrir cuando uno de ellos sobresale y entorpece el acceso o maniobra de otros.
Hay algunas cosas que debemos tener en cuenta para reclamar.
En primer lugar, la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal (LPH) no prohíbe en general aparcar dos vehículos juntos. En el artículo 9.1 indica que deben respetarse los elementos comunes y su buen uso. Además, se debe actuar con diligencia con el resto de propietarios.
Por ello, el propietario ha de mantener sus vehículos en su plaza y no deben entorpecer los accesos o maniobras de los vecinos. Es importante también que sea consciente de las limitaciones que pueden existir en esta plaza. Por ejemplo, el tema de aparcar un coche y una moto juntos es un problema similar.
Qué puede hacer la comunidad si el problema continúa
En caso de que el vehículo invada el paso o entorpezca la utilización de la plaza contigua, es conveniente intentar hablar con el dueño. Si no es posible, podemos pasar la queja al presidente o administrador de fincas. Deberemos indicarle dónde está el problema y cómo nos afecta.
El artículo 7.2 habla de actividades que están prohibidas por los estatutos o que son dañosas para la finca. También incluye las que van en contra de las normas sobre actividades molestas, insalubres, nocivas, peligrosas o ilícitas.
En este procedimiento el presidente requerirá el cese de la actividad. En caso de que el infractor no cambie la situación, el presidente deberá obtener el permiso de la junta para llevar la demanda. Tendrá que adjuntar a la demanda la acreditación del requerimiento fehaciente y la certificación del acuerdo de la junta.
En caso de que la sentencia sea favorable, podrá disponer el cese definitivo y la correspondiente indemnización por daños y perjuicios. En el mismo artículo se habla de la posibilidad de privar de la utilización de la vivienda o local (como máximo 3 años), teniendo en cuenta la gravedad y el perjuicio que se cause a la comunidad.
